ALABAMA CRIMSON TIDE WR LOTZEIR BROOKS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In 2024 their starter threw for 2,844 (64%, 16-11) and was their #1 rusher (726, 4.3). Heir-apparent Ty Simpson (PS#3) hit 14-25-167 in 6 games. Washington transfer Austin Mack (PS#50) hit 2-3-39 and has spent two years in new OC Grubb's system. Last year they added Keelon Russell (PS#5). I said they would not match the run threat (#3 DC) but should improve on his 16-11 ratio. Simpson at one point was the Heisman front runner with the team 8-1 and he had a 21-1 ratio! The last 6 games it was a 7-4 ratio. Mack has a huge arm and Russell put on needed weight while redshirting. They added PS#6 and #26 true frosh. Simpson (#1 DC LAR) threw for 3,567 (65%, 28-5) as a first time starter and they should uncover another solid first year starter. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 they lost their #1 (890, 4.9) and #2 RB (560, 5.0) for a second straight year. In '24 the QB was #1 rusher with Jam Miller #2 (688, 4.6). Last year they lost their #3 (448, 5.7) but had soph Daniel Hill (PS#14), rFr Kevin Riley (PS#12) and added true Frosh AK Dear (PS#2). The run game disappeared with the top 3 RB's all under 4.0 ypc. This year they lose Miller (#7 DC NE, #1, 504, 3.9) but return Hill (284, 3.8) and Riley (224, 3.8) plus Dear (140, 7.4). They add true frosh EJ Crowell (PS#2). This unit can only be much more productive and has plenty of talent. RECEIVERS - In '24 they lost their #1 (798, 20.5) and #2 WR's (668, 13.9) plus a TE (5 st, #3, 327, 16.4). They added true Frosh Ryan Williams (PS#3) and Germie Bernard (419 yd, Wash). Williams had a great frosh year and led with 865 (18.0). Bernard was a solid #2 (794, 15.9). Last year they lost a TE (13 st, #3, 256, 12.2) but added Isaiah Horton (Mia Fla #2 rec) so the unit had 10 VHT's. Williams was inconsistent and fell to #2 (689, 14.1) and true frosh Lotzeir Brooks #4 (441, 13.8). This year they lose WR Bernard (#1, 862, 13.5, #2 DC PIT), Horton (#3, 511, 12.2) and TE Josh Cuevas (#5 DC BAL, 11 st, 411, 11.4). Noah Rogers (PS#4, 441, 13.4 NCSt) was a big addition but was hurt in spring and will miss the start of the season. They add rFr Derek Meadows (PS#6) and true frosh Cederian Morgan (PS#3) plus Rico Scott (98, 8.9) will see a bigger role. Williams returns to form and they are my #10 receiving corps. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '23 Bama allowed a school record 48 sacks (prev rec 43 1996). They did rush for 173 ypg (4.3). In '24 they had 60 career starts and avg 174 (4.6) rush, cutting the sacks to just 24. Last year they lost a 1st tm SEC LG (13/27, #1 DC) and LT (12/12). They returned 1st tm SEC C Brailsford (#5 DC CLE) and 2nd tm SEC RT Kadyn Proctor (#1 DC MIA) plus added Kam Dewberry from A&M and true frosh Michael Carroll (PS#9). They appeared to be a stronger unit but did lose their super mobile QB so the numbers dropped to 104 (3.4) rush with 32 sacks. This year they lose 6 OL (65/138!) and have just 30 career starts. This unit underachieved last year and improving the run game was the focus of the offseason. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '23 they had just three DL with starting experience but 14 VHT's and allowed 125 (3.7) rush with 39 sacks. In '24 they lost a DE (14 st, #4 tkl'r, 7 sk, #4DC) but five of the top six were back, making this the most experienced unit (besides QB) on the team. They allowed 138 (3.7) rush but had just 25 sacks. Last year they lost a DE (13 st, #6 DC) but returned 4 of the top 5 and had 14 VHT's including 6 that rated PS#5 or better. They allowed 127 (3.7) and had 33 sacks. This year they lose all 3 DL starters. They return Yhonzae Pierre, who led in sacks with 8, add Oregon transfers DE Devan Thompkins and NG Terrance Green and have 11 VHT's so are only down a notch. DeBoer says they have more size both inside and outside. LINEBACKERS - In '24 Bama held foes to 56 ypg below avg (#25). Deonte Lawson was OFY vs Oklahoma but still #2 tackler and was back as was #4 tackler Justin Jefferson (PS#4JC) and they added Nikhai Hill-Green from Colorado and DaShawn Jones (10 st WFor '23) and held foes 76 ypg below their average. They return Husky Red Morgan and add VTech starter Caleb Woodson, plus PS#2LB frosh Xavier Griffin and remain strong. In '24 they lost a 1st Tm SEC CB (#2DC), 2nd tm SEC CB (#1DC), 1st Tm SEC S (#1 tkl'r) and 3 backups. They added CB Domani Jackson (PS#2, 11 st USC) and moved up to #12 (60%, 13-17!). OKLAHOMA SOONERS DL TAYLOR WEIN POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 they added Michael Hawkins (PS#19) and he started 3 games (783, 63.3%, 3-2). Last year they had to replace their starter (1421, 63%, 12-3). Their big transfer addition was Wash St's John Mateer (3139, 65%, 29-7, 826 rush) who followed OC Arbuckle here and with a better supporting cast. Mateer was a Heisman candidate early, throwing for 304 ypg (67%, 6-3) the first 4 games but was injured. Hawkins started vs Kent St and Mateer returned vs Texas but it may have been early and he was not the same the next 6 starts with just 174 ypg (58%, 4-4). He did top 300 vs LSU and in the bowl. Hawkins departs so they have Whitt Newbauer (1398, 56%, 12-4 Mercer '24), true frosh Bowe Bentley (PS#8) and rFr Jett Niu (PS#70) as backups. Mateer is back and I look for him to look like he did at the start of 2025. RUNNING BACKS - In 2024 they lost two RB's who combined for over 800 yards. Jovante Barnes led with 577 (4.7) but missed the last 4. PS#45 Xavier Robinson was #3 (233, 4.8). Last year they had the top 3 back and added PS#23 true frosh Tory Blaylock and Cal transfer Jayden Ott. The unit was banged up and the projected top 3 of Barnes/Tatum/Ott combined for a paltry 113 rush yards and all 3 depart. The top two return in Blaylock (480, 4.0) and Xavier Robinson (421, 5.1). They add shifty Colo St transfer Lloyd Avant (417, 4.6) plus true Frosh Jonathan Hatton (PS#5, 230 lb w/speed) and DeZephen Walker (PS#24). This is a talented unit and can only be more productive. RECEIVERS - In '24 the unit was considered a strength. Injuries wiped them out as they were without their top 5 WR's most of the season. The top 4 returnees who combined for 2,299 yards in '23 combined for just 4 catches. Last year they lost their #1 and #2 receivers but they had just 324 (7.7) and 315 (22.4). They added seven transfers including Isaiah Sategna (491, 13.3, Ark) and 3 productive FCS WR's. I said they would be a much improved unit. Sategna had some huge plays and led with 965 (14.4) yards. This year they lose their #2 (620, 10.9), #3 (533, 12.1) and #4 (243, 11.6) receivers but add Virginia's #1, Texas's #3 (516, 17.8) plus Florida and Colo St's starting TE's. This is their best receiving corps in 4 years. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they lost all 5 starters (#1, #6DC). They added five transfers and had 114 career starts. Five OL missed multiple games. They used 7 different OL combo's in their first 9 games and had 3 different starters at each position except RG (13 st). OU rushed for 155 (3.9) and allowed 50 sacks including 19 in a 2 game stretch (broke schl rec twice). Last year they lost 3 OL (16/91) but went from 0 returning starters to four. Injuries hit again with 7 different starting lineup but the final 4 games three frosh started and OL coach Bill Bedenbaugh got them to improve to just 29 sacks allowed but with only 118 (3.5) rush. This year they lose 5 OL including two starters (26/109) but return 5 OL who had 6+ starts in '25, plus add starters from Arkansas and WKU and with 97 career starts will be improved especially if they maintain better health than the last few years. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they lost three starters (#7DC). Jayden Jackson (PS#73) was the first true frosh DT to start here since '01 (Tommie Harris). They allowed 115 (3.1) and had 35 sacks. Last year three starters returned including R Mason Thomas (#1 9 sk) and they added UGA/FSU transfer Marvin Jones (PS#5). They went from one returning starter to three and with 8 VHT backups was my #1 rated DLine. They were a key to the playoff run allowing just 77 (2.4) rush with 45 sacks despite Thomas missing 3 games. This year they lose DE Thomas (6.5 sk, #2 DC KC) and 3 other DL (27 st, 81 tkl, 7 sk). There is plenty of talent returning (10 VHT's) but they are down some from '25's elite unit. DT David Stone (PS#8) is my 1st team AA DT this year. LINEBACKERS - Last year they lost a 2x AA and top 10 all-time tackler for OU. Kip Lewis (#3 tkl'r) had IR td's vs Auburn & Bama in '24 and returned and added Okla St transfer Kendal Daniels (PS#12, 2x All-B12). Kendel Dolby (PS#13JC) started the first two at Cheetah and was one of the top players then was OFY. They had 6 LB's with starting experience. The Sooners held foes to 107 ypg below their average (#7). This year they lose SLB Daniels (#4 DC ATL, 13 st, #4 tklr) their #5 and #11 tacklers. Former walk on Owen Heinecke was #2 tackler and Kip Lewis #1 and both return, plus they add Cole Sullivan (44 tkl) from Michigan so they remain one of the nation's best. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23 OU rose all the way to #8 in the PDR (57%, 18-20!). In '24 they returned 3 starters but one was OFY and they only finished #57 (203 ypg, 60%, 17-9). Last year they lost a 2nd Tm SEC SS (12 st, #4 tkl'r, #4 DC) but had two returning starters. I said they would have a Stock Market climb in the PDR and they did up to #17! CB Courtland Guillory was the 2nd ever true frosh to start a season opener here (PJ Mbanosor '15). This year they lose one starter (#3 tklr) but are more experienced and my #8 secondary. CB Eli Bowen was 2nd team SEC as was S Peyton Bowen and Guillory started 11 games as a true. SPECIAL TEAMS - OU dropped to #51 in my STR in '24. Last year they lost both K's (16-20 fg), and ST RANK L6Y: P (42.3 net). They added UTSA's K Tate Sandell. 2025.....#27 I said they had top 25 potential. Sandell hit 8-9 2024.....#51 50+ and won the Groza Award. JUCO P Grayson 2023 ... #39 ....#70 Miller avg 45.8 (39.2 net) and they were #27. Both 2022 2021 ....#78 are back as is PR Sategna (13.3), and 2nd tm 2020 ... #24 SEC LS Ben Anderson and this is my #7 ST unit. COACHES - Brent Venables enters year five here. He was the DC at Clemson ('12-'21) and before that spent 13 seasons at OU under Bob Stoops. Last year he replaced both his OC and DC for the 2nd straight season. OC Ben Arbuckle was OC at Wash St last year and Co-OC at WKU in '22. The Co-DC is Todd Bates but Venables will call the defense. The STC is Doug Deakin who was SDSt ST Coor the previous 7 years. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE -In 2024, the Oline had 0 returning starters, the WR corps was decimated by injury and versus a much tougher schedule the offense put up just 331 ypg and 24 ppg, their lowest numbers since John Blake's 3rd year in 1998. Last year they brought in Wash St's OC and QB (37 ppg) but only improved to 354 ypg and 26.2 ppg. An early injury to QB Mateer curtailed some of that production. This year they should get to the level I expected last year. DEFENSE - In Venables second year my computer called for them to cut it to 372 ypg and 25.7 ppg and they were close allowing 390 ypg and 23.5 ppg. Venables knows defense and in 2024 my computer had them allowing just 318 ypg and they allowed 318 ypg!!! Last year they lost some top notch players but my computer called for just 280 ypg and they allowed 273 ypg!!! Five of the top 8 tacklers are back and they remain one of the top defenses in the country. 2026 - In Brent Venables, first year after a bowl loss it was the Sooners first losing record since 1998! Oklahoma did have 5 Net Close losses, rated a Stock Market Indicator of +5.2, had 5 Net Upsets which are all signs pointing up! Venables had remade the roster as 56 of the 71 players that participated in the '21 Alamo Bowl were no longer with the team. In '23 the Sooners were my #2 Most Improved Team and upset Texas and were 7-0 and #6. They had 5 and 3 point road losses, but were 10-2 and led Arizona 24-13 but a 87 yd FR td turned it around and they lost for a 10-3 year. In '24 OU moved to the SEC after finishing 176-60 in Big 12 play. Almost all my indicators were pointing down, with the biggest being they faced the SEC's toughest schedule and only had 3 SEC home games! The Sooners offense with 0 returning starters on the Oline and a depleted WR corps had just 279 ypg in SEC play. The D was #6 in the country but the result was another losing season. Last year they faced the SEC's toughest schedule again, plus faced Michigan in non conf action but after going over the team with Coach Venables, I believed this was a playoff caliber roster so despite the rugged schedule they were my #1 Surprise team. I said they had a great shot at going from a losing season all the way to a playoff berth! The Sooners did not let me down and not only make the playoff, but hosted the playoff game! They lost that to Bama despite a 362-260 yard edge. This year they should be more potent on offense, just as strong on D and improved on Special teams. They did benefit from 4 Net Close wins last year and were -16 ypg in SEC play despite their 5-3 record. They do have to play Michigan, Georgia, Texas and Florida all away from home. TENNESSEE VOLUNTEERS OL DAVID SANDERS OFFENSIVE LINE - Tenn had rushed for nearly 200 ypg every year under Heupel. In '24 they were Joe Moore semifinalists for the second straight year and had their highest rush ypg since 1994 with 226 (5.0) but did allow 30 sacks. Last year they lost 4 starters. They added transfers Wendell Moe (AZ, 11/27) and Sam Pendleton (PS#45, NDame, 7/7) plus PS#1 true frosh David Sanders. They went from 112 ret starts to just 46 and zero seniors in the two deep. They fell below that 200 number with 173 (4.5) rush but did allow just 22 sacks. This year they lose one starter but have 5 OL back with 6+ starts and 94 career starts and should be back above 200 and on the Joe Moore Award radar again. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they had 10 DL back who had double-digit tackles in '23. They had 12 VHT's and rotated 3-deep each game. They allowed just 104 ypg (3.0) with 29 sacks. Last year they lost a 2x AA DE (7.5 sk, #1 DC) and 3 DT's (#2DC). They had 14 VHT's but I said would be weaker and they allowed 152 (4.1) rush with 37 sacks. This year they lose all 4 starters and 3 backups! They do add 3 transfers (2 from Penn St) and 5 VHT true frosh but are clearly less experienced and a question mark, plus are learning DC Knowles defense which is usually a learning process. LINEBACKERS - In '24 true frosh Boo Carter emerged at Star (5 st, #6 tkl'r) and Arion Carter led with 68 tackles. Last year they returned their #1, #4 and #6 tacklers going from zero to all 3 starters back. The backups were all frosh but four were VHT's. Boo Carter was dismissed mid year and the Vols slipped to allowing foes 28 ypg above their average. This year they lose their NB (#6 tklr) but return Arion Carter (#1 tklr), Edwin Spillman (#2 tklr) and Jeremiah Telander (#4 tklr) plus add Penn St's #1 tackler Amare Campbell (PS#17) and Kansas St's starting NB and look stronger. DEFENSIVE BACKS - Tennessee's secondary was decimated in the '24 offseason with seven of their top nine gone. Their biggest concern turned into their biggest surprise. Jermod McCoy and Rickey Gibson combined to form one of the top CB duo's in the SEC and the Vols improved from #56 (65%, 15-12) in '23 to #27 (59%, 11-12) in '24. Last year they had McCoy and Gibson back but both were OFY (McCoy DNP ACL Jan, #4 DC LV). With only two VHT's in the unit they fell to #81 (66%, 19-10). This year they lose a FS (#5 tklr) and CB (#2 DC, #7 tklr). They add starters from Michigan, Auburn and App St and 4 other transfers and should have a Stock Market climb up the PDR after an unexpected drop. SPECIAL TEAMS - UT has finished in the top 36 in my ST rankings in ten of the last 12 years. In '24 they lost their K and 4th Tm AA PR (12.9). RFr Max Gilbert was ST RANK L6Y: the Vols first K to made 3 from 50+ in a season 2025 ... #55 since 1985. P Jackson Ross went from 42.5 to 2024 ... #36 43.9 (net 41.3 to 40.5). Boo Carter 16.5 PR. They 2023 ... #22 finished #36 in our STR. Last year everyone was 2022..... #17 ......#2 back but they fell to #55. This year they lose K 2021 2020 ... #64 Gilbert (14-19) but add Louisville's K and should have a Stock Market climb in the STR. COACHES - Josh Heupel took over in '21 after going 28-8 in three years at UCF. He has led UT to 3 straight 9 win seasons for the first time since Phil Fulmer did it from '95-'99. Heupel was OC at Mizzou in '16-'17, OC at Utah St in '15 and Co-OC at Oklahoma ('11-'14). 4th year QB Coach Joey Halzle is the 4th year OC. New DC Jim Knowles was DC at Okla St, Ohio St ('22-'24) then Penn St ('25). STC is Evan Crabtree. OL BRAELIN MOORE LSU TIGERS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '23 Jayden Daniels threw for 3,812 (72%, 40-4), rushed for 1,134 (8.4, 10 td) and won the Heisman Trophy! Garrett Nussmeier (PS#13) was the '23 Bowl MVP. In '24 Nussmeier had -38 yards rush but became just the second LSU QB to top 4,000 yards passing (64%, 29-12) and opted to return for 2025! He was backed by Michael Van Buren (PS#18) who started 8 games as a true frosh for Miss St. Nussmeier (#7 DC KC) was a preseason Heisman favorite. He was injured in August and never really 100% and played behind a weak Oline then was OFY and Van Buren started the last 5. The two combined for 2,937 pass (65.7%, 20-7). All of '25's QBs depart. Kifﬁn brings in Sam Leavitt who led Arizona St to the playoffs in 2024, throwing for 2,885 (62%, 24-6, 443 rush). He was banged up and only had 7 starts in '25. Husan Longstreet (PS#4) hit 13-15-103 at USC as a true. Landen Clark is a dual threat who threw for 2,321 (56% 18-8) and rushed for 614 at Elon last year. As long as Leavitt stays healthy they could have improved numbers. RUNNING BACKSBACKS Last year LSU lost their #1 RB (653, 5.5). In '24 true frosh Caden Durham (PS#11) took control and led with 753 (5.4) despite dislocated toes. A thin unit moved S Ja'Juan Johnson to RB (7-14). Last year they lost their #2 RB (482, 4.1) but added Harlem Berry (PS#1). Durham led again but with 505 (4.5). Johnson was at QB in spring but back at RB and was #3 with 155 (3.8) and is the only loss. Berry was #2 with 491 (4.7) and they add Dilin Jones (PS#15, Wisc), Stacy Gage (PS#20 UCF) and Raycine Guillory (5'10" 179, rFr, PS#67 Utah). I look for improved numbers from the RB unit. RECEIVERS - In '24 they lost their career receiving yards leader (#1, 1,569, 17.6, #1 DC) and #2 WR (1,177, 17.3, #1 DC). Four of their top 6 returned ('23 -1917, 13.4) but they only combined for 1,190 (13.1). Last year they lost a 1st tm SEC WR (12 st, #2, 884, 14.5), their #4 (480, 11.4) and TE (12 st, #3, 546, 9.9, #2 DC). The Tigers added Barion Brown who had 1,528 yards in 3 years with sub QB play at Kentucky to Aaron Anderson (PS#14) who led in '24 with 884 (14.5) and 6'7" TE Trey'Dez Green (2 td bowl). SOUTH CAROLINA GAMECOCKS WR NYCK HARBOR POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In 2023 they added 6'3" 245 lb LaNorris Sellers (PS#25). Their starter threw for 3,186 (69%, 19-8) and was a #5DC . Sellers completed all four pass attempts (86, 2-0, 51 rush). Sellers has great size, is tough to bring down and is a dual threat. In '24 he missed the 2H vs LSU and Akron. Sellers became Superman in the 2H of the year and was just the 3rd SC QB in history to throw for 350 yards and 5 TD's in a game in the win over Missouri. He scored the game winning TD vs Clemson (tkl breaking runs) and threw for 2,534 (66% 18-7) and was #2 rusher (674, 4.1) but did have 14 fumbles (lost 6). Sellers had a solid '25 but nowhere near inflated expectations as he threw for 2,437 (60.8%, 13-8) and had 270 rush. True frosh Cutter Woods hit 8-11-69. I look for Sellers to return to his 2024 form with hopefully a more stable Oline. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 SC for a 2nd straight year had to replace their top two RB's (#1, 707, 4.9). Last year they lost their #1 RB (881, 4.8). Oscar Adaway was a distant #2 RB (295, 3.8). They added Utah St transfer Rahsul Faison (1109, 5.8) who was not cleared until week 0. The top 3 RB's in '24 had 1,299 (4.7). Last year the top 3 had just 870 (4.2). Faison led but with just 470 (4.9), Adaway was #4 (140, 3.4) and both are gone. Matt Fuller (PS#75) is the top returnee (#3, 260, 3.6) along with Jawarn Howell (3 st, 80, 5.7). They add Christian Clark (PS#33 Texas), Sam Dixon (PS#48 Ohio St) and Jabree Coleman (PS#17 Penn St) and can only be more productive. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost a TE (#1, 519, 13.0) and two WR's (13 st, 545, 15.2). They brought in five frosh WR's in the spring and all were in the top 8. This unit was more experienced as two of the top 3 were back in Nyck Harbor (PS#2, #2 376, 14.5) and Mazeo Bennett (337, 11.2). Harbor emerged late with 100+ efforts in each of his last two games and led with 618 (20.6) and true frosh Jayden Sellers (LaNorris' bro) had 13-242 in the last 3 games after just 3 rec in earlier games. This year they lose Vandrevius Jacobs (#2, 548, 17.1) but are more experienced and improved by adding transfers from Oklahoma, Purdue and UCF (see PSL). HC Beamer feels they have more competition and depth than they've had. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '23 South Carolina had and Oline decimated by injuries and rushed for just 85 ypg (2.8). They also gave up 41 sacks. In '24, four starters returned (118 car sts). They benefitted from a 245 lb dual threat QB and better health with only one start missed all year. The first 7 games they struggled with 32 sacks but allowed just 7 during their 6 game win streak and doubled the rush totals to 184 (4.4). Last year they lost 3 starters so the career starts dropped to 78. They added starters from Wake, Troy and WKU but were hit hard by injuries again, fired their OL coach mid year and dropped to 111 (3.2) rush with 43 sacks. This year they lose 6 OL (37/103) and LT Josiah Thompson (12/24) is OFY but they add 7 OL that were full time starters and should get a Stock Market return to '24's numbers and have 126 FBS starts. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 I said this was one of if not the top Dline in the country. The line took over some games and had 41 sacks and allowed 112 (3.2) rush. Last year they had to replace their top 4 DT's, a DE (#2, #4, #4 DC's) and 3 backups. They did return Dylan Stewart (PS#1) but this unit was one of the main reasons I was down on SC as I did not think they would be any near as dominant. They dropped to allowing 137 (3.8) rush and had just 21 sacks. This year 3 starters depart again and 3 backups (comb 38 st, 152 tkl, 12 sk). With Stewart (4.5 sk, 7.5 tfl, #9 tklr) back they lose less than they did last year and should be improved and have added five P4 (4 VHT) transfers. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they had 7 LB that could play. The unit was part of a dominant front 7. Last year they lost their #2, #3, #4 tacklers (#2DC). They added Shawn Murphy (PS#7, Ala, FSU) and Justin Okoronkwo (PS#136, Ala) but neither started in '24. With the loss of the top three (all on NFL rosters) they were weaker but held foes to 31 ypg below their average (75 below '24). This year they lose NB Jalon Kilgore (#5 DC BUF) (11 st, #4 tklr) but return their top two in Fred "JayR" Johnson (12 st #3 tklr) and Okoronkwo (8 st, #2 tklr) plus Murphy (#6 tklr) and add Kentucky starting NB Quay'sheed Scott and true frosh Andrew Harris (PS#14 IFS) and are much more experienced. Beamer calls LB the strength of the team. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23 SC dropped to #50 (61%, 16-10) in the PDR. In '24 three starters returned (#3, #4, #7 tkl'rs) and I expected a move up the PDR aided by a dominating front 7 and they moved up to #9 (58%, 10-14). Last year they lost a 2nd tm AA SS (13 st, #1 tklr, 4 int, #2 DC) and CB (13 st, #7 tklr, 3 int) but they did add 4 transfers including NCSt and Ball St starters. I said they would likely drop in the PDR with a weaker front seven and they fell to #29 (60.3%, 13-12). This year they lose two starters (#1, #13 tklr) but return four with 14+ tackles. SC has created the most takeaways in the SEC over the last 5 years and remain strong. SPECIAL TEAMS - SC moved up to #18 in our STR then finished #1 in '22 then dropped to #35 in '23. While last year's unit underachieved, this group with 9 transfers is less experienced (88 car sts) and will take time to rebuild. The Oline is the big question on offense. JMU transfer LT Jo Simmons is 6'6" 322 and strong and has a shot at the NFL. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 Auburn allowed just 118 (3.1) and had 28 sacks. Last year they lost a 2nd Tm SEC DE (12 st, #3 tkl'r, 8 sk) and 3 DT's (18 sts). They still had 13 VHT's and were a top notch unit, allowing just 99 (2.9) ypg rush with 30 sacks. This year the top 10 DL all depart. The top returnee is Walker (13 tkl) and they add 5 transfers but only one was a starter. DE Jared Smith (PS#5) has a chance to be an early draft pick. They have 8 VHT's but are clearly weaker than '25's top notch unit and depth on the edge is a concern. LINEBACKERS - In '24 the Tigers returned their #1, #3 and #12 tacklers plus added PS#4 and #57 frosh and a Duke starter. Auburn allowed just 21 ppg and held foes 48 ypg below their average. This year they lose their #2 tackler but return Reddick and their #1 tackler Atkins so this remains a strength. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '24 they lost all four starters (2 #5DC, 1 #6DC) but still finished #38 (56%, 12-8) in my PDR. Last year they lost a starting S. VANDERBILT COMMODORES WR JUNIOR SHERRILL POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '23 the three QB's combined to throw for 2,684 (55.6%) with a 23-12 ratio. In '24 they added Diego Pavia who threw for 2,973 (60%, 26-9) and was #1 rusher (925, 5.3) with NMexSt and his OC and HC both came here. Pavia (wrestler in HS) became the leader and the face of the Vandy program, guiding the team to a 6-3 start before injuries slowed him down. He accounted for 5 TD's in the bowl win, threw for 2,293 (59%, 20-4) and was #1 rusher (801, 4.2). Last year Pavia led Vandy to their first ever 10 win season and was the runner up for the Heisman Trophy! He threw for 3,539 (71%, 29-8) and was #1 rusher with 862 (5.2). Vandy brings in their biggest recruit ever in Jared Curtis (PS#2!) and he was in for bowl practices but he has BIG shoes to fill! The depth is Blaze Berlowitz (PS#183, 9-17-131 LY), Whit Muschamp (PS#61) and rFr Jack Elliot (PS#65) and HC Lea says all 4 are in the mix. RUNNING BACKS - In '23 they lost their #1 rusher (1042, 4.5, 169 rec). They signed PS#67, #105 and #117 true frosh. RB JAMAL ROBERTS MISSOURI TIGERS OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they returned three starters and the numbers were nearly the same, with 164 (4.1) rush and 26 sacks allowed. Last year they lost 3 starters (#1, #7 DC). They returned C Connor Tollison and Cayden Green who were both NFL prospects. They added four P4 transfers and had 77 career starts. The RB's tackle breaking skills helped and them improve to 228 (5.3) rush with 28 sacks allowed. This year they lose C Tollison (13/48) and RT Keagan Trost (#3 DC LAR 13/39) but LT Green turned down the NFL so 3 starters are back plus they add 5 transfers including Miss St and ArizSt starters and with 118 career starts could be even stronger. MISSISSIPPI STATE BULLDOGS QB KAMARIO TAYLOR lost a C (12/48), RG (10/14) and LT (7/19). They added five transfers again and the career starts climbed to #39 with 91 starts. They needed to get bigger and stronger on the offensive line and most transfers accomplished that and won jobs. The unit was injury plagued but did have better rush numbers with 158 (3.7) but allowed lots of pressure all year and 39 sacks. This year they lose 4 starters and 3 backups (51/114). They add 8 transfers including a PS#22 & #23 so have 45 career starts. They should cut down on the sack numbers especially with a more mobile QB. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they were less experienced, not as imposing and then injury plagued. The results were even worse than expected with 217 (5.0) rush allowed, and had just 10 sacks. Last year they lost two starters. They added 10 transfers. They had nine 300+ lb DL so added size and could now roll 12-14 bodies in to stay fresher. The unit had 10 seniors & 7 juniors. They did well early but allowed 5.4 ypc in SEC play and had just 21 sacks. This year they lose 7 DL (33 st, 164 tkl, 4.5 sk). DE Will Whitson was OFY after just 1.5 games but his 2 sacks was #2 on the team and he was granted a 7th year. Under new/old DC Arnett they should generate more pressure and added 5 transfers but need to develop pass rushers. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they lost two LB's who were #1 and #2 tacklers for 3 straight years, plus their #5 tackler. The defense went from holding teams to 32 ypg below average to allowing 57 ypg above. Last year they lost their #2 tackler. They returned Isaac Smith (11 st, #1 tklr) and Nic Mitchell (12 st, #3 tklr). They also added Jalen Smith (PS#69 Tenn) and Derion Gullette (PS#16 Texas). With 4 of the top 6 back they improved to allowing 23 ypg above. This year they lose Mitchell (13 st, #2 tklr) but return their #4, #5, #6 #9,and #12 tacklers and are the most experienced since '23. They have 5 LB's that can play and Isaac Smith is a tackling machine and the heart and soul of the defense. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '24 with one starter back they dropped (#107 '23) to #127 in the PDR (70% 23-7). Last year they lost their #6 and #8 tacklers. They added five transfers with FS Jahron Manning (11 st, 85 tkl, ODU) taking one spot and the unit was the strength of the defense. They moved all the way up to #64 in my PDR (60%, 24-13). This year they lose S Manning (#1 tklr) plus their #3, #8 and #10 tacklers. Just one starter returns. They add 6 transfers including two who have started and signed PS#6 Brian Womack who should take a starting spot immediately. The secondary has much better depth but this unit may take a Stock Market drop in the PDR. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '23 true frosh Kyle Ferrie made 16-22 fg's (L/49). They finished #52 in our STR. KENTUCKY WILDCATS DL MI'QUISE HUMPHREY-GRACE POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS- In '24 true frosh Cutter Boley (PS#11) threw for 338 (49%, 2-4). The 3 QB's combined for 2,218 (53.5%, 15-16). Last year they added a well traveled PS#35 transfer who was injured week 2. Boley started the last 10 and after facing 3 rugged D's as a true frosh was much improved throwing for 2,060 (67%, 15-10) and had 114 rush. He set the frosh school frosh record with 4 TD passes vs Tennessee. Boley, a local kid, surprisingly transferred to Arizona St. Kenny Minchey (PS#18) battled CJ Carr for the ND QB job and just lost out but hit 20-26-196 and rushed for 84. He is mobile with a good arm. JacQai Long (PS#94) had one start at Marshall. RFr Brennen Ward (PS#47) and true frosh Matt Ponatoski (PS#16) round out the group. I think Minchey will have a solid year in Stein's offense but this is a very inexperienced unit. RUNNING BACKS - In 2023 they lost their #1 RB (904, 5.2, #6DC) and again in '24 (1129, 5.7, #4DC). RFr Jamarion Wilcox (PS#32) led with 590 (6.4) in '24. True frosh Jason Patterson was #3 RB with 111 (5.6). Last year they lost their #2 (586, 4.5). They added Dante Dowdell (PS#11, 614, 4.3 Neb), Seth McGowan (PS#16, 813, 5.3 NMSt '24) and rFR Tovani Mizell (PS#32). The unit had 4 VHT's but Wilcox was suspended and DNP. McGowan (#7 DC IND) led with 725 (4.4) and Dowdell was #2 (560, 5.0) but they depart. Patterson was #3 (228, 4.0) and is back. They bring in CJ Baxter (PS#4!) who rushed for 659 (4.8) for Texas in '23 and is a year removed from his ACL and Jovantae Barnes (PS#8!) who led Oklahoma with 577 (4.7) in '24 but was banged up last year. If both stay healthy this unit could be even stronger in 2026. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost their #1 (715, 15.2), and #2 (361, 12.4) WR's plus a TE (7 st, 9 rec). Ja'Mori Maclin had 121 vs Louisville (313, 24.1) and Hardley Gilmore had 153 (25.5) and they were joined by transfer Kendrick Law (Alabama). TE's became a bigger part of the offense. They could come close to last year's numbers. Jackson is intelligent and mobile while Hill is a pocket passer with a huge arm. BIG TEN CONFERENCE –– PHIL’S 2026 FORECAST –– 9. Minnesota - PJ Fleck’s teams usually surpass my expectations. Not only has he guided Minny to 7 straight bowls (not counting ‘20), he is 7-0 in those bowl games! Last year he had a Frosh QB and his top RB Taylor was banged up so they did not have their normal powerful rush attack. Minnesota was -142 ypg in B10 play but went 5-4. The Gophers were 7-0 at home but 0-5 on the road. This year they have 5 B10 road games. Lindsay and Taylor are both back as is LB Baranowski and DE Smith. I will call for yet another bowl and yet another bowl win. 9. Illinois - In ‘24, Illinois opened 6-1 with only a loss at Penn St, then lost at Oregon and home to Minnesota. At 6-3, they won the last 4, including a bowl win over South Carolina for their first 10-win season since 2001! Last year they had 19 starters back, avoided Penn St, Oregon and Michigan and looked like a playoff contender. They were blown out by Indy 63-10 but upset USC the next week. After losses to Ohio St and UW they were just 5-3 but went 4-1 after that with a bowl win over Tennessee. This year they have 12 starters back and lose their veteran QB, but add in Katin Houser from ECar. They do have 5 Big 10 road games, so they don’t figure to match last year’s 9-win total, but should make a bowl. 12. Wisconsin - In ‘24 they faced a much tougher schedule. The Badgers first 5 losses were to Bama, USC, Penn St, Iowa and Oregon - they dropped the last two for their first losing season since 2001! Last year they faced the toughest schedule in the country! In all three of Fickell’s years, he has lost his starting QB early in the year and last year was hit hard by injuries at many positions. They upset Wash and Illinois and the D held foes to 49 ypg below their average (#26) despite their 4-8 record. Finally, the schedule gods have set them up with the easiest schedule in the Big 10 and maybe finally the injury gods will allow them to stay healthy. They were -11 in TO’s and I feel the AD made a very solid decision to keep Fickell, a quality coach, and will be rewarded. Five of my 9 sets of power ratings call for a bowl as they have a top-notch D and add Colton Joseph to two QB’s that have experience 12. Northwestern - In ‘22, NW was -70 ypg and 1-8 in B10 play. In ‘23, they fired their HC over the summer and figured to be a dog in 10 or 11 games with an interim HC. HC Braun did a remarkable job getting them to 8-5 with a bowl win over Utah! In ‘24, they rated an SMI of -6.0, had +13 in TO’s, 5 Net Upsets and +4 Net Close Wins. They were also -43 ypg in Big Ten play despite their 5-4 record all making the Going Down Boxes. Last year I called for a return to the postseason and thanks to a top notch O-line and run game they opened 5-2 with an upset of Penn St and got to a won their bowl for a 7-6 year. They return the RB combo of Komolafe and Himon and add in QB Aidan Chiles (Mich St). The defense held foes to 30 ypg below avg (#42) and returns 5 starters. They do face the 3rd toughest B10 schedule, but open their brand-new home stadium and have a great shot at a 3rd bowl in 4 years. 12. UCLA - In ’23, UCLA was +79 ypg in Pac-12 play, but were just 4-5. In ‘24 UCLA drew Indy, Penn St, Oregon, and LSU on the schedule early and opened 1-5 but went 4-2 the last 6. UCLA did have 3 Net Close Wins and in ‘25 had 5 Big Ten road games. They added QB Nico Iamaleava but lost to New Mexico and let go of their HC. At 0-4 they caught Penn St in a letdown spot after an OT loss, then upset Mich St and beat Maryland for 3-4. The Bruins dropped the last 5 and was just 3-9. Indiana brought in a James Madison head coach and a bunch of transfers and immediately shot to the top, and UCLA now brings in a JMU HC and a bunch of transfers (JMU RB Knight 1,373, 2 start OL & more) and Iamaleava is back. With transfers, UCLA has 17 returning starters, so it is much more exp’d. They play the 3rd best schedule in the B10. Two of my 9 sets of power ratings call for 9 wins, but my main one has 6. 15. Maryland - The Terps were the 4th-best team in the East under Locksley, but in nonCovid years were 0-15 vs Michigan, Ohio St and Penn St. In ‘24 in the new 18-team league, they opened 3-1 and 4-3 but lost their last 5 by 23 ppg! Last year, true frosh Malik Washington (PS#10) looked great at QB. Maryland got off to its normal hot start at 4-0, including a road win at Wisconsin, but blew a 20-3 4Q lead vs Wash, 31-24 4Q lead vs Neb, gave up a FG with :02 left in a loss to UCLA then dropped the last 5 all by DD’s for a 4-8 year. MD has 16 returning strs and avoids Indiana, Oregon, Mich and Iowa (4th-best sched). They have a pair of dynamic pass rushers and 5 of my 9 sets of power ratings call for a bowl, with two calling for 8 wins. They were -81 ypg in B10 play. 16. Rutgers - In ‘23, Rutgers beat Miami in a bowl for its first winning season since 2014. In ‘24 Rutgers did not play any of the top five teams in the Big Ten (B10’s best schedule)! They were hit hard by injuries mid year dealt them a 4-game losing streak and they were 7-5 and blew a big lead in the bowl. Last year, they were a stronger team but faced one of the Big Ten’s toughest schedules. Injuries hit the defense and they allowed 230 ypg rush and 7.1 ypc in B10 play! The offense loses their QB but adds Dylan Lonergan (PS#10 orig Ala) and has their top notch skill players back. They host USC, Indiana and Mich so most of their winnable games are on the road yet 4 of my sets of power ratings call for a bowl. 17. Michigan State - The Spartans have now had 4 straight losing seasons and just let go their coach after two years. Pat Fitzgerald did wonders at Northwestern and should bring stability. Mich St has just 11 starters back. The Spartans best trait last year was late TD’s for back-door covers, which means they were not as good as their -61 ypg in Big Ten play. QB Milivojevic is back, but this is a transfer heavy team once again and this looks like a rebuilding year for the Spartans. 18. Purdue - In ‘22 Purdue won the West. Purdue went 4-8 then in ‘24 was 1-11 and -192 ypg in Big Ten play and -30 ppg. Last year, Barry Odom took over, which was an upgrade, but had just 2 returning starters from ‘24. He did some magic at UNLV and opened 2-0, but lost the last 10. They did cut it to losing Big Ten games by 20 ppg and were -126 ypg. This year, they are a portal-heavy team again, but do return QB Ryan Browne. They figure to be a much improved team in Odom’s 2nd year but have a lot of ground to make up. 1. Ohio State - Ohio St’s veteran squad won the CFB title in ‘24 and lost 15 NFL DC’s last year. They beat Texas in the opener and plowed through a soft schedule at 11-0 then finally beat Michigan and was #1 AP. Indiana beat them in the B10 title game and then Miami knocked them out in their first playoff game for a 12-2 season and they were +231 ypg in Big Ten play. The schedule gets harder this year with Texas, Iowa, Indiana and USC all on the road, but they return a now veteran QB Julian Sayin, the nations top WR Jeremiah Smith and a 1,000 yard RB in Bo Jackson. They lose 11 NFL DC’s including 3 of the first 10 picks but are a more veteran team. Now they just need to win the Big Ten for the first time in 6 years! 1. Indiana - The Hoosiers were just 3-24 in Big Ten play from ‘21-’23 and were -105 ypg in ‘23. New HC Curt Cignetti hit the portal hard and had 21 ret starters and an easier schedule. I had Indiana on my Most Improved list and they were the media’s pick for last in the Big Ten but made the playoffs in an 11-2 season! Last year they had 16 starters back including Cal QB Mendoza. They faced Penn St, Oregon and Iowa on the road but I said were even stronger and they went 12-0 (narrow escape at Penn St) were +186 ypg in Big Ten then beat Ohio St for their first Big Ten title since 1945, destroyed Bama and Oregon in the playoffs and beat Miami for a perfect 16-0 season and first ever national title in football! This year they rate a -8 in the SMI, were +21 in TO’s and almost all indicators are pointing down. Indy brought in some excellent transfers like RB Richard, WR Marsh, OL Brunner and have 17 returning strs plus host Ohio St and are a prime contender to repeat as both B10 and national champs. 1. Oregon - The Ducks were #1 in the Pac-12 in ‘22 with +136 ypg and #1 again in ‘23 at +212 ypg! Oregon was actually #1 in my AGG for 2023! In ‘24 they went 13-0 winning the Big Ten (+110 ypg #4 B10), then were one of the 4 bye teams that all lost after extended rest in the playoffs. Last year they lost QB Gabriel and the bulk of their OLine and DLines but brought in quality transfers. They had to face Penn St., Iowa and Washington on the road but won all three! They did lose a home game to Indiana so at 11-1 missed out on the B10 title game. They shutout powerful Texas Tech in round 1 but lost to Indiana 56-22. QB Dante Moore was a top NFL prospect and expected to leave but he returns as does my #2 DLine. They had a banged up WR corps in ‘25 and look even stronger. Could they be the 4th different B10 team to win a national title in 4 years? 4. USC - In ‘24 the Trojans opened 4-5, but were 5 plays away from 9-0 (all close losses)! They beat A&M in the bowl to finish 7-6. Last year they avoided Ohio St, and Indiana. They were my #5 Surprise team and had a legitimate shot at the playoffs when they traveled to Oregon at 8-2 where an upset would have put them in. They did have a 2 point road loss to Illinois on a FG at :00 and a loss to ND. In the bowl they led TCU 24-14 with 5:00 left but lost in OT. This year QB Maiava returns and has a veteran O-line and the top 2 RB’s back and Gary Patterson takes over a veteran D. My talent ratings have them tied for the 4th best team but they face the toughest B10 schedule. This team is a legit playoff contender and get both Oregon and Ohio St at home where they were 6-0 last year. 5. Michigan - Michigan won the National title with a veteran team (#7 Exp Chart) in 2023, then that dropped to #117 on my Exp Chart in ‘24 (lost 13 NFL DC’s). They also lost HC Jim Harbaugh and every indicator pointed down. Michigan appeared headed for a 6-6 season, but beat Ohio St then Alabama in the bowl, so the drop to 8-5 felt much better after those two wins. Last year they “only” lost 8 NFL DC’s and avoided Oregon and Indiana plus got Ohio St at home with the easiest schedule in the Big Ten. True Frosh QB Bryce Underwood (PS#1) had some growing pains in road losses to Okla and USC. A win at home vs OSU would have put them in the playoff but they lost 27-9 (163-419). HC Moore was fired. They dropped the bowl to Texas but made a great hire in Kyle Whittingham, whose Utah teams were built on the same principles that Michigan was. He brought some key transfers from the Utes to add to an already talented lineup. This time they face Oregon and OSU on the road and host Indiana, but could find themselves back in the playoffs. 5. Penn State - In 2024, Penn St avoided the trio of Oregon, Michigan and Iowa! Penn St lost at home to Ohio St., but went 11-1. They lost to Oregon in the B10 title game. Penn St finally made the playoff and beat both SMU and Boise St., with a narrow loss to ND. Of the final 4 teams, Penn St. returned the most. I went out on a limb picking them for the national title but, after an OT loss to Oregon at home, they were upset by UCLA then by NWstern at home and HC Franklin was let go. QB Allar was then OFY and they lost at Iowa, and home to OSU and Indiana like most teams would. At 3-6 they won the last 4 including beating Clemson in the bowl. Penn St made a great hire in Matt Campbell and he brings 24 Iowa St players with him to help compensate for 42 Nittany Lions that hit the portal. The best thing for Penn St this year is schedule as they avoid the top 3 teams in the league and have 5 home games. 7 . Washington - In ‘23 the Huskies were 13-0 before losing the National title game. UW benefitted from seven Net Close wins, rated a -6.5 in the SMI (were -5 ypg P12) and had only 6 ret starters and a new HC, who was hired late. They drew the Big Ten’s toughest schedule, and I picked a team from the National title game to finish 11th in the B10. They were in a 3-way tie for 9th at 4-5 (11th). Last year they were a more veteran team with 5 Big Ten home games and a manageable schedule. UW improved to 9-4 (5-4 B10), losing to Ohio St and Oregon at home and Michigan on the road but also to Wisconsin. They have 14 starters back including QB Demond Williams, but do lose RB Coleman and WR Boston. UW is 25-2 at home the last 4 years but does have 5 B10 road games and one home game is vs Indiana. 7. Iowa - In 2024 Iowa was favored in 11 games, but lost outright to Iowa St (blew DD lead), UCLA and Mich St and, at 8-4, blew a DD lead vs Missouri in the bowl game. Last year they had a tougher schedule (favored in 8 games) and, while they were 9-4, they were a handful of plays away from 12-0! Iowa St got a late 54-yd FG to win by 3. Indiana got a TD with 1:28 left to win by 5. Oregon got a FG with :03 left to win by 2. Iowa led USC 21-7 but lost 26-21. This year they have just 9 strs back and lose QB Gronowski. They figure to be a dog at Michigan and Washington and home to Ohio St, but if they can break through and win those close ones they could be a surprise contender. Ferentz always has a top-notch group. 9. Nebraska - In ‘24 Nebraska got to 5-1 but their streak of losses when needing a win to get to a bowl reached 8 before they beat Wisconsin. When the Huskers beat BC in the bowl, it was their first winning season since 2016! Matt Rhule finally benefited from bowl practices and his teams usually thrived in Year 3. The Huskers opened 7-3 with a 3 pt loss to Mich and 4 pt loss to USC. It was a sour finish with 3 losses by 24 ppg. This year they have 3 mobile QBs and bring in the MW Off POY in Anthony Colandrea, who should thrive in the Holgorsen offense. Nebraska does face the 2nd toughest schedule in the B10 facing all three playoff teams, have 5 Big 10 road games (Ill & Iowa). The Huskers gave up 5.0 ypc rush in B10 play but bring in TE DJ VONNAHME IOWA Rob Aurich as DC and should tighten that up. They are #7 on my Exp Chart. 92 QB DRAKE LINDSEY MINNESOTA

Iowa 0 2024 3RD TEAM ALL GAMES 2026 Homegrown Talent Chart This year I have added a new feature to the magazine putting the home grown talent on each team page. Every year I talk to 125+ head coaches, team chemistry is what coaches that hit the portal hard and have a lot of new players wonder most about. Those with more stable rosters seem to have better chemistry especially when things go wrong. Some coaches on transfer heavy teams told me they felt that players were wondering about their next destination late in the year when dreams were gone. Last year I devised a formula to test my “Homegrown” theory. I took all the players on the roster. If a rFr, Soph, Junior or Senior signed as a true frosh and had remained on the team they earned 2 points. This years Frosh got a half point. JUCO’s were -1 as teams have used JUCO’s for years. This years transfers were -2 coming from other schools. I gave -3 for any player added after spring. If a player had transferred to the school in a prior year it was only -.5 as they had time to learn the individual team culture. If a coach brought a player with him from his previous school they got 3 points cancelling out the negative transfer points. There is not enough space to list the whole chart. After adding up the points of course the service academies came up at ht top. The chart on top to the right shows the top 17 teams from last year. While Penn St and Clemson fared way below expectations it is interesting to note they both rallied for a winning record. Of the top 17 teams on the Homegrown Chart, 16 made a bowl game! Notre Dame and Texas just missed a playoff spot while Georgia, Texas A&M, Oregon and Alabama all made the playoffs. I also list the bottom of the chart to the right. Of the bottom 24 teams UNLV, WKU and New Mexico had better than expected seasons. Two other teams had winning record in Memphis and Texas St but both had seasons well below expectations. Of the other portal heavy teams 19 of the 24 had losing records. There probably will not be as many teams with negative points this year as there was not Spring window. On the right hand page of each team I list the Homegrown % and the points for this year. OHIO STATE BUCKEYES WR JEREMIAH SMITH POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Ohio St has basically had the best QB in the Big Ten in 9 of the last 15 years. In '24 they added two VHT QB's including Julian Sayin (PS#1, orig Ala). Will Howard threw for 4,010 (73%, 35-10) and led Ohio St to a national title (#6 DC Pit). They added PS#3 Tavien St Clair and Lincoln Kienholz (Iron Buckeye) was battling for the top job. Sayin became the first QB to win his first start vs the AP#1 team since 1984 (Jim Harbaugh vs Miami) when they beat Texas in the opener. He set a school record completing his first 16 passes vs Grambling. Sayin had a fine year and was a Heisman finalist throwing for 3,610 (77%, 32-6). Kienholz hit 11-14-139. Kienholz left for Louisville so they added Justyn Martin (PS#20) from Maryland for depth. Sayin is back and was held under wraps in some games last year as a rFr, but will probably top 4,000 yards this year and is a Heisman Frontrunner. INDIANA HOOSIERS WR CHARLIE BECKER POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - HC Curt Cignetti had a 1st team all-conf QB each of the previous 5 years and added Kurtis Rourke (33 car sts & 7,650 yards w/Ohio) in '24 and Alberto Mendoza (PS#87) LY. Rourke had a great year throwing for 3,042 (69.4%, 29-5) and was 2nd team Big Ten. Last year they added Cal transfer Mendoza, who threw for 3,004 (69%, 16-6, 105 rush). Mendoza was an upgrade and threw for 3,535 (72%, 41-6) with 276 (3.1) rush and took home the Heisman Trophy (#1 DC LV)! His brother Alberto hit 24-33-390-7-1 but both depart. They add in Josh Hoover, who started 31 games for TCU throwing for 9,629 yards (65.2%, 71-33). It will be tough to match the #1 overall NFL pick's (Indy's first s/FB Corby Davis -1938) stats, but Cignetti always produces all-conf caliber QB's. RUNNING BACKS - Last year the Hoosiers lost their #1 (848, 5.3), #2 (668, 4.7) and #4 (201, 6.9) RB's. They returned Kaelon Black (#3, 251, 5.5) and added in UAB's top RB Lee Beebe (885, 5.3), rFr Khobie Martin (6'0" 207, PS#111) and Roman Hemby, who had 2,347 yards (4.9) with 22 td's rushing with Maryland (2x HM B10, 1 car fum, 921 rec yd). In 3 starts vs Indy he had 371 yards. I said the unit could be even stronger and it was. Beebe was OFY after 3 games (209, 7.7). Hemby led with 1,120 (4.9) and Black (#3 DC SF) was #2 with 1,039 (5.6) and both depart. Martin had 506 (6.5) and is back, plus they add in Turbo Richard from Boston College (749, 5.2) and rFr Sean Cuone (PS#70). This will be a strong deep room just like '25. RECEIVERS - In '24, the Hoosiers added five transfers including Elijah Sarratt (1,191, 14.5 JMU '23), and I said they would easily top 23's numbers. Sarratt led with 957 (18.1) and Omar Cooper was #2 (594, 21.2). Last year, they lost their #3 (466, 12.3), #4 (448, 11.5), #5 (324, 12.0) WRs and TE (13 st, 189, 9.0). Saratt missed 2 games and was #2 with 830 (12.8). Cooper made the remarkable catch vs Penn St and led with 937 (13.6) and Charlie Becker emerged with 679 (20.0). This year they lose Cooper (#1 DC NYJ), Saratt (#4 DC BAL), #4 EJ WIlliams (443, 12.3) and TE Riley Nowakowski (#5 DC PIT) (16 st, 387, 12.1). They add in Nick Marsh (PS#18, Mich St, 662, 11.2), Shazz Preston (PS#8 Ala/Tulane, 723, 16.8) and Tyler Morris (PS#22 Mich, OFY LY), so they remain a dangerous unit. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they returned two starters, but added two starters from JMU (but they comb to start just 4 gms). They retained solid OL coach Bob Bostad. They lost their RG (4/35) in August and his replacement Drew Evans vs Mich St. The unit improved to 165 (4.4) rush with 21 sacks allowed. Last year, they lost two starters but added in C Pat Coogan (13/26) from Notre Dame and Kahlil Benson was back from Colorado after starting 12 games at RT here in '23. They basically went from two to 4+ returning starters and were one of three O-lines to be a Joe Moore Award finalist! This year they lose Coogan (#6 DC TEN) and Benson but return 1st TM B10 LT Carter Smith, C Drew Evans, RG Bray Lynch and add in RT Joe Brunner (PS#14 24 sts Wisc) and are - once again - a Joe Moore Award favorite. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 Cignetti brought in some key transfers and they allowed just 80 ypg rush (similar to JMU run D '23) and had 35 sacks. Last year they lost 3 starters (#4DC). They added in 1st TM CUSA DL Hosea Wheeler (74 tkl, 5 tfl, WKU), DE Kellan Wyatt (28 st, 80 tkl, 8 sk 3Y MD), Stephen Daley (12 st, 51 tkl, 4 sk Kent), plus DE Mikail Kamara (10.5 sk) turned down the NFL to return! DE Wyatt was OFY after 8 sts and Daley OFY vs Ohio St. Wheeler lost his job to Mario Landino after 5 starts. This year they lose 5 DL (37 sts, 12 sk, 143 tkl) including Kamara, with Tyrique Tucker (6 sk) and Landino (5 sk) both NFL caliber DT's returning. They add in 4 productive transfers, including a pair of DE's from Kansas St and figure to be down a notch after allowing just 77 ypg rush (3.0) with 46 sacks. LINEBACKERS - In '24 Indy went from allowing foes 56 ypg above their average to holding foes to 90 ypg below (#6). Last year they returned 1st TM Big Ten MLB Aiden Fisher (#1 tklr, 5.5 tfl) but did lose their #2 tackler. They added in NB Devan Boykin (10 st NCSt). Indy held foes to 105 ypg below their average (#9). This year they lose 1st TM AA Fisher (#7 DC HOU) and Boykin (10 st, #5 tklr) but return Rolijah Hardy (#1 tklr) and Isaiah Jones (#4 tklr). They remain solid, but I will call them down a notch with the loss of their leader. They are not as deep and need a 3rd LB to emerge. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In 2023, they were #92 (61%, 2510) in our PDR. In Cignetti's first year they jumped to #17 (62%, 10-14!). Last year they had two starters, plus Rover Amare Ferrell (13 st, #5 tklr) and they added in '23 starter Louis Moore (#2 tklr), who returned from Ole Miss. The Hoosiers remained strong at #12 (62%, 10-19). This year they lose S Moore (16 st, #3 tlkr) and CB DeAngelo Ponds (#2 DC NYJ, 15 st, #5 tklr, 11 pbu) but have 2 starters back and add in Ryland Gandy (13 st Pitt '24) and Preston Zachman (12 st '24), who was Wisconsin's Green Dot guy before being OFY in Wk. 3. CB Jamari Shape has AA and NFL potential and they add AJ Harris (PS#3 Penn St). They are my #9 rated secondary. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In '22, my computer called for a jump to 25.9 ppg and 334 ypg and Indiana had 328 ypg and 23.3 ppg. In '23, my computer called for 321 ypg and 23.8 ppg and they were right there again with 333 ypg and 22.2 ppg! In '24, my computer called for a large jump to 401 ypg, and they had 426 ygg and 41 ppg. Cignetti always has an all-conf caliber QB and brought in Fernando Mendoza from Cal, and had a more veteran O-line. Mh computer called for a jump to 442 ypg and they beat that with 473 ypg and 41.9 ppg. They lose a lot but Cignetti brought in great replacements. It will be tough to match last year's numbers but they remain one of the nations best! DEFENSE - In '24, my computer called for them to improve by over a TD per game but sold them short as the Hoosiers allowed just 80 ypg rush and had 36 sacks allowing 256 ypg and just 15.6 ppg. Last year, 5 starters were back, including DE Kamara, LB Fisher and CB Ponds so they had a star at all 3 levels. My computer called for just 278 ypg and they were a little better at 257 ypg and just 10.8 ppg. This year, they lose those 3 stars but remain one the of nations best. 2026 - From '21-'23, Indiana was just 9-27 (3-24 B10). In '24, new coach Cignetti - (13 win ssn 13Y HC)- said he expected to shock the world. All the indicators were pointing up, including a much more experienced team and a much softer schedule (pg 27). They made my coveted Most Improved list and I picked them way higher than everyone else. Needless to say, the Hoosiers were a big part of me winning the Magazine title once again. They were picked dead last in the Big Ten by the media! Indiana opened 10-0. Their punter fumbled a snap and Ohio St got a TD in the final minute of the half, then a PR TD and the Hoosiers lost in Columbus. They made the CFB. They were at ND and trailed 27-3, scoring two late TD's in a 27-17 loss. Many expected a step back last year but they were actually a stronger team on both sides of the ball. They got their 2nd ever win at home over a Top 10 team when they thrashed Illinois 63-10. They were 1-72 vs top 5 teams in Indiana history, but beat #2 Oregon on the road 30-20! After a win over Mich St, they were #2 AP (highest schl history). In a battle of unbeatens, they knocked off #1 Ohio St for their first Big Ten title since 1945. Indiana locked up the #1 seed in the playoffs, went to the Rose Bowl for the first time since 1967 and blew out Bama 38-3, destroyed Oregon 56-22 and beat Miami 27-21 for their first-ever college football national title!! In two years, they are the only playoff team to win after the bye. They lose the Heisman Trophy winner and 7 draft picks, but my 2-time National Coach of the Year Cignetti will have them at the top again. USC TROJANS RB WAYMOND JORDAN POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Lincoln Riley has produced three Heisman winners (plus a finalist). In 2024 they added UNLV QB Jayden Maiava (3085, 64%, 17-10). When USC was 4-5 they benched the starter and turned to Maiava. Jayden threw a Pick-6 on his first series, but would guide USC to 3 wins in the last 4, throwing for 906 (61%, 7-2, 49 rush). Last year Maiava was solid throwing for 3,711 (66%, 24-10) and had 157 (2.9) rush. His PS#5 backup hit 13-15-1-3-1-0 but transferred to LSU. Sam Huard (PS#2) hit a TD pass on a fake punt last year and threw for 2,247 (61%, 18-10) at Cal Poly in '23. They add PS#7 Jonas Williams, who was IFS and impressive and have JC transfer Will Doherty. Maiava has a big arm and is a sneaky good athlete. With a big year, he could become a high NFL DC, so this is my #7 QB unit. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they lost their #1 (1133, 5.7), and #2 (478, 7.6) RB's. They added in Eli Sanders (1063, 7.2 NMex) and Waymond Jordan (PS#25 JC, 1614, 7.4). HC Riley said it is the best RB room he has had here. Unfortunately both Jordan (576, 6.5) and Sanders (258, 5.9) were OFY after 6 games. Fortunately walk-on King Miller emerged and had four 100+ games and led with 972 (6.2). This year they lose Sanders but return Jordan, Miller and Riley Wormley (PS#33, 44 yd) plus add in true Frosh Deshonne Redeaux (PS#7, fastest RB) and Shahn Alston (PS#9, physical). They should remain healthier and this is my #9 RB corps. RECEIVERS - In '24, Makai Lemon (PS#7) led with 764 (14.7), and Ja'Kobi Lane was Bowl MVP and had 525 (12.2). Last year they lost their #3 (503, 10.7), #4 and #5 (396, 17.2) WR's. Lemon (#1 DC PHI) won the Biletnikoff Award with 1,156 yards (14.4) and Lane (#3 DC BAL) was #2 with 743 (15.2). TE Lake McRee was #3 (450, 15.0) and all 3 depart. Tanook Hines emerged late with 561 (16.5) with 100+ games vs Oregon and TCU. Riley added NCSt's top WR Terrell Anderson (PS#33, 629, 16.1) and added in 4 VHT Frosh (PS#3, 6, 12, 37). They will have a solid group but are down some losing their top 3. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '23, they had 95 career starts. Alani Noa (PS#65) became the first true frosh OL here to start an opener since 2015. They rushed for 135 (4.8) and allowed 35 sacks (7.2%). In '24, they lost 3 starters and had 145 (5.2) rush, allowing just 15 sacks. Last year they had to replace 3 starters and had 54 career starts. They were injury plagued with 7 different starting lineups and improved to 169 (5.1) rush with just 15 sacks despite losing the top 2 RB's to injury! This year they lose two OL (11/36) but have five OL back who each started 7+ games, plus two backups who drew starts and add in 7 OL from USC's #1 rated Frosh Class (PS#6, 16, 33, 34).With better health, they should be a Joe Moore Award contender. DEFENSIVE LINE - In 2024, USC allowed 141 ypg rush with just 21 sacks. Last year they added two transfers but added in two large (330 & 350 lb) SEC DT's. USC was more experienced. Riley felt it would be one of the most impactful D-Lines and they had 14 sacks the first 3 games but were banged up and allowed 145 (4.4) and had just 14 more sacks the rest of the year. This year they lose three DL (31 st, 88 tkl, 7 sk) but get back Jamall Jarrett (PS#28, 360 lb Georgia) who missed last year, their top two sack guys in DE Kameryn Crawford (5.5 sk) and DE Braylan Shelby (4.5 sk) and add in Alex VanSumeren (12 st, Mich St, PS#34) and Zuriah Fisher (11 st, Penn St). Also Jahkeem Stewart (PS#3) played 11 games with a stress fracture in his foot as a true and could be a force. DT Jidi Abasiri has AA potential. They also add in PS#5, 14, 23 & 27 true Frosh and will be stronger. Riley says it is his best DL here. LINEBACKERS - In '23, they allowed 34.4 ppg but in '24 cut it to 24.1 ppg. Eric Gentry was a stud with 33 tkls, but was injured and redshirted. Last year they lost their #1, #2, #5 and #9 tacklers. Gentry was back and the unit had 4 VHT's, but I called them down a few notches. They went from holding foes 62 ypg below avg to 31 below. This year they lose Gentry (#2 tklr) and NB Kamari Ramsey (#5 DC HOU) (9 st, 27 tkl). They return Desman Stephens (#1 tklr) and Jadyn Walker (#10 tklr) so are more experienced, plus they add transfers Deven Bryant (62 tkl, 10 st Wash), Giancarlo Rufo (103 tkl, Georgetown), a PS#6 and 18 true frosh and go 3 deep with experience. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23, the unit had 10 VHT's but dropped to #111 in our PDR (246 ypg, 64%, 31-7). In '24 they moved up to #68 (68%, 15-12). Last year, the Trojans lost 3 starters. They added in Bishop Fitzgerald (str NCSt). They finished #78 (65%, 21-11) in the PDR. This year they lose 1st TM AA Fitzgerald (10 st, #4 tklr, 5 int) and CB DeCarlos Nicholson (12 st, #5 tklr) but add in CB Jontez Williams, who was 2nd TM B12 at Iowa St in '24, and have 8 VHT's. They should have their highest finish in years but have less exp'd depth than the LB's. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '23 USC made the expected climb to #15 in the STR! In '24 Eddie Czaplicki won the ST RANK L6Y: Ray Guy (45.4 net)! The return game was avg and 2025.... #86 they dropped to #43. Last year they lost their P & 2024.... #43 K, and fell even further to #86. RFr K Ryon Sayeri 2023.....#15 hit 21-25 FG and had 68 TB on 89 KO after Caden 2022.....#76 #60 Chittenden (26-33 fg UNLV '24) was injured. Both 2021.... 2020.... #46 are back. They lose their P (35.6 net) and top KR and PR but add in Memphis's P Lachlan Carrigan (41.6 net!) and Nebraska's STC. They will make a solid climb in the STR. COACHES - Lincoln Riley guided Oklahoma to three playoff berths in five years and is 82-23 as a HC. He almost made the playoff in his first year here and enters his fifth season. The 1st year OC is Luke Huard (uncle of QB Sam), who had been an assistant here since '22. Riley calls the plays. New DC is none other than Gary Patterson, who was the HC at TCU ('00-'21) and DC prior to that. New STC Mike Ekeler was Nebraska STC in '25 and was at Kansas, NTexas and Tenn in that role prior. In '24 they lost QB Williams, their top 2 RB, top 2 WR and 3 starting OL. My computer called for 412 ypg and 33.2 ppg, and they topped the yards with 437 ypg but only 30.2 ppg. This year 9 starters are back and their RB's were banged up last year and should stay healthier. Replacing their #1 and #3 DC WR's is my biggest question, but they will be potent. DEFENSE - In '23 they allowed 34.4 ppg - the most this century - and fired their DC with two games to go. Riley made a great hire, bringing over UCLA's DC D'Anton Lynn. He brought over two of his DB's, plus Oregon St's #1 tackler. My computer called for them to improve to 23 ppg and and they allowed 24 ppg and 377 ypg! This year Riley feels they have a shot as he brought in the top recruiting class to blend with a ton of returning talent. MICHIGAN WOLVERINES WR ANDREW MARSH POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24, three QB's combined to throw for just 1,678 (62%, 11-13). Last year, they brought in true Frosh PS#1 Bryce Underwood and I said they should have a significant upgrade, going from a weakness to a potential strength. Underwood was kept under wraps in some games but had a solid year, throwing for 2,428 (60.3% 11-9) and was #3 rusher (392, 4.5). This year they add in Brayden FowlerNicolosi, who threw for 3,460 (62%, 22-16 for Colo St in '23). His numbers dropped in '24 and he was benched after 3 starts last year. Chase Herbstreit (PS#99) and true frosh Brady Smigiel (PS#11) add depth. Tommy Carr (PS#28) wowed everyone in the spring game and is a solid backup. Underwood should have a much better year and be one of the Big Ten's top QB's. RUNNING BACKS - In '24, they lost their #1 rusher 1,245 (4.8, #3 DC). Last year they had to replace their #2 (589, 4.6) and #1 (948, 5.1) RB's. Both left prior to the bowl and true frosh Jordan Marshall (PS#8), who created a lot of buzz in August and was the top KR, had 100 vs Bama. Last year they added in Justice Haynes (PS#3, 443, 5.7 Ala). I said they could match '24's production and they did. Haynes became the first-ever Wolverine to top 100 rush in each of the first 5 games of the season! He was injured vs USC and then was OFY and was #2 (857, 7.1). Marshall had 4 straight 100 yard games (wk 7-10) but missed Maryland and former walk-on Bryson Kuzdzal had 20-100 vs the Terps. Adding depth are Sophs Tomas O'Meara (2 gm LY) & Micah Ka'Apana (OFY). OL ANTHONY DONKOH OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the career starts dropped to 45 losing 3 NFL draft picks but the numbers improved to 202 (5.3) rush with just 20 sacks allowed! Last year they had 4 starters back (83 car sts) with a total of 14 VHT's in the group. The numbers were similar with 174 (4.8) rush and 19 sacks. This year they lose 6 OL (4 starters 53/122) including Vega Ioane (#1DC BAL) and Drew Shelton (#4DC DAL). They add in 7 transfers (4 from Iowa St) and two starters but the career starts drop to 51 and they ﬁgure to be down a notch. Campbell does say C Brock Riker could be the best C in the FBS and RT Anthony Donkoh is an AA OT, so this unit is an absolute strength. DEFENSIVE LINE- In '24 Penn St allowed 102 (3.1) ypg rush with 44 sacks. Last year they lost 3 of the rotating 4 DT and their top pass rusher (#1DC). DE Dani Dennis-Sutton and DT Zane Durant were back and the unit had 12 VHT's. In the new defense they allowed 143 (4.1) rush and had 32 sacks. This year they lose all 4 starters including DE Dennis-Sutton (#4 DC GB, 13 st, 8.5 sk) and DT Durant (#5 DC BUF, 12 st, 25 tkl, 4 sk). They add in 8 transfers including UCLA and Iowa St starters and could be just as solid despite some big losses. LINEBACKERS - "Linebacker U" has had 14 LB's drafted the last 18 years. In '24 Penn St held foes to 99 ypg below their average (#3). Last year, they lost their #2 tackler (#6 DC). Rojas was OFY after 4 starts but they held foes to 32 ypg below their average. This year they lose DeLuca (#3 tklr) and Campbell (#1 tklr) but add in three Iowa St starters plus get Rojas back. Campbell calls it the best LB room he has ever had. They are my #12 rated LB corps. DEFENSIVE BACKS - Penn St was #9 in my PDR (59.5%, 11-14) in '21, #2 in '22 (52.1%,12-14), #14 in '23 and #14 in '24. Last year they lost two starters but added King Mack (PS#18) from Alabama. Last year was an underachieving year for the team and Penn St ﬁnished just #60 in my PDR (63.8%, 16-6). This year they lose 3 starters (#2, #4, #7 tklrs) but add in 3 Iowa St starters and should get back towards the top in the PDR. Campbell's Iowa St secondaries were #10, #5 and #34 the last 3 years. Jeremiah Cooper would be in the NFL right now if he did not get injured last year and FS Marcus Neal is one of the best defensive players he has coached. WASHINGTON HUSKIES OL JOHN MILLS OFFENSIVE LINE - In '23 they had just two returning starters (36 car sts) but won the Joe Moore Award. In '24 they lost all five starters (#1, #2 DC) and some of the expected starters did not join the team until this summer. They shuffled the lineup early and, naturally, the sacks climbed to 39 with 129 (4.0) rush. Last year they lost 3 starters. They added in two transfers (NFL LT Carver Willis) and the career starts rose to 54. UW improved to 165 (4.6) with 34 sacks. This year they only lose Willis (#4 DC SF) and 3 OL (comb 11 st). Four starters return, plus they add in PS#4 true frosh and rFr Champ Taulealea (PS#35). They are once again a Joe Moore Award contender. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '23 they lost all four starters (#3DC). UW allowed 162 (4.6) rush and had just 20 sacks. Last year they lost 3 starters. Fisch said adding size was important and they brought in 3 transfers. They were more experienced, bigger and got their injured players back. The rush D did indeed improve to just 100 (3.3) but they had just 24 sacks. This year they lose 8 DL (29 st, 136 tkl, 11 sk) but return 2 starters and add in 4 DL who were starters and should improve on that sack total. Jacob Lane led the DL in tfl with 8.5 and Isaiah Ward led the DL with 6.5 tfl in '24, but was banged up last year. LINEBACKERS - Last year they lost their top 2 (#1, #2 tklr) LB plus the NB (9 st, #8 tklr) and an LB, who Fisch called the future of the defense (35 tkl).They added in 5 transfers, (Wash St, Ariz, UCF st'rs). The new guys did well and true Frosh Zaydrius Rainey Sale, who was off an ACL, played in 8 games and had 21 tkls. They went from holding foes to 54 ypg below their average to 48 below. Jaco Manu was limited to 4 games in order to RS. This year they lose Deven Bryant (10 st, #3 tklr) but return Manu and #2 tackler "X-Ray" Alexander and, including the Husky position, have 5 guys that started last year so they will have to manage snaps to keep this deep room happy. DEFENSIVE BACKS - UW had 7 straight top 25 finishes in my PDR no matter who they lost. In '22, UW plummeted to #107 (62.9%, 26-7). In '23 I called for a Stock Market climb in the PDR and they finished at #12 (59.2%, 23-16). In '24 as usual they finished high at #8 in the PDR (55%, 13-8). Last year they lost 2.5 starters but added in 2nd TM B10 CB Tacario Davis (#3 DC CIN) plus FIU and NAriz starters. They surprisingly slipped to #24 (61&, 16-9). This year they lose 5 DB (38 st, #4, #5 tklrs). They return their #1 tackler S Alex McLaughlin and have 3 other DB's with starting experience plus add in CB Emmanuel Karnley (10 st, Virg). They are less exp'd but should finish in the same area of the PDR. SPECIAL TEAMS - Fisch's ST units were #92, #82 and #78 in his 3 years at Arizona. This unit was ST RANK L6Y: a problem all year in '24 and finished just #129 2025.... #56 in the STR. Grady Gross hit 18-26 fg with only 21 2024... #127 TB on kickoffs. Last year they lost their P (only 2023.... #45 34.9 net). I said they should have a Stock Market 2022.... #49 #80 type bounce in the STR and they did up to #56. 2021.... 2020...#125 Gross hit 10-13 FG, Luke Dunne avg 40.1 (34.5 net). This year they lose Gross but add in Tyler Robles (21-23 Tex St) and they should move up some more. COACHES - 3rd-year HC Jedd Fisch was interim HC in UCLA's final two games of '17. Fisch spent '20 as the QB coach of the Patriots. He took over Arizona in 2021 and went 1-11, 5-7 and 10-3. Fisch will operate this season without an official OC, choosing to call his own plays. The 2nd year DC is Ryan Walters, who was the Illinois DC in '21-'22 and the Purdue HC in '23-'24. The 2nd year STC is Chris Petrilli, who was STC for Walters at Purdue ('23-'24). POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24, true frosh Demond Williams (PS#16) played in every game and Week 8, Fisch called him the face of the program. He took over for good and started the final two games. Williams threw for 944 (78%!, 8-1) and was #2 rusher (282, 3.4). His two starts were vs. teams that were 22-5. Last year I said he should have a fine season with a stronger supporting cast than the QB's had in '24. Williams was electric at times and threw for 3,065 (69.6%, 25-8) and was #2 rusher with 611 (4.3). Williams, the face of the program, hit the portal in January but withdrew 2 days later due to his NIL deal. Eilijah Brown (PS#7) had 3 starts for Stanford (829, 58%, 4-2) and rFr Dash Beierly (PS#37) and Treston McMillan (PS#75) are the depth. Williams straightened things out with his teammates and should be one of the B10's best, but he does lose his star RB and WR. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 they lost their #1 rusher (Miss St transfer) again (1,195, 5.1). They brought in Jonah Coleman, who led Arizona with 871 (6.8). Coleman was the workhorse and had 1,053 (5.5). True frosh Adam Mohammad (PS#147) was #2 (193, 4.6). Arizona transfer Jordan Washington (PS#42) has breakaway speed. Last year Coleman (#4 DC DEN) was injured and in the last 4 games had just 16-28 rush then 85 in the bowl to finish with 758 (4.9). PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In 2023, my computer called for 36.7 ppg and 486 ypg and they had 36 ppg and 462 ypg! No '24 players had more than 200 snaps in 23's offense as all 11 starters departed. I said they would drop by over a TD per game in ppg and my computer called for 380 ypg and they had 390 ypg and fell to 23.4 ppg. Last year with QB Williams, RB Coleman, WR Boston and a much stronger OLine, my computer called for 419.2 ypg and they had 410 ypg! This year they lose their top RB and WR, but Williams is back with a strong O-line. This time my computer adds it all up and says 31.1 ppg and 419.7 ypg. DEFENSE - From '21-'24 my computer hit the Huskies defense numbers on the head including 2024 when a 6-7 Husky team allowed just 24 ppg! Last year they went from 3 to 7 returning starters and added in Ryan Walters, and my computer called for 23.0 ppg and they did even better at 18.7 ppg. This year they lose #3, #4, #6 and #7 DC's and 12 of the top 18 tacklers. They could be upgraded at DL, LB and maybe even in the secondary. They should finish about the same as last year on the D. 2026 - In '23, they opened a dominating 4-0, winning by 33 ppg. Then it became a weekly escape for 8 straight weeks, with no win by more than 10 with 7 close wins. As a 9-pt dog in the Pac 12 title game, they won 34-31 to go 13-0 and make the playoff. Then, as a dog, beat Texas before losing to Michigan in the title game. Kalen DeBoer left for Alabama in January and 13 Huskies were in the NFL Combine, plus many more hit the portal. Jedd Fisch took over late and has 2 starters back from that 2023 team, plus they rated an SMI of -6.5, benefitted from 7 Net close wins, were -5 ypg in P12 play despite being unbeaten, had 4 Net Upsets and were -74 All Conf Pts returning. When we asked the Washington SID office for pictures for the pages, they jokingly said, "We don't have any players left from last year's team," and that was not far from the truth. To top it off, they drew the toughest schedule in the Big Ten! UW barely made a bowl game at 6-6 - they were undefeated at home but were +12 ypg in Big 10 play. They had a 1-point loss to Louisville in the bowl to go from National Title game to a losing season. Last year they were a much more experienced team and made my Most Improved List! Washington was in playoff contention at 6-2 but lost at Wisconsin. After a bowl win vs Boise they were 9-4 and scored 45.1 in their wins and just 9.3 in the losses. QB Demond Williams is back and they have a veteran OLine and top notch D. They do replace their star RB and WR. IOWA HAWKEYES RB KAMARI MOULTON POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In 2022, three QB's combined to throw for 2,037 (55%, 7-9). In '23, their backup started the last 9 due to injury (1,152, 49%, 5-8). In '24 their main starter (8 sts) threw for 1,017 (60.5%, 6-5). Last year they added Hank Brown (PS#62), who hit 27-43-403-6-3 with Auburn, and Mark Gronowski, who led South Dakota St to B2B FCS national titles (49-6 as starter) as a 3-year starter (93-20 career ratio). Gronowski was banged up early and did not have the expected stats, throwing for 1,741 (63%, 10-7) but was also the #2 rusher (545, 4.2) and set the NCAA record for wins by a QB with 56! His 16 rush TDs tied a Big Ten QB record (Denard Robinson). Brown is 6'4" with a strong arm and hit 11-21-107-1-1. Jeremy Hecklinski (PS#51) hit 2-2-8 as a rFr and can make every throw and reads defenses well. They have a pair of rFr in Jimmy Sullivan (PS#66) and Ryan Fitzgerald (PS#106). They are not as experienced as '25 but could top the passing stats. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they lost Kaleb Johnson (#3DC) who had 1,000 yards after contact and led with 1,537 (6.4). Kamari Moulton had 473 (5.6) and was the heir apparent. Jaizun Patterson had 309 (4.9). Moulton was injured in the opener and missed 3 games but led with 878 (5.2). He topped 75 yards each of the last 9 games but never got to 100. FB Xaiver Williams (230 lbs) had 122 in the opener and was #4 (285, 5.8) and he is faster than you think. True Frosh Nathan McNeil had 169 (4.6). This year they lose Patterson (#3, 299 (5.2) but add in LJ Phillips, who led the FCS with 1,921 (6.5) with South Dakota. They are much more experienced and improved. RECEIVERS - In '23, the top two were both OFY after weeks 3 & 7. The top 5 in 2023 combined for just 1,111 yards. In '24 they had to replace their #1 WR (7 st, 299, 14.2, #4DC), #2 WR (255, 8.2), and a TE (8 st, 8 rec). Northwestern transfer Jacob Gill led with just 411 (11.7). True frosh Reece Vander Zee had 5-66 in the opener but, after missing the final 5 games, was only #4 (176, 12.6). Last year they lost a TE (#2, 231, 8.3, #7 DC), but the top 5 had just 1,024 yards. Vander Zee missed 5 games (#4, 219, 14.6). RFr DJ Vonnahme led with 434 (15.0) and his 146 yards (bowl vs Vandy) were most for a Hawkeye since 2011 (Marvin McNutt 151 vs Purdue). This year they lose Gill (260, 11.8) and #3 WR (261, 16.3). They add in two productive FCS transfers who had 875 (12.9) and 796 (12.2) and can only top last year's top 5 production of 1,343 yards. Iowa has 5 B10 Away games and a brutal 3-game stretch (at Mich, OSU, at Wash), but they will have their usual 8+ win season and have to be considered a Big 10 contender as they were very close last year once again.
