NEBRASKA CORNHUSKERS OL JUSTIN EVANS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In 2024 true frosh QB Dylan Raiola looked like a PS#2 QB in the spring and started the season great with a super 9-2 ratio the first 5 games, but then looked like a freshman with a 4-9 ratio the last 8 games. He did top the school frosh record for passing yards (Adrian Martinez). Raiola had a solid 2005 throwing for 2000 (72%, 18-5) but was OFY vs USC. Rhule covets a dual threat QB and true frosh TJ Lateef (PS#20) fit that role better (Raiola -87 rush). He led the win over UCLA but lost his last 3 starts. Lateef threw for 904 (60.2%, 5-1) and rushed for 120. Raiola transferred so they bring in Anthony Colandrea, who had 11 starts for Virginia then was 1st TM MW at UNLV in '25 throwing for 3,459 (65.9%, 23-9) with 649 rush. Daniel Kaelin (PS#34) also returns after a year at Virginia and was contending for the starting job there. Holgorsen is emphasizing the QB's extending plays this year with their legs and has 3 mobile QB's, so the depth is great and Colandrea should have a big year. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 they had to replace their top RB (413, 4.0). Emmett Johnson was the top RB at the end (528 yd L4 gm) after Holgorsen became OC and had 598 (5.1) rush and 286 (7.3) receiving. Kwinten Ives (PS#113) had a TD in the bowl. Johnson continued to thrive in the Holgorson system in '25 and was 2nd team AA with 1,451 (5.8) rush and #4 receiver (370, 8.0). RFr Mekhi Nelson (PS#70) had 88 yards in the bowl (147, 5.4) and power back Ives (limited hamstring early) had 133 (6.7). Mozee, a converted WR with good hands, had 115 (4.4). The three had 228 all-purp yards in the bowl with Johnson sitting out. True Frosh Jamal Rule (PS#46) has home run ability. Rhule likes his top 4 RBs, but they won't match Johnson's (#5 DC KC) production. RECEIVERS - Last year for a 7th straight year they lost their #1 WR (587, 13.3) plus #2 (455, 13.4) and their TE (9 st, 373, 10.4, #7 DC). True frosh slot WR Jacory Barney led the team in receptions with 55 (447, 8.1) and was the top returnee. They added Dane Key (PS#34), who was Kentucky's #1 receiver (715, 15.2) and Cal transfer Nyziah Hunter (578, 14.5), plus QB Haarberg moved to TE. Hunter led with 617 (14.3) Barney was #2 (484, 10.8) and TE Luke Lindemeyer was #5 (312, 10.8). This year they lose Key (#3, 452, 12.6) but add in Kwazi Gilmer (12 st, 535, 10.7 UCLA). They are more experienced and finally have their top guy back, making this unit the best in a long time. OFFENSIVE LINE - Injuries have plagued this unit the last 4 years. Last year they had to replace two starters. They added Rocco Spindler (12/22, ND) and Elijah Pritchett (12/12, Ala) and had 7 OL with 9+ career starts (131 car sts). RT Teddy Prochazka was OFY after 5 starts and Gunnar Gottola was OFY after 4 starts. They allowed 7 sacks to Michigan, 5 to Mich St and 9 to Minnesota, but just 12 in the other 10 games. This year they lose 4 OL (30/117). They add in Iowa St, LSU, South Carolina starters so they have added 123 career starts. I have said it the last couple of years and was wrong, but they can only stay healthier and so should be stronger. Having more mobile QB's will help the rush and sack stats. Rhule says they are significantly more talented than last year. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '23 they allowed just 93 (3.0) ypg rush with 32 sacks, their most since 2013. In '24 five of the top six returned led by their 325 lb NT Nash "Polar Bear" Hutmacher and DE Ty Robinson. The Huskers allowed 101 (3.4) rush with 30 sacks. Last year they lost their top 4 DL and I said it went from a strength to a question mark. Nebraska slipped to allowing 175 (4.8) rush with just 22 sacks. This year they lose DT Elijah Jeudy (11 st, 18 tkl), NT Keona Davis (12 st, 32 tkl) and a JLB Dasan McCullough (7 st, 2 sk). They move to a 4-man front and DE Williams Nwaneri (PS#3) should emerge. Plus they add UCLA, Pitt and BC transfers (see PSL) and are a little bigger and should be tougher vs the run. LINEBACKERS - In '24, they lost their #5 and #6 tacklers but had 6 of the top 8 back and held foes to 53 ypg below their average (#29). Last year they had to replace their #1, #3 and #4 tacklers. Their NB (#5 tklr) was OFY after two starts. Javin Wright (#9 tklr) was back, as was Vincent Shavers (Blackshirt, SD jersey as true) plus they added SBC Def POY Marques Watson-Trent along with PS#14 and #15 true frosh. They went from two to one returning starter, but held foes to 39 ypg below their average. This year, they lose Wright (#1 tklr) and Watson-Trent (#7 tklr) but have those VHT rFr. Plus they add in Owen Chambliss, who had 110 tackles under DC Aurich at SDSt, and Oregon St transfer Dexter Foster (11 st, 95 tkl, 2Y). This unit is bigger and more experienced and are the top unit of the defense. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23 they moved up to #22 in my PDR (60%, 14-9). In '24, they lost 3 DB who combined for 24 starts (#3, #9, #10 tklr), then a CB was OFY after 5 starts and plummeted to #96 (64%, 23-11). Last year they went from one to four returning starters (most veteran unit on tm) and took a Stock Market leap back up to #30 in the PDR (58%, 7-6). This year they lose two S's (17 st, #2, #13 tklrs) but Rex Guthrie started the last 8 there and was #3 tackler. Both CB's return in Andrew Marshall and Donovan Jones, plus they add a SDSt starting S and they are my #15 rated unit. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 they had 4 punts and 2 FG's blocked, had snapping problems and were just #125 in my STR. Last year they lost their P (44.7, ST RANK L6Y: 35.7 net due to blocks). They added Aussie P 2025 ....#18 ..#125 Archie Wilson. Wilson avg just 39.4 (38.3 net) 2024 2023 ... #96 and Kyle Cunanan hit 16-19 FG (L52). Kenneth 2022 ... #59 Williams had a 95 yard KR TD and they were +3 2021 . #129 in the TD/Blk category and moved all the way up 2020 .. #112 to #18, their highest finish since 2014. They lose KR Williams (32.9) and their STC and could drop some after the large rise last year. COACHES - Fourth-year HC Matt Rhule took over as HC of Temple in 2013 and went 2-10, 6-6 then 10-4 and 10-3. At Baylor he went 1-11, 7-6 then was 10-1 and #8 in the AP and finished #13. He was also HC of the Carolina Panthers from '20-'22. OC Dana Holgorsen took over the last 4 games '24. He was HC at Houston & West Virginia (92-69). The new DC is Rob Aurich who, in his first year at DC, had SDSt go from allowing 30 ppg to just 15 ppg LY and was a Broyles nominee. New co-STC's are Brett Maher and Nick Humphrey. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In '23, they had their sixth OC in six years, and dropped to 18 ppg and 313 ypg. My computer had them at 28.1 ppg and they had 28.7!! This year they add UNLV QB Colandrea so they now have the mobile QB Rhule covets. They do lose their top player in RB Johnson and take on a tougher schedule. DEFENSE - In '23, then-DC Tony White moved them to more of a 3-3-5 defense. The defense was vastly improved allowing just 304 ypg and 18.3 ppg! In '24, seven starters were back and they had the #5 DLine and my computer called for them to allow 325 ypg and 20.3 ppg and they were right there with 318 ypg and 19.5 ppg (missed by .8). Last year they lost their stud DT's, 5 other starters and their DC but my computer called for them to allow 325 ypg and 21.2 ppg and they gave up 329 ypg and 24.6 ppg! New DC Aurich is moving them from the 3-3-5 to the 4-2-5 and did wonders at San Diego St last year. They are facing a tougher schedule, but this unit remains strong. 2026 - Nebraska went 58-19 (75%) in six years under former HC Frank Solich ('99-'03) without a single losing season, including four double-digit win totals (12-1, 10-2, 11-2, 10-3). The Huskers have had nine losing seasons and just two 10-win seasons since. Bo Pelini was fired after a 9-4 season in 2014. In Scott Frost's five years, they were 16-31 and he was 5-22 in one-score games. They made a great hire in Matt Rhule, who quickly built and took Temple and Baylor to unexpected levels of success. Nebraska opened 5-3 in his 1st year but they finished 5-7! All the signs were pointing up in 2024. Nebraska had 5 Net Close losses in '23, were -17 in Turnovers and avoided Michigan, Oregon and Penn St. They made my Most Improved list at #2. The Huskers opened 5-1, but then lost 4 in a row before finally beating Wisconsin 44-25 to lock up a bowl, then beat BC in the bowl for their 1st winning year since 2016! They had a 18-11 FD edge over Ohio St and 20-5 vs Iowa in losses. The win over Wisconsin ended a streak of 8 games lost when trying to get win #6 and become bowl eligible. Last year they had 5 Big Ten home games and opened 5-1 and 7-3 but lost their last 3 by 23 ppg for a now disappointing 7-6 year. The new offense will feature more QB runs but does lose top guy RB Johnson. Improved QB and OL play will have them more potent. This is Rhule's best team but they do face a tougher schedule, drawing Ohio St, Indiana and Oregon after avoiding all 3 in '25. MINNESOTA GOLDEN GOPHERS OL GREG JOHNSON POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Minnesota has not had a QB selected in the NFL draft since 1972 (Craig Curry #8DC), or a 1st TM B10 QB since 1961 (Sandy Stephens). In 24 PJ Fleck brought in Max Brosmer, who threw for 3,459 (64%, 29-5) with New Hampshire and was a Walter Payton Award (FCS Heisman) finalist. I said he should easily top '23's Gopher passing numbers. Brosmer was at his best in the 4Q and threw for 2,828 (67%, 18-6), setting the school record for completions in a season with 268 (Adam Weber 258-'07). Brosmer was a UFA and stuck with the Vikings in '25. True frosh Drake Lindsey (PS#60) hit 4-5-50. Fleck told me Lindsey was playing at a higher level than any frosh he has had at QB and he is 6'5" 230. Lindsey had a solid first year as a starter throwing for 2,382 (63%, 18-6). Max Shikenjanski hit 4-5-80. Dylan Wittke (PS#63) hit 1-3-7. They add in Michael Merdinger (PS#62) who started the bowl for North Carolina in '24 and had 2 starts at Liberty last year and PS#61 and PS#81 true frosh. Lindsey has won more games as a Frosh than any QB in school history and now is bigger and stronger. RUNNING BACKS - In '23, they lost their all-time career rush leader (1,685, 5.2), plus their #2 RB (474, 4.7). VHT true frosh Darius Taylor (PS#24, IFS) had 193 vs EMich, 138 vs NCar and 198 vs N'Wstern but was injured. He had 208 in the bowl (#1, 799, 5.8) and avg 159.2 ypg. In '24 Taylor missed the opener, but led again with 986 (4.8). Last year they added in AJ Turner, who rushed for 864 (8.3!) for Marshall in '24. Taylor was injured early, basically missing 5 games and led with 670 (5.6). Turner was OFY Week 3 which also set the rush game back. Fame Ijaboi had 108 vs Michigan and was #2 (441, 4.6). True Frosh Grant Washington had 20-126 vs NWSt. This year they add Elon and Purdue transfers and true frosh Ryan Estrada (PS#30) and Zeke Bates (PS#66). Bates was a surprise of the spring. Xavier Ford (5-10 210 rFr) is a big back. Taylor should top 1,000 if he stays healthy and this unit will have more the typical production you expect from the Gopher RB's. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost their #1 (863, 11.5), #2 (684, 13.2) WR's, and TE (3 st, 9 rec). They added in 1st TM MAC Javon Tracy (818, 14.4, Miami OH) and 3 other transfers. They did have 5 solid TE's. Daniel Jackson was one of 17 Big Ten players all-time with 200+ rec and 2,000+ yards receiving and I said it would be tough to replace. Le'meke Brockington led with 484 (10.5) and TE Jameson Geers was #5 (206, 7.9) and both depart. Tracy was #2 (454, 12.3). Jalen Smith had two outstanding clutch end-zone catches in the bowl & was #3 with 419 (15.0). They add in 4 transfers including Perry Thompson (PS#12, Texas) and TE Kaden Helms (PS#17 Okla) and are more experienced overall. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they returned four starters but had just 116 (3.7) rush and 26 sacks. Last year they lost 3 starters and had just 24 career starts, but added 4 transfers (55 car sts). Fleck has done a solid job with inexperienced lines but with banged up RB's they slipped to just 103 (3.6) rush. They did allow just 24 sacks. This year they lose two starters (24/71). The Gophers add in 6'7" 325 PS#17 Bennett Warren from Tennessee and return 3+ starters, so the career starts climb to 66 and I expect better production in 2026. LG Greg Johnson is my 1st team AA and LT Nathan Roy (PS#40) is already on NFL scouts radar, so this unit will more resemble your typical Fleck offensive line and is one of the offense's strengths. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they had the most experienced front in 3 years. Fleck told me it was one of the best DLines he has had here at Minnesota. The numbers improved to 110 (3.5) rush allowed with 28 sacks. Last year they had to replace both DE's. Both DT's returned. DE Anthony Smith (PS#60) could be yet another #1 or #2 DC DL here. They added in two productive FCS transfers and a PS#24 from LSU. Smith had a dominant bowl game and still opted to return. The D had 9 sacks vs Nebraska and 7 each vs Rutgers and Mich St (35 on year) and allowed 122 (3.8) rush. Karter Menz had 6.5 sacks and is a solid pass rusher. This year they lose both DT's (24 st, 3 sk, 53 tkl) but with Smith's return and the addition of 4 transfers including TJ Bush (13 st, 5.5 sk at Cal) put them in the upper half of the Big Ten DLines. LINEBACKERS - In '24 I called it a very underrated group of LB's. UM allowed just 17 ppg (27 ppg '23). Last year they had to replace their #1 and #7 tacklers. This did return Maverick Baranowski (#2 tklr) and Devon Williams (#9). The D went from holding foes to 78 ypg below their average to allowing foes 7 ypg above. This year they lose Williams (12 st, #2 tklr, 7.5 tfl) and a NB (6 st, 26 tkl). Baranowski (#1 tklr) and Matt Kingsbury (#8 tklr) both return and they should be stronger. Fleck feels they are 6 deep at LB (see PSL) and they are a strength of the D. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '21, Minny moved up to #10 (55.6%, 15-8) in my PDR and then #12 (58.1%) with a super 8-14 ratio in '22! In '23, they lost two #5DC's and dropped to just #84. In '24 they lost two starters (#2DC). They added a VHT true frosh S Koi Perich (PS#20) and made a Stock Market move back up to #11 (59%, 11-16). Last year they lost two starters (#3DC) and slipped back to #96 (68%, 16-8). This year they lose Perich (13 st, #3 tklr) and a CB (10 st, #8 tklr) but return a couple of HMB10 DB's and could still move up in the PDR. CB John Nestor and SS Kerry Brown are the top guys and they feel this unit is equally strong at covering and stopping the run. SPECIAL TEAMS - Last year, they lost both K & P. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In '23, Minny took a big step back with just 301 ypg and 20 ppg. In '24 I said with much stronger QB play, a deep set of RB's and finally a veteran offensive line, my computer called for a large jump of almost 10 points to 29 ppg. They came up a little short at 26.3 ppg. Last year my computer called for 26.0 ppg and again they came up a little short a 23.0 with the RB's banged up and a Frosh QB. This year they have a now veteran QB, a healthy Darius Taylor and a top notch OLine and they should have their best output since at least 2022. DEFENSE - In 2024 the Gophers allowed just 18 ppg and 291 ypg - including their first B2B shutouts since 1962! Last year they lost their DC. They were one of 9 schools that has had a 1st or 2nd round DC the previous 6 drafts on defense. My computer called for a drop to allowing 21.5 ppg and they were right there at 22.9. They had a school record 9 sacks vs Nebraska. This year they lose S Koi Perich. The draft streak was broken because DE Anthony Smith turned down the NFL and opted to return. They also get back #1 tackler Baranowski so they are strong at all 3 levels and a sneaky strong defense. 2026 - In 2019 UM got to 9-0 for first time since 1941's National Title team. The Gophers were 11-2 and #10! After a 3-4 Covid year, the Gophers have now had 6 straight bowl wins. In 2023, they were actually 5-7 but got to a bowl and won for 6-7. In '24 the Vegas Over-Under was just 4.5, but my main set of power ratings called for a bowl, so I said I was taking the Over. Fleck, as usual, exceeded my expectations. UM opened 2-3, then upset USC and got to 6-3. After close losses to Rutgers and Penn St (led most game), they beat Wisconsin 24-7, then won yet another bowl game, beating Virginia Tech 24-10. Last year the the Vegas Over/Under was 6.5. Minnesota had a dream schedule with 7 home games and went 7-0 at home. They had a rugged road schedule including Ohio St, Oregon and Iowa and went 0-5 on the road and were -194 ypg and lost by 24 ppg on the road. They won their 9th straight bowl to finish 8-5. This year they return 35 lettermen - 7 starters on offense & 6 starters on defense - and lose 23 lettermen. They were -142 ypg in Big Ten play last year and had 3 Net Close Wins so both signs are pointing down. Going thru the roster with coach Fleck, I feel good about this team as they have a veteran QB, one of the nations top RB's, a veteran OLine and are solid at all 3 levels of the defenses. They avoid Oregon and Ohio St - teams they were -250 ypg vs last year. They have 7 home games and games vs Michigan and Iowa are big. ILLINOIS FIGHTING ILLINI RB AIDAN LAUGHERY OFFENSIVE LINE - Bielema always fields a strong O-Line. With Nick Saban retiring, Bielema said he has produced more OL drafted than anyone and in '24 they improved to 154 (4.4) rush with 32 sacks. Last year all five starters were back and both OT's NFL prospects. Surprisingly they struggled vs some of the top D-lines with Duke, Indy, Ohio St and Wisconsin avg 5 sacks each. The rush totals dropped to 131 (3.8) with the same 31 sacks. This year they lose four starters (50/165!!) including 4th TM AA JC Davis (#6 DC NYG). They add in starters from Wisconsin and Colo St but the career starts drop from 103 to 70. It would not surprise me if the numbers improved this year, but this is a less experienced group. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they allowed 148 (4.4) rush with 31 sacks. Last year they had to replace 3 starters. Gabe Jacas led with 8 sacks and was 3rd Tm AA in '24 and was back, plus they added two DL who were full-time starters at Wisconsin and two other transfers. They were more experienced and stronger up front and improved to allowing 124 (3.9) rush PG but the sacks dropped to 24. This year they lose Jacas (#2 DC NE) (13 st, #5 tklr, 11 sks!) and 4 other DL (35 sts, 91 tkl, 6 sk). They add in 5 transfers (0 strs), so this unit is a major question mark for me. LINEBACKERS - In 2024 they improved by a TD to allowing 21.7 ppg. Dylan Rosiek was OFY vs Minny but was still #3 tackler. Last year they lost one LB (8 st, #8 tklr), but James Kreutz (4 st, #4 tklr) and Rosiek (#3 tklr) were back, as was Alec Bryant (PS#30, 22 tkl). Bielema said it was the best two deep of LB's he has had in his 5 years here. In '24 they allowed foes 31 ypg above their average. Last year they held foes to 22 ypg below. This year they lose 4 LB (18 sts, #3, 5, 11, 12 tklrs). They add in Colo St transfer Robert Edmonson (49 tkl) and return Chief Matthew Bailey (#1 tklr) and Kreutz (1 st, 29 tkl). Daniel Brown (PS#31 JC) had 18 sacks in JC in '23 and should emerge. I like the talent, but they are less experienced. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '22, Illinois rose all the way to #1 in my PDR (51.3%) allowing just 9 td's with 24 ints! In '23, they lost all 4 starters (#1, #2, #3 DCs). As you would expect, they dropped to #79 (60%, 22-7). In '24, they lost two starters. The more experienced unit moved up to #39, led by S Matthew Bailey (#1 tklr, 7 pbu). Last year, the unit returned in tact and Bielema said it has a lot of next level talent. 1st Tm B10 CB Xavier Scott was OFY after 3 starts and they fell to #61 (63.6%, 19-6). This year they lose two starters (#2, #4 tklr) but get Scott back, along with CB Juice Clarke and S Mac Resetich and they could live up to the promise of last year's group. Bielema calls it the best position group on the team. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 K David Olano hit 17-20 FG (L50) and Hank Beatty had 14.7 on PR's. Illinois moved up ST RANK L6Y: to #20 in my STR. Last year they lost both P's, they 2025 ... #63 added in Purdue P Keelan Crimmons (41.3 net!). 2024 ... #20 Beatty had 133 PR yds vs W. Illinois, breaking Red 2023 ... #56 Grange's 102 yr old school record (100 yd). Olano 2022 ... #54 ....#75 hit 17-20 and had 51 TB on 67 KO. Their P avg 43.9 2021 2020 ... #93 (38.4 net). They dropped to #51 and all 3 depart, but K Ethan Moczulski (kickoff man '23) returns from Washington. COACHES - 5th year HC Bret Bielema returned to the Big Ten, where he guided Wisconsin to three Rose Bowls. He led Arkansas to three bowls in 5 years and spent 2 years in the NFL. The 5th year OC is Barry Lunney, who was OC at SJSt ('03-'04) and UTSA ('20-'21). New DC is Bobby Hauck who won 151 games and 8 league titles in two stints as Montana's HC. He was HC at UNLV ('10-'14) but this is his first DC job. 1st Year STC Chris Hurd enters his 4th yr as an Illinois assistant. He was STC at Akron ('19-'21), Chattanooga ('17-'18) & FAU ('14-'16) before coming to Illinois. POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '23, they brought in Luke Altmyer (PS#24) from Ole Miss. He threw for 1,883 (64.8%, 13-10). In '24, Bielema called Altmyer one of the most improved players on the team, and he was! Altmyer threw for 2,717 (61% & 22-6!). Last year, Altmyer threw for 3,007 (67.4% 22-5!). He departs. RFr Carsno Boyd (PS#38) who was #3 QB last year, rFr Jershaun Newton (PS#82) and true frosh Michael Clayton (PS#43) will battle for the backup spot. They add in Katin Houser (PS#15) who started 7 games at Mich St in '22, then had 7 starts at East Caroina in '24. Last year in 12 starts at EC he threw for 3,300 (65.9%, 19-6). It is tough to replace a rare 3-year starter that improved yearly but Houser is now a 4th-year starter that has gotten better. This is his first in this system. Clayton was solid in the spring and may have the best arm of the group & Boyd has the best mobility so they all have different strengths. RUNNING BACKS - In '23, they lost their #2 career rusher (#5DC) but added frosh Kaden Feagin (PS#18). Feagin led with 438 (4.6) but missed the last two. In '24 they lost their #1 again (567, 4.9). They had a Feagin/McCray/Aidan Laughery 3-headed monster at RB. Laughery had 172 vs NW and was #2 (589, 6.1). Feagin was #1 after 5 games but was OFY (306, 4.6). True frosh Ca'lil Valentine (PS#37) had 212 (4.0). Last year they lost McCray (#1 609, 5.2), but again had a 3-headed monster. Valentine led with 614 (4.7), Feagin was #2 (507, 4.2) and Laughery was #3 (382, 5.1). All three return (Feagin moved to TE). Jordan Anderson (6'4" 240 Jr, PS#67) is the big back and true frosh Javari Barnett (PS#36) and rFr John Forster (PS#38) give them a solid top five. WISCONSIN BADGERS WR CHRIS BROOKS 3 starters again plus added in 3 transfers. All 3 returnees were all Big 10 caliber but C Jake Renfro was injured in August and started just 3 games. The line shuffled often early so despite their 111 career starts the numbers dropped to 117 (3.3) with 28 sacks. This year they lose 5 OL (50/159) but have two starters back (both were rFr in ’25) plus they add in 4 transfers so they should be much more stable. LT Kevin Heywood was slated to start in ‘25 but was OFY and is back. DEFENSIVE LINE - In ‘24 they lost 2.5 starters and allowed 165 (4.6) rush with just 17 sacks (fewest s/1983). Last year they lost two starters and two backups. They had just three DL that were 300+ lbs in ‘24 and had nine last year so the unit as a whole was bigger. NORTHWESTERN WILDCATS OL EZOMO ORATOKHAI POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In ‘24, four QB’s combined to throw for 2,231 (53.7%) with a 7-11 ratio. True frosh Ryan Boe (PS#105) hit 4-13-42 in the ﬁnal vs Illinois and was the lone returnee. They added in Preston Stone (PS#12), who started 12 for SMU in ‘23, (3,197, 60%, 28-6, 196 rush). Stone had 4 int’s in the opener and 3 vs Illinois but threw for 2,400 (60%, 17-12). Boe hit 2-17-17. Stone departed. A transfer has opened the season as starter every year here since 2019. They add in 3 transfers this year. Aidan Chiles (PS#37) had 20 starts at Mich St, throwing for 3,807 (61%, 24-14, 452 rush). Nicco Marchiol (PS#18) had 7 starts for West Virginia the last 3 years. Gavin Frakes started 5 games for NMexSt in ‘23. I think Chiles will produce stronger numbers in ‘25. HC Braun feels they have 3 guys they can win with and the room is much deeper. RUNNING BACKS - In ‘23, Cam Porter led the way with 651 yards (3.9, 121 rec) . RFr Joe Himon (PS#45) was #4 with 136 (3.9). The overall RB rush yards were 1,025 (4.1). In ‘24, Porter led again with 501 (4.0), Himon was #2 (257, 4.9) and rFr Caleb Komolafe #4 with 139 (2.8). The RB rush numbers dipped to 906 (4.0). All 4 were back last year and they added true frosh Daniel Anderson (5’11” 210, PS#49). Porter had 137 (7.6) but was OFY after two games. Komolafe stepped up and had four 100+ efforts and led with 941 (5.0) while Himon was #2 (486, 4.9). Robby Preckel had 22-82 vs Illinois with the top two out. The overall RB rush yards improved to 2,082 (4.6) and all the top RB’s return. Plus they add Gavin Sawchuk (PS#2 Flor St, 7 st, 486, 4.5), rFr Marcus Romain (PS#63) and BG transfer Markel Porter (5’11” 225 So, PS#187) so they are my #26 RB corps. RECEIVERS - In ‘23, for the ﬁrst time since 2016, the top 3 WR’s combined for 1,800+! In ‘24, the top 3 had 1,453 yards and all 3 departed. They added in Grifﬁn Wilde (1,147, 16.4 SDakSt) and used plenty of “12” personnel. Early on this was a one-man show as Wilde was the go-to man. He led with 880 (12.4). Hayden Elgion had 11 rec’s the ﬁrst 6 games but had 7-127 vs Minny and 8-99 vs Illinois and was #2 (521, 14.1). Those two are both back. This year they lose their TE (#3, 296, 10.6), but with 4 of the top 5 back, are much more experienced. I list the PSL below and they add in TE Alex Honig (275 lbs) from TCU/ UConn and WR Luke Dehnicke, who could be their big play guy. OFFENSIVE LINE - In ‘23, with just 27 career starts, they had just 102 (2.9) rush while allowing 51 sacks (13.1%). In ‘24 the career starts climbed to 78. They greatly cut down on the sacks (24) but still had just 99 (3.3) rush. Last year they had two starters back, added in Liberty and South Dakota St starters, and had 10 OL with starting experience. I called for a stronger run game with both Evan Beernsten (#7 DC BAL) and Caleb Tiernan (#3 DC MIN) NFL prospects. The Cats improved to 160 (4.6) rush with just 17 sacks allowed. This year they lose 4 starters, including both draft picks. They add in 3 transfers but the career starts drop to 43. Last year’s OLine was worthy of Joe Moore Award mention, but this year’s ﬁgures to be down a little from that level. C Ezomo Oratokhai is the top guy. DEFENSIVE LINE - In 2024 they had 7 of the top 8 back and Braun felt depth was the strength of the unit, as they could rotate 10 DL. DT Carmine Bastone (9 st ‘23) missed 5 games. The Cats had 15 sacks the ﬁrst 6 games, but 8 the last 6. They did cut the rush ypg allowed to 130 (4.0). Last year they returned 3 starters. The numbers slipped to allowing 136 (4.3) with just 23 sacks. This year they lose 3 starters (35 st, 13 sk) so are less experienced. Braun likes the DE’s in Michael Kilbane and Jamaal Johnson, so they will have more sacks. But, they need some guys to develop on the interior to improve the rush D. LINEBACKERS - Last year they had to replace their #2 and #10 tacklers. They returned Max Uihlein (#1 tklr) and Star Braden Turner (#8 tklr). Braydon Brus (PS#88) was one of the most talented LBs. They held foes to 30 ypg below their average. This year they lose 2nd TM B10 Uihlein (13 st, #2 tklr, 6 tﬂ) but have two starters back in Brus (#3 tklr) and Turner (#4 tklr) plus add in Kobie McKenzie (PS#15, 8 sts) from Oklahoma. They should remain strong. Nigel Glover (PS#56, Ohio St) has a high ceiling, but needs to emerge as depth is a question. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In 2023, the LB’s had 5 ints, the DB’s had 6 and the Wildcats were #73 in my PDR. In ‘24 they were #70 in my PDR (63%, 15-10). Last year they lost 3 starters but had six DB’s that have started 4+ games in a season, plus added in two transfers I said they should ﬁnish in the same area and they did at #73 (63%, 12-8). This year they lose two starters (#5, #7 tklr). They return Robert Fitzgerald (#1 tklr) and CB Josh Fussell (18 st, 2 yr) and should move up some more in the PDR. This is a now veteran unit and Braun says it is the best the back half has looked in years. SPECIAL TEAMS- In ‘24, everyone was back, including Luke Akers, who was the P in ‘22. When K Jack Olsen ST RANK L6Y: was injured, Akers took over P, K and kickoffs! 2025 ... #95 The Cats were just #101 in the STR. Last year, 2024 .. #101 everyone was back but they were just #95. Duncan hit 21-34-235-2-0. Both brothers return plus they add in Ty Dieffenbach (PS#80 Pitt) who threw for 1,305 at Cal Poly. RUTGERS SCARLET KNIGHTS OL KWABENA ASAMOAH POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 Rutgers added Athan Kaliakmanis (12 st, Minn) and true frosh AJ Surace (PS#45, IFS, accurate), whose dad is HC at Princeton. Kaliakmanis, who looked solid in '22 under OC Ciarrocca at Minnesota, won the job (incumbent then transferred), throwing for 2,696 yards (54%, 18-7) with only 3 other Rutgers QBs in history topping 2,700 and the first to top 2,000 here since 2015. Those two returned in '25 and they added true frosh Sean Ashenfelder (PS#84). Kaliakmanis became the first QB here since 2008 (Mike Teel) to top 3,000 yards passing with 3,124 (62%, 20-7). He moves on and Surace hit just 4-9-58. Schiano adds in Dylan Lonergan (PS#10, Ala) who had 9 starts at Boston College last year throwing for 2,025 (67%, 12-5) and he should come close to Kaliakmanis's (#7 DC WAS) numbers. RUNNING BACKS - In '23 Kyle Monangai was the first Knight to top 1,000 yards since 2012 (Jawan Jamison) and led the Big Ten in rushing with 1,262 (5.2). In '24 Monangai led with 1,279 (5.0). Early enrollee Antwan Raymond had 113 vs Kan St and was #2 with 457 (4.6). Last year they lost their #2 all time rusher (#7 DC). Raymond (18-113) and Ja'shon Benjamin (7-33) looked good in the bowl. Raymond was not the projected starter but took charge and had 161 vs Minny, 41-240 vs MD and 29-189 vs Penn St and led with 1,241 (5.1). Benjamin was #2 (328, 4.8) and both return plus they add in Clay Thevenin (634, 4.8 LTech), soph Edd Guerrier (PS#131), rFr Terrell Mitchell (PS#124) and true frosh Michael Dukes (PS#73). Raymond should net them a 4th-straight 1,000 yard rusher. RECEIVERS - In '23, the Knights lost 3 of the top 4 (#1, 440, 16.9). A former walk-on led with 468 (13.0) and true frosh Ian Strong was #4 (230, 14.4). In '24 they lost their #2 (361, 16.4), #3 (326, 12.5) and TE (12 st, 121, 8.6). They added in a Monmouth transfer, who led the FCS (1,293, 14.4 '23) and true frosh KJ Duff (PS#70, IFS). Strong emerged and was #2 (676, 15.7). Duff was #3 (425, 15.7). Last year they lost their top guy (757, 12.8, first Rut rec 700+ s/'15). They added in DT Sheffield (822, 12.5, NTex) and this unit went from a long time weakness to one of the B10's better WR corps. Duff had a Rutgers B10 record 241 yds vs Purdue and led with 1,084 (18.1). They lose Strong (#2, 762, 14.7), Sheffield (#3, 577, 13.1). and TE Fletcher (#4) but add in Ball St's TE and remain strong. OFFENSIVE LINE -In '24, they had four starters back and the best O-Line since Schiano returned (123 car sts). LG Bryan Felter was OFY after 4 starts. They rushed for 175 (4.4) with 21 sacks allowed. Last year they lost their LT (13/50), but with Felter's return, had 5 starters back plus they added 5 transfers. They had 9 OL with 4+ starts in a year, 106 career starts but the numbers dropped to 141 (3.6) with 39 sacks. This year they lose 3 starters (37/90!). Last year, they redshirted Colorado's starting C and two FCS starters. They have 83 FBS career starts and 87 FCS starts and could improve on last years lower than expected production. RG Kwabena Asamoah and LG Dantae Chin are the top guys and both have NFL potential. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they allowed just 143 (4.7) in Big Ten play and had 22 sacks overall. Last year they lost 3 starters and 2 backups. They added in Eric O'Neill (29 sk 3Y JMU) and Bradley Weaver (14.5 sk 2Y Ohio) and 2 other transfers. Rutgers has not topped 23 sacks in a year in 11 years (last DL 25+ sks 2016)! In the first 6 games they allowed 136 ypg rush and had 9 sacks. Over the last 6 games they allowed 284 ypg rush (8.4) and had just 2 sacks!!! This year they lose 4 DL (30 st, 116 tkl, 7 sk) but add in 5 transfers who were full time starters and can only improve on '25's finish. LINEBACKERS - Schiano is known for crafting solid LB corps. In '24 it was an injury plagued unit and DJ Djabome was #1 tackler as a soph - the first to top 100 tackles here since 2020. Moses Walker (PS#32) had 31 tackles. Last year they lost their #4 and #5 tacklers. They added Cam Miller (PS#63 Penn St) and looked stronger but allowed foes 40 ypg above their average (#111). They lose Djabome (#2 tklr) and NB Miller (#6 tklr). Walker was OFY after 4 games and is back as is Abram Wright (#4 tklr) plus they add in Rice's Ty Morris (88 tkl) and Sean Allison (126 tkl, Drake) and will be stronger in 2026. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '22, they were #31 in my PDR and in '23, #31 again (60%, 16-9). In '24 they lost a #2 DC then had some injuries and dropped to #60 (60.0%, 18-8). Last year they lost all 4 starters. True frosh Kaj Sanders was #8 tackler and rFr Bo Mascoe was #6. They added in starters from Marshall and UNLV and fell even further to #129 (64.4%, 25-3!). This year they lose 3 starters (#1, #5, #7 tklr) but add in a starter from South Dakota (DC from there) are more experienced and will make a Stock Market leap in the PDR. SPECIAL TEAMS - Since '09, the Knights lead the NCAA in blocked kicks with 67. Schiano puts a large emphasis on this group and, in '23, rFr Jai Patel set a school record hitting 15-18 fg's (83%). Rutgers was #23 in the STR. In '24, ST RANK L6Y: Patel hit 15-19 FG (L49), Jack Scullion had 34 2025 .. #107 TB on 70 KOs and P Jakob Anderson averaged 2024 ... #83 42.6 (39.1 net). Rutgers dropped to #83. Last year 2023 ... #23 everyone was back so I expected a Stock Market 2022 ... #30 ..... #5 leap but they fell to #107. Patel hit 13-18, Anderson 2021 2020 ..... #5 had a 41.8 net and Scullion had 33 TB/67 KO. I will call for Rutgers to get back to their normal level (top 30) this year and block some more punts. COACHES - Greg Schiano is in Year 7 of his return (HC here '01-'11 Big East). He opened 12-34, then was 56-33 with six bowls over his last 7 years (RU just one bowl prior), including an 11-2 '06 (#12 AP). He left for the NFL (TB HC) and Ohio St (DC). He is the school's all time leader in wins. 4th year OC Kirk Ciarrocca was the Co-OC here from '09-'10 (Schiano). Ciarrocca was OC at Minn ('22, '17-'19) and Penn St ('20, #3 B10 ppg). The new DC is Travis Johansen who was DC at South Dakota '19-'24 then HC there in '25. Eddie Allen (STC Conn '18-'21) is the lone STC this year after sharing duties. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In '24, they had 8 returning starters and my computer called for a large jump to 29.1 ppg and they missed by .2 with 28.9 ppg! (best here s/'08). Last year my computer took an improved offense but factored it in vs a much tougher schedule and projected 29 ppg and the Knights had 29 ppg! This year the Knights lose their QB but the new QB has 1,341-yard RB Raymond, top WR Duff and a solid offensive line to work with. Plus with a softer schedule, they should be improved. DEFENSE - In '24, 8 starters were back, but they were injury plagued mid year. My computer called for them to allow 23.0 ppg and they allowed 23.8 ppg! Last year with a tougher schedule my computer called for them to drop by a TD to 30.3 ppg and they allowed 31.8 ppg! Schiano was not happy with the DC's. They lose 9 of the top 11 but face a better schedule and new DC Johnson should have them much tougher vs. the run. This time my computer is calling for 28.7 ppg. 2026 - After '19, Rutgers had lost 21 straight Big Ten games (2nd longest ever, NW 38 '78-'82). Rutgers lost its Big Ten games by a 39-6 avg and -241 ypg. The talent level was lacking and Schiano was one of the unfortunate first-year HC's with zero spring practices. In '21, Rutgers was 5-6 and lost to Maryland at home, but got a late call to play Wake Forest in the Gator Bowl. Rutgers had not won a B10 home game in four years! In '22, Rutgers opened 3-0 but finished 4-8. They were -135 and -133 ypg in Big Ten play in '21 & '22. In '23 they had the Big Ten's toughest schedule. Four of my nine sets of power ratings called for them to be bowl eligible (including my main one). Rutgers got to 6-2, then lost the last 4 games, but beat Miami for a 7-6 finish (6 losses to teams 58-16), its first winning season since 2014! In '24, they had the Big Ten's best schedule (avoid OSU, Mich, PSt, Ore, Iowa!). Most of my power ratings had them at 8-4, and they opened 4-0. But injuries had them drop the next 4. A bye got them healthier and they went 3-1 (lone loss 4&13 40-yd td pass with :04 left) to get to 7-5 (best s/'14) then blew a 17-point lead in the bowl. Five players were invited to the Combine. Last year, they had Schiano's best team since his return with 16 returning strs, but the schedule was much tougher. The defense fell apart mid-year and they were just 5-7 with close losses to Minny and Penn St so were 1 play away from a bowl. The defense will be improved this year and they have a new QB. MICHIGAN STATE SPARTANS QB ALESSIO MILIVOJEVIC POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24, all three QB's hit the portal so they added transfer Aidan Chiles (PS#37, dual threat), who played the 3rd series of every Oregon St game and knew the system well. Chiles was a wild card with plenty of long TD passes, showing off his arm and some solid runs (225, 2.3), but also had just a 13-11 ratio (4 fum) and some turnovers were very costly. He threw for 2,617 (60%, 13-12). RFr Alessio Milivojevic (PS#59) can make all the throws and was the backup with Leo Hannah (PS#40). Chiles had an up and down season in '25. Milivojevic threw int's on his first 2 passes, but led 3 late back door cover drives (Neb, Ind, Mich) before starting the final 4 and threw for 1,267 (64.2%, 10-3). ACC ATLANTIC COAST CONFERENCE –– PHIL’S 2026 FORECAST –– 1. Miami - Miami joined the ACC in 2004 and has never won the ACC title. Even last years’ national title game team due to a bizarre ACC tie-breaker was not even in the ACC title game. After going 12-13 his first two seasons with Miami Mario Cristobal got them to 9-0 in 2025 but they were upset by GTech and Syracuse and missed out on the title game. Last year Carson Beck took over at QB and they were dominant on both the offensive and defensive lines. Miami had a 3 point loss to L’ville and a 6 point loss to SMU but in the playoff beat Texas A&M, Ohio St and Ole Miss. They do lose 9 NFL DC’s including DE’s Bain and Mesidor plus QB Beck. They add Darian Mensah of Duke at QB and return RB Mark Fletcher and WR Malachi Toney. Miami was +119 ypg in ACC play last year and are now favored to win that first ever ACC crown. 2. SMU - In ‘23 SMU went 8-0 AAC & won the AAC title game. SMU is 35-6 at home since 2019. In ‘24, 4 of my 9 sets of power ratings called for and 11-1 year. SMU even stepping up in competition to the ACC went 8-0 (+128 ypg) in ACC play. They lost the title game to Clemson but still made the playoff! Last year they dropped early games to Baylor and TCU and had a 1 point loss to Wake. SMU controlled their destiny but lost to Cal in the final and lost their bid for the ACC title game. QB Kevin Jennings was hobbled the 2H of last year and returns healthy and has a veteran O-line. SMU opens ACC play with road trips to Florida St and Louisville then will be favored in their last 7 ACC games. SMU is 22-2 in conf play the last 3 years and draws the best ACC schedule. 2. Clemson - The Tigers have won 8 of the last 11 ACC titles. In ‘24 Clemson was on the outside of the ACC title game but Miami lost to Syracuse then moved in and beat SMU for the title and a playoff berth. Last year Clemson was one of the most experienced teams in the country led by QB Klubnik and was #4 AP preseason but shockingly opened 1-3 then 3-5 before winning the last 4 to get to a bowl. This year they have a new QB but Tom Allen should have the defense improved in his 2nd year and the Tigers draw a favorable ACC schedule. Clemson was +66 ypg in ACC play despite their 4-4 record last year but need to regain their home field edge after a 3-4 year in Death Valley (had been 56-5 prev 9 yr). 2. Louisville - HC Jeff Brohm got to the Big Ten title game in ‘22 with Purdue then made the ACC Title game here in ‘23. In ‘24 they lost at ND, at home to both SMU and Miami and a stunning loss at Stanford, all 4 by 7 or less. Last year the Cards drew the 2nd toughest schedule in the ACC and were banged up at RB. They lost to Virginia and Cal by 3 and Clemson by 1 then a depleted team (QB, RB inj) were blown out by SMU for a 4-4 ACC year. The Cards blew out Kentucky and won the bowl. Brohm has a mobile QB in Kienholz and get the return of his dynamic RB combo of Issac and Keyjuan Brown. The Cards schedule is a lot more manageable and they have 5 ACC home games. 5. Pitt - Pitt won the ACC in 2021 and was #1 in the ACC at +123 ypg. They went 9-4 in ‘22 then plummeted to 3-9 in ‘23. In ‘24 Pitt rated a SMI of +7.0!! They opened 7-0 and #18. Their starting QB was injured and Pitt then dropped the last 6 including a 6 OT bowl loss. Last year Pitt opened just 2-2 with a pair of 7 point come from ahead losses to WV and L’ville. They switched to true frosh QB Heintchel and won thier next 6 ACC games including a road win at GGT. Pitt lost to Miami at home 38-7 costing them a berth in the ACC title game. Heintchel is back and they are strong on both lines of scrimmage. PItt does have 5 ACC road games including Miami, L’ville and Vtech. 5. Virginia - The Cavs have been patient with HC Elliot and it paid off as they have gone from 1 to 2 to 3 wins in the ACC his first 3 years to 7-1 and the ACC title game last year coming up just short of making the playoff! This year Virginia loses their 1,000 yard rusher, veteran QB and top 4 receivers. The Cavs rate a -7 in my SMI and most arrows are pointing down. My main set of power ratings have them at 7-2 but the other 8 have them below that. NCSt went from Brazil to a home game so they do not have to worry about the trip and are an ACC contender. 5. Virginia Tech - In ‘23 the Hokies were +107 ypg in ACC play, and in ‘24 had 21 ret starters (#2 Exp Chart) so expectations were high but they had a disappointing 6-7 season. Last year they were one of the rare teams to make my Most Improved List and have a losing season at just 3-9. VT makes my Most Improved list this year as they had a great offseason. First they hired James Franklin and then Brent Pry the HC the last 4 years showed no animosity for being fired mid year and takes over as DC where he and Franklin did wonders at Penn St. VT makes the Going Up Box on 4 different metrics this year and brought in a ton of transfers many from Penn St. They do have 5 ACC road games including trips to Miami, SMU and Clemson but could open up as strong as 7-0 and that give them confidence heading into a tough stretch . 5. NC State - In ‘24 NCSt needed a TD with :25 left to beat NC just to keep alive a 5 year bowl streak. Last year they avoided Clemson, SMU and Lville in ACC play. They beat Virginia in a “non conf” game but after a 4-4 ACC slate where they were -52 ypg the Wolfpack are now 7-9 the last two years in conf play. This year QB CJ Bailey is back but they do lose 9 starters on D and the top RB, top 4 WR and 3 starting OL but did a good job in the portal. The schedule is manageable as they avoid Miami, SMU and Clemson! 9. Georgia Tech - Brent Key took over GT after a 1-3 start and went 4-3 in ACC play. In ‘24 GT faced 5 of the top 6 teams in the ACC and they had just 3 ACC home games but went 5-3 ACC and was +33 ypg. Last year they avoided Miami, LVille and SMU. Key was 4-0 SU vs ranked ACC teams! GT appeared headed to the ACC title game at 8-0 but then were upset by NCSt and Pitt and lost out on the tie breaker. A loss to Georgia and in the bowl had them finish 9-4. This year they lose the driving force in QB Haynes King plus 8 of the top 11 tacklers on defense. They do face Pitt, VT and Clemson all on the road. 9. Florida St. - In ‘23, 17 starters were back and FSU went 13-0 winning the ACC title but with no playoff were a depleted team that was whipped by Georgia. In’24 they went from #2 on the Exp Char to #73 and all indicators were pointing down. FSU went thru a miserable 2-10 season and were -132 ypg in ACC play. Last year FSU figured to be much improved and opened with an upset of Alabama and blowout wins by a combined 143-13 and at 3-0 were #7 AP. FSU had 4 straight losses (OT, 6, 3, 7 pts) and at 5-6 played their worst game in the final losing at Florida 40-21. This year Mike Norvell is on the hot seat and FSU takes on the Toughest schedule in the ACC facing all the top contenders. Despite their 3-5 ACC record they were +76 ypg in ACC play (#3!). This is a transfer heavy team once again. 11. Duke - Duke has now done better than I have expected 4 straight years! In 2024, I said it would be an accomplishment to make a bowl. Manny Diaz had an amazing 5-0 start and went 9-3 before a bowl loss. They were -55 ypg in ACC play. Last year I said I did not see them matching ‘24’s 9 win total. Duke opened just just 5-5 in a mediocre year but won their last two games somehow won the tie breaker to get to the ACC title game then upset Virginia and Duke was ACC Champion! The Blue Devils then beat Ariz St in the bowl for a 9-5 year. QB Mensah was a late and unexpected loss and Duke was -18 ypg in ACC play. Duke has 5 ACC road games and can Duke beat my expectations a FIFTH straight year? 132 12. North Carolina - In ‘22 NC clinched the Coastal with two games to go (9-1) but then lost those two games, the ACC title game and the bowl (28-27). In ‘23 NC opened 6-0 and #10 but went 8-12 after that (6-7 ‘24). Last year the Tar Heels made headlines with the hire of Bill Belichick but had a even more disappointing 4-8 season. Coach did have practically a brand new team last year but has a transfer heavy team once again. There figures to be a little less off field noise this summer and maybe a more cohesive team. 12. Wake Forest - In ‘21 Wake went 7-1 and got to the ACC title game! In ‘22 WF was #22 preseason and at 6-1 with only a close loss to Clemson was #11 AP. Wake went 10-20 the next 30 games and in ‘24 was 2-6 in the ACC and -133 ypg. New HC Dickart brought in a a ton of transfers focusing on snaps played and also avoided Clemson, Miami and L’ville. Wake had a much better year than expected going 9-4 with a bowl win over Miss St! This year WF makes the Going Down box on three pages (-5 SMI). They bring in Gio Lopez from North Carolina at QB and draw a tougher schedule with 5 ACC road games. 12. California - In ‘24 Cal opened 3-4 but was 4 plays from being 7-0 and won the next two but finished 6-7 overall and 2-6 in ACC play despite being even in yards. Last year was the debut of JKS at QB and he was dynamic. Cal went 5-6 then with interim HC Rolovich upset SMU to knock them out of the ACC title game and put Cal into a bowl. Cal was -54 ypg in ACC play and lost the bowl for a 6-7 season. This year new HC Tosh Lupoi has a veteran OLine and JKS is back. Cal gets 5 ACC home games but did have 3 Net Close Wins last year. 15. Syracuse - In ‘23 Syracuse -146 ypg in ACC play. New HC Fran Brown brought in some top notch transfers like QB Kyle McCord (Ohio St). The Orange finished a super 10-3 (+42 ypg ACC) but did benefit 4 Net Close Wins and 4 Net Upsets. Most indicators were pointing down plus they faced the toughest schedule of the ACC. With Steve Angeli at QB they opened 3-1 including a road upset of Clemson and appeared to beat the odds again but Angeli was injured and they lost their last 8 games and were -125 ypg. With Angeli and Odom at QB the offense should return to form but they still face the 3rd toughest schedule in the league. They make the Going Up box on 5 different pages (-13 TO’s, +5 SMI) and will contend for a bowl especially with DC Kehres improving the defense. 16. Stanford - In ‘24 the Cardinal were 2-7 in ACC play and -96 ypg. Last year interim HC Frank Reich did a decent job getting them to 3-6 in the ACC but they were -97 ypg again. This year they have a new HC as well as both coordinators. Stanford plays Miami, SMU and GTech at home and has 5 ACC road games so will be favored in maybe one ACC game so this looks like another rebuilding year. 17. Boston College - In ‘24 BC in Bill O’Brien’s first year went 7-6. Last year they faced the ACC’s 3rd toughest sked. The season did not go as planned as BC lost their first 10 vs FBS foes before beating Syracuse in the final for a 2-10 season and they were -103 ypg in ACC play (2nd worst). BC hit the portal hard and have just 4 returning starters on offense. OBrien did more with less in his years at Penn St and BC will be much more competitive this year. MIAMI HURRICANES DL AHMAD MOTEN POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 Miami added Cam Ward who set school records for TD passes, passing yards, completion %, yards per att. He threw for 4,313 (67%, 39-7) with 204 rush. Last year Miami brought in Carson Beck who led Georgia to the SEC title in '24, and threw for 3,941 (72%, 24-6) in '23 then 3,485 (65%, 28-12) in '24. Beck had his ups and downs (4 int vs Lville) but led Miami to the National Title game and threw for 3,813 (72.4%, 30-12). Beck (#3 DC ARZ) moves on and Miami got a last minute portal addition in Darian Mensah who threw for 2,723 (66%, 22-6) with Tulane in '24 then 3,973 (67%, 34-6!) with Duke last year. RFr Luke Nickel (PS#22), true frosh Dereon Coleman (PS#17) and Judd Anderson (6'6' 230 So, PS#64) provide the depth. Mensah could top Beck's '25 numbers and Cristobal feels this is the best depth they've had here. RUNNING BACKS - In '23 they added true frosh Mark Fletcher (PS#9) and he had 126 vs L'ville and 115 vs NCSt and was #2 (514, 4.9). In '24 they lost their #1 (625, 6.3) and #3 (478, 5.1) rushers. They added a 1st tm Pac 12 RB who led with 1,002 (6.3, #7DC). Fletcher was #2 (607, 5.4) and true frosh Jordan Lyle was #3 (400, 7.4). Last year they added Girard Pringle (PS#14) and Charmar Brown (1181, 4.8 NDSt). Fletcher missed 2 games but led with 1192 (5.5) and was a force in the playoffs. Brown was #2 (474, 3.9), Pringle had 116 vs NCSt and was #3 (375, 6.0) and Lyle #4 (108, 3.1). This year all 4 return and this is my #4 RB corps. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost the schools all time receiving leader (12 st, 1127, 16.3) and their top 5 overall who all had 500+ yards including a #2 DC TE (no WR drafted). They added CJ Daniels (1067, 19.4 Liberty '23) and Tulane's TE plus had 5 WR's rated PS#38 or better. True frosh Malachi Toney was the team's top play maker on offense, set the school record for receptions in a season (94) and led with 1,008 (10.7). This year they lose Keelan Marion (16 st, #2, 746, 13.1), CJ Daniels (#6 DC LAR) (12 st, 469, 11.2) and TE Alex Bauman (11 st, #7 rec). Toney is one of the nation's most dangerous offensive weapons. They add Cooper Barkate who had 1,084 with Harvard in '24 and 1,106 at Duke in '25 plus South Carolina's #2 and West Virginia's #1 receivers so are more experienced. Cristobal feels he has 4 or 5 legit starters and they are my #3 receiving corps. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they had 88 career starts back. I called it one of the ACC's best and they opened holes for 189 (5.7) with 23 sacks. Last year they lost two starters but added one and had 87 career starts and Cristobal knows Olines. Miami dropped to 152 (4.3) rush but allowed just 11 sacks from its mammoth Oline (3 OL 340+ lb). This year they lose 4 starters including RT Francis Mauigoa (#1 DC NYG) & 1st tm ACC Anez Cooper (#6 DC NYJ). They add PS#1 true frosh Jackson Cantwell, and have PS#3 and #12 backups to take open spots for OL Alex Mirabel's crew but the career starts drop to 30. Matthew McCoy has 5 position value and may be as good as any OL Cristobal has recruited here. They are close in talent to last year but have less experience playing together. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they lost 8 DL (comb 20 sts). They added 4 transfers who combined for 120 career starts. DE Rueben Bain missed 4 games and had just 3.5 sacks. LB BRANDON BOOKER SMU MUSTANGS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In 2023 the starter was OFY week 12. Kevin Jennings led the AAC title game win and hit 24-28-191 in the bowl. Both QB's went to ACC media days. Jennings took over vs BYU and threw for 3,245 yards (65%, 23-11) with 354 rush. True Frosh Ty Hawkins (PS#21) was IFS '25, is thicker than Jennings and a dual threat as well. Jennings got injured early and was hobbled most of the year, playing on a bad ankle, so his rush yards dropped to 54 but he threw for 3,641 (66%, 26-13). Hawkins is the QB of the future here. He's strong and runs well. There is a big drop off after the ﬁrst two. I look for Jennings to have a super senior season now that he is 100% healthy and hopefully he gets back to the running threat of 2024 and could be a Heisman candidate in 2026. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 they moved a WR to RB and he led with 1,332 (5.7) and had 327 receiving. True frosh Derrick McFall (PS#82) only played late and rushed for 106 (4.1). Last year they lost their top guy (#7DC). They added Chris Johnson (PS#41) from Miami and TJ Harden from UCLA (1658, 5.1 3Y). They were as experienced as '24 but I said it would be tough to match the production. Harden led with 787 (4.6) while Johnson was #2 (479, 7.1) and McFall was #3 (189, 5.4). This year they lose the top two but add Kendrick Raphael (PS#48, 943, 4.1 rush, 245, 7.2 rec), rFr Dramekco "Chucky" Green (90, 3.6) and true frosh Christian Rhodes (PS#21) and should be just as strong. Raphael actually scored Cal's game-winning TD against SMU last year. He is a big kid that can do it all and a potential draft pick next year. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost their #1 (663 15.8), #2 (527, 16.0), #4 (386, 18.4) and #6 (275, 14.5) receivers. They got back TE Russell Maryland (518, 18.2 '23), Romello Brinson (431, 15.4 '23) and #3 Jordan Hudson (422, 10.8) plus TE Matthew Hibner (8 st, #5). They added two VHT true frosh. Hudson led with 766 (12.6), Brinson was #2 (638, 14.8), Hibner (#4 DC BAL) #4 (436, 14.1) and Maryland #5 (322, 11.9) and all 4 depart. Yamir Knight #3 (#3, 637, 11.8) is back and they add Yannick Smith (11 st, 583, 13.3 ECar) and 3 TE's (A&M, FSU, TT) plus Jalen Hale (PS#11, Ala). They are close to '25 experience and talent wise. This group has a chance to be their best under Lashlee. Hale is healthy for the ﬁrst time in 3 years. Knight is a true slot that will have a lot of catches. OFFENSIVE LINE- In '24 they lost a 1st tm AAC LT (10/29) and 2nd tm AAC C (14/33) and another starter but added four P4 transfers, and with 120 career starts, and 8 VHT's in the 2-deep. They rushed for 168 (4.3) and allowed just 18 sacks. Last year they had 3 starters back and added Addison Nichols (12 st Ark), and two more P4 transfers (117 car sts) with 3 NFL prospects. With Jennings running less they dropped to 134 (4.3) rush with 19 sacks allowed. This year 3 starters return (91 car sts) and the unit should have improved numbers. They have better young players and Lashlee feels they have 8 to 10 guys they can win with. DEFENSIVE LINE- In '24 a Senior laden Dline allowed just 100 (2.9) rush and recorded 43 sacks. Last year the Mustangs lost all 4 starters and 3 backups (64 tkl). DT Jonathan Jefferson (PS#23) was injured in spring. They added eight transfers but still did well, allowing 111 (3.2) with 35 sacks. This year they lose all 4 senior starters once again! They add 4 transfers so are in the same shape as '25. SMU is 2nd in the country in sacks over the last 3 years. They might not have a bell cow on the Dline but there are 10 guys in this unit that can be really productive. LINEBACKERS- In '24 everyone was back and they held foes 44 ypg below their average. Last year they lost the top two (#1, #3 tklr) plus the NB (12 st, 48 tlk, 6 tﬂ). This year the top 3 LB's all return and they add NB Jarvis Lee (55 tkl, 4 sk USF) so they are much more experienced. They are deeper, longer and more athletic and bring back productive guys. MLB Brandon Booker has NFL size. DEFENSIVE BACKS- In '23 they added 7 transfers who combined for 99 career starts, and moved up to #19 in my PDR (57.7%, 17-12). In '24 they lost 2 starters but were still #26 in the PDR (56%, 24-16). Last year they lost two starters again and were my #23 rated secondary and ﬁnished #36 (60.9%, 26-18). They are longer, more athletic and have a good mix of experience and youth but could drop some in the PDR though HC Lashlee feels they could be improved. CLEMSON TIGERS WR BRYANT WESCO OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 four starters returned (106 car sts) with 10 VHT's. The unit was a strength early, but then were depleted with 4 starters out at times and 3 backups OFY. Clemson had 173 (5.1) rush with 25 sacks. Last year they lost one starter. They had 10 OL that could play but dropped to 124 (3.9) rush, their lowest s/'08, cutting the sacks to 21. This year they lose 4 OL (41/161!) Including #1DC Blake Miller (DET) and the career starts drop to 39 but they return 5 with starting exp and have 8 VHT's in the unit. LT Brayden Jacobs has 1st round DC talent and will be the difference maker and RG Collin Sadler also has NFL potential so I look for improved rush numbers. LOUISVILLE CARDINALS LB ANTONIO WATTS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 the starter threw for 3,195 (63%, 23-6, #2 DC) and sat out the bowl. Last year they added Miller Moss who threw for 2,555 (64%, 18-9) for USC before losing his job. On the team were Brady Allen (PS#11) and rFr Deuce Adams (PS#49). Moss topped 300 in 3 straight games (Pitt, Virg, Mia) and had a 9-4 ratio but had just 184 ypg his next 4 starts with a 2-3 ratio then missed the SMU game. Adams hit 12-17-94 in the loss. Moss returned in the finale and had a 3-0 ratio in the shutout of Kentucky. Moss threw for 2679 (64%, 16-7). Brohm has had 3 transfer QB's in 3 years. This year they add Lincoln Kienholz (PS#55) who was one of the best athletes on a talented Ohio St team and hit 21-36-250-1-0 in two years as a backup. Davin Wydner started 18 games for West Georgia the last two years. Kienholz gives Brohm his first run threat at QB here but must stay healthy. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 they lost their top guy (1128, 6.2, #6 DC) and their #2 RB (810, 6.1, #4 DC). Two true frosh stepped to the front. Isaac Brown (PS#28) became the school's first ever frosh RB to top 1,000 yards and led with 1,173 (7.1). Duke Watson (PS#41) was #2 with 597 and led the FBS in ypc at 8.9! RFr Keyjuan Brown (PS#62) was #3 (243, 5.2). Last year all 3 returned and when healthy were dangerous. Isaac Brown led with 884 (8.8) despite missing 4 games. Keyjuan Brown missed 3 games but had 136 vs Cal and 135 vs Clemson and was #2 (704, 7.3). Braxton Jennings became the first walk on in school history to top 100 with 113 vs Kentucky when the top 4 RB's were out. This year the top three all return and they add Marquis Davis (PS#11, Missouri, 200, 5.9) so this is my #3 rated RB corps. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost their #1 (1013, 16.6) WR but returned Chris Bell (#2, 737, 17.3). They added Dacari Collins (NCSt, 314, 13.1) and 5 others plus got Caullin Lacy for the full year (inj '24). Bell (#3 DC MIA) was the top guy, had 3 straight 100+ games (Pitt, Virg, Mia) and led with 917 (12.7). Lacy was #2 (635, 10.6) and Collins #3 (219, 16.8). This year all 3 depart. They add 1st tm AAC TE Brody Foley (Tulsa, 528, 14.3) and Vanderbilt starting WR Tre Richardson (806, 17.5) plus Florida St WR Lawayne McCoy (PS#51) and 4 other transfers but overall the unit is less experienced. OFFENSIVE LINE -In '24 they lost 4 starters including the Jacobs Blocking Award (Top OL ACC) C. They added 7 transfers and the career starts climbed to 172. Brohm felt they had more depth on the line and that it was the strength of the offense. The Cards rushed for 185 (5.7) with just 15 sacks! Last year they lost 4 OL (34/133). They added 6 OL who were full time starters so had 203 career starts. The numbers dropped to 164 (5.1) rush (RB's banged up) with 25 sacks allowed. This year they lose 4 starters. They add 5 transfers so have 142 career starts so this is a typical Brohm L'ville Oline and are led by C Lance Robinson who was 3rd team ACC. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the rush D slipped to allowing 133 (3.7) and they again had 34 sacks. Last year they lost a #3 DC, two other starters and 5 backups (9 st, 80 tkl, 12 sk, 7 tfl). The top returnees were DT's Jordan Guerad (6 st) and Rene Konga (5 st) and they added 6 transfers including Clev Lubin (9.5 sk CCar). Lubin led with 8.5 sacks and the unit surprised me by allowing just 114 (3.5) with 31 sacks (they did have dominant LB corps). This year they lose 3 starters but Lubin is back and need Brohm to extract the same portal success (5 DL in) that he had last year. Brohm feels they are much stronger on the outside but weaker on the inside. LINEBACKERS - In '24 the Cards held foes to 14 ypg below their average (#62). Last year they returned their #1 tackler in TJ Quinn, #2 Stanquan Clark and #6 Antonio Watts plus had TJ Capers (PS#13) in reserve so were in the best shape in three years and a strength. Clark was OFY week 2. Louisville held foes to 76 ypg below their average (#14). This year they lose TJ Quinn who became just the 5th Cardinal to lead the team in tackles 3 straight years, joining CJ Avery ('19-21'), Tyrus McCloud ('94-'96), Mark Sandler ('88-'90) and Tom Jackson ('70-'72). They also lose their #5 tackler but Benjamin Perry, who started 24 games in '22-'23, returns after 1 year at UCLA. They get back Clark, Watts and TJ Capers (#7 tklr), making this a solid unit in the frontline but not great depth. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '22 UL was #27 in our PDR and #34 (55%, 22-13) in '23. In '24 they lost three starters (#5DC) and dropped to #66. Last year they lost all 4 starters (#3DC). They returned D'Angelo Hutchinson (0 st - #5 tklr) and added six transfers (4 full time st'rs) including 1st tm CUSA Jojo Evans. The Cards PDR took a Stock Market rise to #20 (59%, 15-14). This year they lose 3 starters (#2, #3, #6, #11 tklrs). They return CB Tayon Holloway (13 st, #9 tklr) and add 7 transfers including Koen Entringer (Iowa #3 tklr) so are in the same shape as last year and could be just as strong. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 the Cards were ST RANK L6Y: +4 in TD/blk and finished #6 in my STR. Last year 2025 ..... #5 they lost their K, one P and top two PR. Caullin 2024 ..... #6 Lacy became the first Cardinal to return 2 punts for 2023 ....#61 TDs in a season s/1978 and avg 20.0. Nick Keller 2022 ... #40 hit a school record 57 yd fg and Cooper Ranvier hit 2021.... #50 21-25 fg. Two P's had a net of 36.9 and UL was #5 2020 ....#81 in the STR. This year they lose Lacy, both P's and Ranvier and figure to drop some. They do add Eastern Kentucky's P (40.8 net '24) and Rhode Island's K (14-18 L54) . COACHES - Jeff Brohm returned to his alma mater and led Louisville to the ACC title game in his first year, his 2nd straight P5 conf title game. He was HC at Purdue ('17-'22) and WKU ('14-'16) and enters year 4 here. OC Brian Brohm followed his brother here (Purdue OC '17-'22). The Cards DC stepped away so Co-DC's are Steve Ellis (DB cch) who was DC at MTenn ('11-14) and MarkIvey (LB cch '23-25). ST Coor Karl Maslowski was ST coach Purdue '22 and ST analyst here ('19-'21). PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In 2024 the Cards improved by a TD with 36.5 ppg and 449 ypg! Last year expectations were high but the numbers dropped back to 2023's level with 385 ypg and 29.9 ppg. This year they return their dynamic RB combo in Isaac, and Keyjuan Brown and for the first time here Brohm has a QB that is a run threat as well. They do lose their top 3 WR's but last year's offense was hindered by injuries to the top RBs and their return to health should have this offense improved. DEFENSE - In 2023 my computer had them allowing 22.7 ppg and 321 ypg and they were right there at 21.3 ppg and 317 ypg. In '24 my computer called for them to allow 25.2 ppg and they right there at 24.1 ppg. Last year they had replace 7 starters (#3, #5 DC's) but had my #18 LB corps. My computer called for 351 ypg but they were much better, allowing just 303 ypg and holding foes to 76 ypg below their average (#14). This year they have my #21 LB corps and return their top DL Clev Lubin and remain a solid group. 2026 - In 2023 Jeff Brohm became the first Cardinal HC to open 6-0 since Tom King back in 1925. They were 10-1 but blew a pair of 10 point leads vs Kentucky, lost to FSU in the ACC title game and USC in the bowl to finish 10-4 and #19 AP. In '24 the Cards finally beat their rival Kentucky and won their bowl game 35-34 over Washington for a 9-4 season. Including transfers, Louisville had 16 returning starters in '25 and their new QB Miller Moss (USC transfer) was the one that shredded them in the bowl game in '23. In '24 the Cards 4 losses were by 7, 7, 7 and 3 so they were close to an even stronger year and Brohm was 12-5 in ACC play. The Cards got to 7-1 with a road upset of #5 Miami and were #14 AP! They suffered a 2nd OT loss to Cal, then lost by 1 to Clemson before a depleted team was blown out by SMU in a game they were shorthanded without their QB and top 2 RB. The Cards at 7-4 and still depleted blew out Kentucky 41-0. Louisville then won the bowl game for a 9-4 year but did not earn a ranking in the final poll. This year Louisville avoids Miami and Clemson. They do open with a huge game vs Ole Miss. My 9 sets of power ratings are all over as they call for anywhere from just 3 ACC wins all the way up to 9-0! The key will be keeping the RB's healthy and how Kienholz does at QB. This team is a legitimate threat in the ACC and last year two of their losses were in OT and over the last two years, of their 8 losses, 7 have been by 7 or less. PITTSBURGH PANTHERS RB JA'KYRIAN TURNER and had 142 (4.4) rush with 43 sacks allowed. Two returning starters combined to start just 3 games. Last year they had 3.5 starters back and added 3 transfers so had 78 career starts. Their LG was OFY after 4 starts and LT again missed 5 starts. Pitt had just 117 (3.5) rush and allowed 44 sacks. This year they lose 2 OL (21/41). They add 3 transfers including All-Ivy LT Netinho Olivieri (28 sts Penn) and the unit has 127 starts with 6 OL that have started 11+ FBS games in a year. I once again say they can only remain healthier and should be improved and will cut down on that sack total. DEFENSIVE LINE - Pitt held their opponents under 100 rush ypg each year from '20-'22. They also led the ACC with 54 sacks in '21 (#2 - 48 '22). In '23 Pitt lost 3 starters including a 1st Tm AA (#1DC) and dropped to 150 rush ypg allowed (3.7) with just 31 sacks. In '24 Pitt lost all four starters and their long time DL coach but Narduzzi told me he liked the DL depth better and felt they would generate better pass rush from the interior. With a super LB corps the numbers improved to 113 (3.1) rush with 41 sacks. Last year they lost a DT (13 st, 22 tkl, 5 sk) and 5 backups (4 st, 53 tkl, 4.5 sk, 5 tfl). They added 3 transfers and allowed just 95 (2.7) but the sacks dropped to 31. This year they lose 4 DL (18 st, 91 tkl, 6 sk) but are the most experienced in years and should improve on that sack total. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they lost all three starters (#3, #4, #6 tklr). The "Sharks" took over and this unit was the best on the team. LB Kyle Louis was my 2nd Tm AA (101 tkl, 7 sk, 4 int, 9 qbh). Rasheem Biles was #3 tackler (5.5 sk, 9 pbu) and Braylan Lovelace was #5 (53 tkl, 10.5 tfl). Last year they lost their MLB (13 st, #4 tkrl, 5.5 tfl,UFA KC) but the trio returned. They lost two backup LB's in August and then the unit was hit by injuries mid year yet still held foes 58 ypg below their average. This year they lose Biles (#1 tklr) and Louis (#4 DC MIA, #2 tklr) but add starters from Purdue and Memphis. They could have LB's emerge like they did in '24 and the unit has better depth. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23 Pitt dropped to #89 in my PDR (62%, 16-10) and in '24 lost their top 3 CB's but moved up a little to #49 (59%, 22-13). Last year they lost their top 2 DB's. They added 4 transfers and had better depth but dropped back to #77 (63%, 28-15). This year they lose 4 DB (38 st, 5 int, #4, #6, #7 tklrs). The secondary returns 2 DB with 5+ starts and CB Shawn Lee who was HM ACC as a true frosh plus add in a transfer that was 1st tm MAC in '24 in Raion Strader. They could actually move up in the PDR if the front 7 produces the sacks they normally do. Narduzzi loves the depth at CB but depth at S is one of his biggest concerns. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 I said they could make a big climb up the Special Teams Rankings with their ST RANK L6Y: new STC Bronowski. Pitt did just that finishing at 2025 ....#15 #12! P Caleb Junko improved to a 40.5 net, Last 2024 ....#12 year they lost their super K (21-24 6 50+). True 2023 ... #69 Frosh Trey Butkowski hit 20-23 (L47) and Pitt 2022 ....#41 was a strong #15. This year they lose P ( 40.5 2021.... #62 net!), K, top PR, LS and STC and will drop some. 2020 ..... #3 COACHES - Pat Narduzzi enters his 13th year and led Pitt to their first ever ACC Title in '21. 3rd year OC Kade Bell was OC under his dad Kerwin at Western Carolina ('21-'22). His offense led the SoCon in scoring (37.5 ppg). They lose their 9Y DC and the new DC is Cory Sanders, who has been DB coach here since 2018. New Special Teams Coordinator is Mike Priefer who was an NFL STC for 6 teams including Cleveland ('19-'22) and last year was at North Carolina. POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 Bama transfer Eli Holstein (PS#8) got off to a great start with a 17-5 ratio after 7 games but got injured and Pitt lost the last six. Last year Holstein threw for 1,081 (62%, 12-6) but was benched and true frosh Mason Heintschel (PS#56) started vs BC and led the team to wins in his first 5 starts. He threw for 2,354 (64%, 16-8)with 4 road wins including at Florida St and Georgia Tech. He did have 9 fumbles and 5 of his 8 int's came in the last 5 games. Heintschel returns and is backed by Holden Geriner (PS#28) from Auburn and PS#70 and PS#80 true frosh. Heintschel is talented, a leader and also a film room junkie. He can make all the throws and should be one of the ACC's top QB's. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 they added Desmond Reid who rushed for 897 (6.8) in 8 games under OC Bell at Western Carolina in '23. Reid was the star of the offense with 962 (5.3) rush and was #2 receiver (579, 11.1) despite missing 2 games. Reed was great last year when healthy but missed half the year with injuries. True frosh Ja'Kyrian Turner led with 745 (5.3) and Juelz Goff (PS#67) was #3. This year they lose Reid (#2, 278, 4.6, #4 rec 317, 13.8) and Goff (270, 3.9). VIRGINIA TECH HOKIES DL KEMARI COPELAND POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Last year Kyron Drones (PS#30) stayed healthy and threw for 1,919 (57%, 17-9) in his 3rd year as a starter here. The QB room is brand new this year. Ethan Grunkemeyer (PS#8) has two years in this offensive system and last year was thrown into the ﬁre when Penn St’s starting QB was OFY. His ﬁrst three starts were vs Iowa, Ohio St and Indiana, three of the toughest defenses in the country. They almost upset the eventual national champs then Grunkemeyer won his last 4 starts including a bowl win over Clemson. He threw for 1,339 (69%, 8-4). They add Bryce Baker (PS#11) from North Carolina, rFr Kelden Ryan (PS#65) along with true frosh Troy Huhn (PS#19). Grunkemeyer has a strong arm and makes good decisions and is more mobile than people give him credit for so I look for him to put up improved numbers in ‘26. RUNNING BACKS - Last year Tech lost their #1 RB (1159, 6.3, #4 DC). They added 1st tm MAC Terion Stewart (2359 yd 4Y BG), and DII RB Marcellous Hawkins who had 1,053 (6.7) in ‘23 for Central Missouri. Hawkins had 167 vs Cal and led with 749 (6.3) and QB Drones was #2 (644, 3.8). True Frosh Jeffrey Overton (PS#37) had 146 (5.8). This year they lose Stewart who had 174 vs NCSt and was #3 with 469 (5.7). They add Bill Davis who had 796 (4.9) and 763 (4.8) the last two years at Louisiana and true frosh Messiah Mickens (PS#12) and return Tyler Mason (PS#57). Hawkins is a big back at 226 lbs but did miss spring. This is a solid RB corps with excellent depth and will have improved numbers. RECEIVERS - Last year Tech lost their #1 (506, 18.1), #2, (466, 12.3, #4 DC), #3 (373, 24.9) and #4 (360, 11.3) receivers. They added Donavon Greene (WFor) and Cam Seldon (PS#16, Tenn). Ayden Greene (PS#67) had 268 (14.1) in ‘24 and led with 516 (16.6). This year they lose Donavon Greene (9 st, #2, 274, 17.1) and their #4 receiver (194, 13.9). VT adds Duke’s #2 receiver Que’Sean Brown (846, 13.2), three Penn St VHT’s including TE Luke Reynolds (7 st, 269, 10.0) and LA Tech’s #3 receiver Marlion Jackson. This unit is much more experienced and HC Franklin feels they have a legit 3 deep at every WR spot while TE is their strongest position, returning Benji Gosnell (12 st). TE Reynolds is a Mackey candidate and WR Brown is the fastest on the team so I expect improved production. OFFENSIVE LINE - In ‘24 Tech had 178 (4.7) rush and 34 sacks allowed. Last year they had to replace 4 starters. They added West Virginia’s OL coach and 3 WV OL (1 str) but the career starts dropped to 63. The unit was then hit hard with injuries, starting 4 frosh in a couple of games. The line still produced solid rush numbers with 182 (4.9) and cut the sacks to 29 but the QB was the #2 rusher which helps. This year they lose one starter (5 @LT, 7@RG) but have 6 OL back that started last year (4 starters) plus add 4 P4 transfers (Ohio St, Okla, Mich St, Penn St) and coach Franklin has a solid Oline to work with. They have 12 guys that are legit competing for starting jobs so this is a deep group. DEFENSIVE LINE - In ‘24 the Hokies allowed 147 (3.9) ypg rush with 37 sacks. Last year they lost an AA DE (12 st, 43 tkl, 16 sk!, #6 DC), 1st tm ACC DT (12 st, 31 tkl, 3 sk, #6 DC) and 3 other DL (comb 20 sts). They added 5 transfers (2nd tm MAC, 2nd tm SBelt, 1st tm SoCon, 2nd tm MVFC) and a PS#15 JC. The rush D was similar allowing 153 (4.3) but the sacks dropped to 19. This year they lose 2 starters and 2 backups but add 7 transfers (4-Penn St) including Javion Hilson (PS#6 Mizzou) and should have improved numbers. DT Kemari Copeland (12 st, 48 tkl, 4.5 sk, PS#16JC) has NFL grades and they have six DE’s that can compete and play. LINEBACKERS - In ‘24 Jaden Keller was #1 tackler and Caleb Woodson was #2. Last year they lost their #3 and #5 tacklers. They added three transfers. In ‘24 they held foes 40 ypg below avg (#40). Last year it dropped to holding them to 14 ypg below as injuries did impact the unit with Keller (#3 tklr) and Woodson (#2 tklr) combining for just 11 starts. Those two depart as does their NB (7 st, #7 tklr). The Hokies return Kaleb Spencer (#1 tklr) and Noah Chambers (#6 tklr) plus add in 3 transfers and ﬁgure to stay healthier. Spencer is a difference maker and Noah Chambers is all conf caliber and they have ﬁve legit guys that they can win with. DEFENSIVE BACKS - VT ﬁnished #56 (59%, 13-4) in my PDR in ‘22 and #57 (61%, just 6 int) in ‘23. In ‘24 a veteran secondary improved to #19 (55%, 20-15). Last year they lost all 4 starters. They added 6 transfers (4 full time st’rs) but were much less experienced, ended up playing a lot of frosh and plummeted to #112 in the PDR (67%, 18-4). This year the unit returns intact plus adds in starters from UConn and Troy and will take a Stock Market leap in the PDR! . PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In ‘22 VT fell to 19.3 ppg, their lowest since 1989. In ‘23 they had just 23.6 ppg the ﬁrst 9 games but 43 ppg the last 4 and ﬁnished with 29.5 ppg. In ‘24 with 10 returning starters they had just just 28.2 ppg. Last year they lost 4 OL, their top RB and top 4 receivers and had 25.3 ppg the ﬁrst 8 but just 14 ppg the last 4 and had just 21.4 ppg. This year they bring in QB Grunkemeyer and TE Reynolds from Penn St and look improved in every area. This is a team that could top last year’s numbers by a TD per game. DEFENSE - In ’23 my computer called for 25.6 ppg and they allowed 24 ppg and 317 ypg. In ‘24 my computer called for them to allow 328.2 which they did not match, allowing 363 ypg but they only allowed 22.8 ppg (comp 25.6 ppg). Last year the defense had a bunch of transfers and allowed 378 ypg but this time 30.2 ppg. They have 8 starters back on D and Pry takes over the defense so I expect signiﬁcant improvement. Having Pry accept the DC job was one of the best coaching moves of the offseason by any team. This team should improve by about a TD per game with my computer calling for 24.8 ppg. 2026- In 2022 Brent Pry had just 11 ret starters (3rd fewest ACC), and went just 3-8 his ﬁrst year. In 2023 VT beat Tulane in the bowl for a 7-6 season. In ‘24 VT was #2 on my Exp Chart. VT (down 14 strs) lost the bowl to Minnesota for a very disappointing 6-7 losing year. VT was tied or ahead at 2:00 in 4 losses (Vand, Rut, Mia, Syr). Last year VT lost at home to ODU (trail 28-0 H) and HC Pry was let go after an 0-3 start. This year should be a major rebound. They made a great HC hire bringing in James Franklin from Penn St and he brought in a top 25 recruiting class and top 25 portal class. Normally ﬁrst year HC’s go thru a learning curve with the players but he made a great hire in Brent Pry as the DC so there is full knowledge of the players he is inheriting. POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In ‘23 Haynes King was one of two QB’s to have at least 2,700 pass yards, 600 rush yards, 25 pass td’s and 5 rush td’s (other Jayden Daniels). I said if King cut down on the TO’s he would be one of the top QB’s in the ACC and he threw for 2,114 (73%, 14-2!) and was #2 rusher (587, 4.7) in ‘24. True Frosh Aaron Philo threw for 565 (51%, 1-2) but moved the team when in. Last year King was a Heisman contender and threw for 2,967 (69.8%, 14-6) and was #1 rusher (953, 5.2). Philo started vs G-Webb and threw for 373 in his only pass att’s on the year. King and Philo both depart. They add Alberto Mendoza (PS#87), the brother of the Heisman Trophy winner, who hit 18-24-286-5-1 as a backup for Indiana last year. They add rFr Grady Adamson (PS#45) and true frosh Cole Bergeron (PS#34) with Graham Knowles (6’7” 230) adding depth but are a lot less experienced.
