FLORIDA ST SEMINOLES WR MICAHI DANZY starting combos due to injury and ineffectiveness. Last year they lost 6 OL (43/209). They added four full time starters. They had 29 career starts and averaged 322 lbs and as expected the production increased with 219 (5.2) rush and just 25 sacks allowed. This year all 5 starters depart (58/179) so Norvell has rebuilt the unit a 2nd straight year. They add starters from Auburn (2), BG and Troy and an FCS starter. The unit has 107 career starts and both RG Nate Pabst and LT Xavier Chaplin have NFL potential but this unit will take time to gel. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 FSU allowed 185 (4.6) rush with just 27 sacks. Last year they replaced all four starters. They added four transfers, and a PS#20 true frosh. I said they were not up to '23's standards, but would be improved (did not lose #1 & #2 DC's like '24) with 7 VHT's in the unit. FSU improved to allowing 138 (3.6) with 31 sacks, led by true frosh Mandrell Desir (6.5 sk). This year they lose NT Darrell Jackson (#4 DC NYJ, 12 st, 45 tkl) and 4 other DL (14 st, 53 tkl, 2.5 sk). The Desir twins return as does NT Daniel Lyons so have 4 of the unit's top 5 tacklers back and they are more experienced and deeper. Deamontae Diggs had a sack vs Bama then was injured and missed 9 games. They don't have extreme size but are athletic and can move well. LINEBACKERS - In '24 even in a 2-10 year, and having to replace #3 and #7 DC's, FSU held foes to 19 ypg below their average. Last year they lost their #4 tackler but had 4 VHT's, add 3 transfers including Elijah Herring (#1 tkl'r Tenn '23) and returned #2 tackler Blake Nichelson, #6 Omar Graham and #8 Justin Cryer. This time FSU held foes to 40 ypg below their average (#37). This year they lose Herring (6 st, #7 tklr) and Cryer (8 st, #4 tklr) plus 2nd tm ACC Rover Earl Little (11 st, #1 tklr). Nichelson (#5 tklr) and Graham (#9 tklr) are back and they add 1st tm SBC Chris Jones (13 st, 133 tkl, SMiss) and NCar's Mikai Gbayor (39 tkl). Ashlynd Barker (9 st, #2 tkl'r) moves to Rover. This is a strong unit and Norvell feels they have great depth. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23 FSU moved all the way to #1 in my PDR (48.3%, 12-10)! In '24 they lost 1st tm ACC CB (13 st, #7 tkl'r, 13 pbu, #2DC) and a SS (10 st, #5 tkl'r). Not much went right for FSU and they dropped to #80 in our PDR (63%, 16-4). Last year they lost two starters (#3 DC) and I expected a Stock Market climb in the PDR but they only rose to #52 (62.3%, 20-12). This year they lose two starters again (#6, #10 tklr) but add 3 transfers and should get back near the top of the PDR. SPECIAL TEAMS - FSU was #28 in our STR in '23, and #29 in '24. Last year they lost their K (13-13 FG RANK L6Y: L59!) and P (49.3, 44.4 net!). I said it was the only ST 2025... .#103 unit that looked weaker in 2025 and it had a rough 2024... .#29 year. Everyone recalls the B2B fumbled PR's vs 2023 ... #28 NCSt. This year they lose their P (net 41.1) and 2022 .... #77 K (12-19, 56 TB 61 KO) but add two transfers. 2021.. #104 FSU slipped to #103 and I expect a Stock Market 2020 ... #56 Rise this year. COACHES - Mike Norvell is in his sixth year here with a perfect 13-0 ACC title team in '23. He was 38-15 in 4 years at Memphis (NY6 Bowl '19!). New OC Tim Harris was OC at FIU ('20) co-OC UCF ('21-'22), OC at UC ('24) for Malzahn and pass gm coor here in '25. 2nd year DC Tony White had 2 Top 20 D's with Nebraska ('23-'24) and was DC at Syracuse ('20-'22, top 25 L2Y). Assoc HC Odell Haggins has been on the staff since 1994! New Special Teams Coordinator is Adam Scheier who has been a STC for 20+ years most recently at Rutgers ('20-'21), Temple ('22-'24) and UNLV ('25). POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Last year they added Thomas Castellanos who ran for 1,113 yards with 2,248 pass (57%, 15-14) with Boston College in '23. They added true frosh Kevin Sperry (PS#24, IFS). Castellanos said they would upset Alabama and they did and got off to a great start but was injured vs Kent St and never really 100% after that. He threw for 2,760 (58%, 15-9) and was the #1 rusher (557, 4.1). Sperry is back and they add PS#20 true frosh Jaden O'Neal and PS#63 JUCO Malachi Marshall who was the JC POY. Norvell brought in transfer Ashton Daniels (PS#69) who started 22 games for Stanford and 3 for Auburn. Lafayette transfer Dean DeNobile (2nd Tm Patriot, 2542, 19-7) adds depth. Daniels is a powerful runner with 1,397 career rush yards and has thrown for 4,783 (60%), with a 24-22 ratio but should have a solid year. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 they lost their #1 (905, 5.8 #3DC) RB. True frosh Sam Singleton (PS#12) had 93 (4.4). They added Gavin Sawchuck (PS#2 Okla) and Jaylin Lucas (PS#70 Indy). Last year they lost their starter (#1, 456, 4.2) but had six VHT's and I said could only be more productive (top 3 RB 722, 3.8) in the run first Malzahn offense. Sawchuck led the RB's with 486 (4.5), true frosh Ousmane Kromah had 408 (5.7) and Samuel Singleton had 360 (7.1). This year they lose Sawchuck but add Quintrevion Wisner (PS#22) who had 1,064 (5.7) for Texas in '24 (597 4.6 9 st '25) and Gemari Sands (465, 4.4 FAU). DUKE BLUE DEVILS C MATT CRAYCRAFT OFFENSIVE LINE - In ‘24 Duke only had 37 career FBS starts returning and a new OL Coach and only had 5 OL available during the spring. As you would expect the rush numbers dropped to 92 (3.2) but they did only allow 12 sacks. Last year they had 4 starters and 82 career starts back and I said should be much improved. Duke was a Joe Moore Award semi-ﬁnalist! They improved to 138 (4.3) rush with 28 sacks. This year they lose 3 starters (41/107) including 3rd Tm All-American RT Brian Parker (#6DC). They add two transfers and have 83 career starts. Four of the projected starters are Seniors including their leader C Matt Craycraft so they remain an older group but are down a notch or two. DEFENSIVE LINE - In ‘24 they lost the top 5 DL including 3 starters (#3DC) . Duke did have four DE’s with starting experience. Surprisingly the rebuilt DLine helped the D to 43 sacks and allowed 150 (3.7) rush. Last year they had 3 starters back but allowed 147 (4.3) and had just 26 sacks. This year they lose all 4 starters but maybe like ‘24 they will have increased production despite the inexperience. They don’t have the star power but Diaz feels they have more guys operating as a unit. I list the three deep below. DE Bryce Davis (PS#9) is their most powerful DE and should emerge as a soph and DT Preston Watson can ﬁnish plays in the backﬁeld. LINEBACKERS - In ‘24 they allowed 24.5 ppg. Last year they lost their #1 , #2, and #3 tacklers. With the loss of the top 3 tacklers this unit was less experienced but Nick Morris (‘23 str, inj ‘24) was back, they returned their #5 tackler and added Utah St transfer Jaiden Francois. Morris was OFY after 4 starts and Luke Mergott took his spot and was #2 tackler. This year they lose their #4 and #6 tacklers. WLB Bradley Gompers has great size (6’5” 225) and speed and is really hard to block. Duke allowed foes 46 ypg above their average, are more experienced this year and this is a deep unit. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In ‘23 Duke was #26 (62%, 11-10) in my PDR. Manny Diaz’s teams usually have a strong secondary and they were #31 in the PDR (58%, 19-13) in ‘24. Last year they again lost two starters and a 3rd missed the year with injury. They returned 1st tm ACC Chandler Rivers and added 1st team CUSA Caleb Weaver. This time they dropped to #106 (66.2%, 21-14). This year they lose Weaver (#1 tklr) and Rivers (#5 tklr #5 DC BAL) but have 3 DB back with 6+ starts including #3 tackler DeShawn Stone plus add in 4 experienced transfers. They are much more experienced (1 str back ‘25) and should have a Stock Market rise in the PDR. SPECIAL TEAMS - In ‘23 Duke had their 5th straight top 40 ﬁnish in my Special Teams rankings. In ST RANK L6Y: ‘24 they lost their P (43.5 net!) and KR (23.3). K 2025 .... #11 Todd Pellino hit 15-20 (L53). True Frosh P Cade 2024 ... #62 Reynoldson avg 43.8 (40.3 net). They dropped to 2023 ....#21 ... #23 #62. Last year everyone was back and I called for 2022 2021 ... #36 a Stock Market climb in the STR and they moved 2020 ... #20 up to #11! This year they lose Pellino (14-19 L/49) but will remain in the top 40. COACHES - Manny Diaz was 16-9 vs ACC in three years at Miami. He was Penn St’s DC the previous two years and was also DC at Texas, Miss St and Miami. He just won Duke’s ﬁrst ACC title since 1989 in his 2nd year! Jonathan Brewer is the 3rd year OC. He was Co-OC/QB Cch at S Miss ‘23 and a Quality Control Asst for Diaz 2 years at Miami. Jonathan Patke is the 3rd year DC. He was DC at Texas St and LB Cch/ST Coor at Miami under Diaz. Gabe Infante is the 3rd year ST Coor. POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS -In ‘24 Malik Murphy threw for 2,933 (60%, 26-12) breaking Anthony Dilweg’s 1988 school record of 24 td passes in a season. Henry Belin started the bowl after the top two hit the portal (25-44-236-2-1). Last year they added Darian Mensah who threw for 2,723 (66%, 22-6), leading Tulane to nine wins. Mensah reset the record with 33 td passes and just 6 int’s, throwing for 3,973 yards (67%). Mensah hit the portal late and unexpectedly. Walker Eget has started two years for San Jose St and last year threw for 3051 (59%, 17-9). They also add Ari Patu (PS#35 Stanford ‘21) who started 6 games for North Alabama in ‘25 (517, 50%, 5-4), Blaine Hipa who started 9 for Princeton in ‘24 (1655, 55%, 15-10), rFr Dan Mahan (PS#60) and Terry Walker (PS#33). It will be tough to match Mensah’s production but with Eget they are in better shape than ‘24 and Mahan has a strong arm and took every rep in spring. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they lost their #1 rusher (871, 4.1). Peyton Jones was #2 with 317 (3.9) and Jaquez Moore only played in 3 games (inj, 86, 2.7). Moore and Jones were back and they added Anderson Castle (246, 4.9 App St) and true frosh Nate Sheppard (PS#59). The top 3 RB’s had just 1,274 in ‘24 and despite losing their top guy I said they could top that total. Sheppard took charge early, had 168 vs Syracuse and led with 1,132 (5.7). This year they lose Castle (488, 4.2) and Moore (201, 4.9). They add CJ Campbell (844, 5.1 FAU ‘24) and William Daal (439, 5.5, Yale). Castle’s power running will be missed but the Nate Train should be one of the ACC’s best. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost their #1 (861, 15.7) and #2 (798, 13.3) WR’s plus a TE (5 st, #5, 167, 15.2). The top returnees were Que’Sean Brown (#3, 445, 10.9) and Sahmir Hagans (#4, 413, 8.8) plus they added Cooper Barkate (1084, 17.2 Harvard). I said they were less experienced but could be more explosive. Barkate became the go-to man and led with 1,106 (15.4), Brown was #2 with 846 (13.2) and Hagans #3 (508, 11.8). Barkate hit the portal late so they lose the top 3. Top returnees are TE Jeremiah Hasley (454, 11.4) and Jayden Moore (7-42). They add another Ivy League transfer in Jared Richardson (1033, 12.9, Penn) who was 3x All Conference and Javen Nicholas (740, 12.3 Charlotte) plus Louisville TE Nate Kurisky (6 st, 157, 9.2) so are close to ‘25 experience wise. NORTH CAROLINA TAR HEELS WR JORDAN SHIPP POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 Max Johnson won the job but was injured in the opener. He was the only QB back in '25 and after spring they added South Alabama QB Gio Lopez (PS#90) who threw for 2,559 (66%, 18-5) and rushed for 463 (5.6) in 2024. Lopez won the job and was banged up early and Johnson led a TD drive vs TCU and UCF then started vs Clemson but Lopez took almost all the snaps after that. Lopez threw for 1,747 (64%, 10-5) and had 133 rush. It is a new cast this year with only rFr Au'tori Newkirk (PS#77) returning. They add Billy Edwards (PS#108) who started 11 games for Maryland in '24 (2881, 65%, 15-9, 150 rush) but was OFY with Wisconsin after 2 games in '25 and Miles O'Neal (PS#33) who OC Petrino recruited to Texas A&M in '24. True frosh Travis Burgess (PS#13) and rFr Newkirk are also in the mix. Their starting QB last year wasn't on the roster in spring so they are already in better shape and I look for improved numbers from this unit. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 Omarion Hampton (PS#13) led again with 1,660 (5.9). True frosh Davion "Bullet" Gause (PS#23) was #2 (314, 5.1). Last year they added Benjamin Hall (PS#36 Mich) and true frosh Demon June (PS#110) so they had talent but I said it would be tough to match Hampton's (#1 DC) production. June had 148 vs Richmond and 101 vs Syracuse and led but with just 464 (5.5). He was also #3 receiver (159, 9.4). Hall was #2 (274, 3.9). They lose Gause (#3, 259, 4.2) but add Kaleb Jackson (PS#8, LSU) and true frosh Crew Davis (PS#32). June has the most experience, Jackson and Hall are both over 230 lbs. The depth is improved and I look for signiﬁcantly better production. RECEIVERS - Last year they had to replace their #1 (582, 16.2, 13 st) WR and a TE (#2, 414, 10.4, 12 st) losing 5 of the top 6 receivers, with the top returnee Kobe Paysour (#4, 365, 17.4). Jordan Shipp (PS#32) had just 9 rec's as a true but went to ACC Media Days and led with 671 (11.2). This year they lose Paysour (#2, 437, 12.5) and Javarius Green (#4, 150, 11.5). The Tar Heels add 5 transfers including 3 experienced TE's so are more experienced and could have their best production in 3 years. WR Trech Kekahuna came with QB Edwards from Wisconsin and will be productive in the slot. The TE room is a strength as well. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they had 182 (4.8) rush with 33 sacks. Last year they lost their 2nd tm AA G (12/60) and a LT (12/12) but added six OL that had been full time starters and basically went from 1 to 4+ returning starters. They were stronger with 155 career starts but I said might not match '24's numbers with RB Hampton moving on. Injuries hit the unit had with RT Christo Kelly OFY after 1 start, G Aidan Banﬁeld after 4 starts and only 2 OL started more than 8. Jordan Hall started the last 4 at LT. The numbers dropped to 105 (3.7) rush with 22 sacks allowed. This year they lose 5 OL (48/177). They add 4 transfers including JacQawn "Shaq" McRoy (PS#18) who had one start for Petrino at Arkansas and while the career starts drop to 21 they should have improved rush numbers. This is the second year of the offense, Petrino always has a solid rush attack and they ﬁgure to remain healthier than 2025. DEFENSIVE LINE- In '24 they allowed 149 (3.9) rush with 41 sacks. Last year they lost 7 of the top 8 DL and Belichick said when he took over they had 3 DL on the roster. He added 7 transfers (2 strs) and after a slow start a good sized Dline got better. NC allowed just 126 ypg rush (3.5) and had 31 sacks. The star was FCS transfer Melkart Abou-Jaoude (10.5 sks). This year they lose two starters (21 st, 64 tkl, 3 sk) and 2 backups (2 st, 64 tkl, 7 sk) but add 3 transfers including Richmond transfer Donovan Hoilette (9 sk) and a PS#49 (Penn St). The starting group is experienced and this should be one of the stronger ACC fronts but depth is a concern. LINEBACKERS - In '24 NC allowed teams 26 ypg above their average (#99). Simpson was #2 tackler and Gbayor was #8 and both depart and their #1 tackler House hit the portal. They are a little less experienced but Belichick will mold another strong unit (held foes 26 ypg below '25). DEFENSIVE BACKS - The Tar Heels were #76 in my PDR in '24. Last year they lost 3 starters (#1, 4, 7 tklrs). They added 4 transfers plus NB Kaleb Cost (#5 tklr) so had 3 starters back and moved up in the PDR to #50 (63.6%, 15-6). This year they lose two starters (#3, #9 tklrs). They add one transfer but a solid crop of true frosh which Belichick gets to mold and could move up some more. Greg Smith had a great spring and should ﬁll one of the Safety spots. SPECIAL TEAMS - NC plummeted to #118 in our STR in '23. In '24 they made a Stock Market leap to #19. NC was outscored 120-33 vs Power 4 foes then fumbled into the EZ for Touchbacks vs both Cal and Virginia in close losses. They beat Syracuse and Stanford and were 4-5. NC led Duke 25-24 when Duke got a TD with 2:18 left and with a losing season clinched they were waxed by rival NCSt. Numerous players hit the portal after the season as it is a different type of culture than most schools but what you would expect. They have just 7 starters back from last year but probably have players that ﬁt the system better and the defense was solid last year. They rate a +3 in my SMI and did have two net close losses so were two plays away from a bowl game. They do draw the 2nd toughest schedule in the ACC and facing TCU in Ireland is not easy with teams struggling after their trips overseas. They also draw Notre Dame on the non conf schedule. They had a great schedule last year and did not take advantage of it. I do not have them picked high but Belichick still knows how to coach. Expectations are much lower this year which makes them dangerous. DC Hazelton did a great job last year having them unexpectedly strong, and now has more talent to work with! 2026 - In 2021 WF opened 8-0 for first time in school history (7-0 in 1944), got their highest ever ranking in the AP at #10 (#11 in 1947), and won the Atlantic. WF won the bowl for their 2nd DD win season in school history. In '22 they opened 6-1 with only an OT loss to Clemson, and were #10 AP (first time schl hist top ten 2 straight yrs). From that point thru '24 Wake was just 10-20 and Coach Clawson stepped away after fighting the good fight. Wake has been to 17 bowls in their history and Clawson had a streak of 7 straight bowls (5-2 in those)! New HC Jake Dickert took over with more NIL money than Clawson had and brought in a Top 25 transfer class. He did lose 18 of 22 starters but Wake was the winningest P4 program in North Carolina and the only one with an ACC title in the last 40 years. Clawson left the program in good shape and Wake faced a softer schedule (pg 27). Jake Dickert did a great job and focused on experience and snaps with the transfers they brought in. He became the first ever Wake Forest coach to lead the team to a bowl berth in his first year. His 8 wins also was the best for a first year HC here topping Bill Dooley's 7 wins in 1987. After the bowl win it was just the 4th Wake team to achieve 9 wins in a single season. Wake was under the radar last year and figure to be so once again this year. They rate a -5 in my SMI, benefitted from +4 Net Upsets and had 3 Net close wins, all factors pointing down. The offense is not as strong overall but will have improved QB play and the defense remains top notch. CALIFORNIA GOLDEN BEARS OL BASTIAN SWINNEY POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 eventual Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza threw for 3,004 (69%, 16-6). He transferred to Indiana. They added Devin Brown (PS#7) from Ohio St. True Frosh Jaron-Keawe Sagopolutele (PS#15) beat him out and had a great year, throwing for 3,484 (64%, 18-9) and he opted to return for his soph season! New backups are Jackson Brousseau who had 8 starts for Colo St (1354, 64%, 9-3), EJ Caminong (PS#50), PS#129JC Dominic Ingrassia and true Frosh Nainoa Lopes (PS#78 IFS). JKS did not look like a freshman last year and now has a full year under his belt. He is very accurate, moves in the pocket well, has size and arm strength and picked up the NFL type offensive system well. He will be one of the ACC's top QB's. RUNNING BACKS - Last year the top 5 RB's hit the portal post spring! The top guy did only have 626 (6.3). Wilcox did a solid job bringing in 3 transfers (SMU, NCSt, UTSA) who combined for 1,223 (4.9) yards last year and the top 3 here in '24 had just 1,135 (4.7) from a unit underachieved. Kendrick Raphael led with 943 (4.1) and the #2 had just 117 (3.4). The top 3 depart again. Raphael scored a GW TD in the upset of SMU then left to play for them. They add Adam Mohammed (523, 4.9, Wash PS#147), Ashten Emory (569, 4.8 UTEP), Carter Vargas (445, 5.5 UCDavis) and true Frosh Victor Santino (PS#33 IFS) to leading returnee Anthony League (PS#69, 38, 3.5). Lupoi feels that Mohammed is NFL caliber and has size and speed. This is a decent group and should top last year's RB's (1158, 4.1) despite losing the top guy. RECEIVERS - Last year they had to replace their #1 (623, 11.5) and #2 (623, 11.1) and 9 of the top 10 overall. Trond Grizzell was the only returnee (#3, 401, 14.9). They added 1st tm MW WR Jacob DeJesus from UNLV (Bowl MVP vs Cal) and he led with 1,030 (9.5). Grizzell was #2 with 788 (14.3). 6'4 240 TE Mason Mini was #3 (387, 11.1) and QuaRon Adams was #4 (273, 13.7). This year they lose the top two but add 2nd tm MAC Chase Hendricks (1037, 14.6 Ohio), Ian Strong (762, 14.7 Rutgers) and 1st tm MW TE Dorian Thomas (560, 10.0) so are more experienced. Thomas had 3 td's vs Michigan and NFL Size and Mini is a 240 lb complete package at TE. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 Cal rushed for 122 (3.6) with 50 sacks allowed so it was a problem area. Last year just two starters returned, but they added 5 transfers that were full time starters and two VHT P4 transfers. They had 110 career starts. With 4 games to go they reshufﬂed the Oline with LT Braden Miller, C Bastian Swinney, RG Tyson Rufﬁns and RT Nick Morrow all taking over jobs. They had a paltry 82 (2.8) rush and allowed 32 sacks. This year they lose 4 OL (33/57) but return 4 with 4+ starts last year and add 5 transfers (2 full time strs) and can only improve on last year's numbers. LT Frederick Williams and LG Tyson Rufﬁns are the top guys. DEFENSIVE LINE - Cal had two starters back in '24 (I include JLB as DL), they had four DL with starting experience and they allowed just 110 (3.3) rush with 35 sacks. Last year they lost their JLB (13 st, #6 tklr, 9 sk) and a DT (4 st, #13 tklr). The returnees had just 5 sacks in '24 but two starters returned and they added two experienced transfers and PS#5 & #20 transfers. Cal slipped to allowing 157 (4.7) rush and had just 21 sacks. This year they lose 3 starters (#4, #9, #11 tklr, 8 sk) They add 7 transfers (0 were strs) and return Jayden Wayne (PS#6!) but this unit remains a question mark for me. LINEBACKERS - In '24 Cade Uluave missed 4 late games and was "only" #2 tackler (3.5 tﬂ). Cal held foes 56 ypg below their average (#19). Last year they lost their #1 tackler (#4 DC) and four backups (11 st, 102 tkl). Uluave was back and they had six LB's with starting experience. Ryan McCullogh was OFY after 4 starts and rFr Luke Ferrelli emerged and was #2 tackler. Cal allowed foes 13 ypg above their average. The portal took away their two stars in Uluave (11 st, 100 tkl, 12 tﬂ) and Ferrelli (13 st, 91 tkl) plus their #12 tackler. They return both NB's (#6 & #13 tklr) and add 3 transfers (0 strs) so they are clearly down a few notches and the question mark of the defense. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23 Cal was just #83 (63%, 30-12) in my PDR and '24 played great all year, vaulting up to #6, allowing 17 td's while snagging 17 int's. Last year they lost all 4 starters including their ﬁrst consensus All American since '19 (#3 DC) and a #4 DC S plus two backups. Naturally they dropped in the PDR, but only to #40 (61.7%, 14-8). This year they lose 3 starters again (#3, #6, #8 tklrs) including 2nd team AA Hezekiah Masses (#5 DC LV) and a 2nd tm ACC CB. True frosh Aiden Manutai (PS#121) was #7 tackler and they add 5 transfers so are a little more experienced but it will be tough to match last year's PDR ﬁnish. This is still the strength of their defense and CB Ricky Fletcher (Ole Miss) and S Kingston Lopa (Oregon) are two transfers that are all conference caliber. SPECIAL TEAMS - Cal fell to #127 in our Special Teams Rankings in '23 but rose to #33 in '24. Last year ST RANK L6Y: they lost their K, P (39.7 net) and their top KR 2025 ....#81 (27.6). SYRACUSE ORANGE DB CHRIS PEAL POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 Kyle McCord blew away the school record, throwing for 4,779 (66%, 34-12) and topped Deshaun Watson's ACC record! Last year Rickie Collins (PS#12) from LSU was #1 in spring. They added Steve Angeli (PS#17) who looked good in the playoffs for Notre Dame (58-80-77110-1 2Y) after spring. Angeli was leading the FBS in passing and guided the upset of Clemson and in just 4 games threw for 1,317 (63%, 10-2). He had 6 TDs vs Colgate, tying the great Jim Brown (6 td vs Colgate - 1956). Collins took over but in 7 games threw for 1,042 (54%, 6-10!) and was benched for a true Frosh walk on Joseph Filardi who hit 45% (1-3) with 226 yards pass in 4 games. If Angeli stays healthy he could put up huge numbers like McCord did and this unit would be vastly improved. The backup spot is improved as well with Kenn St starter Amari Odom (2594, 65%, 19-8 347 rush), USC/Boise/ UTEP transfer Malachi Nelson (PS#2!) and Georgetown's Danny Lauter (6'3" 220 Sr) who has started 13 games in 2 years (2484, 61%, 16-11). They have five QB's with starting experience so depth and competition is a strength and Odom is one of the nation's best backup options. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they lost their top RB (1,021, 4.5, #7 DC). True frosh Yasin Willis (PS#38) was a distant #2 with 130 (3.6) in '24. Washington transfer Will Nixon was OFY after 3 games. The top 3 RBs had just 1,227 (4.3) in '24. Willis missed 3 games but led with 558 (4.3). Nixon (OC's son) was #2 with 432 (4.0) and true frosh Tylik Hill (PS#155) had 129 (5.4). The top 2 depart so they add Ahmad Miller (1054, 4.6, Jackson St), rFr Malachi Coleman (PS#69) and Ju'Juan Johnson (PS#49 LSU). They should at least equal last year's top 3 RB production (1119, 4.3) and they feel much better about the depth as it was lacking last year. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost their #1 (1021, 13.1), #2, (941, 11.2) and #3 (934, 12.8, #5 DC) receivers. They added PS#6 Johntay Cook (Tex) and he was #1 with 549 (12.2). Darrell Gill was the #2 with 506 (15.8), TE Dan Villari #3 (412, 10.6) and Justus Ross-Simmons (#4, 312, 10.6) and the top 4 all depart. PS#4 true frosh Calvin Russell was injured in spring and will be out until November. They added Miami, OH's #2 Cole Weaver (642, 14.3) and WKU TE Noah Meyers (357, 11.2). Umari Hatcher returns from injury. He was their #2 in '23 (482, 15.1) and was the Offensive MVP in spring. This unit is little less exp'd than last year but should have a big jump in numbers with stronger QB play. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they only had 98 (3.2) rush with 29 sacks allowed. Last year they had to replace 4 starters. They added 5 transfers, but were less experienced with only 37 career starts. They had 10 starts missed due to injury. The numbers improved some with less passing as they rushed for 123 (3.4) and allowed 37 sacks. This year they lose 3 starters (30/63). They add two transfers and have 42 career starts. C Joe Cruz and LG Oluwafunto Akinshilo (UCLA) are the top OL's. New Oline Coach Juan Castillo has 28 years of NFL experience so I expect an improved unit. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 Cuse switched from a 3-3-5 to a 4-2-5 and suffered injuries and allowed 150 (5.0) rush with just 27 sacks. Last year they lost 2 starters (#7DC) but they added three experienced transfers and returned seven DL that started in '24. They had a need to get bigger up front and they accomplished that. The numbers dropped as they allowed 175 (5.3) rush with just 19 sacks. This year they lose all 4 starters and 4 backups (comb 47 st, 144 tkl, 10 sk). They add 4 transfers including DE Keyshawn Johnson (13.5 sk UT Martin). Maryland's Dillan Fontus (7 st, 27 tkl) is an ideal 3-Tech. With new DC Kehres I expect improved numbers despite this unit being completely rebuilt. He felt they made good progress in the spring. LINEBACKERS - In '24 with a veteran unit the Orange held teams to 12 ypg below their average. Last year they lost their #1 and #7 tacklers. STANFORD CARDINAL OL NIKI PRONGOS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 both QB's returned, plus they added Elijah Brown (PS#7 IFS). Brown was injured early, hit 16-32-153 vs SMU and started vs Wake. Last year the top two saw the writing on the wall and transferred. VHT rFr Brown battled Dylan Rizk (PS#48) who started the last 4 for UCF and Ben Gulbranson who was 7-1 as a starter for Oregon St in 2022. Gulbranson won the job and started slow, peaked vs San Jose with 444 yards passing (3rd highest total schl hist) but threw for 1,813 (57%) and had a 9-10 ratio. Brown took over as starter vs Pitt and threw for 829 (58%, 4-2). Only Rizk and Charlie Mirer (PS#206) returns. They add Davis Warren who started 9 games for Michigan in 2024 (1199 64%, 7-9) and true Frosh Mike Mitchell (PS#31). Warren is off an ACL and missed the spring but they could top last year's numbers (14-12 ratio). RUNNING BACKS - This unit had been under whelming with no RB topping 500 yards since 2020. In '23 the top 3 RB's combined for just 546 (4.7). In '24 the top 3 had 727 (4.8). True Frosh Micah Ford (PS#60) had 122 vs Clemson but was banged up and led the RB's with just 309 (4.1). Chris Davis (PS#44) was #2 with 288 (5.3). Cole Tabb (PS#89) was #3 with 130 (4.8). Sedric Irvin had 69 (3.8). Last year all 4 returned and Ford ﬁnally broke thru that 500 ceiling with 643 (4.4) and Tabb came close with 445 (3.9). Irvin added 118 (2.8). This year they lose Tabb but could improve some more with the top guy back. They have great size with 4 RB's that are over 200 lbs. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost their #1 (831, 13.2, #4 DC) and #2 (525, 10.9) WR's. TE Sam Roush was #3 (334, 8.4) in '24 and was back. They added CJ Williams (PS#9 USC/Wisc) and true Frosh JonAnthony Hall (PS#29) and had 3 VHTs. Williams (#6 DC JAX) led with 749 (12.7), TE Roush (#3 DC CHI) was #2 (545, 11.1) and Bryce Farrell was #3 (455, 15.7). All 3 must be replaced with the top returnee Caden High (414, 11.2). They add David Pantelis who had 901 (14.8) for Yale in '24 (RS '25 ACL) and Nico Brown who had 1,065 (15.3) for Yale in '25 and was 1st Tm All Ivy. TE Benji Blackburn (5 st, 109, 12.1) is the next great Stanford TE. They are in about the same shape as last year. The depth is young but talented. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they had all ﬁve starters back including 9 of the 11 OL who started. The unit had ﬁve VHT starters and I thought should be one of the most improved Olines in the ACC. They shufﬂed the unit early, giving true frosh Kahlil House a starting spot. They improved a little, to 133 (3.6) with 39 sacks. Last year they had 3 starters back, added 3 transfers (UCLA and Sac St strs) but actually dropped to 85 (2.6) rush and allowed 41 sacks as the QB's were less mobile (top 2 QB 764 rush '24, -297 yds LY!). Simione Pale started as a true in '23, then 12 in '24 but was injured in '25 (3 sts) and is back. This year they lose two OL (11/11) and should be much improved. HC Pritchard feels good about the starting 5 and this unit will set the tone for the offense with LT Niki Prongos NFL caliber. DEFENSIVE LINE - DE David Bailey was the top sack man with 6 in '24 and Stanford improved to allowing 134 (4.2) rush with 26 sacks. Last year they lost one starter and Bailey transferred to Texas Tech and became an AA. Stanford improved a little, allowing 119 (3.8) and had 23 sacks. This year they lose 3 DL (32 st, 64 tkl, 4.5 sk) but both starting DE's are back in Earnest Cooper (PS#26) and Tevarua Taﬁti (PS#44) and NT Zach Rowell emerged in the spring as an interior pass rusher. They were solid vs the run last year and should have an improved pass rush in 2026. LINEBACKERS - Last year they lost their #1 and #3 tacklers and their #8 tackler was injured (6 tkl). They returned Matt Rose (#7 tklr). They added two transfers from Idaho and Cal. Stanford allowed foes 5 ypg above their average (#75). This year they lose their #10 tackler (4 st), but return Rose (#1 tklr) and Jahsiah Galvin (#3 tklr) and 5 of the top 6 including Dylan Stephenson (PS#20) so should be a much improved unit. Galvan and Rose are the anchors and Pritchard feels they both have NFL potential and new NB Leroy Bryant had 2 ints in the bowl for Washington. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23 they lost all four starters (#5, #7 DC's). I said their PDR may be in for a nose dive. The Cardinal fell all the way to #131 in the PDR. In '24 they lost their #5 tackler but then S Jay Green and a CB were both OFY and the very banged up secondary was just #122. Last year they basically had four returning starters but surprisingly were just #113 with a 22-3 ratio. This year they lose 3 DB (24 st 99 tkl, 1 int) but should have the rise in the PDR I expected last year. S Green (#4 tkl'r) is all ACC caliber, long, rangy and will hit you. BIG 12 CONFERENCE –– PHIL’S 2026 FORECAST –– 1. Texas Tech - In ‘22 they brought in Joey McGuire and Tech opened 4-5 but won their last 4 games including a bowl win over Ole Miss. Tech has 17 ret st’rs in ‘23 and were pegged 4th in B12 but went 6-6 then won the bowl. In 2024 they opened 5-1 but after a bowl loss were 8-5 and -15 ypg in B12 play. Last year they pushed all the chips to the middle putting a lot of money in and ending up with the top portal class. They were already #2 on my Exp Chart and with transfers had 18 returning starters. That money was well spent as Tech dominated foes weekly and in their 11-1 season (only loss at ASU with QB out) all 11 wins were by 22 points or more! Tech beat BYU 34-7 in the Big 12 title game. Surprisingly in the playoff they were shutout by Oregon 23-0 as they were off a long layoff. The defense held foes to 128 ypg below their average (#2) and Tech was +183 ypg in Big 12 play (#1). This year including transfers they have 16 starters back. Brendan Sorsby is a question as I write this. They do lose 9 NFL draft picks but are my favorite to win B2B Big 12 titles. 2. BYU - In ‘24 they were picked #13 in the B12 by the media but opened 9-0 with some narrow escapes. They were upset by Kansas at home and ASU on the road but won the last 2 with a blowout of Colorado in the bowl for a super 11-2 record (#13 AP). Last year coming out of spring the big question was would QB Retzlaff be available? He transferred to Tulane and it was a true Frosh QB in Bear Bachmeier who did not even enroll until summer who won the job. BYU faced the 2nd easiest schedule in the league and Kalani Sitake did a great job once again. BYU was 8-0 and #8 but lost at Texas Tech. They were 11-1 but lost the Big 12 title game. After a bowl win they were 12-2 and #11 AP. This year they have 14 ret strs including QB Bachmeier and RB Martin and the Cougars could be on a collision course for a Big 12 title rematch. I feel this is Sitakes best team yet. 3. Utah - Utah won the P12 in 2021 and 2022. With the Cam Rising (will he play?) situation they struggled in ‘23 & ‘24. In ‘24 after a 4-0 start they lost 7 in a row with a 5th string QB starting the last two games. Last year the Utes were my #2 Most Improved team in the magazine and did not disappoint. They trailed TTech 13-10 in 4Q and were SOD 3 times vs BYU in a 3 pt loss and just missed the title game. They won their Big 12 games by an avg of 40-22 and were +60 ypg (#3). Whittingham stepped down then took the Michigan job and took some key players with him. This year Utah has just 4 ret strs on both sides of the ball. but do bring back both QB’s and their top RB from the nation’s #2 rush offense. They do have 5 Big 12 road games and rate a -4.5 in my SMI. The rebuilt O-line and D-line are my biggest concerns. 4. Houston - The Cougars were a member of the SWC that was not invited to the Big 12 but finally made it in 2024. New HC Fritz had just 10 ret st’rs. They were picked 15th in the B12 media and did pull upsets of Utah and Kan St to get to a surprising 3-3 before dropping the last 3. Fritz had a much more Exp team with 18 ret st’rs and the defense held foes to 75 ypg below their avg in ‘24 (#13). The Cougars were a much improved team as they opened 7-1 before an upset loss to WVirg and a 3 point loss to TCU but had their 7th 10 win season in school history. They do have 5 B12 road games, rate a -4.5 on my SMI and did benefit from 4 Net Close wins and were just +21 ypg in B12 play. This is year 3 for HC Fritz and he has 19 returning starters including QB Weigman and gets reunited with RB Hughes who had two 1,000+ years at Tulane. The Cougars face the 2nd best schedule in the Big 12. 5. Arizona - In ‘23 they went 10-3 including a bowl win over Oklahoma! The 3 losses were by just 7, 7 and 2. In ‘24 Jedd Fisch left for Washington and new HC Brennan got a late start. The Cats rated a SMI of -7.0. Despite returning the duo of QB Fifita and WR McMillan the Cats which opened 3-1 went just 4-8 and were -104 ypg in B12 play (#14). Last year 16 starters were back and Brennan has a full offseason with the team and they were a much improved team. Arizona opened 4-1 but blew a 10 pt 4Q lead with 5:00 left and lost in OT to BYU and lost on a FG with :00 left to Houston. The Cats won their last 5 and were +81 ypg but a depleted team lost the bowl. This year QB Fifita is back and they have 13 ret strs. Arizona did benefit from +18 in TO’s and face the 3rd toughest schedule in the B12. 6. TCU - In ‘22 Sonny Dykes inherited the most veteran team in the Big 12. TCU walked the tightrope during the year with one close comeback win after another but went 12-0 before losing the Big 12 title game. The Frogs upset Michigan in the playoff but then lost the title game to Georgia 65-7. All indicators were pointing down in ‘23 with 4 Net Close wins, and a SMI of -6.9. This time they had 4 Net close Losses and went just 5-7. They were +56 ypg in Big 12 play and all indicators pointed up in ‘24. TCU was just 3-3 but finished 9-4. Last year they drew the B12’s toughest sked. TCU had an up and down season but after a bowl come from behind win over USC they were 9-4 again! This year TCU has 14 starters back (incl transfers) but they do lose QB Hoover to Indiana. Dykes will have them in contention once again. 7. UCF - UCF was #1 in the AAC in ‘22 at +105 ypg (AAC title game). UCF moved up to the B12 in ‘23 and lost their first 5 B12 games before a solid finsh got them to a bowl in a 6-7 year. Despite the 3-6 record they were +21 ypg in B12 play. In ‘24 UCF opened 3-0 with a big road win at TCU but finished just 4-8. Last year HC Scott Frost returned after guiding UCF to 6-7 and 13-0 seasons and took over a team that was +72 ypg in B12 play (#2!). He brought in a lot of new players and he felt they were very talented just not experienced. UCF took a step back to -10 ypg in B12 play and they were just 2-7. This year 13 starters are back and they hit theh portal hard again. They get 5 B12 home games and are 47-12 at home the last 9 years. 7. Kansas State - In ‘24 KSt was #1 in the Big 12 with +72 ypg and needed a big comeback in the bowl to finish 9-4 again. Last year they had just 9 starters back and a tough road slate plus had to deal with a trip to Ireland which many times have struggled in the after effects. KSt opened just 1-3 but after a bye was back on track and went 3-1 with the only loss by 1 to Baylor. The Cats lost to TTech and had 472 yards rushing at Utah but blew a 47-35 4Q lead. They were 6-6 and bowl eligible but Klieman surprisingly stepped aside and they declined a bowl. New HC Klein has 11 ret strs from a team that was -21 ypg in B12 play. Kan St did have 4 Net Close Losses and rate a +3 on my SMI both signs pointing up. 7. Arizona State - Kenny Dillingham was just 3-9 in year one. In ‘24 all the indicators were pointing up as they were -11 in TO’s in ‘23 and rated a SMI of +2.5. ASU was picked 16th by the media in the B12 but went 10-2, beat Iowa St 45-19 for the B12 title and took Texas to 2OT in the playoff. Last year they lost their heart and soul RB Skattebo. QB Leavitt missed 6 games with injury. ASU was still in the running for the Big 12 title at 8-3 but lost to Arizona 23-7 and then dropped the bowl to Duke. They were +50 ypg in B12 play (#4) but only have 9 starters back. The Sun Devils have to deal with a trip to London but get a bye to recover. 170 7. West Virginia - In ‘23 Neal Brown and WV were motivated by being picked last in the B12 media poll and they went 9-4 including a 30-10 bowl blowout of N.Carolina. In ‘24 they were 6-5 before a blowout loss to Texas Tech and Brown was let go. Rich Rod returned last year and had a ton of transfers with 20+ coming in post spring. I pegged WV last in the Big 12 which got a lot of publicity in WV! They did upset Pitt (big comeback) and Houston but were a banged up team and finished 2-7 and -125 ypg (#14). This year they have a lot of transfers but all were IFS and they add AA RB Cam Cook, Oklahoma transfer QB Hawkins (PS#18). They do face the 2nd toughest schedule in the B12 but have 5 HG’s and rate a +3.5 on my SMI. . 7. Cincinnati - In ‘23 HC Scott Satterfield had just 9 ret strs (-48 All-Conf pts) and a much tougher sked. I picked them last in the B12 and they finished in last at 1-8 (-42 ypg). In ‘24 they opened 5-2 but dropped the last 5 to become one of my rare Most Improved teams to not make a bowl. Last year they had 15 ret strs and were by far the best team Satterfield has had here. After a 3 point loss to Nebraska, Cincy got to 7-1 and #17 AP! They lost the last 5 games including when a depleted team lost the bowl to Navy for a 7-6 finish. This year QB Sorsby went to the portal, and they have just 10 ret strs and were -30 ypg in B12 play. Cincy also draws the toughest schedule in the Big 12 but have a top notch Oline and RB’s. 12. Baylor - In 2021 Baylor rated a +6.3 on my SMI and in Dave Aranda’s 2nd year won the Big 12 title game and beat Ole Miss in the bowl to finish with a school-record 12 wins (#5 in the AP). All signs pointed down in ‘22 Baylor got to 6-3 but lost their last 4 games. In ‘23 Baylor was 3-4 then lost the last 5. In ‘24 they had an SMI of +6.0. After they allowed a Hail Mary TD to Colorado they were just 2-4 but won the last 6 before a bowl loss. Last year 15 starters were back but it was a very disappointing year. They opened 4-2 with 6 and 3 pt losses. They went just 1-5 over the last 6 (rush D allow 5.3 ypg L6) but brought back Aranda for another year. Baylor has 13 ret strs and adds in QB DJ Lagway plus have a solid three headed monster at RB and add in Kan St’s DC. Aranda is at his best when little is expected and they were +25 ypg in B12 play and had -13 TO’s and a Def YPP of 12.0 all signs pointing up. 12. Kansas - Lance Leipold took over this struggling program and in his 3rd year they had 17 ret st’rs and 5 Big 12 home games and got to 7-2 including an upset of Oklahoma and went 9-4 (most wins s/2007) despite QB Daniels only starting 3 games. Kansas is off a pair of 5-7 years despite having Daniels at QB and moving back into their remodeled stadium last year. The Jayhawks were 4-2 and 5-4 but lost the last 3 and were -30 pg in B12 play. This year they have just 5 ret strs on each side of the ball and lose Daniels. They add RB Dylan Edwards from rival KSt but have to deal with a trip to London and have 5 Big 12 road games on top of it! 12. Oklahoma State - In ‘23 OSU had the best schedule and went 7-1 their last eight B12 games before losing to Texas in the B12 title game. They beat a depleted A&M in the bowl to finish 10-4. In ‘24 they had a veteran team including RB Gordon but shockingly went 0-9 in B12 play (-163 ypg). Gundy had not won less than 3 B12 games in 19 years. Last year it was almost a brand new team as they hit the portal hard and had a ton of transfers come in after spring. After a 69-3 loss to Oregon and embarrassing home loss to Tulsa HC Gundy was let go and an interim HC with a ton of transfers went 0-9 in B12 play and -134 ypg! This year new HC Morris brings his QB, top RB and top 3 WR’s from a North Texas team that played in the American title game. OSU crashes the charts making my Going Up box in 6 different categories! This team will bear no resemblance to that 2025 squad and OSU draws the 3rd best schedule in the league. 15. Colorado - In 2022 the Buffs were just 1-11 losing by 30 ppg (-236 ypg in P12 play). All the key indicators were pointing up ( SMI +5.8) in ‘23 and Deion Sanders hit the portal hard and they opened 3-0 and 4-2 but lost the last 6 (4-8). In ‘24 CU went from #133 Exp Chart to #48. A Hail Mary TD vs Baylor spurred a big finish just missing the B12 title game and Travis Hunter won the Heisman. Last year they lost their superstars. Most key indicators were pointing down and the Buffs did take a Stock Market type tumble back to 3-9 and -130 ypg in Big 12 play (#15). This year they have 15 ret strs (incl transfers). Sanders has Julian Lewis (PS#2) at QB, AA WR Scudero, a big veteran O-line and a ton of transfers on D. I like Brennan Marions Go Go offense and DC Livingston worked wonders in ‘24. I am not looking for a ‘24 type of season but they should be much improved. 16. Iowa State - In ‘24 I felt it might be Campbell’s best team yet and they opened 7-0 but had tough losses to TTech and Kansas. At 10-2 they lost the Big12 title game but beat Miami in the bowl for the Cyclones first double digit win season in their 133 year history! Last year QB Becht was one of 13 ret st’rs. Iowa St survived the trip to Ireland and opened the year 5-0 with wins over Kan St, Iowa and Arizona! TEXAS TECH RED RAIDERS RB CAMERON DICKEY his best OLine yet with 7-8 OL that he felt could start. The line (138 car sts) opened holes for 183 (4.6) rush and allowed just 27 sacks. This year they lose two starters (28/101) including 2nd tm B12 G Davion Carter. They add in 3 transfers (none full time strs) and have 87 career starts and could come close to last year's standards. McGuire says this is his deepest OLine. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 Tech allowed 152 (4.5) rush with just 21 sacks. Last year they lost 2 starters. They added five DL including NFL prospect DT Lee Hunter (UCF), pass rusher DE Romello Height (USC/GTech), Stanford DE David Bailey and transfers from NIU and Houston (2 solid DT's). Scouts told McGuire that Tex Tech had top 5 talent on the DLine and they had 10 DL that had started a FBS game. The results were staggering as they allowed just 68 (2.2) ypg rush and had 41 sacks. This year they lose 2nd tm AA Hunter (#2 DC CAR), 1st tm B12 Height (#3 DC SF, 10 sk), 1st tm AA Bailey (#1 DC NYJ) (13 st, 14.5 sk), and 4 other DL (22 st, 31 tkl, 3 sk). They bring in 8 transfers again (see PSL) including 1st & 2nd tm MAC DL and a D2AA but figure to be less dominant. McGuire feels DE Adam Trick, DT Anthony Holmes and DE Trey White will be next year's NFL draft picks in April and the unit is close to '25. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they lost an ILB (7 st, #4 tkl'r) and NB (9 st, 37 tkl) but Jacob Rodriguez (inj '24) was bowl MVP and had 32 tackles in just 5 games so they were more experienced with Ben Roberts (#1 tklr) also back. Rodriguez was #1 tackler (5 sk, 5.5 tfl) and Roberts was #2 (4.5 tfl). All 3 starters were back in '25 and backup LB's Bryce Ramirez was a team captain plus John Curry was #7 tackler so they had solid depth. This elite unit held foes to 124 ypg below their avg (#3). This year they lose the Butkus Award winner Rodriguez (#2 DC MIA, #1 tklr, 11 tfl, 4 int) and Ramirez (22 tkl) but Roberts (#2 tklr) and Curry (#4 tklr) are back plus they add in two transfers including 2nd tm B12 Austin Romaine (Kan St) so they remain strong but will miss their Heisman contending LB. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23 TT jumped up all the way up to #20 in the PDR (60%, 16-13). In '24 they lost three starters and they were just #102 in the PDR (64%, 28-14). Last year they lost two starters but added 3 experienced transfers who were full-time starters and had 6 of the top 8 back and I said they should make a Stock Market type climb in the PDR and they had great length and experience at CB. Tech did indeed make that jump up to #8 (59.2%, 11-17). This year they lose their FS (14 st, #3 tklr) and a CB (7 st, 23 tkl). The unit remains strong with 2.5 starters back but will probably drop some in the PDR. CB Brice Pollock will be a high NFL DC next year. DT KEANU TANUVASA BYU COUGARS OFFENSIVE LINE - BYU ran for just 104 ypg (3.5) in '23 which was #118 FBS. In '24 they returned 88 career starts and rushed for 161 (4.6) allowing just 18 sacks. Last year they lost 3 starters but had three OL back with 6+ starts and added Andrew Gentry (PS#7, Mich). They had 61 career starts and improved to 178 (4.7) rush with just 16 sacks. This year they lose 3 starters again (36/99) but return 4 OL with 49 career starts and add in 3 transfers (17 sts) so are close to 2025 unit. HC Sitake feels really good about the 3-deep and that Bruce Mitchell is one of the best C's in the country. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 BYU cut it to 126 (3.9) rush allowed and had 20 sacks. Last year they had to replace all 4 starters. They added DE Tausili Akana (PS#13 Texas) and DT Keanu Tanuvasa (19 st, 2Y Utah). Tanuvasa is an NFL talent and Sitake felt good about the top 6 at both DE and DT, so they were better than expected and improved to allowing 123 ypg (3.7) with 30 sacks. This year they lose a DE (14 st, #5 tklr) and a DT (9 st, #9 tklr) but are more experienced and even stronger. They are strong in the middle, HC Sitake loves the combination of vets and young players and this is the bulkiest team he's had. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they added 1st tm Big Sky Jack Kelly from Weber St (10.5 sk) and he knew the defense. Sitake felt like this unit was 10 deep and the 3 starters in Kelly, Harrison Taggart and Isaiah Glasker combining for 190 tackles, 27 tfl, 10 sacks, 5 int's and 4 FF's. Siale Esera (PS#34) played in 5 and RS. They were one of the best ever units here. Last year they lost Taggart (12 sts, #2 tklr). Glasker and Kelly were both NFL prospects and BYU held foes to 64 ypg below their average. This year they lose Kelly (#6 DC NYG, #4 tklr) who led with 10 sacks but return Glasker (#3 tklr) and Esera (#6 tklr) and add in 4th tm AA Cade Uluave so are my #7 LB Corps. This was already a solid unit, and the addition of Uluave makes it even stronger this season. DEFENSIVE BACKS - BYU was #117 (67%, 25-8) in my PDR in '22, #46 (61.3%, 23-14) in '23 and had five DB's who had been full time starters back in '24 and I said should make a solid climb. BYU finished #1 in the PDR with a 13-22 ratio! The 22 int's were tied for #1 FBS (Texas). Last year they had to replace 3 starters but remained strong at #11 (57.5%) with 17 int's and just 17 tds allowed. This year they lose a FS (14 st, #2, 4 pbu) but with 3 starters back are my #12 rated secondary. UTAH UTES S JACKSON BENNEE POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '25 they were down to their #5 QB who started the last two weeks. Last year they added Devon Dampier who threw for 2768 and rushed for 1166 yards at New Mexico under OC Beck in '24 with 31 total TD's. True frosh Byrd Ficklin (PS#71) was impressive in the spring. I said it was was a vastly improved unit. Dampier threw for 2490 (64%, 24-5) and was the #2 rusher (835, 5.7). Ficklin looked good as a backup then started vs Colorado and both played after that. Ficklin threw for 301 (60%, 3-0).Their new OC ran a similar offense at Utah St with the QB the #1 rusher. True frosh Michael Johnson (PS#49) and Kane Archer (PS#35) are the depth. With both QB's back this is a dyamic 1-2 punch as both QB's are dangerous and they could both be on ﬁeld at the same time to utilize them. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they had to replace a RB that had Utah's ﬁrst 1,000 yard season since 2019 (1009, 5.1, #5 rec) and their #2 (158, 3.4). They added in Wayshawn Parker (735, 5.4) from Wash St, Naquari Rogers (1208 yd 3 yr NMex). I looked for more production after the top 4 RB's had just 1,293 yards rush in '24 especially with the option added. Parker led with 981 (6.6) with QB's #2 and #3. Rogers had 387 (3.9) and true frosh Daniel Bray showed off his speed with 272 (6.8). This year they lose Rogers but are more experienced and add in Steve Chavez-Soto (446, 5.1 SJSt) and true frosh Lamarcus Bell (PS#28). Parker is the bellcow and Bray can create mismatches off the bench with his speed and quickness. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost their #1 (702, 13.3), #2, (505, 14.4), #3 (294, 14.0) and #5 (113, 11.3) receivers. They added in Ryan Davis who had 747 yards with OC Beck at NMexico. They used more 3 WR sets and I called for more production from this unit. Davis led with 725 (11.7), Dallen Bentley (#7 DC DEN) was #2 (620, 12.9) and JJ Buchanan #3 (427, 16.4) as a true frosh. All 3 depart. The top returnee is Larry Simmons (280, 18.7). They add in 6 transfers including Braden Pegan who had 929 (15.4) with OC McGivin at Utah St, Kyri Shoels (768, 13.0 SJSt) and Tobias Merriweather (PS#17 Cal) and they are a little more experienced than '25. HC Scalley thinks this is the most dangerous receiving corps in the 20 years he's been at Utah! OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the Utes dropped again to 130 (3.9) rush with 25 sacks. Last year the unit returned intact including 2nd Tm AA Fano. New Mexico had less talent and experience up front but had 254 (6.7) rush and just 5 sacks allowed (Dampier escapes sacks) in this offense in '24. They had two potential high DC's at OT and were a legitimate Joe Moore Award candidate. Coach Whittingham told me it was the best O-Line he had ever had in his 20+ years and they lived up to that billing with 266 (6.0) rush and just 14 sacks allowed. This year they lose all 5 starters including Utah's ﬁrst ever consensus offensive AA LT Spencer Fano (#1 DC CLE) so will take a step back. The team is excited about PS#9 true frosh Kelvin Obot who is already eyeing a starting job and is the next in a long line of elite Ute blockers. This is the biggest question mark on offense despite making gains in the spring. DEFENSIVE LINE - This has been Utah's primary recruiting emphasis annually and they have sent 19 DL's to the NFL s/1994. In '24 they lost a 1st Tm AA DE (10 st, #7 tkl'r, #3DC) but had 7 of the top 8 back. The unit was banged up with the starting 4 rarely playing together. Utah allowed 129 (3.8) rush with just 24 sacks. Last year they lost 4 DL (31 sts). They added two P4 transfer backups so were much less experienced and allowed 181 (4.8) rush (worst s/1996!) with 34 sacks. This year both starting DE's and the top 3 DT's all depart. They add in 4 transfers and while the rush D numbers could improve this unit is even less experienced. As the DL goes, so goes the entire defense this season. LINEBACKERS - In '24 Utah held foes to 87 ypg below their average (#6 FBS). Levani Damuni started 7 and was #1 tackler but missed 2024. Lander Barton was #1 tackler and NB Smith Snowden was #4. Last year they lost their #3 tackler but Barton, Snowden, #8 tackler Johnathan Hall were back and they got the return of Damuni so this was my #12 LB corps. They held foes to 15 ypg below their average. This year they lose Barton (12 st, #3 tklr), Damuni (2 st, #6 tklr) and Snowden (13 st, #9 tklr). They return #1 tackler Hall and add in Elijah Reed (12 st Akron 47 tkl) but are less experienced and talented. DEFENSIVE BACKS - Last year Utah continued their streak of having at least one pick-6 by the D for an amazing 22nd straight year. In '23 they moved up to #15 (58%, 17-8) in my PDR and in '24 they lost a CB (11 st, #6 tkl'r), 1st Tm P12 S (10 st, #3 tkl'r, #2DC) and 1st Tm P12 S (#5 tkl'r, 12 st, #4DC). The Utes moved up to #3 PDR (52.4%, 15-12). Last year the returned 2.5 starters and did it again at #2 in the PDR (49.4%, 12-15). This year they lose two starters but remain one of the nation's best (as always). The Utes have top talent and experience at each position, and the healthy return of SS Rabbit Evans will provide a boost to the unit. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In '24 the Utes were down to their 5th string QB for the last two games and had just 299 ypg and 20 ppg in Big 12 play. In '25 they added new OC Beck who did a remarkable job at New Mexico in '24 as they went from 27 to 34 ppg with 254 (6.7) rush in an option offense that also threw for 231 ypg and he brought his QB with him! I said this would be one of the most improved offenses in the country. Utah improved to 483 ypg and 41 ppg! This year both electric QB's are back plus their top RB and what Scalley calls the best WR corps in his 20 years here. The question is the OLine and they ﬁgure to drop off some from last year's record production. DEFENSE - In '21 my computer called for them to improve to allowing 339.4 ypg and 23.6 ppg and they gave up 342 ypg and 22.6 ppg! In '22, it called for 21.1 ppg and 326 ypg and they allowed 21.4 ppg and 334 ypg!! In '23 it called for 21.8 ppg and 317 ypg and they allowed 19.3 ppg and 307 ypg. In '24 it called for them to allow 21.5 ppg and 324 ypg they gave up 20.7 ppg and 330 ypg! Last year my computer called for 318 ypg and 21.6 ppg and they allowed 359 ypg and 18.9 ppg! Check out page 43 to see what my computer has this year. 2026 - Cam Rising led Utah to a pair of Pac-12 titles and Rose Bowls in '21 and '22. The Utes then went thru two "Will he play?" seasons and ﬂoundered at 8-5 then down to a 5th string QB the last two games were 4-8 in 2024! Last year there was no weekly Rising mystery. Utah had 3 net close losses, 3 Net Upsets and rated a +4 on my Stock Market Indicator all signs clearly pointing up. The last time Utah had a losing season was 2013. They made my Most Improved List that time in '14 and went 9-4. Last year off that rare losing season they were my #2 Most Improved team with a much improved offense and my #4 Surprise Team (non top 10 to contend for playoff). They lived up to those expectations and if not for a 3 point loss to BYU could have been in the Big 12 title game playing for a playoff spot. The Utes were 7-2 in Big 12 play but had an average score of 40-22 and were +60 ypg. They ﬁnished the regular season 10-2. HC Whittingham stepped down but said he was entering the transfer portal and took the Michigan job! The last two years Morgan Scalley has been the head coach in waiting and now the job was his. In his ﬁrst game they wiped out Nebraska 44-22 for Utah's ﬁrst 11 win season since 2019 and were #14 AP. They broke the school record (3264 in 1984) for rush yards in a season with 3462. They do rate a -4.5 in my SMI but lose their HC and 4 key transfers to Michigan. The strength of last year's team was the QB, OLine and DLine. While Utah always is solid at the line, last year's units were elite and they are down some in those areas. Despite that big fact, the schedule is very manageable and two of my 9 sets of power ratings call for 12-0. HOUSTON COUGARS LB CHRISTIAN BRATHWAITE 135 (3.8) ypg rush with 33 sacks and was part of the problem for the QB's having a 9-17 ratio (weak protection). Last year they lost 3 starters. UH improved to 178 (4.2) rush with just 19 sacks. This year they return 2 starters but add in 3 quality full time starters from Toledo (1st tm MAC), Tulane (1st tm AAC) and Miami Ohio so they should continue to improve. The OL has much more depth and veteran leadership up front than in recent years. DEFENSIVE LINE- UH allowed just 107 (3.4) rush and the 'Sack Avenue' D had 44 sacks in 2021! They have not been the same since. In '24 they allowed 136 ypg rush (3.9) but with just 20 sacks. Last year they lost 2 starters but added 4 transfers (3 were full time st'rs) and Fritz signed what he called seven Big 12 DL (3 IFS). The numbers were similar with 129 (3.7) rush allowed and 28 sacks. This year they lose NG Carlos Allen (13 st, #1 tklr!, 7 tﬂ) and DE Eddie Walls (13 st, #4 tklr, 7 sk) their top two DL. They add four transfers but need that crop of big DL to emerge. If they do, they have the depth and talent mix to be as good or better than last season in the trenches. Last year my computer called for them to double the ppg to 27.3 and they nearly hit that on the head with 29.1 ppg!! This year they have QB Weigman, their top WR Thomas a top notch O-line and add in two time 1300+ rusher Makhi Hughes who played for Fritz at Tulane so are even stronger and will improve again. DEFENSE -In 2023 my computer called for them to allow 31.2 ppg and 413.5 ypg and they gave up 31.5 ppg and 424 ypg! In '24 depite going just 4-8 the D allowed 325 ypg, just 22.9 ppg and held foes to 76 ypg below their average (#12!). Last year my computer called for them to allow 337 ypg and 23 ppg and they hit those on the head with 348 ypg and 22.8 ppg! This year 6 starters are back and they should be even tougher. 2026 - In 2023 Houston was 4-8 and -113 ypg in Big 12 play. Willie Fritz had some work to do here with just 6 starters back. The schedule was more manageable and they made the Going Up box for Offensive YPP. Houston was -8 in turnovers in '24 all signs pointing up. Houston did indeed improve opening 7-1 after knocking off defending Big 12 champ Ariz St but were upset at home by West Virginia and TCU and ﬁnished 9-3. They beat a depleted LSU team in the bowl for the 7th 10 win season in school history and ﬁnished #22 in the AP poll. They added 17 players from the portal with 8 having been all conf and over 14,000 Division I snaps. This has a similar feel to what Fritz did at Tulane as he is building this team into a Big 12 and perhaps playoff contender. They do rate a -6.5 in my SMI and had 4 Net Close wins which are both signs pointing down. Pointing up is the talent level he is accumulating and if RB Hughes returns to his Tulane form and the O-line and D-Lines are sufﬁciently rebuilt. KANSAS STATE WILDCATS DE TRAVIS BATES POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Avery Johnson (PS#9!) turned heads in fall camp in 2023 as a true freshman and finished with 479 pass yds and 296 (5.7) rush in 8 games (started bowl). Johnson was the starter in '24 but had an up and down soph season, throwing for 298 vs WVU and 253 vs Kansas, but also had 4 int's in two crucial losses vs Houston and Ariz St. He threw for 2,712 yards (58.3%) and set a K-State single-season record with 25 td's (10 int). Johnson ran for 605 (5.4). Blake Barnett (PS#40) was the backup in '25 with a similar skill set and even stronger arm. Johnson threw for 2385 (59.8%, 18-6) and was #2 rusher (477, 4.4). Barnett played in 4 games (40 yds rush, 0 pass). Johnson should have his best season now that Klein is back (was OC in '23). Three of the 4 QBs run faster than 20 mph so the Cats will stretch defenses in all directions this season and there is competition for #2 (see PSL). RUNNING BACKS - Last year they had to replace their #1 rusher (1343, 6.6). Dylan Edwards (PS#14) never had more than 8 carries in a regular season game, but ran for 196 (10.9) in the bowl. Edwards (546, 7.4) was back as was Joe Jackson (227,5.8). Expectations were high for Edwards but he was injured on a PR in the opener. He had 20-166 vs UCF but played in just 4 games and hit the portal. Joe Jackson (PS#86) had 110 vs TCU then had a school record 293 vs Utah and 142 vs Colorado and led with 911 (5.4). Jackson is back and they add Jay Harris (151, 3.6, Ore), Rodney Fields (PS#69 614, 5.0 Okla St), rFr Monterrio Elston (PS#64) and Makari Bodiford (PS#160 Mem). If Jackson stays healthy they should have improved numbers and each of the 3 experienced backs are capable of carrying the load if needed. RECEIVERS - In '24 Soph Jayce Brown finished with over double the amount of yards as the #2 guy. Brown (12 st, 823, 17.5) returned along with TE Garrett Oakley (9 st, 236, 10.7). They added transfer (TT/BC) WR Jerand Bradley (1368, 14.0, 12 td) plus PS#1 true frosh TE Linkon Cure. Brown was the top offensive weapon until he was OFY weekk 10. He still led with 712 (17.4) while Purdue transfer Jaron Tibbs was #2 (595, 12.7) and Oakley #3 (389. 10.2). They lose Brown but Cure should emerge as a threat and they add in 3 transfers including Missouri starter Josh Manning (315, 11.0). The receivers made big strides in the spring but this area will continue to be a focal point in fall camp and they will play a lot of "12" with 3 solid TE's. OFFENSIVE LINE - KSt lost 4 starters and returned just 36 career FBS starts in '24 (RG had 26). The unit had only 2 starts missed and came together well and paved the way for 215 rush ypg (6.1) allowing just 13 sacks. Last year they lost 3 starters. They added transfers from Penn St, Pitt, USC and Ohio St and had 48 career starts back. The line was shuffled early but the same unit started the last 7 together. The 472 rush vs Utah helped them rush for 171 (5.1) with 13 sacks allowed. This year they lose 4 starters and a backup (46/83) including 1st tm B12 C Sam Hecht (#5 DC CAR). George Fitzpatrick (PS#30) missed '25 and returns and they add in 6 transfers but figure to take a step back. While there's uncertainty on the OL, HC Klein is not worried and likes its size and talent up front. DEFENSIVE LINE - KSt's DLine brought 3 of the top 4 back entering '24 with the lone loss being a DE (13 st, 19 tkl, 2 tfl). The exp'd unit allowed just 119 rush ypg (3.6) and collected 35 sacks. Three DL started all 13 games. Last year they lost a 1st Tm Big 12 DE (49 tkl, 8.5 sk!). Tobi Osunsanmi was leading the team in sacks in '25 when OFY week 5. K-St allowed 164 (4.1) rush with 28 sacks. This year they lose seven DL (48 st, 142 tkl, 17.5 sk). Last year's rush D was the weakest since 2020 and they do add the B12 Def Newcomer of Year in Wendell Gregory (4 st, 4 sk, Okla St) and 6 other transfers but this is a completely rebuilt unit. The bigger upside is on the edge as the Wildcats work to remake the interior. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they returned three starters. The defense held teams to 31 ypg under their average. Austin Romaine (5 st '23), led the Wildcats with 96 tackles (5.5 tfl, 2 sk) and was 2nd Tm Big 12. He returned in '25 along with Desmond Purnell (12 st, #7 tklr, 5.5 tfl, 4 sk). The Cats did have to replace their #3 and #8 tacklers. Romaine was the top guy but was OFY week 9. This year they lose Purnell (12 st, #1 tklr), Romaine (#2 tklr) and Star S Qua Moss (10 st, #5 tklr). They bring in Mekhi Mason (12 st, 68 tkl, LTech), Gabe Powers (PS#11, Ohio St, 21 tkl), 3rd tm ACC Star Ja'Son Prevard (12 st, Virginia) and two other transfers and won't fall off much despite losing all 3 starters. While a true bellcow has yet to emerge, HC Klein really likes what he's seen from his LBs this offseason. DEFENSIVE BACKS - K-St was #9 in my PDR (#56%, 16-13) in '23! Despite 3 starters being back K-State was only #46 in my PDR (58.7%, 20-10) in '24. Last year they lost 3 starters including #3 and #5 NFL DC's. The Cats still moved back up to a more customary #22 in the PDR (57%, 14-13). This year they lose S VJ Payne (#7 DC NYJ) (12 st, #3 tklr) and their #7 tackler (6 sts) but have 2+ starters back they should remain near the top 25. This is a very talented secondary, led by a corner tandem that frees up the staff to more things around them and will lead to more cover sacks from the DL. ARIZONA STATE SUN DEVILS RB DEMARIUS ROBINSON POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '23 four QB's threw for 198 ypg, 55.7% with a 7-13 ratio and they used the Wildcat QB often. In '24 they added Sam Leavitt (PS#36) from Mich St and Jeff Sims (PS#16) who had 25 career starts (GT/Neb). Leavitt had a 3-2 ratio after his first 4 starts and Dillingham said "This is the worst he's ever going to be". Leavitt did indeed get better and had a 21-4 ratio his final 9 games leading ASU to a Big 12 title and the playoffs. Leavitt who threw for 2,855 yards (61.7%, 24-6) with 443 rush in '24 was back. He missed Utah then was OFY vs Houston and threw for 1628 (61%, 10-3). Sims did go 3-2 as a starter throwing for 1261 (56%, 10-6). Both depart. They add in Cutter Boley (PS#11) who threw for 2160 (66%, 15-12) with Kentucky in '25, Mikey Keene who threw for 8245 yards in 34 starts for Fresno (and guided 29-0 win over ASU in '24) and true frosh Jake Fette (PS#10, IFS). The numbers were down in '25 so despite Leavitt's transfer there won't be much dropoff. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 they added Raleek Brown (PS#4) who was #4 rusher with USC (227, 5.4) in '22 but he redshirted. Cam Skattebo was the key player vaulting ASU to the playoffs as he set the school record (Eno Benjamin '08) with 1711 (5.8) rush and was #2 receiver (605, 13.4)! Last year they lost Skattebo (#4DC). They added Kanye Udoh who rushed for 1117 (6.2) with Army and brought back Kyson Brown (#3, 351, 4.0) and Raleek Brown. Udoh had 105 vs Miss St but fell out of the rotation. Kyson Brown had 11-73 in the opener but was OFY week 2. Raleek Brown had four 100+ efforts and 255 vs Colorado to lead with 1141 (6.1). Jason Brown (PS#7) had 6 carries in two years but had 13-134 in the bowl. Raleek transferred to Texas. They add two FCS transfers and get Kyson and Jason Brown back. Demarius Robinson (PS#120) started the bowl and they add true frosh Cardae Mack (PS#20) but are down a few notches without Raleek. RECEIVERS - In 2023 the top four put up just 1,524 yards. In '24 Jordyn Tyson became the go to man with 1101 (14.7) more than triple the #2 WR but he was OFY vs Arizona. RB Skattebo was #2. Last year they lost thier #3 (339, 15.4) receiver. Tyson and TE Chamon Metayer (#4, 306, 9.6) returned and they added some transfers. Tyson missed 3 games but led with 711 (11.7). Malik McCain was #2 (441, 14.2) and TE Metayer was #3 (375, 9.9). Those three all depart. They add in Omarion Miller (Colo), Reed Harris (BC) and Raiden Vines-Bright (Wash) and could come near '25's numbers despite the loss of a #1 NFL DC (NOrl) as they have more experienced depth. OFFENSIVE LINE - In 2024 they lost 4 OL (23/79) but added 7 transfers and had 9 OL with starting experience remained healthier and improved to 200 (4.7) rush with 21 sacks allowed. WEST VIRGINIA MOUNTAINEERS DL NATE GABRIEL POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Nicco Marchiol (PS#18) had 3 starts combined in '23 & '24 (434, 66.1%, 5-2 -'24). They added QB Jaylen Henderson (PS#64) who started four games for Texas A&M in '23 and Max Brown (4 st, 561, 46%, 3-6) from Charlotte (orig Florida).True frosh Scotty Fox (PS#31) was IFS. HC Rodriguez's QB's are always dangerous running threats and Rich Rod told me it could be the deepest QB room he has ever had. He neeed the depth. Marchiol was injured and hit the portal after 4 starts. Henderson looked good but was OFY week 5. Khalil Wilkins got a start but then was banged up and the Scotty Fox era begun. Fox became the first true frosh to start here since 1952 (Fred Wyant). He lost his first two starts then guided wins over Houston and Colorado and threw for 1276 (59%, 7-6) and was #4 rusher (201, 2.4). This year they add Michael Hawkins (PS#19) who started 4 games for Oklahoma in '23 and is the mobile QB Rich Rod covets. After 4 QBs started last year this unit will be much more stable and productive with 2 capable players that the offense can be built around. RUNNING BACKS - In '23 Jahiem White led with 842 rush (7.7) and again in '24 White led with 845 (5.7,122 rec yds). Last year they added Jaylan Knighton (PS#18) from SMU joining rFr Diore Hubbard (PS#64). They did lose their #2 RB (734, 4.5). Knighton was ruled ineligble mid-August. White was OFY week 2! Edwards had 141 yards vs Pitt then he was OFY! Hubbard had 108 vs Houston but only played in 8 games and led with 335 (3.5). Cyncir Bowers was #2 (249, 4.0). This year they lose the top two but add in 2nd Tm AA Cam Cook who had 1659 (5.6) with Jax St. They also add Martavious Boswell who had 1109 (9.5) at JC, true frosh PS#22 Amari Latimer and PS#41 SirPaul Cheeks. Also added is a FB in Arizona transfer Kayden Luke. This unit is upgraded talent wise, can only stay healthier and will blow away last year's paltry production. With Cook set to shoulder the load, the team is now focused on beefing up backfield depth. RECEIVERS - Last year they brought back just one of the top five receivers (top 3 - 1615 yd) in Rodney Gallagher (7 st, 288, 11.1). They added four transfers who were full-time starters (2 from Jax St). Cam Vaughn was the top offensive weapon at times and led with just 541 (15.5). Gallagher was #3 (243, 8.7), Jeff Weimer #2 (6 st, 383, 18.2). This year they lose the top 7 receivers. They add in 8 transfers. The top 3 combined for just 1116 yards so this unit should be more productive. Rich Rod likes his options in the passing game and feels this unit will be vastly improved from a year ago. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they returned 113 career starts and paved the way for 194 rush ypg (4.8) allowing 27 sacks. Last year they only brought back Landen Livingston (1 st at C), but did add a VHT (PS#27 Ark) and 3rd Tm AAC (Tulsa) OL. This was a completely rebuilt unit (lost all 5 strs #3DC). They dropped to 161 (3.7) with 31 sacks despite QB's being the #3, 4 and 5 rushers. This year they lose 5 OL (3 strs, 37/82) but return two starters and add in 4 full time starters including two from Jax St (where OL coach is from) and the career starts increase to 120 and Rich Rod will have a much improved Oline. The staff has also added veteran OL coach Rick Trickett which will benefit the entire unit. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they allowed 144 ypg (4.2) with just 20 sacks (7 sk L/7). Last year they had to replace 3 starters. They again allowed 144 (3.6) and while the sacks increased to 28, the top 2 sack men were LB's. This year they lose 7 DL (48 sts, 139 tkl, 9 sks). While all 4 starters depart they add in a 3rd team SBC DE (5 sk), 3rd tm CUSA DE, BGreen starter, and PS#3, 31, 33, and 69 JUCO's. They should at least equal last year's production. The depth in the trenches has improved but the team is going to need the interior guys to take the next step this season. Size up front could be a concern against the more physical opponents on the schedule. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they added Reid Carrico (PS#10) from Ohio St. WVU did allow 413 ypg/32 ppg in Big 12 play in '24. Last year they returned Carrico (3 st, 54 tkl) and Ben Cutter (2 st, 39 tkl), plus they added Chase Wilson (13 st, 98 tkl, 2 int Colo St) and 1st tm CUSA S Fred Perry (12 st, 110 tkl, 10 tfl, Jax St). They did have to replace their #2, #3 and #4 tacklers. Carrico led the tam in sacks (4.5) and was #3 tackler. This year all 3 starters depart again (#1, #3, #4 tklrs). They add in 7 transfers (6 with 39+ tkl in a ssn) so are on par with 2025. This unit may not have a star yet, but it'll be a lot deeper with more experience than last season. DEFENSIVE BACKS - WVU jumped to #66 (60%, 26-11) in my PDR in 2023 but fell to #125 (64%, 26-5) in '24. Last year they lost all 4 starters. They added a 1st Tm MW CB (Nevada). The completely rebuilt unit finished #123 (64.9%, 28-11). This year they lose all 4 starters again. They add 7 transfers including starters from Kent St, Memphis and SFAustin plus a PS#100 LSU transfer and are in same shape as last year but could move up some in the PDR. Rich Rod is excited that his secondary has more length to neutralize the Big 12's bigger threats on the outside. SPECIAL TEAMS - The Mountaineers ST RANK L6Y: finished #60 in my STR in '24.
