CINCINNATI BEARCATS OL EVAN TENGESDAHL OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the line returned intact and had 184 (5.2) rush with just 19 sacks. Last year they lost 4 starters (40/91). They added RG Taran Tyo (11/23 Ball St) and Joe Cotton (2nd Tm MVFC SDak, 14/27) but went from 5 to 3 returning starters and the career starts dropped to 81. They improved a little to 176 (5.7) rush with just 8 sacks allowed and were a semi-finalist for the Joe Moore Award. This year they lose their C and RT (25/83). They return a 1st, 2nd and 3rd tm Big 12 OL and remain one of the Big 12's top O-lines. LG Evan Tengesdahl and LT Joe Cotton both have NFL potential. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 2nd Tm B12 NT Dontay "Godfather" Corleone was questionable prior to the year but returned week 2 (not 100%). Cincy allowed 163 (4.7) rush with just 21 sacks. Last year they lost one starter but Corleone and 6 of the top 8 were back plus they added some transfers. Corleone did miss 2 games but they allowed 179 (4.3) rush with 23 sacks. This year they lose all 3 starters including the Godfather (10 st, 13 tkl). They add in 5 transfers (3 were full time strs, 2 FCS) and last year's numbers were not great. The staff will allow this unit to pin its ears back and attack the backfield which will lead to an increase in havoc and overall production. LINEBACKERS - In '24 Cincy moved to a 3-3-5 look (similar to Iowa St) and they returned Jack Dingle (12 st, #5 tkl'r). Cincy held foes to 26 ypg below their average (#54). Last year they lost thier #1 tackler (7.5 sk) and two backups (26 tkl, 2 sk). They returned Jake Golday (#2 tklr, 7 tfl), Johnathan Thompson (#4 tklr), Jiquan Sanks (#7 tklr) and Jack Dingle (#8 tklr) so they looked even stronger with six LB's that drew starts. The Bearcats allowed teams 41 ypg above their average. This year they lose 1st tm Big 12 Golday (12 st, #1 tklr, 3.5 sk), Dingle (10 st, #5 tklr, 3 sk) and their #8 tackler (7 sts), but do return their #2, #6 , #10 and #12 tacklers with Atwan Peek being a Thorpe Award semifinalist. Golday (#2 DC MIN) was their top defensive player but they add in 4 transfers led by NIU's Filip Maciorowski and have experience. DEFENSIVE BACKS - Cincy had 5 straight top 20 finishes in my PDR from 2018-'22! In '23 they had just one starter back and fell to #69 (56.7%, 20-8). In '24 they were just #69 (61.2%, 16-5). Last year they lost all 4 starters. They added 3 transfers (3 full time st'rs) but had just two interceptions all year and fell to #124 in my PDR (67%, 20-2). This year they lose all 4 starters again and add in 6 transfers but can only improve. HC Satterfield really likes his safety room and is expecting more big plays and takeaways this year. SPECIAL TEAMS -In '24 Cincy added Max Fletcher (Mason's brother) who was 2nd Tm SEC at Arkansas ST RANK L6Y: (46.9 avg, 40.3 net) and he redshirted. Surprisingly 2025 ....#51 they were only #85 in STR. Two K's combined 2024 ... #85 ... #95 for 16-22 FG (L55) but super P Mason Fletcher 2023 2022 ..... #6 avg 42.6 (only 38.0 net). Last year they added 2021 ....#13 Charlotte's K (11-11 '24). Max Fletcher avg 45.4 2020 ... #34 (41.7 net). Cincy moved up in my STR but only to #51. This year, they get back Fletcher and K Stephen Rusnak who was 13-17 on FG's last year and is 28-32 in his career. COACHES - Scott Satterfield was the HC at Louisville ('19-'22) and App St ('13-'18) with a career record of 80-56. New co-OC's are Nic Cardwell (OL cch '23-'25 here) and Pete Thomas (QB Cch '23-'25 here) . New DC's is Nate Woody who has been the Army DC ('20-'25) and was DC at GTech in '18. The ST coord is Luke Paschall. POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 the Bearcats added Brendan Sorsby from Indiana who threw for 1,582 yards (57%, 15-5) with 276 rush in '23 and true frosh Samaj Jones (PS#29, IFS). Sorsby had a fine year here throwing for 2813 (64%, 18-7) and was the #2 rusher (447, 4.3). Brady Lichtenberg hit 3-5-25. Last year Sorsby after their 7-1 start had a 19-1 ratio and was being mentioned in the Heisman race. He had a 4-4 ratio the next 3 games and finished throwing for 2800 yards (61.6%, 27-5) and was #2 rusher (580, 5.8). He hit the portal before the bowl. In the bowl, Jones hit 2-5-19 and had 15-57 rush splitting time with Lichtenberg. They add JC French who threw for 2929 (64%, 20-8) with 315 rush in his 2nd year as a starter for Georgia Southern. Jones has a bigger arm than Sorsby and is a dangerous runner and they add in Penn transfer Liam O'Brien (2376, 67%, 19-6) so will have a capable QB. French may provide more accuracy in the pass game. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 they added Evan Pryor (PS#7, Ohio St) plus returned their 1,000 yard rusher. In '24 their top guy left early for the NFL (1153, 5.7). QB Sorsby was #2 rusher. Pryor upgraded the speed and had 418 (7.5). Last year they added Tawee Walker who had 513 (5.0) with Oklahoma in '23 and led Wisconsin with 864 (4.5) in '24. Sorsby was the #1 rusher after 3 games but Walker led with 709 (5.9). Pryor had 111 vs Iowa St and was #3 (532, 6.9). Manny Covey (PS#75) added 199 (7.1). All 3 depart. The top returnee is Zion Johnson (PS#48, 106, 4.8). The add in Gi'Bran Payne (PS#19, ND), Zylan Perry (1384, 5.1 2Y ULL) and Cole Tabb (445, 3.9, Stanford) and should come close to '25's numbers. This is a very deep room and Satterfield has 4 backs he can trust with carries. RECEIVERS - In '24 TE Joe Royer (PS#29 Ohio St) broke the school record (Travis Kelce!) for TE receptions in a season with 50 (521, 10.4). Last year they lost their #1 (738, 12.5), #3 (449, 9.4) and #4 (349, 12.0) WR's. They added 3 transfers who have been full-time starters and added speed that was lacking. Royer turned down the NFL. BAYLOR BEARS RB DAWSON PENDERGRASS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 Sawyer Robertson threw for 3071 (62.2%, 28-8) and also had 230 (3.7) rush. Last year they added true frosh Edward Griffin (PS#81, IFS). Robertson had a fine senior year throwing for 3681 yards (60%, 31-12) and was invited to the Senior Bowl. Nate Bennett (PS#117) hit 5-7-34. This year they add in DJ Lagway (PS#3) who had a fine Frosh year with Florida but was not 100% last year after an August injury and threw for 2284 (63%) with just a 16-14 ratio and 136 rush yards. Lagway should rebound and opp's will have to defend the whole width of the field this year but it will be tough to match Robertson's stats. A 100% healthy Lagway was a Heisman contender into '25 and he is healthy again. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 rFr Bryson Washington did not have a rush attempt until week 3 but became the first frosh RB here to top 1,000 yards (1028, 5.9). Dawson Pendergrass (338, 4.3 '23) seemed like more of a short yardage back but had 6-142 vs Okla St and 11-104 vs Kansas and was #2 (671, 5.5). They added two VHT true frosh in Michael Turner (PS#18) and Caden Knighten (PS#45) and Aranda called it his best RB corps. Pendergrass (foot inj) was OFY in August so the dynamic combo was broken up. Washington avg 21 carries per game the first 4 then got beat up and avg less than 10 per game the rest of the year and led with just 788 (5.1). Knighten had 104 vs UCF and 100 vs Arizona and was #2 with 469 (4.5). Turner was the leading rusher vs TCU and Cincy and was #3 (320, 4.9). This year they lose Wshington but the other 3 return and they add Ryelan Morris (PS#23) and should top last year's production. RECEIVERS - In '24 Baylor added Ashtyn Hawkins (13 st, 874, 15.9, Tex St) and TE Michael Trigg (PS#6, Ole Miss!). Cameron (#6 DC JAX) led with 872 (12.6), Trigg was #2 (694, 13.9), Hawkins #3 (621, 11.7), Wilson #4 (591, 13.4) and Kobe Prentice #5 (380, 14.6). This year all 5 depart. They add in 4 transfers and have 5 or 6 they can count on in the pass game but take a big step back. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they had 69 career starts. OKLAHOMA STATE COWBOYS OL JAKOBE SANDERS OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the Cowboys returned all 5 starters and 214 career starts. The rushing numbers actually dropped to 112 rush ypg (3.7) but they allowed just 13 sacks on 449 pass attempts. Last year they lost 8 OL (every player who started in '24, 264 car sts). After underachieving in '24 they had similar numbers with 118 (3.5) and 22 sacks allowed. This year they lose 7 OL (54/104) but they add in 9 transfers and the career starts rise to 117. Morris's offense usually put up solid numbers. The coach is conﬁdent in his top 7 or 8 OL and will now focus on determining the best rotation for his attack. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the defense suffered multiple injuries and Okla St went to a 4-man front, but ﬁnished #128 in the FBS allowing 215 rush ypg (5.4) including 234 (5.7) in Big 12 play. Last year they lost 3 starters but I said could only be tougher vs the run. Even in a horrible 1-11 season they were improved allowing 166 (4.3) and 22 sacks. This year they lose 7 DL (30 st, 117 tkl, 9 sk). They return 4 DL (13 st, 64 tkl, 5 sk) and add in 10 transfers (3 from NTexas) so are a little more experienced and could improve again but not like the offensive units. OSU is in better shape on the outside while still needing to develop reliable run-stuffers on the interior. Morris's North Texas D's allowed 5.6, 4.7 and 5.0 ypc rush in his 3 years. LINEBACKERS - In '24 the LB corps was inexperienced and the defense allowed 501 ypg and 36 ppg (#131 FBS allow foes 106 ypg above avg). Last year they lost all 4 starters (#3 and #5 DC's). They added Bryan McCoy (8 st, 120 tkl, 2nd Tm MAC) and 3 other transfers so despite the losses I said could only stay healthier. They improved to allowing 25 above opp average (#88). This year they lose McCoy (#2 tklr) and their #3, #6 and #10 tacklers. They add in 7 transfers with Isaiah Chisom (84 tkl, 10 st UCLA), Ethan Wesloski (9 st, 113 tkl, NTex) and Trip White (PS#129, 33 tkl, Ole Miss) the projected starters so they could improve a little. COLORADO BUFFALOES QB JULIAN LEWIS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Shedeur Sanders threw for 4,134 yards (74%, 37-10). He was the first QB drafted (#5DC Cle) from here since 1997 (Koy Detmer). Last year they added Liberty QB Kaidon Salter who was CUSA Off POY in 2023 and true frosh JuJu Lewis (PS#2, IFS, 17 yrs old). Three different QBs started with Salter starting 9, returnee Ryan Staub started 1 and Lewis two. The three combined for 2434 yards (58.7%, 17-11) with 351 rush and only Lewis returns. They add in Isaac Wilson (PS#17) who had 7 starts for Utah in 2024 and true frosh Kaneal Sweetwyne (PS#60). I look for Lewis to thrive in the Go-Go offense and have much improved numbers. RUNNING BACKS - In '23 their #1 rusher had just 321 (4.2) rush (#4 rec 299, 8.3). In '24 the top guy had 384 (4.5), Dallan Hayden (PS#25) was #2 (196, 3.1) and true frosh Micah Welch (PS#71) had 186 (4.3). Last year Hayden (hand inj) had 2 carries after 5 games but was #3 with 326 (4.7). DeKalon Taylor (909, 6.0, Inc Word '24) had 189 yards but was OFY week 4. Welch was the top rusher with 384 (4.0). QB Salter was #2. This year Hayden departs but they add in Richard Young (PS#2!) from Alabama and two Sac St RB's who topped 500 yard rushing in this offense last year in Damian Henderson and Jaquail Smith. Welch is back and in the new offense the run game will be featured more so the leading rusher will easily top 400 yards for the first time in 4 years. The staff feels the backs have the right mix of toughness and temperament to be an elite room and this is one of the most improved RB rooms in the FBS. RECEIVERS - Last year the top four all left for the NFL including Heisman winner Travis Hunter (13 st, 1258, 13.1, #1DC), their #2 (12 st, 931, 12.6, #6DC), #3 (13 st, 621, 12.9) and #4 (11 st, 441, 11.9, #6 DC). True frosh Drelon Miller (PS#16) was #5 (277, 8.7). They added Joseph Williams (588, 19.6, Tulsa), Sincere Brown (1028, 16.9 Campbell) and 3 others. The numbers dropped dramatically. Omarion Miller led with 808 (18.0), Williams was #2 (489, 13.2) and Dre'Lon Miller #4 (158, 7.9). Only Williams and TE Zach Atkins (#5, 149, 7.5) are back. They add in Danny Scudero was led the FBS with 1297 (14.7), Kam Perry (976, 22.7 Mia O), DeAndre Moore (PS#18, Tex 532, 14.9) and Ernest Campbell (755, 20.4 Sac St). OC Marion thinks this is the best receiving corps he's ever coached, which includes stops at Texas and Pitt. OFFENSIVE LINE - In 2023 they allowed a school record 56 sacks (55 in '79) and opened holes for just 69 ypg rush (2.3!). In '24 four starters departed and Sanders added 11 transfers but none were a full-time starter. They also added PS#1 Jordan Seaton. They had just 65 (2.5) rush with 43 sacks allowed. Last year they had 3 starters back, but RT Phillip Houston (8 sts '24) was OFY gm 1. They added five transfers who had been starters and Sanders was pleased with the improvement as the had 126 (3.5) rush with 38 sacks. This year they lose 4 starters but add in transfers (4 full time starters LY) and the rebuilt line has 100 career FBS starts. This unit is plenty physical and will be focusing on technique and pass sets in the summer. Leon Bell and Bo Hughley look like NFL OT's DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they lost two DL (17 sts). They added 6 transfers and led the Big 12 in sacks (39) and tfl (93) allowing 151 (3.9) rush. Last year they lost a 1st Tm Big 12 DE (11 st, 33 tkl, 7.5 sk) and two other starters. They added in starters from Texas St and Fresno, and a VHT from Bama. They had 12 DL with 12+ tackles in a season. They took a big step back allowing 223 (5.2) rush and had just 13 sacks. This year they lose all 4 starters. The Buffs add in 1st tm AAC Santana Hopper from Tulane, Vili Taufatofua (11 st, San Jose) and 11 other transfers (2 1st tm CAA) and should have improved numbers but not to '24's level. LINEBACKERS - In '24 Liberty transfer Preston Hodge (10 st, 48 tkl, 10 pbu '23) filled the nickel spot and this unit keyed a dynamic front seven. Last year they lost a 1st tm B12 LB (11 st, #2 tklr, 11 tfl) and their #5 tackler. They added 2nd Tm AAC Martavius French (80 tkl, 17 tfl, UTSA) and 1st Tm CUSA Reggie Hughes (12 st, 83 tkl, 4.5 sk, Jax St). The Buffs held foes to 62 ypg below their average in '24 but allowed foes 25 ypg above last year. This year they lose all 3 starters (#3, #4, #5, #6, #10 tklrs). They add in Liona Lefau (PS#37, 22 sts Texas 2Y), 1st tm MAC Gideon Lampron, 2nd tm CUSA Tyler Martinez and 2nd tm CUSA Naeten Mitchell at NB so could be improved. Overall, this is a mature group that processes very well. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '22 the inexperienced secondary was just #129 (67%, 31-6) in our PDR. In '23 they added two PS#1 DB's but only moved up to #103 (65%, 28-10). In '24 Travis Hunter led what I said would be one of the most improved secondaries in the country and they moved up to #18 in the PDR (58%, 16-15). Last year they lost 3 starters including Hunter. They added six transfers but by the end of the year all 4 DB's that started the opener were injured and out. Colorado only dropped to #43 (55.4%, 18-6). This year they lose thier #1, #7, and #8 tacklers. They add in 9 transfers (3 full time starters) and are stronger at S than CB this year . COACHES - Deion Sanders' has put Colorado back on the map nationally and enters year four. He was 27-6 taking over a Jackson St team off five straight losing seasons. New OC is Brennan Marion who was the OC for UNLV '23-'24 with his Go-Go offense and last year was HC at Sac St. The 24th DC is Chris Marve who was the VTech DC ('22-'24). The Special teams coordinator is Michael Pollock who has been an asst on Sander's staffs since 2021. In year two with QB Sanders my computer called for 380 ypg and the Buffs put up 383 ypg and 32.9 ppg! Last year they lost QB Sanders and their four star studded WR's and had a big drop off to 21 ppg and 328 ypg. This year they have a much upgraded WR corps and bring in Brennan Marion to run his Go-Go offense and should improve by over a TD per game. DEFENSE - In '24 under then new DC Robert Livingston they made dramatic strides down to 352 ypg and just 23.1 ppg! The 101.4 ypg drop was the best in school history. They led the Big 12 in sacks with 39. Last year they lost 8 starters including the Heisman Trophy winner. My computer called for them to drop to allowing 28.4 ppg and they allowed 30.5 ppg adn 426 ypg. This year they hit the reset button as the top 19 tacklers are all gone and they have a new DC in Chris Marve. Marve will have his work cut out for him with Makari Vickers the top returnee and he had just 13 tacklers last year. 2026 - In 2022 Colorado was not only 1-11 but -229 ypg! IOWA STATE CYCLONES CB DAVID COFFEY POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In 2023 rFr Rocco Becht had a rocky start, but became the fifth ISU QB to top 3,000 yards (3120, 63%, 23-8) in a season, and set the school record for td passes by a freshman (Brock Purdy 16). Becht threw for 3,505 yards (59.4%) and had a 25-9 ratio in 2024. Connor Moberly (PS#56) hit 5-10-50 in '24. Becht last year played thru a partial labrum tear on his non throwing shoulder (had surgery in Dec). He lost his two star WR's and the numbers dropped to 2584 (60%, 16-9). This year Becht left for Penn St but they add in Jaylen Raynor who threw for 3361 (66.5%, 19-11) with 423 rush (2.7) in his third year as a starter at Ark St. They also add Zane Flores (PS#26) who had 8 starts with Okla St. Last year's Cyclone pass numbers are attainable for Raynor. RUNNING BACKS - In '23 true frosh Abu Sama (PS#64) ran for 276 in the regular season finale and finished #1 with 614 (7.3). The Cyclones lost their #2 and #3 RB's entering '24 but Sama was back along with Carson Hansen (big RB) who complemented Sama well. Hansen led with 752 (5.0, 13 td!) while Sama was #2 (587, 4.7). Last year Hansen had five 100+ games the last 5 weeks and led with 950 (5.1). Sama had 177 vs Colorado and was #2 with 732 (5.2). Dylan Lee (PS#65, 35, 3.2 '14 true) was #3 with 117 (4.7) and Aiden Flora was a dynamic return man and had 58 (14.5). The top 3 all depart. They add Cam Pettaway (365, 5.1 BG) Salahadin Allah (PS#155, 258, 4.7 Ore St '24) and rFr Ryver Peppers (PS#63) and Jayden Jackson (PS#127). Allah tore his achilles in spring. It will be tough to match the production of their dynamic duo. RECEIVERS - Last year Iowa St had to replace the first duo in school history to each tally 1,000 yards (#2 & #3 DC's). The Cyclones had a deep TE room led by Gabe Burkle (8 st, 296, 11.4) and Benjamin Brahmer (2 st, 179, 17.9). They added Chase Sowell (9 st, 678, 19.9 in '24) from East Carolina. Campbell felt they had the top TE room in the country. This time the top two WR's each topped 500 yards in Brett Eskildsen (526, 17.5) and Sowell (500, 15.6) with TE's Brahmer #3 (446, 12.1) and Gabe Burkle #4 (302, 11.6). This year the top 8 receivers all depart! They add in 11 transfers including Raynor's TE from Ark St Tyler Fortenberry. In '24 the top 4 had 2846 (14.0) and last year the top 4 had 1774 (14.1) so the production wont drop much but they are less talented and less experienced. OFFENSIVE LINE - During his career HC Matt Campbell did a great job developing strong OLines. In 2024 Iowa St had 161 rush ypg (4.4) allowing just 16 sacks (3.4%). Last year they lost their C (14/47, UFA LV) and LT (10/26, #4DC IND). The Cyclones had 105 starts return and rushed for 174 (4.4) with 22 sacks allowed. This year they lose all 5 starters (54/139). Naturally this is a completely rebuilt unit with zero OL that have been a full time starter in FBS but 5 who were starters in FCS including an AA. The FBS career starts drop to 15 and they must gel quickly together and Rogers calls it the deepest OLine that he has been a part of so they could surprise. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the run defense allowed 140 (4.2) in the first six games, but over the final eight allowed 225 ypg (6.1)! Last year they lost all 3 starters. They added Tamatoa McDonough (27 tkl, 6.5 sk LY) from Yale. They returned "Big Citrus" NG Domonique Orange (#3 DC MIN) (7 st, 24 tkl, 4.5 tfl) and with a healthier LB corps they improved to allowing 138 (4.4) but did have just 13 sacks. They year they lose all 3 starters again and shirt to a 4 man front. They do add in 5 Wash St transfers including Isaac Terrell who had 7 sacks last year so are almost on par with '25 experience wise but Big Citrus is a big loss. Wash St allowed 125 (3.8) with 31 sacks. LINEBACKERS - ISU returned an experienced LB corps entering '24, but injuries took a toll as they lost Caleb Bacon (60 tkl '23) in the opener and another starter missed the F/9 games and another missed 7 starts. Kooper Ebel was the only LB to start every game (69 tkl, 6 tfl). ISU held teams to 55 ypg under their avg (#26) despite the attrition. Last year they returned the injured players only losing their STAR starter. HC Campbell told me this was his best LB corps in his 10 years here. Iowa St held foes to 8 ypg below their average. This year they lose their #1, #2, #3 and #7 tacklers! They add in Wash St transfer Sullivan Schlimgen (4 st, 49 tkl) and D2 Cliff Harris Award (top def player) winner Tristan Exline but are a lot less experienced. DEFENSIVE BACKS - Iowa St finished #10 (56%, 2116) in my Pass D Rankings in '23, and despite losing a #4DC at CB rose to #5 (52.7%, 18-15) in '24! Last year they had to replace 3 DB's (27 st, #3DC). They had two NFL caliber CB's in Jontez Williams and Jerimiah Cooper and both were OFY week 4! They were down 5 DB's at times but still finished #39 in the PDR. This year they lose 7 DB (40 sts, #4, #5, #6, #8 tklr). They add 10 transfers and should stay heathier but took a hit with Toledo transfer Braden Awls (12 st, 52 tkl, 5 int 1st Tm MAC) OFY. They had a similarly experienced secondary last year at Wash St and was #66 so I expect that type of finish this year. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 Kyle Konrardy (64 yd fg fall practice) hit 21-28 fg's including a GW 54-yd fg at Iowa. P Tyler Perkins, avg 44.4 (38.7 tm net). This unit finished ST RANK L6Y: #79. Last year they lost a 2nd Tm Big 12 PR (15.3). 2025.....#79 Konrardy hit another 54 yd GW FG vs Iowa and 2024.....#79 hit 14-18 FG incl a school record 63 yd FG! Aiden 2023 ....#51 Flora had 26.1 on PR and 21.4 on KR. They had 2022 . #126 just 10 TB on KO's (an OL did some KO's with top 3 2021 ... #85 K injured) and was once again #79. This year they 2020 .. #107 lose P Perkins (40.8 net) but everyone else is back and they could move up with Rogers calling Konrardy the best PK he has had. COACHES - Jimmy Rogers (37) is the new head man. He led Wash St to a bowl in his one year there. In two years as HC at South Dakota St he was 27-3 with one FCS National Title. He was DC there in ‘22 (co-DC ‘19-’21). The new OC is Tyler Roehl who was OC at North Dakota St ('19-'23), RB coach here in '24 and the NFL Lions TE coach in '25. New DC is Jesse Bobbit who was DC at South Dakota St ('23-'24, FCS top D '24) and Wash St in '25 (#15 FBS D!). The 3rd year ST coordinator is Jordan Langs, who spent the previous 8 years as the HC at Indiana Wesleyan. NOTRE DAME FIGHTING IRISH QB CJ CARR POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Notre Dame's previous 3 QB's had all been transfers, who combined for 88 td passes with just 20 int's. Last year they returned Kenny Minchey (PS#18), who hit 3-3 in three games the last 2 years, and CJ Carr (PS#6, elbow inj). They also signed true frosh Blake Herbert (PS#23). CJ Carr not only won the job, he was one of the top QB's in the country, playing beyond expectations. Carr threw for 2,741 (67%, 24-6) and now as a Soph gives the Irish long term stability at this position. Minchey (20-26-196) hit the portal. Herbert will battle a pair of true Frosh in Noah Grubbs (PS#15) and Teddy Jarrard (PS#100) for the backup job. As long as Carr stays healthy, he will be a Heisman contender and now has experience. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 the unit lost their top guy (1341, 6.4, #5DC). Jadarian Price (PS#17) was a year removed from an ACL and the unit had plenty of talent (5 VHT's). Price improved to 746 (6.2) but the star was Jeremiah Love (PS#5), who had 1,125 (6.9) plus 17 td. He had 6.9 ypc in the regular season but take away a 98 yd td run vs Indy and a banged up Love had just 2.8 ypc in the playoffs. True frosh Aneyas Williams (PS#16) finished with 219 (6.4) and Kedren Young (PS#13) had 116 (5.5). Last year I rated them as my #2 rated RB corps but might have sold them short. Love had a ND stadium record 228 vs USC, was a Heisman finalist rushing for 1,372 (7.1) and Price added 674 (6.0) and was a dangerous return man. Those two both left early for the NFL and were both #1 DC's (Love-ARZ, Price-SEA). They still have plenty of talent. They return Williams (224, 9.3!), Young (short ydg RB), who missed '25 with injury and rFr Nolan James (PS#52). They also add two VHT True Frosh Jonaz Walton (PS#11) and Javian Osborne (PS#10). They may not match the Love/Price combo output but this is still my #20 RB Corps. RECEIVERS - In '24 Jaden Greathouse (PS#23) with 6-128 vs Ohio St led with 592 (14.1). Last year they lost their #2 (490, 12.0) & #3 (421, 9.8, #5 DC) WR's. They added transfers Malachi Fields (24 st, 1417, 12.5 2Y Virg) and Will Pauling (23 st, 1244, 10.7 2Y Wisc). HC Marcus Freeman said it was the deepest WR corps he has had. TE Cooper Flanagan (5 st, 55, 138) missed the season with injury while Greathouse was banged up and played in just 4 games (2 st, 73, 18.3). Fields was #2 with 630 (17.5), TE Eli Rairdon was #3 (482, 15.8) and Will Pauling #4 (381, 14.7) and all 3 depart (Fields #3 DC NYG). The unit returns #1 Jordan Faison (640, 13.1) and get back Greathouse and Flanagan. The unit has 11 VHT's including Ohio St PS#8 and #13 transfers and remain a solid unit. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 in noisy College Station for the opener ND lined up 5 OL with a combined 6 career starts but won. C Ashton Craig was OFY week 2, rFr LT Charles Jagusah missed 13 games and G Billy Schrauth missed 3. The unit still performed beyond it's years with 201 (5.7) rush with 15 sacks allowed in regular season (10 in playoffs). Last year they lost 2.5 starters then Jagusah missed the year. They were more experienced (54 car sts) and HC Freeman told me it was his best OLine top to bottom that he has had here. Ashton Craig was OFY after 6 starts and Schrauth after 7 but ND rushed for 203 (5.7) and allowed just 12 sacks (3.7%). This year they lose RT Aamil Wagner (12/28) and Schrauth (7/22, #5 DC TB). They get back Craig and Jagusay, so basically have 4 starters back and return 64 career starts making this my #1 rated OLine! DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the Irish DLine went from one to 3 returning starters. They lost DE Jordan Botelho (12 st '23) early (3 st), then Boubacar Traore 2 games later. ND allowed 138 (3.8) rush (worst s/'19) but had 40 sacks (8.9%). Last year they lost 3 starters. With Botelho and Traore back, they basically returned two starters and also added two P4 transfers. They allowed just 99 (3.0) rush with 30 sacks. This year they lose 6 DL (27 st, 96 tkl, 7 sk). DE Traore (11 st, 37 tkl, 6.5 sk) is back along with DT Jason Onye (9 st, 26 tkl), who was granted a 6th year. They also add 3 transfers from Pitt, Oregon and Alabama (15 comb st LY) and they could be even stronger under new DL coach Charlie Partridge. This is my #5 rated DLine. LINEBACKERS - In '24 ND held foes to 83 ypg below their season average (#8). Last year they lost their 1 tkl'r (#4 DC) and NB (8 st, 37 tkl, 2 tfl). They returned their #3, #5, #6 and #8 tacklers, added in Bama starter DeVonta Smith at NB and had nine LB rated PS#40 or better. ND held foes to 91 ypg below their average (#12). This year they lose Smith (5 st, #14 tklr) but return 5 of their top 6 so this is my #1 LB corps. DEFENSIVE BACKS - Into '24 ND had finished #3, #8, #13, #19, #12, #21 and #30 the prior 7 years in my PDR. In '24 finished #4 (52%, 14-19!). Last year they lost a 1st Tm AA S (16 st, #2 tkl'r, 6 int, 10 pbu, #3 DC), and a #2 DC DB. They added a VT transfer and were more experienced overall finishing #3 (55.6%. 14-21) in our PDR. This year they lose a FS (5 st, #7 tklr) but with 7 of the top 8 back including 1st team AA CB Leonard Moore this is my #1 secondary! Coach Freeman says it is the deepest secondary he has ever fielded. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '22 ND blocked 7 punts, the key to moving up to #7 in our STR. CONNECTICUT HUSKIES DL MATT HOFFMAN OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the OLine lost their 3 interior starters including a #3DC. They added 3 transfers and returned 80 career starts. UConn improved to 199 rush (5.0) allowing just 14 sacks (3.5%)! Last year they lost their RT (13/39, #6 DC), 1st Tm IND LT (13/38, UFA Ariz) and RG (13/20). They returned 3 OL, who started 5+ and added PS#21 (ND) & PS#180 (MD) transfers making them deeper than you would expect with just 38 career starts. They were solid again with 161 rush (5.1) and allowed just 16 sacks (3.5%). This year 4 starters depart and they return just 24 career FBS starts. They add 10 transfers: 3 from P4, 5 from Toledo and 2 FCS starters (18 FCS car st). HC Candle likes the talented depth but they are less experienced. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the DLine had 3 starters back and the rush D, thanks to strong bowl, only allowed 132 (3.8) with 25 sacks. Last year they had to replace all 3 starters. They added 6 transfers but none had been full time starters, so this unit was my biggest concern on the team. While they improved to 37 sacks they allowed 200 (4.8) rush but did face three option teams (comb 958 rush). If you take out those 3 games, they allowed 164 ypg rush (4.3) in their other 10. This year they lose all 3 starters and 5 backups (33 st, 165 tkl, 6.5 sk) but LB's were the sack leaders last year. They add in full time starters from Ohio,Toledo and Colo St and 9 other transfers. HC Candle thinks that the overall unit is one of the best DLine he has ever had. They also go from a 3 to a 4 man front. LINEBACKERS- Last year the unit lost all 4 starters. They added 1st Tm AAC Tyquan King (Temple), Bryum Parham, who had 106 tackles with San Jose St in '23 and returned their #11 tackler. The D slipped to allowing 54 ypg above opp avg. NAVY MIDSHIPMEN DT GRIFFEN WILLIS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In 2023 Newberry was high on two newcomers. Blake Horvath started vs North Texas and they led at half but he was injured. True frosh Braxton Woodson led the win. Later Woodson (can make every throw) hit 9-18-71 and 104 rush vs SMU. In '24 Horvath became the first Navy player to top 1,000 yards rushing since 2019 and tied a school record with 13 TD passes. Woodson played 3Q's vs Tulane in the shutout loss (Horvath inj) then started vs ECU and led five TD drives in the 2H. He has the measurables (runs 22 mph, huge arm). Last year HC Newberry felt good about #3 QB Jackson Gutierrez (PS#197). They were in the best shape since 2019 (Malcolm Perry's magical year). Horvath set the school record with 469 yards (339 pass, 130 rush) vs Air Force and finished as the #1 rusher (1200, 5.4) and threw for 1580 (61%, 12-6). Woodson was used often and started vs ND and led two 4Q TD drives in the upset of USF. He has sprinter's speed and had 414 (8.6) rush and threw for 110. Horvath is gone and while Woodson will have a fine year, they need a #2 QB to develop to be as deep as last year. RUNNING BACKS - In '23 SB Eli Heidenreich led with 382 (20.1) receiving and 214 (7.9) rushing. The FB's led the way with Alex Tecza as the top rusher (758, 6.0). In '24 the FB's were used more like a TB. Tecza led the RB's in rushing with 576 (4.6). Heidenreich was actually the biggest producer with 444 (6.8) rush but was also the leading receiver (671, 17.2). Brandon Chatman had 250 (5.2) rush and 257 (14.3) receiving. All 3 were back in '25. Heidenreich set the school-single game receiving record with 243 vs Air Force (179, Rob Taylor '67 & Dave King '76). Tecza was the top RB rusher (902, 5.7) with Heidenreich #2 (499, 6.5, #7DC Pitt), 941 rec 18.5!) and Chatman #3 (431, 7.6). This year all 3 depart so they are a lot less experienced. I list the 4-deep below. RECEIVERS - In '24 Nathan Kent missed the spring (sprinter on track team) but led the WR's with 222 (22.2). The SB's were again the top receivers. Kent was back in '25 and TE Cody Howard was poised for a breakout year at TE but was injured (4-128). Kent had 4-68. Both depart but the unit could be more productive and the top guy, Luke Hutchison (134, 26.8), is back. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 Navy made the midseason honor roll for the Joe Moore Award. They opened holes for 248 (5.4) with just 11 sacks allowed. Last year they lost 3 starters. The career starts dropped from 51 in '24 to 31. Despite some injuries, this time they improved to 286 ypg (5.8) with just 9 sacks! Malcolm Johnson became the first frosh to start on the OL since 1997 (Duncan Cave). This year they lose their leader in LG Ben Purvis (13/32) but have 4 starters back and 58 career starts, so are an unusually veteran group for a service academy and will be a Joe Moore Award contender. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they lost two starters on the D-line. Landon Robinson made the "Freaks List" then had 4 sacks but they slipped to allowing 156 (4.2) rush with 29 sacks. Last year they lost a DE (12 st, #8 tklr, 6 sk, 4.5 tfl) but five of the top six were back including Robinson (29-yd run fake punt vs Army). Navy cut it to 141 (4.1) and had 27 sacks (they did face 3 option teams). This year they lose the American Conf Defensive POY in Robinson (#7 DC CIN, 13 st, #5 tklr, 6.5 sk) and Julien Moutome (13 st, 41 tkl, 3.5 sk) and are down a notch, but they are still solid as always up front. LINEBACKERS - An ILB has led the team in tackles in 19 of the last 21 years here. Navy held foes to 33 ypg below their average in '23 and 19 ypg below in '24. Last year they lost their #1 and #2 tacklers, but did have six of the top eight back. Newberry felt the replacements were all-conf caliber and the unit had more speed. MarcAnthony Parker finished as the #1 tackler. Job Grant started the first 6 (#10 tklr) then Coleman Cauley took over (#3 tklr). They do lose Striker Jaxson Campbell (13 st, #8 tklr) and Luke Pirris (12 st, #4 tklr) but this is one of the American's top LB corps. DEFENSIVE BACKS - Navy doesn't get to work on pass defense too often in practice vs polished throwers. It should be no surprise they've finished #100 or worse in my PDR in 19 of the last 23 years. In '24 I said they could finally get to DD's in PDR with all four starters back. Navy did just that, finishing #53 (59%, 19-17), their best finish since 1995 (#45). Last year they lost 3 starters (#6 DC). The less experienced unit dropped to #120 (66%, 21-7). Ten different DB's started and 8 of them are back! They lose their #12 and #17 tacklers. CB Ira Oniha has NFL potential and Newberry says they are as deep at CB as they have been since he has been here. This year it could be another DD finish in the PDR. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 they lost their all-time avg punt leader at Navy (44.4). Nathan Kirkwood hit 5-9 FG (L46). The return game was average and Navy finished ST RANK L6Y: #109 in my Special Teams Rankings. Last year 2025 ... #26 they returnede their LS, K, top PR and KR. New 2024 . #109 ....#74 P Jacob Carlson avg 44.5 (39.5 net!). Navy rose 2023 2022 ....#108 all the way to #26 as they had better depth. This 2021 ......#91 year they lose K Kirkwood (10-11 L48) and it will 2020 ...#115 be tough to stay at that level. COACHES - 4th year HC Brian Newberry was the DC here from '19-'22 and was the DC at FCS Kennesaw St from '15-'18. 3rd-year OC Drew Cronic was Mercer's HC for 4 years (28-17) guiding them to their first FCS playoff berth in '23. In addition to his HC duties, Newberry will also excitedly return to his DC roots as he will additionally serve as his own DC this year. Mick Yokitis is in his 15th year as the WR's coach at Navy, while also serving as Special Teams Coordinator. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In 2024 new OC Drew Cronic brought in the Millennial Wing-T, which incorporates triple-option, run pass option and pro style elements. They had an advantage early on by teams not knowing what to expect and had 7 starters back. The offense increased the ppg by almost 2 TD's to 31.3 ppg and 371 ypg. They were also #1 in the country in Red Zone TD % (81%). Last year 8 starters returned including QB Horvath. Teams did have a year's worth of film on the offense. My computer called for 30.9 ppg and they had 31.5 (miss by .6!). This year Horvath, Tecza and Heidenreich depart but Woodson has a top-notch O-line and they will remain potent. TULANE GREEN WAVE RB JAMAURI McCLURE POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Last year their starter (2723, 66%, 22-6) transferred to Duke. They added Kadin Semonza, who threw for 2,904 (64%, 25-10) in 11 starts with Ball St. Then after spring, they added transfer Brendan Sullivan who had 11 starts in 3 years. They then also added BYU transfer Jake Retzlaff, who won the job and had a solid year, leading Tulane to the playoffs. Retzlaff threw for 3,168 (62%, 15-7) and was the leading rusher (634, 4.9). Sullivan hit 19-30-222-2-2. Both depart so they added Zeon Chriss-Gremillion who had 13 starts for Louisiana in '23-'24 and was a backup at Houston in '25. The last 2 years I said they would have a tough time matching the previous QB's stats, but they did each time. I will say it again. RUNNING BACKS - In '23 they lost the AAC Offensive POY (1581, #5 in NCAA, 6.9, 19 td). RFr Makhi Hughes led with 1,378 (5.3). He had 1,401 (5.3) in '24 while Arnold Barnes had 402 (4.6). Hughes transferred and they added Louisville transfer Maurice Turner (734 rush, 4.8 in 3Y). Jamauri McClure (PS#130) had 121 (6.1) while RS in '24 and I said might be the most talented RB. Sumrall liked the depth and planned to use all 5 RB. Turner had 14-86 in the opener but was injured. True frosh Javin Gordan (PS#122) had 516 (4.0). McClure had just 8 carries the first 8 games but avg 98 ypg the last 5 and led the RB's (a QB was the #1 rusher) with 540 (6.5). This year they lose Gordon and Barnes (217, 4.3) but add three P4 transfers and McClure could be a 1,000-yard guy. Tulane will use a two-back offense as this unit has their top playmakers. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost their #1 (1031, 17.2), #2 (598, 19.3) and #3 (470, 13.4) WR's, plus their TE (13 st, 212). Shazz Preston (PS#8, Alabama) played in the last 6 games (hamstring, 99, 24.8). They added 5 transfers and while they were in the same shape as '24 (lost top 3), I said I did not see a 1,000-yard WR emerging. Preston led with 723 (16.8). Anthony Brown-Stephens (PS#98, Kentucky) was #2 (523, 12.8), FAU transfer Omari Hayes was #3 (515, 13.2), Bryce Bohanon #4 (417, 13.5, was #1 when OFY wk 10) and rFr Zycarl Lewis #5 (330, 13.8). This year they return their #2 and #5 WR's and add 5 transfers. Last year they returned 16 rec's from '24 and this year they return 77 from '25. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they lost two 1st Tm AAC OL but had 6 OL who started 8+ games in a year (143 car sts). I said they could improve the numbers and they did to 196 (4.8) rush with 18 sacks allowed. Last year they lost 3 starters plus their 6th OL (1/16). They added App St C Jack Hollifield and three others but dropped to 93 career starts. They had solid numbers with 166 (4.5) rush and just 12 sacks (2.5%) allowed with a QB being the #1 rusher. This year they lose 4 starters (52/114) and the career starts drop even more to 41, but Coach Hall still feels the unit is one of the offense's strengths. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they allowed 146 (4.5) rush (did face Army & Navy) but still had 35 sacks. Last year they lost a 1st Tm AAC DT, 2nd Tm AAC DT and 6 other DL (22 sts, 106 tkl, 7 sk). They added 5 transfer starters (App St, UAB, UTEP, S Ala, Liberty) and 3 other transfers. Then-HC Sumrall felt they had 5 all-conf type DL so it looked like a strong unit. Tulane cut it to 123 (3.6) rush with 36 sacks. This year they lose their top 5 DL (52 sts, 22.5 sk, 159 tkl)! They add 4 transfers but were hit hard by the portal (4 DL transferred to P4 teams) and only add one starter. DE Gerrod Henderson is the best pass rusher. LINEBACKERS - In '22 their #1 tackler (2nd Tm AAC) was OFY and they lost their NB (#5 tklr, 12 pbu) and #4 tackler. They held foes to 61 ypg below their average (#21). Last year they lost their #1 tackler again. Walk-on Sam Howard, who was a revelation in '24 (#2 tklr, 5.5 tfl) returned with #7 tackler Dickson Agu. Sumrall said he would take this unit over a lot of P4 units. Agu was the #1 tackler but was OFY after just 5 games and Howard missed 3 games and was not 100% when he returned. Chris Rodgers started the last 8 and was the unit's #1 tackler. Tulane held foes to 31 ypg below their average. This year they lose Howard (#5 tklr) and NB Javion White (#6 tklr) but remain strong with Agu's return and Rodgers has NFL potential. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23 Tulane was #49 in the PDR (65%, 18-17) and moved up to #33 (58%, 13-14) in '24, their best finish since 2002 (#11). Last year they lost 4 starters including #3 and #7 DC's! They added four transfers but naturally, they took a step back and were #98 (67.6%, 23-15). They allowed UTSA and Memphis 64 comp on 80 att's in B2B games and facing Ole Miss twice did not help. This year they lose S Bailey Despanie (14 st, #3 tklr) and their top cover CB but with 2 starters back, plus adding 5 transfers (3 were full time starters), they could take a Stock Market rise in the PDR. This is a deep unit. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '23, Tulane was #9 in the STR! In '24 they lost their K and top PR (12.2) and were #31. Last year they lost their K and P (39.8 net) and top KR ST RANK L6Y: (34.5, 2 td!). They added Marshall P Alec Clark 2025...... #8 who avg 46.5 (41.3 net). Tulane had not made a 2024 ..... #31 FG of 50+ for 11 years but Patrick Duncan hit a 2023..... #9 super 25-28 (4-6 50+) on FGs and had 69 TB on 2022.... #52 #103 80 KO's. Tulane moved back up to #8! This year 2021.. 2020.... #49 both their P and K depart. They do bring in Jackson Courville (11-13 fg, L53, Ball St '24) but will drop in the STR. COACHES - New HC Will Hall was Tulane's OC in '19-'20 and Tulane avg 33.1 and 34.7 ppg, respectively. Hall was the HC at SMiss 2021-24 going 14-30, but from '11-'16 was HC of West Alabama ('11-'13) and West Georgia ('14-'16) with a combined 56-20 record making the DII playoffs four times. The OC is Russ Callaway who was OC at Florida in '25. The DC is Tayler Polk who was DC at Cent Ark ('21), co-DC at Troy ('22'23) and co-DC here ('24-'25). TL 71/11 fg 24-0, 27-0. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In 2024, Tulane rebounded to 405 ypg and 35.1 ppg. Tulane had a 1,000-yard rusher and receiver in the same season for the second time ever (2009). Last year they lost their QB, a 1,401-yard RB and their top 5 receivers. They got a late addition in BYU QB Jake Retzlaff. My computer called for 401 ypg and 32 ppg and they had 411 ypg and 27.7 ppg. This year they return their top RB and more experience at WR but lose 4 OL starters as well as QB Retzlaff. New QB Zeon Chriss-Gremillion is an electric runner (22 mph) and has 13 career starts. HC Halls likes the O-line and the RB's are solid so they will not fall off much. DEFENSE - Tulane and Troy ran identical defenses so there was not a scheme change under Sumrall and they returned 7 starters in '24. My computer called for them to allow 24 ppg and they were slightly better at 20.6 ppg. Last year they had just 3 returning starters, but with the transfers added they had 8 overall, and my computer called for them to allow 24 ppg and they gave up 23.9 ppg! This year they return a solid back 7 but need the reworked D-line to be solid to match last year's numbers. 2026- Tulane had never won consecutive bowls or even tallied back-to-back winning seasons in the 20 years prior to Willie Fritz. After 3 straight bowls, Tulane went 2-10 in '21. In '22, Tulane made my Most Improved list but still surpassed everyone's expectations. Tulane got their first shutout in 25 years and beat their first P5 team (Kansas St) since 2010. Tulane opened 3-0 for just the second time s/1974. The Green Wave also received their first Top-25 ranking in 24 years. Tulane eventually beat UCF for the league title (first s/1998)! Tulane's last major bowl game was under Red Dawson 85 years ago in the 1939 Sugar Bowl. They played USC in the Cotton Bowl and had a miracle comeback (trailed 45-30 with just 4:30 left) to record the largest turnaround (from 2-10 to 12-2, ranked #9) in FBS history. In '23 they were ranked in the preseason for the first time ever and went 11-1 but lost in the AAC title game and then Coach Fritz left for Houston and they lost the bowl. In Jon Sumrall's first year they had the best YPG in the AAC at +158 and were 9-2, but ended up closing the season with three consecutive losses. Last year they lost most of their skill players. Tulane lost to Ole Miss by 35 and UTSA by 22 but beat North Texas 34-21 in the American title game and made the playoff! Sumrall stuck around for the 41-10 loss to Ole Miss in the playoff. This year just 8 starters are back with only 49 players back from last year's team. HC Hall did a solid job rebuilding the roster as Tulane has one of the better NIL's of the American and they remain a contender again this year. The Green Wave did benefit from 5 Net close Wins. EAST CAROLINA PIRATES WR BROCK SPALDING POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 Mich St transfer Katin Houser (PS#15) took over and started the last 7 throwing for 2,006 hitting 60.8% but with a 18-11 ratio. Last year they added in Mike Wright (PS#60), who started 16 games with Vandy, Miss St and N'western. As you would expect, Houser was improved and threw for 3,300 (66%, 19-6) and had 193 rush. Wright had 732 yards rush. Both depart (Houser to Illinois). They added Mitch Grifﬁs who had 9 starts for Wake Forest in '23 throwing for 1553 (9-7) and was at Texas Tech last year. They also bring in Emory Williams (PS#41), who started 2 games in 3 years for Miami (FL) throwing for 813 (63%, 4-2). Williams has all the tools and takes care of the ball, and Grifﬁs is 26 years old, and is more of a gunslinger. HC Harrell feels he can win with both. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they had to replace a 1,000 yard rusher (1166, 5.7). Penn St transfer London Montgomery (PS#28) was #2 (359, 5.1) in '24 and Marlon Gunn was #3 (224, 3.7). Montgomery was the starter but only had 240 yards after 6 games. Then as the O-line matured, he improved and led with 742 (4.8). Houston transfer Parker Jenkins had 256 (3.4). Soph TJ Engleman was #5 on the depth chart in August, but was #3 with 306 (5.2). Gunn was #2 (582, 5.2). This year only Engleman returns. Michael Allen (PS#22) had 251 (4.8) in 3 starts for NC St in '23, then 4 starts at Marshall in '25 with 365 (5.0). Ashton Gray (PS#168) was in the same offense at North Texas in '25 and had 377 (6.5). DeJuan Lacy (PS#187JC) was emerging as the #1 RB last year but was OFY in week two (44, 4.4). They are similarly experienced to last year and go 4 deep. RECEIVERS - In 2024, NC St transfer Anthony Smith led with 799 (19.5) and true frosh Yannick Smith was #4 (434, 17.4). Last year they lost their #2 (678, 19.9), #3 (556, 10.3) and #5, (281, 8.5) WR's, plus two TE's (14 st, 30 rec). They added 3 transfers, but 5 of the top 7 were gone. Anthony Smith led again with 1053 (16.5, #7 DC Dal) and Yannick Smith moved up to #2 (583, 13.3). Brock Spalding (injury plagued) stayed healthy and was #3 (554, 13.2). TE Desirrio Riles was #4 (362, 12.9). This year they lose 6 of the top 7 with only Spalding back. MEMPHIS TIGERS OL PARKER MITCHELL POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Last year they had to replace their career pass leader who he threw for 3,502 (65%) with a 25-6 ratio his senior year. They brought in Brendan Lewis who threw for 2,290 (67%, 16-7) and was #1 rusher for Nevada (775, 4.9) Lewis threw for 2673 (68.8%, 16-7) and was #2 rusher (660, 4.4).Three QB's played and all 3 depart. Marcus Stokes (PS#31) was committed to Florida but an off-field incident had him drop to West Florida (DII). He redshirted in '23, threw for 1540 in '24 and last year was the GSC Off POY throwing for 3297 (61%, 30-13) with 367 rush. He will battle Air Noland (PS#5) who signed with Ohio St and transferred to South Carolina in '25 and has just 3 career passes. Denzel Gardner (PS#147) comes over from Southern Miss with Huff after missing last year with injury. There is talent here and the unit could come close to last year's production and even top it. RUNNING BACKS - Memphis has a history of explosive 1,000-yard RB's (6 since '17). Last year they lost their #1 (1,362, 5.8) and #2 (335, 5.9) RB's. Sutton Smith (PS#65) had 306 (4.8) in '23 and missed '24. Smith had three 100+ games including 147 vs Arkansas and led 669 (6.6). Greg Desrosiers had 204 vs FAU and despite missing 2 games had 563 (5.7). This year the top 4 depart. They add in Dallan Hayden (PS#25) who rushed for 326 (4.7) with Colorado, Manny Covey (PS#73, 198, 7.1) and Jaylin Carter (PS#306, 166, 4.4, SMiss) and add in true frosh Jordan Thompson (PS#78) and Eric Perry (PS#106). Carter is one of the top 4 fastest on the team and Thompson should challenge for time this year. They are just as experienced as last year. RECEIVERS - In '24 their #1 WR had 950 (14.4) and #2 (677, 15.0). Last year they added 4 transfers but had to replace the top 4 receivers so were much less experienced. They got a huge pickup in July when Nevada WR Cortez Braham (caught passes from Lewis in '24) was granted an injunction and he led with 889 (14.1). Slot WR Jamari Hawkins had 623 (17.4) and Brady Kluse #4 with 240 (10.9). This year they lose their top three. They add in 7 transfers with WR Tychaun Chapman (SMiss) and TE Hunter Tipton (MTSU) each topping 400 yards in '25 so are on par with 2025 experience wise. Chapman is the teams fastest and Stonka Burnside (PS#34) will thrive here. OFFENSIVE LINE - In 2024 they had 124 career starts and the numbers improved to 174 (5.1) rush with 19 sacks allowed. Last year they lost their C (13/29, 3rd Tm AAC), RG (13/42, 3rd Tm AAC) and RT (6/37). They added 6 transfers who have all been full-time starters and had 96 career FBS starts. All 5 starters started all 12 games and the Tigers rushed for 183 (5.0) but did allow 33 sacks. This year they lose 4 starters but do add in 7 transfers with 6 having been full time starters. They have 90 career starts so are on par with last year. C Philip Gray, Maarten Woudsma and LT Riley McGehee are the top OL. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they lost two starters but I said could only be tougher vs the run. They added 6 transfers and cut it to 112 (4.0) rush with 25 sacks. Last year they lost 2 starters. 1st Tm AAC DE William Whitlow was back plus they added 4 transfers who had been full-time starters. They slipped some to allowing 131 ypg rush (3.7) with just 21 sacks. This year they lose all 4 starters including 1st tm AAC Whitlow. They add in 15 transfers (5 from Southern Miss) including DE J'Mond Tapp (70 tkl, 7.5 sk Southern Miss) who has NFL potential, but do not have as many full-time starters back as the '25 DLine. Coach Huff feels it could be the best unit on the team with their depth and flexibility. LINEBACKERS - Last year they lost a 1st Tm AAC LB (#1 tklr, 7 sk), #2, 3, 4 and 11 tacklers. They added 7 transfers (5 full-time st'rs) and were still solid and held foes to 43 ypg below their average. This year they lose their #1 #2, #4 and #5 tacklers. They add in 4 transfers with 2 starters from Southern Miss in Michael Montgomery (105 tkl) and NB Ian Foster (75 tkl) who are both all-conference caliber with Foster perhaps the best player on the team. They are not as deep as the 2025 group. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '24 they had 3 starters back and added transfers from Indiana, ULM, UTEP and 2 non-FBS teams. I said they could have their best finish in my PDR in at least 4 years and they did at #62 (60%, 17-11). Last year they lost 4 starters (#7 DC). They added 8 transfers but none were full-time starters. They performed better than I expected and were #58 (61.2%, 14-12) in the PDR. This year they lose all 4 starters again but add in 10 transfers with five from Southern Miss including two starters and the Golden Eagles were #44 in the PDR so they are more experienced and improved. SPECIAL TEAMS - In 2023 3rd Tm AAC Sutton Smith was the top KR (24.2) he missed '24. In '24 they ST RANK L6Y: were #41. Last year they lost their P again (41.5 2025 ... #50 net!) but got Smith back and added Ohio's K and 2024 ... #41 were still solid. Memphis was a solid #53 in the STR. This year they are a brand new crew (see PSL) as everyone departs. Including LS they add in 5 transfers. Huff's Southern Miss team was #87 in the STR in '25. TULSA GOLDEN HURRICANE CB ELIJAH GREEN OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they lost five OL (43/84). The career starts dropped to 36 and a starter (12/23) was OFY after 3 starts. The rush numbers dropped to 151 (4.0) with 26 sacks. Last year they returned one starter and added two former starters among the eight transfers. The career starts dropped to 25 and this unit was rebuilt and learning new schemes. Lamb did a solid job as they improved to 176 (4.3) with 25 sacks. This year they lose two starters (24/35) but return 5 OL who drew starts last year and add in South Alabama's starting C so the they have 62 career starts so look even stronger. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they lost the top 3 DL and allowed 181 (4.9) rush with just 19 sacks. Last year they lost 3 starters. They played a lot of young DL in '24 and returned Tai Newhouse (12 st). They also added 4 transfers (two from the Power 4) who all started some in '24. They were similar to '24 in experience and production allowing 182 (4.3) rush with 23 sacks. This year 6 DL depart (34 st, 20 sk!, 180 tkl) including 2nd team American J'Dan Burnett (6.5 sk). They return Newhouse and add in 6 transfers and HC Lamb feels he has 4 DE's that are all conf caliber and that DE will be one of the team strengths, which means more sacks. They are not as deep on the interior but are improved. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they lost all 3 starters with the top returnee having 19 tackles. Tulsa allowed foes 136 ypg above their average (#133!). Last year they lost their #1 and #5 tacklers then team captain Chris Thompson (PS#10 #4 tklr) was OFY in August. I really liked the addition of East Tenn St transfer Ray Coney (97 tkl, 5 sk). They still cut it to allowing foes 26 ypg above their average (#92). This year they lose 1st tm All Conf Conley (12 st, 129 tkl) and their #10 tackler but return two starters (#4, #6 tklr) get Thompson back and add in UAB's Devin Hightower PS#78, 81 tkl). William Alexander (6'2" 230 Jr, #4 tklr) is OFY with an ACL but this remains a strong unit and WLB Will Collins should emerge as a force in '26. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23 Tulsa was just #120 in my PDR (64.4%, 24-10). In '24 the unit was hit hard by injuries and played a lot of true frosh. They dropped to dead last #134 allowing 316 ypg (66%, 38-9). Last year they lost two starters but upgraded with transfers and 24's returning starters were now backups. They moved up to #100 in the PDR (63.4%, 21-7). This year they lose 2nd tm All Conf Lento Smith (12 st, #2 tklr, 4 pbu) but have 3 starters back and add in 6 more transfers and should move up more in the PDR. CB Elijah Green (pictured) has All American potential and FS Zach Williams is top notch. He was HC at East Tenn St in '24 and they improved from 3-8 to 7-4 with a lot of GWebb transfers. New OC is Kevin Barbay has been the OC at CMich ('21), App St ('22), Miss St ('23) and Houston ('24). POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Four different QB's started in '23 and they had a combined 19 int's. In '24 Kirk Francis started the first seven but four QB's combined to throw for 2,812 (56.6%, 23-12). Last year only Francis returned. They added Baylor Hayes (1 st, 18-30-181 ETSU) and true frosh Andrew Alford (PS#223). Lamb prefers a mobile QB and that was Hayes strength. FLORIDA ATLANTIC OWLS QB CADEN VELTKAMP OFFENSIVE LINE - Former HC Tom Herman was high on the group and they lived up to that promise in 2024 with 189 (5.0) rush but did allow 32 sacks (9.1%). Last year they lost 3.5 starters and had just 18 career starts. FAU dropped to 105 (3.5) rush in the new offense but the unit only allowed 19 sacks (3.3%!).This year they lose RG Alex Atcavage (9/19), G/T Scarlee Jean (12/12) and two other OL (14/24). They return starters in C Vincent Fiacable and LT Ja'Kavion Nonar plus add in two FCS full time starters. They have just 26 career FBS starts but I like this units potential and I look for improved rush numbers in 2026. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they allowed 184 (4.9) rush and had just 17 sacks. Last year they lost all 4 starters and two backups (3 st, 23 tkl, 3.5 sk). They added six transfers including an Ohio starter and three from the B10. Despite losing 6 of the top 9 DL, I said they should be close to 24's standard. They allowed 201 (4.7) rush but did increase the sacks to 24. This year they lose three DL (18 st, 81 tkl, 3.5 sk) but have everyone else back including 3rd tm AAC DT DJ Doggette, DE Deshaun Batiste (9 st, 3.5 sk). They add in 6 transfers (see PSL) and have 7 DL with FBS starting experience and HC Kittley said he was most excited about this unit on defense as they are much stronger than last year. LINEBACKERS - In '24 the top 4 LB's had starting experience, so this unit was the strength of the D. Last year they lost their #2, #4, #8 and #10 tacklers. They returned Wendol Philord (#6 tklr) but lost 4 of the top 5 and FAU allowed teams 35 ypg above their average (#107). This year they lose NB Philord (9 st, 16 tkl) and LB Tyler Stolsky (12 st, #2 tklr) but return two starters in Leon Hart (#1 tklr) and NB Chris Tooley (8 st) plus add in Joseph Sipp who was 1st team MAC at Bowling Green in 2024 and 4 other transfers so are much more experienced and should spearhead a much improved defense. Hart, Sipp and Tooley all have all-conf potential so this is a strong group. DEFENSIVE BACKS- In '24 they were #75 (56%, 25-11) in my PDR. Last year they lost their top 6 DB's. They brought in 8 new DB transfers and I said would drop in the PDR. They were starting from scratch and HC Zach Kittley told me this unit was the biggest question mark on the team. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In 2024 my computer called for 24.2 ppg and they were right there but after exploding for 63 points vs Tulsa in the season ﬁnale, the Owls topped it with 25.9 ppg. Offense is HC Zach Kittley's forte. In his last year at WKU, they averaged 535 ypg and in his ﬁnal year at Texas Tech, they put up 463 ypg. Kittley recruited QB Veltkamp when he was at WKU. Last year my computer called for jumps to 31.8 ppg and 453 ypg and they had 30 ppg and 446 ypg! This year Veltkamp is back as is top WR Messer and they should be even more potent and Kittley feels they will be one of the top offenses in the country. DEFENSE - In 2024 they allowed 30.3 ppg, their most since 2018. Last year they had just one returning starter on defense and a faster paced offense which I said would have them facing more plays. My computer called for them to allow 38.0 ppg and they gave up 36.3! This year they are much more experienced and add in 19 transfers so should make solid gains across the board on D! The front 7 looks much stronger but the secondary is still a concern. 2026- Former HC Lane Kifﬁn gave this program the best three-year run in school history (the Owls went 11-3 in '19), but he left FAU for Ole Miss. Willie Taggart and Tom Herman could not get the team to six wins in any of the ﬁve years since Kifﬁn's departure. Zach Kittley took over as a ﬁrst-time head coach last year taking over a team that went 3-9 and were -48 ypg in American play in '24. He had an inexperienced team but there were some signs were pointing up. FAU had a Stock Market Indicator of +1.5 and had 2 Net Close Losses in '24. I said they should be able to top 24's 3-win total but it would be tough to get to that six-win level. FAU improved to 4 wins with a last-second loss to UConn. They led FIU 21-10 at half and were int'd in the EZ twice in a loss. They were -46 ypg in American play. This is year two for coach Kittley and he has a much more veteran team to work with and adds in X transfers. There are signs pointing up as the Owls are the poster child for my Turnover = Turnaround article after being -21 TO's last year and they go from #126 on my Exp Char to #14. Florida Atlantic makes my Most Improved list and my 9 sets of power ratings have them any where from 6 regular season wins to 11 but all point to a bowl game. They could be a surprise contender in the American. Kevin Terry was projected to start at LT but was injured and Giakoby Hills took the spot and did not give it back. They made strides in the fall and had just one missed start all year and paved the way for 147 (4.4) rush with just 20 sacks allowed. Coming into last year, Temple was 13-42 the previous 5 years. KC Keeler came from Sam Houston but is an East Coast guy who was also the HC at Delaware prior. Most coaches bring a ton of their former team's players with them when they move but he brought just one. Temple opened with two wins by a comb score of 97-17 but then lost to powers Oklahoma and Georgia Tech. NORTH TEXAS MEAN GREEN They had just one starter back but did have 5 seniors and had 161 (5.4) rush with just 13 sacks allowed. Last year they lost 6 OL (comb 41 sts). They added a 3-year starter from Abilene Christian, a 2Y starter from Kent St and get top OL Blair back, plus returned 3 OL who started 6+ games including Braydon Nelson who started 11 as a true frosh. Morris said they were way better in terms of talent and depth. They were also bigger with 7 OL at 320+ (2 in '24) including 3 starters. NT had 194 (5.3) rush with just 18 sacks (3.8%). This year they lose all 5 starters (1 1st tm, 2 2nd tm, 2 3rd tm AAC). The unit has just 2 OL with starting experience as C Strong has 32 of the units 34 career starts and this is an area of concern despite 6 transfers. Coach Brown feels they could be as good as last year (see PSL). DEFENSIVE LINE - In '23 they allowed 255 (5.6) rush with just 18 sacks. In '24 they improved some to 196 (4.7) rush and 24 sacks. Last year they lost 3 starters but added 9 transfers including four from Sam Houston and switched to a larger four-man front. The results were similar allowing 216 ypg rush (4.8) with just 24 sacks. This year they lose 10 DL who all had 10+ tackles last year and the two DL that return had just 13 & 5 tackles. They add in 9 transfers with starters from UTEP, Ill St, UMass and Georgia Southern. The numbers were not great last year and they could actually improve this year. JLB David Onuoha and DT Terrell Washington are the top guys up front. This year they lose their #1, #2, #5, #7 tacklers with the top returnee Brayden Knox (19 tkl). They add in 5 transfers but only one was a starter so they are clearly less experienced. NT had never had a 3,000-yard passer, 1,000-yard rusher and 1,000-yard receiver but did in '23, but all 3 departed. They added QB Chandler Morris from TCU and my computer called for 31.7 ppg and they had 33.5 ppg! Last year my computer called for a jump to 477 ypg and they topped it by a little with 512 ypg and 45 ppg. This year they lose all 11 starters from their explosive offense and will clearly take a step back this year. My computer calls for 32.9 ppg this year. They broke a 7 game bowl losing streak and finished 12-2. This year ZERO starters return so Neal Brown steps into a tough situation off their best season ever with no one back! UAB BLAZERS OL ADAM LEPKOWSKI POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In 2024, Jalen Kitna averaged 235 ypg the last 4 and finished throwing for 2,209 (62%, 17-11). Last year the backups were Ryder Burton (PS#77, WVU), Nate Rogers (PS#273) and Adrian Posse (PS#57). Then-HC Trent Dilfer believed Kitna could be a high DC in the draft. Kitna threw for 2,464 (66%) but with only a 13-10 ratio. Burton started for an injured Kitna and led the upset of Memphis and started the next two games before Kitna regained the job back. Burton threw for 708 (63%, 7-5). Rogers was used as a runner (13-84) with just 2 pass attempts (1-2). Kitna moves on. While the ypg may decrease, the unit should cut down on the 15 total interceptions of last year. Coach Mortensen feels they have a good combination of experience with Burton/Rogers and a couple of high-ceiling guys with Posse and Cam Jennings (6-1 225 So). RUNNING BACKS - In '24, Solomon Beebe led with 884 (5.3) and was the #5 receiver (219, 7.3). Last year they added Jevon Jackson (754, 3.9, UTEP). Jackson took charge with 166 vs Ala St and had 159 vs NTexas and 117 vs Tulsa and led with 900 (5.4). Isaiah Jacobs had 342 (4.3). Beebe added 338 (6.0) and was the #4 receiver (284, 9.2) and also the top KR. This year all 3 depart. They add Braylon "Bam" McReynolds who was #2 with ULM with 637 (5.2), Ja'vin Simpkins (PS#27) who led Coastal Carolina with 591 (4.7) and Rod Robinson (PS#15) who had 221 yards in 3 years at Georgia and did catch a TD pass in the SEC title game last year. Marquise Collins (5-9 210 Jr) adds depth. This unit is on par with last year experience wise and Mortensen feels it will be one of the team's strengths. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost 7 of the top 8 (all 179+ yds, top two 670, 656 yds) with Corri Milliner, who had 385 yards the last 5 (#3, 418, 17.3), the top returnee. They added 4 transfers including Kaleb Brown (PS#7) but the unit was completely rebuilt. Dilfer felt they were very deep at WR. Milliner was #1 with 268 yards the first 3 games then stepped away for a few games and only played in two more. Iverson Hooks had 11-172 vs Memphis and 10-146 vs USF and led with 927 (12.9). Brandon Hawkins had 540 (13.2). This year they lose the top 4 with Brown (255, 15.5) the top returnee. They did add 7 transfers with the most notable Ty Mims (445, 11.4 at SMiss '23) and KJ Daniels (PS#94, Oklahoma). They are in the same shape as '25 and Brown could finally live up to his PS#7 billing. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 UAB dropped to 131 (4.0) rush with 32 sacks. Last year they lost 4 starters. The career starts dropped to 19 and they did not add any full-time FBS starters. Dilfer liked the talent and said for the first time they had real competition at the spots so despite being less experienced, they had similar numbers with 139 (4.2) rush and 30 sacks allowed. This year they lose 3 starters (34/46) but have two starters back and 39 career starts led by C Adam Lepkowski and RG Calib Perez. This is a little more veteran group and Mortensen feels good about the ability, but it is mostly unproven. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24, UAB did take on two option offenses but slipped to allowing 213 (5.1) and produced just 18 sacks. Last year they lost all 4 starters. The Blazers used most of their NIL money on this position bringing in 5 transfers, so they had good depth but a 325 lb projected starting DT was OFY in August. They had similar numbers allowing 191 (4.6) with 18 sacks. This year they lose 6 DL (47 sts, 232 tkl, 6 sk) with the top returnees being Chris Burge (0 st, 32 tkl, 3.5 sk) and Kyle Mosley (1 st, 10 tkl). They added 10 transfers so are in similar shape to last year with the top newcomers being NG Nigel Tate (Boston College) and DE Marlin Dean (Georgia St). This unit passes the eye ball test but is another unproven unit. LINEBACKERS - Last year they lost their top 4 LBs (#1, #2, #5, #6 tklrs). They added 3 highly productive FCS transfers, plus UNLV and Maryland transfers. UAB actually held foes to 1 ypg below their average (#71). This year they lose their #1, #4, #5, #6 and #9 tacklers. They added 3 FCS starters including Braden Sullivan (12 st, 79 tkl, EKU) so are in the same shape as last year. The top guys figure to be Muaaz Byard (Middle Tennessee) and Ike Esonwune (Oklahoma St). DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23, they finished a respectable #81 in my PDR (62%, 24-10) and improved to #65 (55% 18-8) in '24. Last year they lost 3 starters but added 5 transfers, so they were on par with '24 experience wise. Injuries were a big part of the problem as last year 13 different DBs drew starts and UAB finished dead last in my PDR (66%, 27-4). BOISE STATE BRONCOS QB MADDUX MADSEN POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In 2024 Maddux Madsen missed spring, but still beat out a PS#2 VHT QB and won the job and had a solid year throwing for 3,018 (62%, 23-6!) along with 221 rush (3.9). Last year Madsen was the clear cut starter. He was inured in the 1Q vs Air Force and not 100% and tossed 4 int's vs ND. He was injured 1Q vs Fresno and missed 4 games. Walk-on Max Cutforth struggled in the loss to Fresno and they did not pass much in the rain vs SDSt, but he had a solid final drive and they turned him loose. He threw for 239 and 341 in wins over Colo St and Utah St. Madsen returned and was MVP of the MW title game. Eight days later, a less than 100% Madsen and Cutforth combined for 5 int's in the bowl loss. They combined for 3,175 yards (58.7%, 24-9). Both are back, so it is a deep experienced unit. Plus they add PS#41 and #63 true Frosh. If Madsen stays healthy, he will have is best year and the backup now has experience. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 Ashton Jeanty had a season for the ages, finishing #2 all-time (behind Barry Sanders) in FBS with 2,601 (7.0) rush yards. He was #2 in the Heisman race. True Frosh Sire Gaines has a lot of Jeanty attributes and had 110 vs Ga. Southern, but was OFY after 3 games (156, 7.8). Jeanty was #1 DC LV. Last year, they added Malik Sherrod who had 966 (5.6) with Fresno is '23. Dylan Riley had 135 (6.1) in '24 and was #3 RB into the year but had 171 vs Air Force and had 201 vs UNLV and led 1,125 (5.8). Gaines was #2 with 811 (5.0). Both are back as they only lose Sherrod (418, 4.9), plus add in Julez Goff (PS#67, 270, 3.9 Pitt) and Harry Stewart (PS#58, 96, 4.7, Kansas). It should be yet another highly productive year for the Boise RB's. RECEIVERS - Last year, they lost their #1 (903, 15.6) WR. In '24, TE Matt Lauter was #2 (619, 13.2) and Latrell Caples #3 (473, 12.5). They added Chris Marshall (PS#4), who RS in '24, and were more experienced as a group. Ben Ford was #2 receiver, but was OFY vs UNLV and was #3 (325, 15.5). Marshall was #1, but OFY vs Nevada (467, 19.5). This year, they lose WR Caples, who finished #1 (10 st, 617, 12.1), Marshall, Chase Penry (#3, 394, 13.1) and TE Lauter (8 st, 330, 8.9). While the top 4 depart, they return Ford, TE Matt Wagner (10 st, 251, 10.5) and Cameron Bates (8 st, 325, 15.5) and should remain healthier. True Frosh WR Rasean Jones is the top newcomer. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24, they had 4 OL back who started 7+ games in '23, led by 2nd TM MW LT Kage Casey. A total of 66 career starts returned, putting them on par with '23's top-notch unit. C Mason Randolph (11/21) was OFY Week 3 and RG Roger Carreon (last 7 st '23) was OFY Week 6. But the unit (thanks to Jeanty) opened holes for 240 (6.1) with just 15 sacks allowed. Last year they lost a 1st TM MW LG (14/38). But with 99 career starts back, they were the top OLine in the MW with 6 OL that had 7+ starts in a season. Boise had 179 (4.5) rush and allowed 26 sacks. This year they lose 1st TM MW OL's C Randolph (14/38), LT Casey (#4 DC DEN, 13/41) and two backups (6/22). With 3 starters back, they will have a typical strong Boise OLine, but do lose their top two. Roger Carreon looks to be the next drafted Boise OL and OT's Daylon Metoyer and Tyler Ethridge are solid. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24, they had all 4 starters back and Boise improved to allowing 122 (3.8) rush with 55 sacks! Last year, they lost two starters and 2 backups. Jayden VirginMorgan had 10 sacks, and was 1st TM MW in '24 & 2nd TM MW in '25. They added 3 transfers, but did lose their star DE (#6DC, 9.5 sk). The numbers dropped more than I expected as they allowed 162 (4.8) rush and had 27 sacks. This year, they lose 2nd TM MW DT Braxton Fely (14 st, #11 tklr, 5.5 sk) and 2 backups (5 st, 21, tkl, 2.5 sk). I look for a much stronger year from the DLine. DE Virgin-Morgan turned down the NFL and could be P12 Defensive POY, and DE Max Stege should emerge as a pass rusher. LINEBACKERS - In '23 Marco Notarainni (5 st, 53 tkl, 3 sk) was #1 tackler until injured. In '24 they lost their #8 tackler. With five of the top six back, they improved to holding foes to 31 ypg below their average. Last year, they lost their #2 and #9 tacklers. Boise improved to holding foes to 64 ypg below their average. This year, they lose Notarainni (14 st, #2 tklr, 1.5 sk). They return Boen Phelps (9 st, #3 tklr), and Jake Ripp (6 st, #7 tklr), plus add in a South Dakota starter at NB. But they are less experienced and NB Mickey moves to CB. DEFENSIVE BACKS - Boise was #96 in my PDR (60%, 24-7) in '24 and were shredded at times (San Jose St). Last year they returned all 4 full-time starters including Ty Benefield (#1 tklr), Zion Washington (#3 tklr) and did make the expected rise in the PDR to #16 (54.4%, 17-14). That was their best finish since 2010. This year all 4 starters depart (#1, #4, #5 and #9 tklrs). They add in NB Jaden Mickey (PS#42, 11 st, #8 tklr) plus 4 transfers including 2nd TM CUSA JeRico Washington, but they are much less experienced and could take a Stock Market type of drop in the PDR. They are solid at CB but have questions at S. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 they lost the MWest all time leading scorer at K plus their P (38.2 net). They ST RANK L6Y: allowed 2 return TD's vs Oregon and slipped to 2025 ... #94 #104 in my STR. COACHES - 4th year DC Spencer Danielson was named interim HC & guided Boise to the MW title in '23 and then took Boise to the playoffs in first full year as HC. He is the 2nd coach in FBS history to win 3 straight conf titles in his first 3 title game appearances. Danielson has been a coach here since 2017. The 3rd year ST coordinator is Stacy Collins, who was Penn St's ST coach in '22-23 and here in '21. FRESNO STATE BULLDOGS LB TYTUS KHAJAVI POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Last year they lost their starter (2892, 70.5%, 18-11). They added EJ Warner (Kurt's son), who had 31 starts playing for Temple and Rice. He had 2,136 career snaps. Jayden Mandel was the only returnee (33 snaps). They also added Sac St transfer Carson Conklin (2876, 62%, 28-8). Warner had an 0-5 ratio after 3 starts but then 7-1 ratio the next 3 games and Fresno was 5-1. After a 3-int game at Colorado St, Entz went with Conklin vs SDst, then - despite the shutout loss - named him the starter. Conklin threw for just 65 ypg in wins over Boise and Wyoming. Warner started the last three including the bowl win. On the year, he threw for 2,030 (69.3%, 13-11). Conklin threw for 354 (49%, 1-2). Both move on. Mandal missed the year with labrum surgery and is back as is rFR Jonathan Craft (PS#155). The Bulldogs added in Khristian Martin (PS#55), who battled for the Maryland job in '25, and true Frosh Deegan Rose (PS#36). Martin is a dual threat QB with a big arm and is cerebral and should improve the passing numbers while bringing a run threat to the position. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 Elijah Gilliam led with 466 (3.9). True Frosh Bryson Donelson (PS#176) was #2 with 462 (6.0). Last year they added in Rayshon "Speedy" Luke (PS#20 Ariz) and Entz called it one of the deepest units on the team. Donelson had 167 vs GSthrn and was the leading rusher after 7 games, ﬁnishing #2 with 600 (4.3). Luke had a high of 92 vs Wyoming and led with 702 (6.3). Brandon Ramirez was #4 (271, 4.5). All 3 return, plus they add in Bucknell transfer Tariq Thomas (1385, 4.7 2Y), rFr Julius Gillick (PS#209) and Jalen Harris (PS#213), so they are deeper and even more experienced. Ramirez was hurt in the spring and may not return until late. RECEIVERS - Last year, Fresno lost their #1 (1065, 16.6, 13 st), #2 (563, 11.7) and #3 (523, 10.3) WR's. The unit was a lot less experienced and contributed to the underwhelming pass game. Josiah Freeman led with 642 (12.3), Ezekiel Avit #3 (255, 9.1) RB Luke #4 (228, 6.3) and Jahil McClain (PS#61 Lville, was #5 169, 13.0). This year, they lose TE Richie Anderson (12 st, #2, 300, 9.7). They use "12" personnel as much as "11" (11 TE's roster) and I list them in 12 in the PSL below. WR Josiah Freeman is NFL caliber and this group should be much improved. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they returned 8 of the top 10 (106 car sts) led by a 1st TM MW C. Surprisingly the numbers dropped again to 98 ypg rush (3.3) with 28 sacks allowed. Last year they had two starters back and added transfers from USC and Iowa (neither started) and the career starts dropped to 50. Entz wanted to be strong at the lines of scrimmage so I said the numbers could improve. Entz did a ﬁne job with this unit and with 6'7" 325 true Frosh Brayden Walton started at LT, they improved to 170 (4.5) with just 19 sacks allowed. This year they lose 2 starters again, but Walton teams with Rolan Fullwood for one of the P12's best OT tandems. San Diego transfer C Oscar Weigel is a solid addition at C. They are longer and more athletic and should be even stronger in Year 2. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24, the Bulldogs improved to 139 (3.8) rush yards allowed with 24 sacks. Last year, they lost 3 starters including their anchor. They added Finn Claypool (30.5 sk 3Y Drake) but ﬁgured to be down some. Entz felt the unit would be in the top third of MW and he was correct, as they allowed 132 (4.1) rush with 25 sacks. This year they lose Claypool (9 st, #4 tklr, 6.5 sk) and two backup DL (4st, 44 tkl, 3 sk) but four DL return that had 5+ starts plus they add Dylan Hampsten (8.5 sk Sac St) and should be one of the stronger Pac 12 D-lines, going from one to three returning starters. Mordecai Hines has NFL potential, DT DJ Lafﬁtte was HM MW in '25 and DE's Jahzon Jacks and Merhauti Xepera both leaned up and will be top notch pass rusers so this is the best group on the roster. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they returned one starter but held foes to 34 ypg below their average (#49). Last year, they lost their #1, #2 and #6 tacklers. This time, the top returnee had just 16 tackles but they did add 4 transfers who combined for 12 starts in '24.
