TEXAS STATE BOBCATS WR BEAU SPARKS SBC's best. The unit paved the way for 208 (5.1) with just 19 sacks and all 5 starters finished with 12 starts in 12 games. Last year, they went from 3 starters back to 2 but averaged 341 lbs - the largest OLine in the FBS. The unit had similar numbers with 222 (5.2) rush and 27 sacks allowed. This year they lose 1st TM SBC LT Dorion Strawn (13/36) and 5 other OL (33/47). They have two starters back again, plus add in 5 transfers and have two 2nd-year JUCO's. C Justin DeLeon and LT Sully Burns are the top guys. The unit averages 337 lbs, so they could be just as strong. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '23 Texas St allowed 152 rush ypg (4.0) but had 40 sacks (9.6%) and was #2 in the nation in tfl's with 108! In '24, they allowed 143 (3.9) rush with 36 sacks despite their top DE being OFY after 4 starts. Last year, they lost 3+ starters and 3 backups (38 tkl, 4.5 sk). They returned top sack man Kalil Alexander (6.5 sk) and DE Jo'Laison Landry (4.5 sk) and added 5 transfers but were not as deep or experienced. Landry was OFY after 1 start. They allowed 165 (4.2) rush with just 27 sacks. This year, they lose 6 DL (41 sts, 166 tkl, 13 sk) but add in 6 transfers and could be tougher up front, with top DL Landry's return and all 4 DL all-conference caliber (see PSL). LINEBACKERS - In '24 the Bobcats went from allowing foes 14 ypg above their average in '23 to holding foes to 32 ypg below. Last year they lost their #1, #2, #4, #7 and #10 tacklers. They added 6 transfers, but none were FBS starters so they were less experienced. This time, the defense allowed foes 35 ypg above their average. Treylin Payne set a school record with 24 tackles vs Marshall (Brad Fulks, 23, 1988). This year, they lose Payne (13 st, #1 tklr, 6.5 tfl). They return their #4, #6 and #11 tacklers, so are more experienced overall. HC Kinne calls it his best LB group since his first year here and MLB Javante Mackey had 84 tackles for Arkansas St in '23, He is two years removed from an ACL and should return to form. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23 they had one starter back dropped to #111 (65%, 24-11) in our PDR. In '24 two starters were back plus they added transfers from Cincy, UTEP and Ark St and as you would expect they made strides moving up to #43 (56%, 13-7). Last year they lost 3 starters so they were less experienced and took a Stock Market dip to #118 (66%, 22-8). This year they lose 5 DB's (39 sts, #3, #7 , #10 tklr). They add in 3 transfers and return #2 tackler Ryan Nolan at FS. CB Trez Moore had 11 starts with UTEP in '24 and Kinne calls it the most talented secondary since he has been here. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 they were #27 in the STR. Last year they lost their top two KR's and they ST RANK L6Y: their super K left post spring. Tyler Robles hit a 2025 ....#16 super 19-21 FG (3-4 50+), Michael James had 44 2024 ....#27 TB on 78 KO's and new P Daid Nunez avg 40.4 2023 ... #40 (net 38.1). KR Jaylen Jenkins had a 100 yd KR 2022 .. #94 #72 TD (27.0) and Texas St was #16 in our STR! Only 2021... 2020 .. #26 Jenkins returns. They do add in Toledo K Dylan Cunanan, but they should drop in the STR. COACHES - GJ Kinne enters Year 4 in San Marcos and has guided Texas St to their first bowl game & bowl win! Kinne was the HC at FCS Incarnate Word, leading them to the FCS Semifinals. Kinne was the co-OC/QB coach at UCF in '21 & he is a former QB at Tulsa ('08-'11). The 2nd-year OC is Landon Keopple (WR cch here '22-'23). The new DC is Will Windham, who was DC at South Alabama ('24-'25). The 2nd year STC is Tanner Burns (STC Auburn '23-'24 and Liberty '20-22). POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '23 Auburn transfer TJ Finley set a school record (Barrick Nealy 3129 in '03) with 3,439 pass yards (67%, 24-8). In '24 they brought in the reigning Sun Belt POY Jordan McCloud from James Madison. Brad Jackson (PS#127) was a promising true frosh. McCloud threw for 3,227 (70%, 3013). His 30 TD passes were a school record. Jackson hit 4-9-16 but rushed for 17-126 vs ULM. Last year they lost their top 2 QBs. Jackson was impressive with 3,224 pass (71%, 21-7) and was #2 rusher (744, 4.3) and set the school record for rushing TD's (17) and total offense in a single season. Backups are Shaker Reisig (PS#68 10-19-142 BColl), rFr Gavin Parkhurst (PS#182) and true Frosh Easton Webb (PS#112). Reisig has more experience while Parkhurst is a gunslinger with a big arm. Jackson will be one of the Pac-12's top QB's and is a great runner with arm strength & accuracy to boot. RUNNING BACKS - In '22, Arkansas St transfer Lincoln Pare was #1 (772, 4.5). In '23 Pare was OFY in August. Ismail Mahdi had a school FBS record (Claude Mathis 1596 '97 FCS) 1,331 yards (6.0, 10 TD) and led the nation in all-purpose yards (2,169). In '24 Mahdi had some fumbling problems early but led with 991 (5.4) while Pare was #2 (554, 5.8) with 143 in the bowl. Last year, Mahdi left for Arizona so they added Greg Burrell (366, 5.6 UNLV). Pare led with 1,128 (5.4) with Burrell #3 with 671 (6.7), Jaylen Jenkins #4 (170, 5.5) and Torrance Burgess (367, 6.1 '24) was #5 (95, 4.8). This year they lose Pare and Burrell but add in Taji Atkins (PS#148, 158, 6.6 Rice) and rFr Cole Pryor (PS#182) and remain strong. HC Kinne has had a 1,000-yard rusher every year he has coached and has a room full of home run hitters waiting for one to be the next. RECEIVERS - In '24 they added Beau Sparks (723, 9.8 '23, Utah Tech). Last year they lost their top 3 WR's and their TE (7 st, 143, 10.2). Chris Dawn (#4, 418, 11.3) and Sparks (#5, 271, 10.8) both returned and they added 6 transfers. Sparks became the Bobcats first 1,000 yard receiver s/2008 (Cameron Luke) with 1,200 (14.3), Dawn was #2 also topping that barrier with 1,007 (15.5) and rFr Kylen Evans was #4 (211, 14.1). The top 3 (RB was #3) all return, plus they add in two P4 transfers so they are much more experienced. WASHINGTON STATE COUGARS RB KIRBY VOORHEES POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Wash St has had a storied history of QB’s including #1DC’s Drew Bledsoe, Ryan Leaf, Jack Thompson and #6DC Gardner Minshew. In ‘23 Cam Ward threw for 3,732 (67%, 25-7) but lost 11 fumbles. In ‘24 they added Zevi Eckhaus, a 3-year starter for Bryant (8527 yds, 75-25) who was Big South POY and a finalist for the Walter Payton Award. John Mateer threw for 3,139 (65%, 29-7) and led with 826 rush (4.6). Eckhaus started the bowl but redshirted. Last year they added Julian Dugger (PS#67, Pitt) who had the mobility that then-HC Rogers craved at QB. 6’5 Jaxon Potter (PS#71) was the surprise starter and Dugger was used as a runner in the first 3 games but Eckhaus led a late scoring drive vs North Texas and took over the job. He threw for 2,094 (63%, 15-12) with 371 rush. Only Dugger and rFr Owen Eshelman (PS#122) return. New HC Moore brings in Caden Pinnick (PS#159) who threw for 3,206 (70%, 32-10) with 437 rush and was Big Sky Frosh of year at UCDavis. He could top last year’s numbers. COLORADO STATE RAMS WR TOMMY MAHER POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Last year, their third year starting QB (Brayden Fowler-Nicolosi) was just 2,742 yards away from being the career leader here, but was benched after 4 starts. Jackson Brousseau took over and threw for 1,354 (64%, 9-3). He was injured and Darious Curry started vs Boise and, in 5 games, threw for 740 (65%, 5-7). After a solid game vs Boise he was suspended. This year, only Curry returns. Mora covets a dual threat QB that can threaten a defense with his legs (Curry fits that role). The Rams add in Hauss Henjy (PS#20) who had 10 passes and 19 rushes for Okla St/TCU. He started the opener in '25 for OSU and led two scoring drives, then was OFY. Mora brings K'Saan Farrar (PS#83) from UConn (11-18-84) and signed PS#68 and #102 true frosh. Despite the inexperience, this unit should top last year's stats. RUNNING BACKS - Last year, they lost their #1 RB (1,006, 5.5) but returned #2 Justin Marshall (746, 4.8). RFr Jalen Dupree (PS#135) was the top RB and led with 508 (5.0) despite leaving the team shortly after Norvell was fired. Tulsa transfer Lloyd Avant was #2 (436, 4.6) and Marshall was only #3 (260, 5.3). The top 3 all depart. The top 4 RB's this year all played for Mora at UConn. Durell Robinson (PS#37) was #2 in '24 with 731 (6.8) and was at Auburn last year. Mel Brown had 673 (5.7) and was a 1st TM All-Conf KR for G-Webb in '24 and had 262 (8.2) for UConn in '25. Oliver Lundberg (PS#192) had 138 (6.0) and rFr Malichi Greaves had 3-15 for UConn in '25. True Frosh Cedric Ross (PS#140) was IFS. CSU had just 64 ypg rush the last 7 games last year and can only be mora (like what I did there?) productive. RECEIVERS - Colo St had produced a 1,000-yard receiver 9 straight years, including 2023. In '24, they lost their 1st TM MW TE (#2, 767, 12.0), and #2, #3 and #4 receivers. Their star Tony Horton (1136 in '24) was OFY after 6 starts (353, 13.6, #5DC SEA). Last year, they lost their #1 (436, 20.8), #2 (386, 10.7) receivers and TE (12 st, 256, 10.7).They added 6 transfers but had another underwhelming year with TE Rocky Beers leading with 388 (12.5) and Tay Lanier #3 (315, 9.0). Both depart. Tommy Maher was #2 (358, 11.9) and is back as is #6 Lavon Brown (244, 12.5). Mora adds in 9 transfers and - this might sound familiar - this unit can only be more productive. I list them in "12" personnel and they may use some "13" as well! OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they had 3 starters back (94 car sts). This unit had great strength & physicality. The MOB (Made of Brothers) line opened holes for 168 (4.7) with just 10 sacks allowed! Last year, they lost a 1st TM MW C and two other starters so they were less experienced and looked to be weaker. They did have 4 OL with a combined 93 starts at the FCS level. Captain LG Tanner Morley (12 st '24) was OFY after 4 starts. The numbers dropped to 108 (3.6) rush with 32 sacks allowed. This year, 6 OL who combined for 54 starts all depart so Mora is starting from scratch with C Phlllip Ocon (2 sts) the only experience from last year. Mora add 5 transfers and built solid OLines at UConn, but they have just 8 career starts in the unit. Mora will have to work his magic. DEFENSIVE LINE - In 2024, CSU allowed 160 (4.5) ypg rush with just 17 sacks. Last year they lost 3 starters and two backups. They added 3 transfers, a New Mexico starter and DE JaQues Evans (Baylor) who was 1st TM CUSA with WKU in '22 (106 tkl, 8.5 sk!). They lost Captain Mukendi Wa-Kalonji after 3 starts and Evans after 5 starts. Due to injuries, 7 different DL started at the 3 DL spots. The Rams slipped to allowing 205 (5.0) rush with just 16 sacks. This year, including the JLB, they lose 3 DL (18 sts, 95 tkl, 2 sk) but return 6 DL that drew starts and add in 6 transfers (4 from UConn), including PS#34 Stephon Wright. This unit should stay healthier, is more experienced and can only be tougher up front. Other than TE. DL is the strength of the team with great depth. OREGON STATE BEAVERS EDGE TAKARI HICKLE POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 rFr Gabarri Johnson (PS#17 Mizzou) was used as a change of pace runner. Last year the top two QBs hit the portal (7-11 ratio!). They added Maalik Murphy (PS#8, Texas), who threw for 2,933 (60.3%, 26-12) with Duke in '24. There was less use of the speed option, as Murphy's longest run was 8 yards last year. Murphy upgraded the pass game with 371 yards vs. Fresno and 358 vs App St (3 other 100+ games) but had 130 vs. Wake and was benched 2Q vs Lafayette. Johnson led the comeback win and started vs Wash St but was injured. He hit 39-42-286 vs SHSt, but he and Murphy combined for 11-25-100 vs Tulsa. True Frosh Trisian Tia led two scoring drives 4Q vs Tulsa, then hit 28-41240 vs Wash St in the final. Only Murphy is back. They added Braden Atkinson (PS#168), who threw for 3,596 (66%, 34-11) with Mercer and Brady Jones, who threw for 4,458 (64%) with 44 td at JUCO in '23 and had 3 starts at Western Michigan last year. The three QB's had a 14-13 ratio last year so should have their best numbers the last 3 years. It is a legitimate 3-QB race with no favorite coming out of spring. RUNNING BACKS - The top 3 rushers departed in '24 (#1, 1,185, 6.1). They added PS#34 Anthony Hankerson (319, 4.1 Colorado) and true frosh Cornell Hatcher (PS#153). Hankerson led with 1,082 (4.7, 15 TD). Last year Hankerson had 204 vs Lafayette and 166 vs SHSt and topped 1,000 again with Hatcher a distant #2 (292, 5.6). This year they lose Hankerson (1086, 4.4). The Beavers add in AJ Newberry (PS#105, 338, 4.3 3Y Vandy) and rFr Kourdey Glass (PS#98) and Skyler Jackson (PS#156). They are less experienced and it will be tough to keep that 1,000-yard streak going. HC Shephard feels it is one of the best position groups on the team as he has a lot of potential contributors. RECEIVERS - In '24 they lost their #1 (746, 13.8), #2 (718, 16.3) WR's and top TE (#3, 438, 15.1). Trent Walker became the go-to WR, leading with 901 (11.1). Last year they lost their TE (11 st, #2, 375, 16.3) and #4 (266, 11.6) receiver but added in Miami, Fla (PS#5) and BYU (PS#17) TE's. Walker led with 823 (12.1) and David Wells was #2 (466, 10.6). This year they must replace their top 4 receivers. The top returnees are TE Gabe Milbourn (185, 10.9) and Eddie Freauff (144, 12.0). The Beavers add in 3 FCS transfers with 550+ yards last year, plus Aaron Butler (PS#28, Texas) and Aeryn Hampton (PS#31 Alabama). True Frosh WR Powell could emerge as one of the top guys and Xavyion Noland was the top guy out of spring. OFFENSIVE LINE - Last year they lost 5 of the top 6 OL. They added in 3 transfers (none full-time starters). With just 44 career starts and less mobility at QB, I said the numbers would drop and they did to 124 (3.6) with 26 sacks. This year they lose 8 OL (37/65). They return 3 OL that started 6+ games last year, but the career starts drop a little to 32. They do have OL with 32 FCS starts and should have improved numbers as they are more experienced overall. RT Josiah Tomoteo has NFL potential and RG Tyler Voltin anchors the interior. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the unit had zero starters back, losing 83% of the sacks. They did add 5 transfers but none started. Injuries then hit and they had to move a TE and OL in to help. Only one 300 lb DL contributed (#18 tkl'r). The smaller speedier unit was overrun early, got better mid-year but still allowed 186 (5.3) rush and was dead last in the FBS with just 7 sacks. Last year they lost one starter but returned 6 DL who drew starts and improved to allowing 157 (4.6) rush with 15 sacks. This year they lose 5 DL (30 st, 120 tkl, 6 sk. They do return 3 DL that had 5+ starts (75 tkl, 4 sk) and add in 3 transfers and could improve again. The line does lack depth but has 3 solid DL in 345-lb DT Jacob Schuster, NG Daniel Matagi (disruptive) and DE Takari Hickle, who could not be blocked in the spring. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they had to replace all 4 starters, and perhaps this unit's inexperience contributed to the poor rush D and low sack numbers. Last year, their top two (#2, #4 tkl'r) departed. They returned Dexter Foster (4 st), who was #5 tackler as a true frosh, and NB Sailasa Vadrawale (8 st, #10). They also added Raesjon Davis (PS#8 USC). Davis was OFY after 3 starts and Foster after 7 (yet still #4 tklr). This year, they lose Foster but return Vadrawale (#6 tklr), Aiden Sullivan (#2 tklr), get Davis back and add in Idaho's #1 tackler Dylan Layne. This unit is the most experienced in 3 years and HC Shephard feels it is not only one of the top 3 units on the team, but also the deepest and most talented on the defensive side. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '22 all four starters returned and I said they should have their best finish in our PDR since 2014 (#31). OSU jumped all the way up to #6 (11-12 ratio). In '23 they lost 3 starters (#7DC) and dropped to #51 (62%, 23-12). In '24 they lost two starters and, paired with a weak front 7, OSU dropped to #89 (59.9%, 15-5). Last year, they lost 2 DB (comb 17 sts). They were more experienced with a stronger front and coach Bray compared the unit to the 2022 group. They did move up, but only to #69 (61%, 24-12). This year they lose their #1 tackler Skyler Thomas and 3 other DB (18 st, 93 tkl). They have two starters back again and could finish in the same areas despite losing their top guy. NEW MEXICO LOBOS QB JACK LAYNE POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Last year their starter who had 2,768 yds pass (58%, 12-12, 1166 rush) transferred to Utah. Idaho transfer Jack Layne started vs Oregon in '24 hurt his collarbone (missed 7 gm) then started the last 5 and threw for 1,472 (65%, 14-4) for the Vandals. Layne had his ups and down here in '25 with 4 int's vs Michigan and 3 vs San Jose but threw for 2486 (65%, 13-10) with 152 rush. James Laubstein hit 10-14-96-2-0 but was used more as a runner and was #3 rusher (363, 6.2). He won his waiver for an extra year and again figures into the offensive plans. Layne is back and rFr Toa Faavae (PS#126, fastest QB) had impressive bowl practices. The Lobos add in Luke Moga (PS#32) who ran a 10.4 100M and got in 3 games with Oregon as a rFr. This unit should have improved numbers in 2026 and it would not surprise me if Moga winds up battling for the top spot. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they lost their #1 (1063, 7.2), #2 (382, 5.2) and #3 (277, 6.9) RB's. They added Scottre Humphrey who had 1,386 (7.0) with Montana St, Damon Bankston who rushed for 1,104 (6.2) with Weber St, Deshaun Buchanan (567, 7.2 Idaho) and CUSA Frosh of the year DJ McKinney (481, 5.0 SHSt). The unit was productive with Bankston leading with 635 (5.8, #3 rec 397), McKinney #2 (464, 5.4) and Humphrey #4 (349, 4.5). This year the Lobos must replace the top two. They add in Kiefer Sibley (PS#101, 274, 6.1 NTexas), Cameron Matthews (Memphis), rFr Darrion Bowere (PS#254) and true frosh Jerod Terry (PS#83). The unit should be just as productive. Humphrey is a bigger physical back and Matthews makes guys miss. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost their top 7 receivers with the top two having 840 and 747 yards. They added Keagan Johnson (PS#69, 359, 12.4 Kan St) but were an inexperienced group. Johnson led with 772 (12.7) while TE Dorian Thomas was #2 (560, 10.0), TE Cade Keith was #4 (253, 12.7) and Shawn Miller #5 (199, 13.3). This year they lose their top two but add in 5 transfers including Troy Omeire (PS#17!, #2, 514, 16.6 UNLV), Miles Williams (12 st, 524, 12.7 EWash) and TE Joey Olsen (PS#16 USC) so are more experienced overall and should have increased production. OFFENSIVE LINE - In 2023 they returned four starters plus and were much improved with 193 (5.3) rush and just 19 sacks allowed. In '24 they lost all five starters, but added eight transfers and I projected five transfers to start. The unit gelled together quicker than you would expect and New Mexico ran for 254 (6.7). They allowed just 5 sacks! Last year they lost 4 starters. They added six transfers but I said with the switch of offense plus losing their dangerous running QB it would be tough to get near 24's stats. The Lobos had 155 (4.3) rush with 30 sacks. This year they lose 4 OL (20/44) but have have 3+ starters back and add in Weber St starter LT Cole Millward so are much more experienced and in the 2nd year of the offense. Kaden Robnett and Malik Aliane are the top guys of a now veteran front. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they allowed 213 (5.4) rush with only 11 sacks. Last year they lost 6 DL who combined for 34 starts. DT Gabriel Lopez was back and they added two Idaho transfers (Idaho allowed 142, 3.9, 28 sk) including 1st Tm Big Sky DE Keyshawn James-Newby (65 tkl, 10.5 sk) and 331 lb Texas Southern transfer Brian Booker. It proved to be a solid unit cutting it to 113 (3.4) rush with 33 sacks! This year they lose DE James-Newby (#7 DC PHI) (13 st #4 tklr, 9 sk), DE Brett Karhu (12 st, 26 tkl, 7.5 sk) and DT Lopez (9 st, 14 tkl, 2 sk). They add in 4 transfers but are less experienced and figure to take a step back. DT is the strength of the team led by Booker but DE may be the biggest question mark. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they allowed foes 132 ypg above their average (#132). Last year they returned their #3 and #4 tacklers but the two combined for 2 starts (39 tkl) in '25. The Lobos added 1st Tm Big Sky LB Jaxton Eck (134 tkl). I called them an underrated unit. New Mexico was vastly improved holding foes to 34 ypg below their average and Eck was the Mountain West Defensive Player of the Year! This year everyone is back including Mercury Swaim (#4 tklr) so this unit could be the MW's best. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In 2023 were #128 in the PDR (61%, 24-4) and in '24 dropped to #130 (65%, 30-3!). Last year they lost all 4 starters (#1, #2, #5, #7 tklrs). They added seven transfers and got back Tavian Combs (miss '24, 25 car sts). They were banged up some during the year but still managed to rise to #111 in my PDR (69%, 16-9). This year they lose two starters (#3, #9 tklr). Frankie Edwards took Abraham Williams spot the last 6 and true Frosh CJ McBean was #7 tackler. They add in 4 transfers. CB Ormanie Arnold and FS Austin Brawley are the top guys and they should make a solid jump in the PDR. SPECIAL TEAMS - New Mexico has not blocked a punt in 16 years (longest streak FBS). In '24 they moved ST RANK L6Y: up to #107 in the STR. Last year new P Daniel 2025 ..... #9 Hughes was a huge addition and avg 45.9 with 2024 .. #107 . #129 a 43.6 net! Damon Bankston had a 100 yard KR 2023 2022 ....#74 td and DJ McKinney a PR td. Luke Krzewiecki 2021.... #98 hit 15-16 FG and the Lobos were #22 in my STR 2020 .. #101 (best s/'18). This year they lose their all 4 guys and figure to take a Stock Market drop in the rankings. They do add Cal P Michael Kern (41.5 net) and Wagner's K (13-14). COACHES - Jason Eck was the HC at Idaho where he was 26-13 making the playoffs in each of his 3 years. Last year his 9 wins topped Marv Levy's 7 in 1958 and Buff Henry's 8 in 1934 for most wins by a first year HC here. His OC is Luke Schleusner (Schlice-ner) who was the OC at Idaho the last 3 years. The 2nd DC is Spence Nowitsky who was Miami,Oh DC ('18-'21), Ohio ('22-'23) and Memphis DC ('24). The 2nd year Special teams Coordinator is Daniel DaPrato who was STC with South Florida ('20-'22) and interim HC '22. He was also STC at Arkansas ('19) and Montana St ('13-'15). AIR FORCE FALCONS RB OWEN ALLEN POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - The last 3 years Air Force has had zero experience at QB and last year once again they only returned 28 snaps (14 att) at the position all belonging to Josh Johnson. They even used 245 lb FB Kemper Hodges (PS#148QB) at QB in the spring. Johnson and Liam Szarka split snaps in game one. Szarka soon took over and the offense ignited. He became the ﬁrst QB in Air Force history with ﬁve straight 100+ rush games and the ﬁrst QB in the FBS since Lamar Jackson to have 3 straight 200+ pass and 100+ rush games. Szarka was OFY vs UConn and Hodges and Johnson took the rest of the snaps. Szarka is 100% recovered from his forearm fracture. Szarka is back and not only for the ﬁrst time in 4 years do they have an experienced starter back, they have three! They did keep Hodges at FB. RUNNING BACKS - This unit took a big hit entering '23 as they lost a FB who led the FBS in rush yards (1728 yards) and was MW Offensive POY in '22. In '24 they lost their FB (#1, 950, 4.7). The top RB back was FB Dylan Carson (1 st, 493, 7.3) who had 323 yards in the 3 games the starter missed. Carson was banged up early but had 447 yards the ﬁnal 4 games and led with 600 (4.3). FB Owen Allen added 335 (4.4). The Superback (FB) position had averaged 2063 yards from '21-'23 but had just 1224 in '24. All the top guys were back in '25 and Allen led with 750 (5.7), Carson was #3 (QB #1) with 418 (4.6) and SB Cade Harris #4 (321, 5.3) and was also #1 receiver (584, 16.7). This year they only return Allen but should match last years numbers and as pointed out have gone through this type of attrition before. RECEIVERS - While Air Force runs the triple option, the receiver position is still a key one in this offense as they are often key blockers and can leak free for big plays down the ﬁeld. In '24 Quin Smith led with just 207 (20.7). Last year they threw more and TE Bruin Fleischmann was #2 (SB #1) with 370 (17.6), Quin Smith was #3 (358, 23.9) and Jonah Dawson #4 (260, 21.7). This year the top three depart but the unit has more yards returning than it did last year. OFFENSIVE LINE - Air Force's OLine is nicknamed "The Diesel" and in 2023 the unit lost an AA RG (13/22) and a 1st Tm MW LT (13/25) but returned 62 career starts and paved the way for 282 rush ypg (5.1) however they ﬁnished #2 FBS in rushing, snapping their streak. In '24 they lost all seven OL who started a game in '23 (3 all MW OL) and the line was shufﬂed due to injuries early. Over the last four games they rushed for 302 (4.6) but on the year were at just 224 (4.0). Last year they lost two starters. The career starts went from 0 to 30 and I said the Diesel would be back in 2025 and they were a Joe Moore Award semi-ﬁnalist. They started the same ﬁve each of the ﬁrst 9 games and improved to 261 (4.8) with 16 sacks. This year the lose 3 starters but they match '25's 30 career starts and remain strong. G TJ Tarascio and RT Luke Vonderhaar look like the top guys from a strong unit. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the lone starter back was NG Payton Zdroik (8 st, 32 tkl, 4.5 tﬂ, 4th Tm MW) and he was banged up. AF allowed 153 (4.6) with just 18 sacks. Last year they lost a DT (10 st, 20 tkl, 1 sk) but the top 3 tacklers were back and all three were all-conf candidates. The numbers were only similar with 159 (5.2) rush allowed and 16 sacks. This year the top 3 are all gone. They return six DL that saw action last year and while this unit is clearly less experienced last year's rush D and sack numbers were unusually poor for a Falcon defense that did not allow over 3.8 ypc rush from '18-'23 and I look for a stronger rush D and more sacks. LINEBACKERS - Air Force lost two starters then lost their SPUR week 1 in '23 but still held teams to 82 ypg below their season average (#9 FBS). In '24 they again lost their #1 and #2 tacklers. This time AF held foes to 37 ypg below avg (#45). Last year they lost their #3, #4, #5 and #6 tacklers. They returned their #7 tackler and had ﬁve LB's with starting experience. AF still allowed teams 44 ypg above their average (#115). Eight different LB's started and 7 return making them the polar opposite of the last two years and they should have a Stock Market bounce in the avg they allow to opponents. Blake Fletcher had 108 tackles and Issac Hubert is a great leader for a top notch LB corps. DEFENSIVE BACKS - Air Force's pass D has ﬁnished outside the top 50 in every season since 2010 and dropped to #114 (65%, 12-4) in '24. Last year they lost 3 starters. They did return 3 DB's who each started 4+ games in '24. By midseason 9 different DB's started and vs Wyoming it was a Soph and 3 Frosh! Air Force fell to #134 in the PDR (69.6%, 17-7). This year they lose one CB (6 st, 29 tkl, 1 int, 1 pbu) but last years unusually young secondary got better late in the year and should grow in leaps and bounds and make a large jump in the PDR. SPECIAL TEAMS - Air Force has had six top 40 STR ﬁnishes under HC Calhoun. In '24 they were just ST RANK L6Y: #132 despite a star K. Last year they lost their all 2025 .. #121 time leading scorer in K Matthew Dapore (9-15 2024...#132 L/45). P Luke Freer had a school record 47.5 2023 ....#81 per punt in '24, topping Mark Simon's 1985 mark 2022 ....#91 #118 (47.3) and last year it was 44.5 (41.4 net). Their 2021.. 2020 ...#111 K hit 3-6 missing game tying FG's vs Navy and UNLV so Reagan Tubbs took over and hit the GW vs Wyoming and was 7-9 (L52). AF was just #121 in the STR and lose both K and P (career avg leader here). COACHES- Coaching consistency runs strong at Air Force, COACHES as Falcons' alumnus Troy Calhoun enters his 20th season as HC in 'The Springs' with a record of 135-89 & leads all active MW coaches with 80 conference wins. OC Mike Thiessen the longest tenured OC in nation, 13th year. New DC Steve Russ was DC here ('14-'17)and LB coach in NFL ('18-'23) UAB DC ('25) and returns. Tim Horton is the ST coordinator. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In 2023 they lost their long-time QB and 3x leading rusher at FB. My computer (pg 41) called for 27.7 ppg and 365.1 ppg and AF hit those numbers on the head with 27.8 ppg and 366.5 ypg!! In '24 they had just two starters back (0 OL strs). In the ﬁrst 4 games vs non service academy teams they had just 243 ypg. Over the last six they had 385 ypg. Last year my computer called for an increase from 19 ppg to 26.6 and they even topped that with 29.8 ppg. This time AF topped 30 pts in each of the ﬁrst 6 games for the ﬁrst time since 1998 with Szarka at QB. The offense had 38.3 ppg the ﬁrst 6 but just 21.3 ppg the last 6. For the ﬁrst time in 4 years they have experience at QB and should resemble that 1H offense of '25. DEFENSE - In '23 with an unusually veteran defense my computer called for them to allow 276.5 ypg and 16 ppg and they gave up 278 ypg and 18.2 ppg!! In '24 just four starters were back and my computer called for a slight slip back to 22.0 ppg and 323 ypg and they were right there at 23.3 ppg and 342 ypg! Last year with 5 starters back they surprisingly had their worst D in 8 years allowing 423 ypg and 30.3 ppg! The young D did allow just 349 ypg the last 4 games and now have another unusually veteran D with 8 starters back and should have a Stock Market type improvement. 2026 - AF is 82-32 at home (46-11 s/'14) under Calhoun. In '21 they had the ﬁrst undefeated season on the road since 1992. In '22 the new rule changes on cut blocks slowed the offense. AF was 40-12 the previous 4 full seasons heading into 2024. AF only had 6 starters back and by playing so many super seniors left little time to develop the roster like they normally do. AF opened a poor 1-7 but then the young team came together winning the last 4 games by 12 ppg! Last year they had 13 starters back including 8 on offense. I put Air Force on my Most Improved List but they were a rare team on the list to not go from a losing record to a bowl. They had three 3 point losses where they missed a late FG and lost to UConn when QB Szarka was injured 2Q and after a 1-5 start went 3-3 for a 4-8 ﬁnish. They rate a +3 in my Stock Market Indicator. The last time AF had B2B losing seasons they bounced back the next year (2019) and went 11-2. They have an experienced QB for once and this looks like the veteran defense they had in '23 when they allowed just 278 ypg. I will call for Air Force to at least double last years win total and I think they are a legitimate contender in the reformed MW! HAWAI'I RAINBOW WARRIORS WR POFELE ASHLOCK #3, #4 and #8 receivers. With Cenacle missing most of '25 they are in about the same shape plus add in 6 transfers. Pofele Ashlock was the Hawaii Bowl MVP and is tough to cover and Washington transfer Audric Harris will be a force. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they had six different starting lineups due to injuries and they opened holes for just 98 (3.4) rush with 43 sacks allowed. Last year they lost three OL (24/78) but went from having two starters back to 3+ so were more experienced. I said it could be Chang's best OLine in his four years. In the run and shoot offense they did have just 103 (3.6) rush with 31 sacks (6.1%) on 491 passes. This year they lose 3 OL (35/66) so drop to two starters back and 35 career starts but remain a strong unit. C Ethan Spencer and LT Dean Briski are the top guys and return at those important spots and HC Chang feels the OLine is improved this year. DEFENSIVE LINE - Last year they lost 5 DL (comb 30 sts, 11 sk) They had three DL back that started and added four transfers and were more experienced than '24. They used a deep rotation and did indeed improve to allowing 134 (4.2) rush with 30 sacks. This year they lose six DL (41 st, 20 sk) including their top two sack guys in DE Jackie Johnson (7.5 sk) and De'Jon Benton (5.5). They add in 7 transfers (see PSL) but figure to take a step back this year. Lesterlaisene Lagafuaina and Luther McCoy are the top guys up front. LINEBACKERS - Last year the Lion's Den returned their #1 tackler Jamih Otis, #6 Jalen Smith and #10 NB Elijah Palmer. They did lose their #2 and #7 tacklers. I called it one of the top units in the MW and UH held foes to 9 ypg below their average. This year they lose Smith (13 st, #2 tklr) plus their #8 tackler but with Otis (#3 tklr) and Palmer (#4) both back they remain one of the MW's top LB corps. Wynden Ho'ohuli (PS#30) came in as a 300 lb DL and is down to 240 and could be a force at the open WLB spot. Otis is recovering from an ACL but should be full go by the start of the year. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In 2024 the Warriors were only #107 in the PDR. Last year they lost one starter but got back Virdel Edwards (2 yr str miss '24) so basically had four starters back after having just two back in '24. They had 7 DB's with starting experience and added 3 transfers so I looked for them to get that large jump in the PDR I was expecting in '24 and they did moving up to #65 (58%, 13-8). This year they lose all 4 starters including FS Peter Manuma (13 st #1 tklr, 6 pbu) plus a pair of backups. They add 5 transfers including Caleb "C-Bo" Brown who was their shut down CB in '24 and spent last year at Virg Techand FS Matagi Thompson is a 6'2" 4 year vet but I expect a Stock Market bounce down in the PDR. SPECIAL TEAMS - Last year they lost their P (40.2 net). Kansei Matsuzawa hit 12-16 FG (L/41). They ST RANK L6Y: did not sign a P until after the magazine went to 2025 ... #38 press. UH was only #124 in the STR in '24 but 2024 ..#124 made a huge jump to #38 last year. The "Tokyo 2023 .. #121 Toe" Matsuzawa hit 25-26 FG (L52) and was a 2022 ... #93 Groza Finalist. True Frosh P Billy Gowers avg 2021.... #95 46.3 (40.8 net). Cam Barfield had a 86 yd KR TD. 2020 ....#87 This year they lose their super K and P and figure to drop some. COACHES - UH legend Timmy Chang, who holds the record here for career pass yards (17,072), enters year 5 as the HC here. Chang took over the play calling mid-year '23. The 2nd year OC is Anthony Arceneaux who was the RB coach in '24. The 2nd year DC is Dennis Thurman who was DC for both the Jets and Bills in the NFL and at Jackson St ('20-'22). Thomas Sheffield is in year four as the ST coordinator. POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 true frosh Micah Alejado (PS#70) enrolled in January. He hit 11-12-111 in relief vs Utah St then got the start in the finale and hit 37-57-469 with 5 td's guiding the win over New Mexico! The Alejado era was officially started. Alejado is just 5'10" 180 but is a lefty with good arm strength a quick release and high football IQ. He looked great vs Stanford but was injured. He started vs Arizona and hobbled around then was injured more. He missed two games and was never 100% the rest of the year. Luke Weaver was 2-0 as a starter vs SHSt and Port St and threw for 600 (605, 5-3). Alejado threw for 3106 (66%, 24-9) but only had 105 rush. Weaver left for San Jose so they add Virginia transfer Bjorn Jurgensen (PS#48) and true frosh Maika Eugenio (PS#101) was IFS. HC Chang is high on all 3 QB's and Jurgensen has a great arm and is the fastest of the 3. NORTH DAKOTA STATE DT KEENAN WILSON POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Cole Payton (PS#207) was a heralded recruit and dressed for every game in '21. In '22 Payton played in 13 (8-12-51-0-1). In '23 Payton made a huge impact on the ground, rushing for 615 (7.3) and 13 td's. He also threw for 289 yards (67%, 3-0). In '24 their 3rd year starter Cam Miller set career highs with 73.5%, 3,251 passing, 33 pass td's (only 4 int's), 631 rushing (4.4, 12 td's) and was 1st Tm AA. He became the 3rd Bison QB to be drafted (#6DC LV). Payton played a much smaller role, throwing for 123 (63%, 2-1) and rushed for 168 (3.6). Nathan Hayes threw for 214 (63%, 3-0, 90 rush). Payton was the starter last year and was solid throwing for 2719 (72%, 16-4) with 777 rush and was 2nd tm AA (#5 DC PHI) . Hayes threw for 381 and passed for 88 and is the heir apparant. Trey Drake (PS#327), rFr Zander Smith (PS#198) and Preston Brown (PS#208) will contend. Hayes will be solid but the numbers will likely drop some again. This is a position that has had 5 straight NFL draft picks so the history says the unit will be very productive once again. RUNNING BACKS - NDSU has an explosive run game that is typically a committee between multiple RB's, their QB and FB's. In '24 four of their top five rushers returned. Last year their #1 rusher (1,181, 4.8, 15 td) transferred to Miami, Fla and they lost their #3 RB (4 st, 168, 3.6, 197 rec). They added transfers DJ Scott (PS#270, Kenn St) & Cortez LeGreant (Minn). FB Truman Werremeyer (2nd Tm MVFC) was back along with #2 rusher Baricka Kpeenu (725, 5.5). Kpeenu led with 1005 (5.3) and he departs as does their FB. Scott was #3 rusher (QB #2) with 502 (5.3) and LeGrant was #4 (131, 5.2) and both return. Myles Mitchell (PS#219, 78, 4.3), Barry Kpeenu (PS#266), rFr Charles Ross and Brad Wavrenek add depth. They should be close to '25's standards but will miss Barika's home run ability. RECEIVERS - In '24 NDSU lost their top two but did return their #3, #4 and #5 receivers. Bryce Lance, brother of NFL QB Trey Lance, led with 1,071 (14.3) and was #1 in the Valley with 17 receiving td's! Four others topped 300 yards. Lance was 25-375 in their four playoff games Last year they lost their #3 and #4 receivers. The Bison got back Lance, plus their #2 Chris Harris (2 st, 392, 13.5) and RaJa Nelson who missed 8 games and still had 256 (9.8). This year they lose Lance (#4 DC NO) (#1, 1079, 21.1), Nelson (#2, 404, 14.4) and a TE (7 st, 8 rec). They return Jackson Williams (#4, 293, 17.2) and TE Reis Kessel (#3, 335, 22.3) plus Mekhi Collins (303, 18.9 '24, 6-159 '25) but need a go to WR to emerge. OFFENSIVE LINE - This has been one of the premier O-Line's in the FCS. They rushed for over 200 ypg each year from 2012 to 2023. In '24 two starters returned and we said this was their youngest Oline in some time. NDSU dipped to 193 ypg and below 5.0 ypc for the first time since '13! They allowed 20 sacks for the 2nd straight season. Last year they lost a 1st Tm FCS AA LT (highest drafted OL FCS history #1 DC) but had three starters back including C Trent Fraley (3rd Tm). They've had 6 OL drafted in the past 13 years and have recovered well each year. NDSU got back to 213 ypg rush (5.2) with 21 sacks. This year they lose 1st tm AA (FCS OL year) C Trent Fraley (to MichSt) and a 1st tm MVFC LT but with 3 starters back remain a premium outfit. The addition of Kansas transfer Kene Anene solidified the unit in the spring. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 nine of their top 12 returned. NDSU allowed 124 ypg (4.0) with 34 sacks. Last year they lost three All-Valley DL's (#2, 9, 10 tklr). They had just 5 of their top 12 back but improved to allowing 104 (3.2) with 33 sacks. This year they lose 2 starters including 2nd tm MVFC DE Toby Anene (7 sk) but have 9 of the top 12 back so could be even stronger. HC Polasek is high on the unit calling it the heart and soul of the defense and they are led by DT Keenan Wilson and DE's Kelton McCaslin and Matthew Stenbroten. LINEBACKERS - In '23 Logan Kopp was was 1st Tm (#2 tklr). This unit was the strength of the defense. Five of their top seven tacklers were LB's. Kopp was their #1 tackler and led with 3 int's. Last year he was back but they lost their #3, 4, 5, 7 and 15 tacklers. NDSU held foes to 122 ypg below their average (#1). This year they lose 1st tm AA Kopp and their #3 tackler Nathaniel Staheling (trans to Mich). They add in a 3rd tm Ivy LB from Cornell and return #1 tackler Donovan Woolen (best overall player on D) but are down a few notches in 2026. HC Polasek does ike the length and athleticism of the unit and Gavin Sell should emerge in his first year as a starter. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23 NDSU lost their top five DB's. SS Cole Wisniewski led the FCS with 8 int's. NDSU posted better numbers (186 pass ypg, 61%, 16-21) but only finished #3 in Pass D in the Valley. In '24 they lost one starter (#6 tklr) then Wisniewski was OFY in August. A SS was OFY after 8 starts. NDSU allowed 197 pass ypg (61%, 17-11) and were #3 again the Valley. Last year they had 2.5 starters back and allowed 148 ypg (54%, x-x). This year they lose 4 DB who combined for 29 starts (#6, 7 and 8 tklr) but return 3 DB who combined for 23 starts (#4, 9, 15 tklr). This is a solid secondary and could be improved despite tougher foes this year. SPECIAL TEAMS - Last year they lost both their P and K. New K Eli Ozick was 3rd tm AA hitting 16-18 FG ST RANK LY: and had 54 TB on 91 KO's. P Aaron Bickerton is 2025 ...#37* back and had a 39.5 net plus they get back super return man Jackson Williams who avg 32.1 on KR's and 13.9 on PR's. NDSU would have been #37 in our STR last year and if the find a K could be in the top 25 in year one! COACHES - 3rd year HC Tim Polasek is won a National Title in his first year. He previously coached here from '06-'12 (RB Cch) and '14-'16 as OC. Polasek was OC/QB Coach under former NDSU Craig Bohl at Wyoming ('21-'23). He was also OL Coach at Iowa ('17-'20). 2nd year OC Dan Larson was OL coach here ('20-'24). Former NDSU SS Grant Olson took overin '24 as DC. This is his 8th year coaching at NDSU. He was ST Coor in '23. Nick Goeser is his 17th year at NDSU but 3rd as Co-DC. The STC is Carleton Littlejohn. He was DE coach in '24 and is in 2nd year as STC. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE -In '24 NDSU lost their top rusher, top two receivers and three starting OL. NDSU still avg'd 38.1 ppg (#1 in MVFC) but dipped to 418 ypg (#4 MVFC). Last year they lost a 4 year starting QB, their top RB and two starting OL. Their QB and LT were drafted. Six starters returned. They improved to 444 ypg and 41 ppg! This year they lose their QB, top RB, top 2 WR and both OT's. This offense has been consistently strong and remains that way. They are taking a step up in level of competition so will probably take a step back in the offensive production numbers this year. DEFENSE - NDSU hadn't allowed over 300 ypg in back-toback seasons since '10 & '11 but allowed 302 ypg and 19.9 ppg in '23. In '24 the Bison had 17 of their top 22 back their SS (#1 tklr) was OFY in August. They allowed 18.6 ppg and 321 ypg (3rd straight year 300+) but held foes 81 ypg below their avg. Last year NDSU returned 5 starters. They only returned 3 of their top 10 tacklers. We said NDSU reloads and should be among the top D's in the FCS and they were allowing just 252 ypg, 13 ppg and held foes to 122 ypg below avg (#1 FCS). This year they have 5 returning starters and will be one of the MWs best. They have 3 of the top 5 tacklers back but are facing tougher foes. 2026 - North Dakota St has won 10 of the last 15 FCS National Titles. North Dakota St is is now 46-2-2 in its yearly Harvest bowl game. They did not win the title in '22 or '23. In '24 HC Entz left to be LB Coach at USC. They brought in Tim Polasek for his 3rd stint here. NDSU beat Abilene Christian, #8 Mercer, #2 SDSt and #1 Montana St to win the National Title. They finished 14-2, were +96 ypg and +109 vs the Valley. The Bison were +18 TO's (+19 in '23). Last year they had 11 starters back again but had to replace a 4Y starting QB and their highest drafted OL in school history. North Dakota St was #1 AP and appeared on their way to another national title going 12-0 including a road win at South Dakota St 38-7. They shockingly blew a two score lead against Illinois St as 24 point favorites and were eliminated in the first playoff game 29-28! This year the Bison join the FBS and move to the MWC so welcome to my magazine. North Dakota St is 9-5 vs FBS teams since 2004. The Bison have a culture of a strong run game, great QB play and a rock ribbed defense and should continue that even stepping up to a higher level of competition. Not only will they be traveling to spots they have not been but they face the leagues other top 4 teams (UNLV, NMex, AF, Hawaii) all on the road and those are all unique and tough venues. The Bison are a legitimate contender in their first year of the MW but must be road warriors to get to the title game. 2026 PROJECTED STARTING LINEUP Jersey # Jersey # in Green in Green DEFENSE QB 2 Nathan Hayes Sr. 6-3 218 PS#200. 10 gm, 381 (57%, 4-1) LY. 10 Trey Drake (6'3" 206 Jr) PS#327. NEVADA WOLF PACK OFFENSIVE LINE - Former HC Chris Ault nicknamed this RB DOMINIC KELLY POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '22 & '23 combined Nevada QB's tossed 13 TD passes with 20 interceptions. They added a PS#35 Colorado transfer who won the job and was a vastly improved QB hitting 68% with a 16-7 ratio and was the teams #1 rusher (775, 4.9)! He transferred to Memphis last year. Chubba Purdy (PS#24) from Nebraska hit 18-25-239 in '24 and AJ Bianco 1624-173. Purdy was one of the fastest players on the team and won the job . True Frosh Carter Jones had a solid 2H vs Fresno and took the job over the rest of the year. Jones threw for 1002 (64%, 6-8). Purdy was used as a QB/RB/WR the rest of the year and in Jones' 7 starts Purdy had as many TD's (2 rush/2 pass) and Jones did (4 pass). Bianco hit 27-45-188 in 10 games. Jones and Bianco return plus they add in UCLA transfer Luke Duncan (PS#32) who started vs Ohio St last year (21-34-235). Duncan is 6'6" 210 and athletic. They should have improved numbers after the unit had a combined 10-17 ratio last year. Jones would be much improved if he wins job and Duncan is accurate but the ratio will be much improved. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they lost their top three RB's (comb 1193 yd). They added Herschel Turner (PS#194, 405, 5.1 Utah St) and brought back Caleb Ramseur (2 st, #5 110, 3.4). UTEP MINERS DB KAM THOMAS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Austin Peay transfer Skyler Locklear won a close battle in '24 lost it, won it back, was injured, and threw for 1583 (64%, 10-6) yards. Last year they added in PS#1 Malachi Nelson who started the first 5 and threw for 404 yards vs ULM but after 4 int's vs LTech, Locklear started the rest of the year. Locklear threw for 1418 (55%, 13-11) and also was #2 rusher with 396 (3.8). This year both depart. EJ Colson (PS#88) had 1 start for UCF as a true then last year as a rFr took over an started 9 games for Incarnate Word throwing for 2142 (71%, 16-4) with 287 rush. RFr Chad Warner (PS#88) is back plus they add in Raymond Moore who had 7 starts as a Frosh for Morgan St (1042, 54%, 9-7) and true Frosh Bodey Weaver (PS#75). I look for Colson to have a solid year and improve on the teams 21-20 ratio from last year and all 4 QB's have solid mobility and are run threats. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they lost their #1 (754, 3.9), #2 (248, 3.9) and #3 (24, 2.4) RB's. They added Hahsaun Wilson (559, 6.1 Charlotte) and rFr Ashten Emory (PS#185). They had added speed. Wilson had a school record 94 yard run vs UTM and was #1 rusher after 5 weeks with 205 yards but was injured and finished #3 (225, 4.9). Ashten Emory had 15-96 vs Sam Houston then 18-181 vs NMSt (most in a game here s/Aaron Jones 301 -'16) and led with 569 (4.8). QB Locklear was #2 rusher. Wilson was third with 225 (4.9). This year they lose the top three. Added in are UTEP native Tavorus Jones (PS#14!) who had 183 yards in 4 years at Missouri, Lamar Sperling (PS#160) who had 234 (6.0) for Buffalo and rFr Josh Bell (PS#172). I look for this group to top '25's numbers and HC Walden calls them an explosive twitchy group. RECEIVERS - In '24 the top 4 receivers hit the portal (incl 1033, 21.5, 1st Tm CUSA). Kenny Odom led with 741 (16.1). Last year they lost their #3 (469, 10.0) WR and TE (10 st, 12 rec). They were much more experienced. RFr Wondame Davis was #4 in the FBS with 23.5 ypc and led with 610 yards. Odom was #2 (582, 9.4). Kam Thomas (#2, '24 532, 11.3) was OFY after one start. This year they lose the top 7 receivers. Thomas does return as does EKU transfer Jaden Smith who was OFY in July plus they add in 1st tm Big Sky Carver Cheeks (929, 13.1). Despite the losses this unit could be upgraded. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they lost all 5 starters but did bring in two Austin Peay starting OL and Walden really liked the unit. They opened slow with 77 (2.5) in non conf play with OFFENSE Jersey # in Orange 12 sacks but improved to 143 (3.6) rush in CUSA play with 17 sacks. Last year they lost 3 starters. The Miners have five rFr OL plus add in 5 transfers including starters from Cornell, Jackson St, SFAustin and Livingstone. RT Jaymon Lamb and LG Brian Williams are the leaders up front. They have 2 FBS career starts but 48 FCS starts and could improve on last years numbers if this group comes together quickly. DEFENSIVE LINE - In 2024 they allowed 179 (4.3) rush in CUSA play and the unit led CUSA in sacks and tfl's. Last year they lost four DL who combined for 31 starts and 20 sacks. They returned 3rd tm MW KD Johnson (12 st, 40 tkl, 3.5 sk) and added in 5 transfers and were in the same shape as '24 and just as productive allowing 170 (4.1) rush with 28 sacks and UTEP was #8 in the FBS in tfl's. This year they lose 7 DL (35 sts, 19.5 sk, 210 tkl). They are on par with last year experience wise with 1+ starters back in Ashton Coker (9 st) and Shakaun Bowser (4 st) plus add 4 transfers and could be near last years group if they develop some pass rushers and Sterling Miles and Derek Burns could be those guys. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they lost a LB that led the FBS in solo tackles (#4DC), their #2 and #10 tacklers. UTEP allowed foes 41 ypg above their average (#114). Davey was #1 in the FBS in tackles with 131 but missed the last game. New Mexico transfer Jayden Wilson was #2 tackler. They allowed foes 20 ypg above (#85). This year they lose their #1 and #10 tacklers. They add former QB Shay Smith (PS#120) and two transfers so are more experienced and could be come close to last years standards. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In '24 my computer only called for 22.7 ppg and 342 ypg and the Blue Blaze Offense came up just short with 19.5 ppg and 321 ypg. Last year they had six starters back and added a bunch of transfers so they had added size at both WR and OL. This time my computer called for 25 ppg and they came up a little short at 23 with 332 ypg. In the 1st 5 vs FBS foes UTEP had 14 ppg and in the last 6 it was 28 ppg and they should carry some of that momentum into this year. This is a more physcial team this year despite having zero returning starters on offense from last year they should have the best production in Waldens 3 years. DEFENSE - In 2024 they returned just 5 starters but HC Walden was very high on the defensive line. My computer called for them to allow 34.7 ppg but the Orange Swarm defense was slightly better at 32.3 ppg. Last year they had 5 starters back and my computer called for them to allow 30.1 ppg and they gave up 30.4 (miss by .3!). They were an outstanding #8 in the FBS in TFL's!! The defense is the veteran unit on the team as 3 of the top 6 tacklers are back and they hit some home runs in the transfer portal and should be improved again in 2026. 2026 - UTEP has not won a bowl game since 1967 (beat Johnny Vaught's Ole Miss team). In '21 they finished 7-5 with their first bowl bid since 2014 then went 5-7, 3-9 and 3-9. In '24 new HC Scotty Walden said he would abandon the JUCO heavy recruiting and bring in Texas high school recruits. He did supplement those freshmen with 10 transfers from his highly successful Austin Peay team that was 9-3. They faced an easier schedule and were +7 ypg in CUSA play in '23 despite their 2-6 record.The Miners opened 0-6 and went 3-9 again. UTEP has had just two winning seasons since 2005. Last year they were a bigger, stronger and faster team but in their last year in CUSA they went just 2-10. They were ahead or even in the last 18 minutes vs Jax St and Kenn St (2 title gm tms) but lost both. UTEP ended their 20 year run with CUSA and move to the Mountain West in 2026. They had the top recruiting class in CUSA (#2 in '23) in '24. There are plenty of signs pointing up this year. UTEP makes the Going Up Box for Turnovers=Turnaround (-12 '25) and had 3 Net Close Losses. Year 3 is the year new head coaches usually hit their stride. UTEP has 6 home games this year and some stability as 5 of the 6 are on a Saturday! The road slate is daunting with Oklahoma, Michigan, NMexico, NDakota St and Air Force but I will call for UTEP to at least win as many games this year as the first two years combined and give them a decent shot at a bowl as coach Walden has his best team. SAN JOSE STATE SPARTANS LB ETHAN POWELL POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 Walker Eget (PS#98) split the duties but started 7 games and threw for 2,504 (57%, 13-10) with 99 rush and shredded Boise for 446 pass yards. Battling for the backup job last year were Xaiver Ward (PS#66, Wash St/SHSt) plus true frosh Tama Amisone (PS#141) and Robert McDaniel (PS#44). Eget threw for 473 yards vs Stanford and 458 vs Hawaii. He was injured vs Wyoming with a 14 point lead and Amisone and Ward combined to hit 8-18-45. Ward was OFY vs SDSt. Eget threw for 3047 (59%, 17-9). His 3 backups combined to hit 44% with a 0-8 ratio! Amisone was the first true frosh to start here this Century (Marcus Arroyo 1998) and was used as run threat playing in 8 games. Eget departs so they bring in Luke Weaver (PS#166JC) who started two games for Hawaii last year (60%, 6-3, 115 rush). It is a 3 man battle for the starting job with True Frosh Daniel Rolovich in the mix and his is a big kid with a big arm. Weaver ran a similar offense and McDaniel can make all the throws. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they returned their #1 rusher Floyd Chalk (721, 4.7), Jabari Bates (#2, 254, 4.3) and Lamar Radcliffe who was #3 (141, 4.3) as a true frosh (7 games) and was the bowl's top rusher with 65 yards. Chalk had just 141 in the first 4 games and opted to redshirt to transfer. Bates took control with 131 vs Idaho and was #1 with 192 (7.1) but was OFY week 4. Radcliffe missed 4 full games and had 340 (5.2). They took the RS off Steve Chavez-Soto in week 5 and he had 102 vs Utah St and led with 448 (5.1). This year only Bates and Viliami Teu (PS#176, 70, 4.1) return. They add in rFr Sir Autry (5-10 165 PS#197), true Frosh Courshawn Hill (PS#94) and Tyler Jacklich who had 842 yards for Mercer in '24 (WVirg '25). This is an underwhelming unit but could top '25's production and should maintain better health. .RECEIVERS - Last year they lost a 1st Tm AA Nick Nash (12 st, 1382, 13.3) their #2 (13 st, 983, 18.5) and #3 (481, 17.2) WR's. Niumatalolo added Danny Scudero to take Nash's slot position and Purdue transfer Leland Smith as the speedy outside threat. He felt the unit was a deeper unit overall. Those two and Kyri Shoals became the first trio here to each top 100 yards in a game since 2013 and did it again vs Hawaii. Scudero set a school record for TD's in a game with 4 vs Wyoming. Scudero was a 1st tm AA and Biletnikoff Finalist (1291, 14.7). This year the top 5 depart! They add in 4 transfers and the slot position has produced stars but they are a lot less experienced. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they lost 4 starters and had just 20 career starts back. The unit did only allow 12 sacks but the Spartans only had 88 (3.5) rush. Last year with three starters back (C Mesa 10 st '24 only 3 '25) I said they should pave the way for a much stronger rush attack and they improved to 132 (4.6) and allowed juist 13 sacks (2.3%!). This year they lose 3 starters (34/56) plus Mesa. The Spartans add in three P4 transfers and are in similar shape to last year and coach Niumatalolo feels the portal pickups make the group a little nastier this year and LG Tyler Chen is the top guy. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they cut it to 148 ypg (3.5) rush allowed with 25 sacks. Last year they lost 2 starters but returned NT Gafa Faga (12 st) and 4 DL who combined for 12 starts so were the most experienced defensive front here in 3 years. HC Niumatalolo called this unit one of the team's strengths.The numbers dropped some to 158 (4.0) rush with just 18 sacks. This year they lose all 3 starters including 2nd tm MW NT Faga (12 st, #7 tklr, 2.5 sk). They add in 3 transfers (0 strs) and the unit is on the small side so they may take another step back. Niumatalolo however really likes the group and says it is one of the deepest units on the team with NT Solomone Langi the top guy. LINEBACKERS - In '24 San Jose went from holding foes to 35 ypg below their average to allowing 24 ypg above. Last year they lost their #5 tackler but returned Jordan Pollard (#1, 115 tkl, 12 tfl), #4 Taniela Latu (12 st #4 tklr, 6 tfl) and overall 4 LB's who started 6+ games so with 7 of the top 8 so looked like one of the MW's top LB corps. San Jose allowed teams 51 ypg above thier average. This year they lose Pollard (12 st, 108 tkls, 2.5 sk), Latu (12 st, #2 tklr, 6 tfl) plus their #3 tackler . Ethan Powell (6 st, #10 tklr) is the only returnee with more than 7 tackles. This unit is a concern but Naseri Danielson and Dylan Lee had solid springs so Niumatalolo felt good about the unit. DEFENSIVE BACKS - SJSt finished #41 (61%, 19-12) in the PDR in '23. In '24 they lost 3.5 starters but only dropped a little to #55. Last year they had just one starter back. They added 3 JUCO's plus PS#28 & PS#66 P4 B10 transfers. This time the Spartans dropped to #126 in my PDR (65.5%, 18-7). This year they lose all 4 starters (#4, #5, #6, #7 tklrs). They add in 7 transfers but only one was a starter (FCS) although they cannot drop much more in the PDR and could move up. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 P Trent Carrizosa (Colo transfer) avg 43.2 (38.3 net) but they fell to #126 ST RANK L6Y: in my STR. Last year they lost their K and finished 2025 ..#125 #125. Carrizosa avg 45.6 (40.4 net) but they hit 2024 . #126 12-23 FG and were -3.2 on PR's and -4.3 on KR's. 2023 ....#87 This year Carrizosa returns and has NFL potential 2022 .. #131 ... #53 plus they add in a 2nd team AA FCS K in Trajan 2021 2020 ... #53 Sinatra who hit 18-22 FG with a long of 56 so they will easily have thier best finish in 3 years. . COACHES - Ken Niumatalolo was a QB for Hawaii ('86-'89) and then did a great job as the Navy head football coach from 2007-'22. He is Navy's all-time career win leader was 109-83 at a school that has plenty of restrictions. The 3rd year OC is Craig Stutzmann, who was the pass game coordinator at Texas St in '23, was an assisstant coach for Green Bay in '22 and was the co-OC/QB coach at Wash St from '20-'21. He runs the Spread-and-Shred offense. The DC is Bojay Filimoeatu who has 36 years as a college coach and took over as DC final two games last year. NORTHERN ILLINOIS HUSKIES WR DeAREE ROGERS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 the Huskies had to replace their QB starter. RFr Josh Holst (PS#97) and Ark Pine Bluff transfer Jalen Macon were in the mix. Macon has a big arm and is mobile (sub 4.8). Holst replaced the starter and moved the team better vs BG. He started vs Toledo and Ball St but then was injured. Holst led the bowl win and for the season threw for 593 (58.6%, 2-2). Macon hit just 4-7-50. In 2025 Macon suffered a hand injury. He could barely grip the ball and was used as a runner early. Holst started the first 4 vs some tough D's. He was benched for true Frosh Brady Davidson, who led NIU to two scores on first 2 poss vs Miami, but little after that. He started vs EMich but then Holst retook the job. After just 3 points vs Toledo, Macon started vs UMass and the offense exploded. He started the last two but was just 1-7-5 vs WMich and 5-10-27 vs Kent St in losses. The 3 QB's combined to hit 53% with an 8-6 ratio. Macon and Davidson return. They will be challenged by Charleston (DII) transfer Ean Hamric (17 st, 2967, 59%, 30-5, 962 rush L2Y), as well as true frosh Dryshawn Brown (PS#84) and Asa Johnson (PS#194). While the QB's still have the ability to run new HC Rob Harley, wants a more balanced offense so they should have an improved passing game. RUNNING BACKS - Last year NIU had to replace their #1 (749, 5.4) and #2 (567, 4.9) rushers. True Frosh Telly Johnson (PS#196), who DNP the first 7 but had 424 (5.0) the last 5 games of '24 returned. They added Chavon Wright, who had 2,235 (6.3) at Charleston (DII) for new OC Quinn Sanders. Johnson had TD runs of 74, 80, 53 & 43 yards (62.5 ypc). He had 120-462 (3.9) on his other carries finishing #2 with 712 (5.7). Wright, a bowling ball tackle breaker, emerged mid-season to lead with 875 (4.5). True Frosh Lazaro Rogers got the starts vs Miami and EMich finishing #4 (189, 5.7). This year they lose Wright (6 st) and Rogers (2 st) but Johnson is back along with Elijah Porter (PS#280, 80 yd), Romelo Ware (PS#204) and rFr Triston White (PS#190). They also add in two true frosh. They are close to '25 experience wise. RECEIVERS - Last year the Huskies lost their #1 (392, 10.6), #2 (391, 14.0), #3 (338 (13.1) and #4 (264, 10.2) receivers plus their TE (6 st, 6 rec). I thought the '24 numbers were poor and figured they would improve with the transfers. DeAree Rogers led with 506 (11.0) but had nearly 4 times the receptions of the #2 receiver Gary Givens. (145, 12.1). This year they lose Givens (9 st) and TE Jake Appleget (9 st). The OFFENSE Jersey # in Red top guy is back and they add Cam Thompson who was #2 here in '24 but transferred to Miss St last year. They are more experienced and along with the changes on offense, will easily top last year's poor receiving numbers. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the OLine returned 4 starters and 113 career starts. The unit improved to 204 ypg rush (4.7) with 19 sacks (5.1%). Last year they lost 4 starters and dropped to just 27 career starts returning. The line had 3 walk-ons and a Division II transfer as starters but did surprisingly well with 187 (4.5) rush and just 19 sacks allowed. This year they bring in new OL coach Matt White from Southern Utah (#13 FCS, 202 ypg, 5.1 LY). They lose 5 OL (3 str) who combined for 42 starts. They return two starters with just 18 career starts, so are similar to last year experience wise. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the DLine had good size, was dominant in the spring and was loaded with seniors. They improved to allowing just 112 (3.5) with 36 sacks (9.7!). Last year they lost two starters and 5 backup DL (incl 2nd Tm MAC DT).They returned two starters but lacked depth. They added 3 experienced FCS transfers. As you would expect their numbers dropped to allowing 183 (4.6) rush with just 14 sacks. This year they lose 7 DL who combined for 44 starts (153 tkl, 5.5 sk). Jayshon Thomas (3 st, 21 tkl) is the top returnee. They add 3 D2 (2 all-conf) and 3 FCS (1 all-conf) transfers. So while they have less FBS experience, they do add some experience and depth. This year they lose their star Urweiler (12 st, 7.5 tfl) plus the #2, #6, #9 and #11 tacklers. The top returnee is Brody Windham (12 tkl). JAMES MADISON DUKES RB GEORGE PETTAWAY West Florida's #1 receiver, VMI's #1, ETennSt's #2 and could have similar production and HC Napier feels it will be one of the top units in the SBC and TE Cole Keller is an NFL prospect. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they had two starters back (78 car sts) but also added three FCS transfers (64 car sts). I expected improvement and they did to 192 (4.8) rush but did allow 34 sacks. Last year they again had two starters back including 1st Tm SBC Pat McMurtrie and added 3 FCS starters. The line was dominant with 242 (5.5) rush and just 23 sacks allowed. This year they lose 4 starters but do add in starters from Colorado, FIU and ETennSt plus return 1st tm SBC C Zach Greenberg and have added size so remain strong. RG Tyler Brown is a future NFL DC and they have length and depth. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 all 4 starters departed and they were not as dominant but remained strong allowing 115 (3.5) rush with 41 sacks. Last year they lost 3 starters (1st Tm SBC DE, 13 sk) and two backups. They added 3 transfers with an FCS starter and a PS#30 Notre Dame transfer plus returned 6'1" 320 lb DT Immanuel Bush so lost less than '24. They were improved allowing a paltry 85 ypg (2.8) rush with 36 sacks. This year, they lose all 3 starters (10 sk) including 1st tm SBC Bush, 2nd tm SBC DT Sahir West plus 4 backups (105 tkl, 13 sk). They return DE Amar Thomas (2.5 sk) and add in 10 transfers (25 sk '25) so they have depth but figure to take a step back. DT Kells Bush could be the best player in the front 7 and is back after missing time in '25. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they lost their #1 (11 st), #2 (9 st), #12 (6 st) and #15 (5 st) tacklers. Trent Hendrick (5 st, 29 tkl) was back and they added a 2x Patriot League DPOY. JMU held foes to 41 below their average. Last year they lost a 1st Tm SBC LB (9 st, 3 sk) who was #1 tackler despite missing 4 games their #10 & #12 tacklers. They returned their #5 and #7 tacklers and added two FCS starters so were in a similar spot. They held foes to 136 ypg below thier average. This year they lose their leader Hendrick (14 st, #1 tklr, 3 sk) plus their NB (#10 tklr) and #5 tackler. Gannon Weathersby (11 st, #4 tklr) is back plus they add in 6 transfers (5 full time FCS strs) so wont fall off much. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '24 the secondary was more exp'd and moved up to #16 (54.5%, 16-17) in my PDR. Last year they lost 3 starters but added two FCS starters. They actually moved up to #13 in the PDR (50.8%, 18-14). This year they lose all 4 starters (#2, 3, 6, 11 tklr) with the top returnee Chase Regan (6 tkl). The Dukes add 6 transfers and 7 true frosh but figure to take a decent drop in the PDR this year. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 JMU dropped to #73 in my STR. Last year they lost their K and P but added LA Tech ST RANK L3Y: P Patrick Rea a left footed Austrailian and added 2025 ... #59 FAU's K Morgan Suarez who hit 11-15 FG (L47). 2024 ....#73 Rea had a 37.6 net. Cristiano Rosa had a super 2023 ... #33 56 TB on 79 KOffs. Curtis Harris-Lopez had a KR 2022 ....#97 TD and JMU moved up to #46 in the STR. This year they lose Rosa and their KR but should be just as strong. COACHES - JMU made a great hire in Billy Napier who was just let go from Florida and he will enjoy not facing the nation's toughest schedule like he did the last two years. His OC is Cam Aiken who was an Off analyst for Ole Miss ('23-'24) and ETennSt OC in '25 (32.5 ppg). The new DC is Robert Bala who was co-DC at Florida in '25 and an ILB coach at Bama in '23. The new Special Teams Coach is Rob Wenger who was at Minnesota ('17-24) and STC at Sac St in '25. POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '23 rFr Alonza Barnett won the starting job but in the opener did not complete a pass past the line of scrimmage (3-11-15) and the transfer threw for 3,657 yards (68%, 35-10) and was SBC POY! Barnett was the surprise starter in '24 and after hitting 1-5 Chesney stuck with him and Barnett threw for 2,598 yards (60%, 26-4!) in an unforeseen turnaround and was #3 rusher (442, 3.3). Barnett suffered a torn ACL vs Marshall and Billy Atkins and true frosh JC Evans split snaps in the bowl with Evans used as a runner. Barnett was questionable after a late ACL injury for 2025 so they added Matthew Sluka who was Chesney's QB at Holy Cross in '23 and Camden Coleman who threw for 2031 (65%, 13-5, 342 rush) with Richmond in '24. Barnett and Sluka split snaps the first 2 games then Barnett took the lion's share of snaps and threw for 2806 (58%, 23-8) and was #2 rusher with 589 (4.6). The top two depart. Coleman and Evans are back and they add in Arrington Maiden (PS#101, 79 yd rush '25 Mem) and Davi Belfort (PS#31, UCF). This group is much less experienced and it will be tough to match the unit's recent production. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 JMU lost their #1 (637, 4.5), #2 (568, 4.5) and #4 (132, 4.0) rushers. They added Ayo Adeyi from North Texas who rushed for 1017 (7.1) in '23 along with George Pettaway (PS#8, NCar), and Jobi Malary (676, 6.6 Port St) and I said the unit would be more productive. Adeyi was OFY early. Pettaway took the lead and rushed for 980 (6.0). QB Barnett was #3. Knight was a solid #2 (449, 5.8) and Malary had 16-106 vs Marshall and was #4 (269, 6.0). Last year everyone was back. Pettaway led with 99 yards in the opener but was injured. Adeyi had 13-87 vs Liberty but was injured. Wayne Knight took over and had a big year with 1373 (6.8). This year they lose Knight, Jordan Fuller (#3, 415, 5.1) and Adeyi (120, 5.0). Pettaway is back and should return to '24's form plus they add in Seth Cromwell (646, 4.3 NAriz), Nich Herman (1034, 7.2 Drake) and Malachi Fannin-Render (Liberty, PS#173) so will be solid but down a notch. RECEIVERS - In '24 JMU lost two 1st Tm SBC WR's who both topped 1,000 yards plus their #3 (442, 8.5) WR and 1st Tm SBC TE (12 st, 275, 10.2). Chesney said they had only 3 legitimate players and the unit had 20+ drops. As you would expect the numbers dropped off. Last year they lost thier top 4 receivers who combined for 2129 yards. They added Richmond's #1 and #2 receivers plus Villanova's #1 WR and were more experienced. Those 3 transfers were #1 (624, 17.3), #2 (500, 17.9) and #4 (396, 13.2). This year they lose 6 of the top 7 with ALSO ON ROSTER: Braedon Wislowski (358, 13.8) the top returnee. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In 2024 they lost their SBC Player of the Year QB plus their top 3 RB's, top 6 rec's, two all SBC OL and their OC. OLD DOMINION MONARCHS DL DeANDRE LYNCH OFFENSIVE LINE - In '23 they allowed a ridiculous 61 sacks (16.9%!). In '24 they had two starters back and 33 career starts and showed significant improvement with 210 (5.2) rush and trimming the sacks to 36 (still 10.8%). Having mobile QB's helped those numbers. Last year they lost 3 starters with the career starts climbing to 52 making them the best OLine here in a couple of years. ODU rushed for 238 (5.6) and allowed just 20 sacks. They were one of the rare units that had all 5 starters start all 12 games. This year all 5 depart. They add in 5 transfers (see PSL) but have 0 FBS starts returning so this unit is my biggest question mark on the team. Coach Rahne says they have better depth but not the high end talent of '25. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 with a veteran line the rush D slipped to allowing 173 (4.3) with just 26 sacks. Last year they lost 2 starters plus two backups. Their top sack guy Kris Trinidad (5.5) was back to the three-man line and they added two JUCO's who were IFS and had 4 of the top 7 back with solid depth. The numbers improved to allowing 140 (3.7) with 39 sacks. This year they lose DE Trinidad (13 st, #11 tklr, 3.5 sk) and 4 backups (7 st, 60 tkl, 7 sk). Nine DL had DD tackles last year and 5 return so they are on par with 2025. Coach Rahne feels this is the strongest overall unit on the team and all 3 starters are all conference caliber. LINEBACKERS - Last year they returned their #1, #3 and #4 tacklers plus added two transfers. Mario Thompson (#3 tklr '24) played in just 3 games (5 tkl). Koa Naotala (#1 tklr '24) played in 1 game (1 tkl). ODU went from allowing foes 12 ypg above their average in '24 to holding them to 47 ypg below last year. This year they lose their #2 , #4, and #5 tacklers. True frosh Jackson Forrest was #7 tackler and King Mario Easterly was #1 tackler and both are back and with the return of Naotala and Thompson they basically go from 1 to 3 returning starters. This unit has depth and is one of the SBC's best. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '24 ODU moved up to #88 in the PDR (61%, 21-12). Last year they lost 3 starters and 3 backups (4 st, 67 tkl, 5 pbu). HC Rahne did feel very good about the safeties. Surprisingly ODU moved up again this time to #34 in the PDR (60.4%, 16-15). This year they lose 3 starters again (#3, #7, #12 tklr). They return 4 DB that started last year so are a little more experienced but will likely drop in the PDR. They have more depth at CB but need to solidify the FS spot and Zion Frink is a team leader and has NFL potential at CB. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 ODU rose to #69 in our STR. MARSHALL THUNDERING HERD WR ADRIAN NORTON emerge. Gibson feels all 4 starters I list below are all SBC caliber. OFFENSIVE LINE - The Herd had to replace 4 OL starters last year. They added 5 transfers but with the bulk of the line gone (24 car sts ret) this unit was in a rebuilding mode. With a mobile QB they ran for 197 (4.7) and allowed just 19 sacks, the second straight year they gave up less than 20. This year they lose 5 OL (36/37). They have two starters back including 3rd tm SBC RG Jalen Slappy and add in 4 transfers including LG Robby Martin and RT Xavier Bausley from neighboring West Virginia. The unit has 41 career starts and could even top last year's solid numbers and HC Gibson feels they are more athletic and improved. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they allowed 179 (4.4) rush and had 36 sacks (9.1%) despite an All-American DE (#2DC). Last year they lost 4 starters and 4 backups. NG Mikailin Warren has NFL potential if he keeps his weight down at at 365 lbs is a force in the middle. DE Braydin Ward is poised for a huge year (4.51 spd). APPALACHIAN STATE MOUNTAINEERS DL CALEB SANDSTROM POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In 2024 their starter regressed throwing for 3,003 yards (56%, 23-14) and hit the portal ending up a quality starter at Tennessee. Last year they added AJ Swann (PS#30) who had 12 starts at Vandy (2731, 56%, 22-9) in '22-'23 and JJ Kohl (PS#13, 9-11 pass Iowa St). Swann started the ﬁrst 4 til injury. True frosh Noah Gillon (PS#150) and Billy Wiles played the next two games. Kohl took over as starter and led wins over Oregon St and Georgia St but Swann came off the bench to lead a pair of late TD drives vs ODU and reclaimed the job. He was 8-25 vs JMU and injured and Kohl ﬁnished the year at QB. Both left prior to the bowl and Gillon split time with Matthew Wilson. The ﬁve QB's threw for 3336 (59%, 23-15) and all 5 depart. The Mountaineers add in Malachi Singleton (PS#19) who threw for 797 (64%, 6-2, 276 rush 2Y) at Arkansas and Purdue, Tommy Ulatowski who had 10 starts for Kent St in 2 years and Henry Hasselback (PS#66 UCLA) who runs 22 mph. He and Singleton are dangerous runners and Ulatowski is a passing QB. I look for improved numbers. RUNNING BACKS - In '22 App St's streak of 1,000-yard rushers was ten seasons but now the non 1,000 yard streak has reached 4 years. Last year they lost their #1 (713, 4.8) rusher. Kayne Roberts (#2, 332, 4.0) was OFY August. They added Rashod Dubinion (PS#37) from Arkansas (7 st, 888, 4.3 3Y) plus true Frosh Jaquari Lewis (PS#81) and I said could top 24's numbers despite losing the top 4 RB's. Dubinion came close to starting a streak as he had 886 (5.0) with three 100+ games. With Dubinion banged up the last two games Lewis showed the future is bright by rushing for 175 vs Marshall and 108 vs App St and was #2 with 618 (4.4). QB's were #3 & #4. The #3 RB had just 56 (4.3). While they lose Dubinion they add in Treyaun Webb (PS#6!, Florida), J'Marion Burnette (PS#18 Houston) and Ja'Quez Cross who topped 700 yards rush twice with Ark St. They get back Roberts so are deeper and improved. RECEIVERS - In '24 Dalton Stroman was #4 again (307, 15.4). Last year they lost their #1 (840, 15.9), #2 (745, 16.2) and #3 (367, 18.4) WR's plus their TE (9 st, 293, 11.8).
