GEORGIA SOUTHERN EAGLES WR JOSH DALLAS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 JC French threw for 2,831 yards (65.6%, 17-11). Last year they added Turner Helton (1 st, WKU), and two true frosh. For the first time under Helton they had a returning starter at QB so expectations were high. French put up similar numbers with 2929 pass (64%, 20-8). Helton hit 14-2674-1-0 in spot duty and true frosh Weston Bryan (#114) hit 7-9-84 and was #4 rusher. Charlie Johnson (PS#80) redshirted and can spin the rock. Helton knows the system adn will be a coach some day. This year French transferred to Cincinnati. They add in Max Johnson (PS#14) who has 23 career starts (LSU, Tex A&M, NCar) throwing for 5361 yards (49-13 ratio!) in an oft injured 7 years. If he stays healthy they could have improved numbers but there is very little experience behind him but Helton does like the depth. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they had to replace their #1 rusher (744, 4.6, 13 td). OJ Arnold was #2 (316, 5.0) and David Mbadinga was #4 (229, 3.9) and both returned. The top 3 RB's had 1,289 yards (4.5) Arnold took the feature role and had three 100+ games including 267 rush vs Coastal with a rush, pass and receiving TD (first player GS history same game). He had just 1 yard on 3 att the last two games but topped 1,000 in the bowl (1032, 7.2). Mbadinga was #3 with 196 (4.0) and Taeo Todd had 97 (3.6) with QB's #2 and #4 rushers. This time the top 3 RB's had 1326 (6.0). This year they lose Arnold (#1 rush, #4 rec) and he leaves big shoes to fill. Terrance Gibbs has yet to live up to his PS#16 billing and they have Bryce Baker (PS#206, 52, 3.3), Jamarian Samuel (5-9 205 Sr) who is a physical runner. They add in true Frosh Ty Cummings (PS#112) and PS#221 JC Tyrese Woodgett who may be the most talent but is recovering from a torn labrum. He is explosive. They should come near the last two year's RB numbers. RECEIVERS - Georgia Southern was one of 4 current FBS teams to have never had a 1,000-yard receiver. Last year they lost their #1 (659, 11.2) plus #4 WR and their TE (249, 10.0). The top returnees were Josh Dallas #2 (614, 13.4) and Dalen Cobb #3 (599, 11.5). They added Camden Brown (PS#85) from Auburn and the streak ended as he had 1079 (16.6) yards and 14 td's! Marcus Sanders was #2 with 797 (15.9) and Dalen Cobb was #3 (506, 8.9). This year they lose the top 5. They do add in 8 transfers including Andre Greene (PS#16, Virg) and Kam Mikell (PS#15QB Colo) but none of the six P4 transfers has had more than 9 catches in a season. Ashton Hollins and Dallas could be the top guys and TE River Helms is NFL Caliber. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they dropped to two returning starters (50 car sts) and fell off a little to 128 (3.7) rush but did cut it to 29 sacks allowed. Last year they lost a 1st Tm SBC RT (13/35) but had 3 starters back and four OL that started 6+ games in '24 with 79 career starts so were a more veteran unit. They improved a little with 154 (4.3) rush and 30 sacks allowed. This year they lose all five starters (63/107) returning Caelan Williams (2/4). They add in starters from Virginia, Charlotte and Tenn St so have 45 career FBS starts but are a completly rebuilt unit. Helton feels they are just as talented as last year but the '25 squad had chemistry and this year's needs to develop that. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 everyone was back with a true 3-deep in place. The numbers slipped to allowing 170 (4.9) with 21 sacks. Last year they lost two starters but had 6 DL that started in '24. They were strong on the edge and at NT but young at DT. I was surprised that they were very poor stopping the run allowing 218 (5.7) and only had 12 sacks. This year they lose 3 DL (28 sts, 77 tkl, 0.5 sk). They return 4 DL that started last year (23 st, 76 tkl, 8 sk) including DE MJ Stroud (6.5 sk) and Latrell Bullard who had 25 starts in '23-'24 but RS in '25. They add 4 transfers including Anthony Bynum (MTSt, 23 sts) and can only be tougher up front. With the returnees and the transfers coach Helton calls it the best unit on defense and his best since he has been here. LINEBACKERS - Last year they lost the SBC Defensive Player of the Year (#2 tkl'r all-time here)! They also lost their #2 and #6 tacklers. They returned their NB (#10 tklr) plus added Brendan Harrington (28 car sts App St) and Brandon Tyson (73 tkl '23 Elon) also known as the killer B's. The Eagles allowed foes 29 ypg above their average in '24 and slipped to 88 above last year. This year they lose Harrington (13 st, #3 tklr) and their NB (#4 tklr) but return Tyson (#2 tklr) and add in Rashon Myles (115 tkl, Ab Christ) and 3 other transfers and should improve on the opponents ypg. Rashon Myles and Brandon Tyson are both all conf caliber and Helton again calls it the best LB unit since he has been here. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '24 the Eagles were #94 in the PDR. Last year they had 3 starters back and added in four transfers and improved to #76 in my PDR (64%, 15-12). This year they lose 2 starters (#1, #7 tklr) but add in 3 FCS starters and have 3 DB back who started 4+ games and while a little less experienced could improve in the PDR. CB Chance Gamble has NFL potential but this unit is the biggest question on the defense. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '23 true frosh P Alex Smith averaged 40.0 (35.4 net) and they were #53 in our STR. In '24, Smith avg 42.7 (41.6 net!) and their K hit 15-18 FG (L/53) plus ST RANK L6Y: the coverage units were top notch. GS was #24 in 2025..... #71 the ST rankings. Last year they lost their K again 2024.... #24 and their top KR. They slipped to #71. P Smith avg 2023 ... # 5 3 ... #42 42.8 (39.8 net) while K Tripp Bryant hit 17-20 FG 2022 2021 .. #101 (L46), Evan Scruggs had 26 TB on 62 kickoffs and 2020 ... #92 Dalen Cobb had a 95 yd KR TD (26.4). This year they lose Cobb but are a top 25 contender again and will have a Stock Market rise in the STR with P Smith an AA candidate. COACHES - GA Southern made a big-time hire in '22 in Clay Helton, who went 46-24 at USC. Helton successfully transitioned GS from the option to a spread pass attack. He was given a fiveyear contract extension in '25. The 3rd year OC is Ryan Aplin (35), who spent '22-'23 here as the Pass Game Coordinator and TE coach. He was previously at Ark St in '21 (RB cch), WKU ('20, co-OC/) and '18-'19 at N Alabama (OC). The new DC is Mike Mutz who was an asst here '15-'16 and was DC at SFAustin the last 3 years. Blake Wilson is the ST coordinator who has been the senior analyst on ST's ('22-'24) here. This year some indicators are pointing down but Helton will have them in the mix for a bowl and battling in the East as always. GEORGIA STATE PANTHERS DE RICHARD KRAMER POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In 2024 Christian Veilleux (PS#33) threw for 2,047 yards (57%, 13-11), Veilleux led the upset of Texas St and Vandy and returned in '25. They added 3 transfers who were all mobile in Cameran Brown (TTech, 4-9-44 pass, 83 yd rush), PJ Hatter (Tex St, 7-45 rush) and true frosh TJ Stanley (PS#138). TJ Finley (PS#37, LSU, Aub, TxSt) joined the team week two. Brown played in the ﬁrst 9 games. Veilleux started the opener then Finley took over vs Memphis and started the next 4. Brown started the next 4 (25.5 ppg) but was injured vs Coastal Carolina and Finley started vs Marshall. Brown started vs Troy but was injured and Veilleux took all the snaps in the last two. Veilleux and Finley combined for 59% with a 9-10 ratio. Brown (65% 13-1!) returns and I was impressed with him last year so he should be a top notch Sun Belt QB. They add in Ayden Periera who started 12 for Merrimack (1813, 51%, 9-7) for an experienced backup. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they lost their #1 (819, 5.4) and #2 (365, 5.8, #3 rec 354, 8.2) RB's. They added Rashad Amos who had 1075 (5.1) with Miami,Ohio in '23, Djay Braswell (PS#38 SCar) and Jordon Simmons (PS#42, 654 Akron '24). Amos was the leading rusher the ﬁrst 9 games and ﬁnished with 267 (4.2). Simmons emerged and had 496 yards the last 5 games. QB Cam Brown was #2 rusher. This year they lose Simmons (#1, 543, 5.6) and Amos. They add in 4 transfers including Lanear McCrary who had 1129 (5.8) for Shorter and Savion Hart (PS#54JC) who had 878 (4.6) for Georgetown. Dennis Murray (54, 4.1) is the top reteurnee along with rFr Ladainnian Martin (PS#55!). They could top last year's average production (top 3 RB 952, 4.6). RECEIVERS - In '24 Valdosta St transfer Ted Hurst led the way with 961 (17.2). Last year they lost their TE (12 st, #2, 558, 11.4) and a WR (11 st, #4, 324, 10.8). Will Healy was the WR coach and had the top guy back plus added 3 full-time FCS starters so the unit was much more experienced. LOUISIANA RAGIN’ CAJUNS LB JAKE ST ANDRE plagued line in the FBS as all 9 OL missed at least one game, they had 3 OL OFY after 3 games and a different lineup each week. Despite all the injuries they improved to 183 (4.6) rush and allowed just 25 sacks! This year they lose 3 OL (26/65). Last year’s injuries make this unit much more experienced and they can only stay healthier and they return 7 OL who started including 4 full time starters. This is one of the SBC’s top OLines. DEFENSIVE LINE - In 2024 they allowed 154 (4.5) rush with just 24 sacks. Last year they lost one starter and two backups. They added a 310 lb transfer Jaelen Crider (10 st, YoungSt) and had three starters back including top sack man Cam Whitfield (6) and went three deep. Louisiana allowed 187 (4.7) rush with just 23 sacks. This year they lose those two (Whitfield 1 sk) plus Jordan Lawson (5 sk) and a NT (5 st, 28 tkl). They add in 3 transfers and are less experienced but could put up better numbers. NT Fitzgerald West and DT Chase Edwards are the top guys and Desormeaux says it is a veteran group that is physically well developed and flies to the ball. LINEBACKERS - In 2024 the unit was more experienced then they have been in a couple of years and did improve to allowing 24.1 ppg. Last year they lost a 1st Tm Sun Belt LB (#1 tklr) plus their #3 and #4 tacklers. The top returnee was Jaden Dugger (14 st, 97 tkl, 3Y). This year they lose Dugger (#5 DC SF) (13 st, #1 tklr, 11 tfl) and Terrance Williams (13 st, #2 tklr, 1 sk). DT KAM CURRY TROY TROJANS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 they had to replace their #3 all-time passer. Goose Crowder (PS#48) was 9-13-94 in limited action. Goose worked with new HC Parker when he was the OC at West Virginia and is a strong leader and won the job. Crowder was injured on a TD run that tied the Memphis game at 7. Tucker Kilcrease did toss a 62 yard TD pass. Crowder started the next 2 but was OFY vs ULM early and Kilcrease started the next two then was injured. The #3 QB led the team to 37 ppg the last 4 games. All 3 QB's topped 130 snaps and the unit produced 2527 yards (63%, 21-9) and 217 rush. Crowder was the starter in '25 but was injured in the 1Q vs Memphis. Kilcrease struggled in that game but got better weekly and hit 30-39-415-5-0 vs Texas St. Crowder returned vs ODU and Kilcrease was OFY in that game and Crowder was rusty (8 sks). Crowder then threw for 361 and 285 (7-1 ratio) in two starts but was injured again in the bowl. Both return and combined to throw for 2864 (58%, 20-11) and this is a deep unit and should maintain better health. They also add Rodge Waldrop (PS#166JC) who was a big surprise in spring and is pushing for #2. RUNNING BACKS - After not having a 1,000 yard rusher since '18 Troy had 3 in a row from '22-'24. Last year they lost their top two rushers. Jordan Lovett has home run potential and they had Tae Meadows (PS#73). GTech RB Trey Cooley (PS#43) was projected to start but he was lost to an ACL in August. Meadows had 186 vs Nicholls and led with 695 (4.4). Lovett had the units only other 100+ effort with 113 vs Louisiana and was #2 (339, 3.8). Meadows went to Auburn so Lovett will battle Jaheim Merriweather (PS#62 Purdue), Gavin Griffin (1168, 5.2 JC '25), Bryce Burgess (607, 5.8 JC) and Soph Dennis Palmer. They are more experienced than '25 and could have improved rush numbers (top 3 1091, 4.0). RECEIVERS - Last year they had to replace the first Troy receiver to top 1,000 yards in a season since 2012. They lost the top two with Peyton Higgins (301, 9.7) the top returnee. They added Rara Thomas (PS#175 Geor) and 3 other transfers. This year they lose their top guy Thomas (629, 16.1) and the top 6 receivers overall! The top returnee is Mojo Dortch (4 st, 7 rec). They add in 6 transfers (0 starters) so are less experienced and JUCO's Noreel White and Howard Kinchen look to be the top guys outside and they have two solid slots (see PSL). OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they had six different starting lineups the first 8 weeks but were more stable down the stretch and had 224 ypg (5.0) with just 4 sacks the last 4 weeks. Troy improved to 156 (4.3) with 21 sacks on the year. Last year had 3 starters back (53 car sts) with four OL back that started 6+ games and PS#61, #78 and #104 transfers added. The unit was hit hard by injuries all year at one point just one OL that started the opener was available. Elijah Prather (12 st '24) was OFY after 6 starts. Troy had just 109 ypg rush (3.0) and allowed 59 sacks. This year they lose 5 OL (39/80). Last year's injuries have them return 6 OL that started here (29/42) plus they add starters from Ohio, Furman and two JUCO's. This is a tougher more physical group and Parker likes his transfer class so with better health will have vastly improved numbers. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '23 Troy allowed just 107 (3.2) rush with 47 sacks (10.8%!). In '24 they lost all four starters including a 4th Tm AA DE. Naturally the defense took a large step back allowing 145 (4.3) rush with just 19 sacks. Last year they lost 2 starters but had 7 back with starting experience and added two P4 transfers and a JC. They were much more experienced but allowed 176 (4.5) rush with 37 sacks. This year they lose all 7 DL including all 4 starters (58 st, 181 tkl, 16.5 sk). DE Donnie Smith did not start but led with 11 sacks and they add 6 transfers (0 strs). While less experienced they have six 300+ DT's add in 3 top 100 JC's and last years unit underperformed so they are stronger. Smith has NFL potential and DT Ty Clemons is the top guy inside with 6 DT's that can play. LINEBACKERS - Last year they lost their top LB (#1 tklr, 16 tfl) but returned Jordan Stringer who tied for #1 tackler and had 7.5 tfl plus Spear Devin Lafayette (#5 tklr) so they were more experienced than the previous two years. Troy held foes to 5 ypg below their average. This year they lose all 3 starters (#1, #2, #8 tklr). TJ Thompson (#11 tklr) and Luke Hodge (#12 tklr) are the top returnees plus they add in 4 transfers but are less experienced. BC transfers Bryce Steele and Keno Jones are the top LB's but they have a battle at Spear. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '24 they had ZERO starters back so I expected a large drop in the PDR and they fell to #118 (67%, 12-6). Last year they lost 3 starters but added 4 transfers and were more experienced and I said should make a solid climb in the PDR. Troy did move up to #68 (60%, 16-10) This year they 3 starters again (#4, #5 , #7 tklrs). They add in 6 transfers again so are in the same shape as last year and could finish as high. HC Parker feels they have 10-12 DB's that could play and feels they will be improved. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 they lost their 1st ST RANK L6Y: Tm SBC LS and had a new ST coach. They did 2025.... #48 have their first PR td here s/'18. K Scott Taylor 2024.. #106 Renfroe hit 11-13 FG (L/50) but with a 34.2 net 2023.... #54 punt they dropped to #106 in the STR! Last year 2022.... #46 new P Evan Crenshaw (big leg) avg 45.7 (42.6 2021.. #126 net!). KO man Paddy McAteer (32 TB) was SBC 2020.... #40 ST POW vs Texas St with a FG and onside kick. Troy moved up to #48. This year they lose their K (9-12) and KOff man but Crenshaw returns so they are solid. COACHES - 3rd year HC Gerad Parker was the OC at West Virginia ('20-'21), then OC at Notre Dame in '23. He was the interim HC at Purdue for 6 games in 2016. New OC is Adam Austin who was the OC at Tarleton St the last 2 years. The 3rd year DC is Dontae Wright, spent '20-'23 as the S's coach at West Virginia and coached S's at Western Mich in 2018-19. Tyler Hancock is the Special Teams Analyst. He was at Baylor "23, Buffalo '24 and was Charlotte STC ('21-'22). ARKANSAS ST RED WOLVES RB KENYON CLAY POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '23 true frosh Jaylen Raynor threw for 2,543 yards (58%, 17-7) and was #3 rusher (380, 3.1) and was SBC Frosh of the Year! In '24 Raynor had similar numbers throwing for 2783 (61.7%, 16-10) with 387 rush. Last year despite a young OLine in front of him Raynor improved to 3361 (67%, 19-11) and had 423 (2.7) rush. Raynor left for Iowa St. Ethan Crawford (PS#56) has 7 career starts (1095, 44%, 3-7 SMiss). Drew Dickey (PS#74) and Jeremy St-Hilaire (PS#63) both come over from Vandy where OC Altman is from so know the offense. I think Trey Owens (PS#23, Texas) will win the job. He is a big kid with a live arm can make all the throws and is more athletic than people think. Crawford is very athletic and an added dimension with his legs. This unit goes from a rare three year starter to inexperience but Owens should have a solid first year. RUNNING BACKS - In 2024 Ja'Quez Cross was #2 with 638 (5.5). True frosh Devin Spencer had 206 (5.2). Last year they lost their top guy (721, 47). They added Kenyon Clay who had 387 rush (4.5) and 225 (10.7) receiving with SMiss in '24. Cross was OFY in the opener. Spencer and Clay became the first duo to each top a 100 in a game here since 2016 (vs GSthrn). Those were the only 100 yard games by a RB and Spencer led with 559 (5.2) and Clay was #2 with 523 (3.8). Both return and they add in Ezell Jolly (PS#57) who had 301 (3.8) with UTEP in '24 and 869 (7.1) for Kilgore College in '25 plus Corey Reddick (641, 5.6, Valdosta St). Damon Sisa (5-8 160 rfr) and true frosh Solomon Baggett are both in the mix. This unit is much more experienced. RECEIVERS - Corey Rucker (826, 14.0, 9 td) led Ark St in receiving in '21 & was a Frosh AA but hit the portal. In '23 Rucker re-joined the team (SCar '22) and led with 705 (19.6). In '24 Rucker led again with 1053 (15.2). Last year 4 of the top 5 departed but Rucker returned and led again with 1032 (13.8). Chauncy Cobb was #2 (797, 10.9), Hunter Summers #3 (505, 11.5). This year they lose Rucker the Sun Belt's career receiving leader with 3693 yards (Sam Pinckney -'18-23) plus a TE (#4, 270., 9.0). Cobb and Summers both return so they have a little more overall experience but will miss their playmaker. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they were down 4 starters early due to injuries and didn't have the full OLine intact until the SAla game but had 157 (4.2) rush with 35 sacks. Last year they lost 4 starters. They did add Wil Saxton (9/9 SMiss) but had just one starter back and 33 career starts. They moved LT Riley McGehee to RT the last 7 games and LG Noah Smith to LT and inserted Tristian Smith at LG. Ark St dropped to 128 (3.6) ypg rush but the sacks were cut to 26. This year they lose McGehee and Smith (18/40) but go from one returning starter to basically 4 (58 car sts) and are much more experienced. Smith and LT Manasse Itete are the top guys and this should be one of the stronger OLines in the Sun Belt with great continuity for a Group of Six team. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they lost a DE (10 st, 49 tkl, 13 tfl) but were more experienced plus added 7 transfers. Surprisingly they slipped back to allowing 212 rush (5.7) with just 19 sacks. Last year they lost 4 starters (34 st, 104 tkl) and 3 backups (6 st, 30 tkl, 3.5 sk). They added 5 transfers and I said could only be improved but I thought the same thing in '24 and they were less experienced than that bunch. They did improve to allowing 168 (4.4) with 39 sacks. This year they lose 6 DL including all 4 starters (52 sts, 246 tkl!, 31 sk!). That was a productive group, and Jones will need to repeat his portal magic with this bunch (11 transfers). DT Ryan Reese and NG Elias Sherman were the top guys but they were a work in progress coming out of the spring. LINEBACKERS - In '24 Red Wolves allowed foes 80 ypg above their average (#126). Last year they lost their #1, #2 and #3 tacklers. They added eight transfers with 3 being full time starters (Mem, Marsh, MTenn) so I said they could actually be improved and they cut it to allowing foes 34 above their average (#105). Kyle Taylor had just 6 tackles the first 5 games but a starter was dismissed (wk 6) and another injured and he had 68 tackles the last 6 games. This year they lose Taylor (6 st, #2 tklr), and their #1 tackler. They return Nigel Nelson (#8 tklr) and Brandon Greil (#7 tklr) plus add in 4 transfers so are more experienced. DEFENSIVE BACKS - Ark St was #112 (60%, 25-6) in my Pass D Rankings in '22 and fell to #132 (69%, 25-8) in '23. In '24 they snagged as many int's as the previous two years combined and moved up to #113 (63%, 19-14). Last year they had to replace all 4 starters. They added five transfers (2 st'rs) but as you would expect dropped to #127 (68%, 21-7). This year they lose two starters (#6, #10 tklr) but add in 6 transfers and have 2+ starters back and should make a good sized jump in the PDR.This is the deepest and most exp'd unit on the team. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 they lost their 1st Tm SBC P and K. Clayton Amaya had 23 TB on kickoffs. Jones is now just 1 of 3 FBS coaches to lead 4 schools to multiple bowl games (Lou Holtz, Tommy Tuberville). The new OC is Garrett Altman who was QB coach for Vandy the last 2 years. The 2nd year DC is Griff McCarley who was LB coach here in '24 and LB coach at Ole Miss prior. The new STC is Kody Schexnayder who was ST Quality control coach ('21-'22) and a ST analyst at Ole Miss ('23-'25). . PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In 2022 my computer called for 25.2 ppg and they had 25.0 ppg! In 2023 my computer had them at 25.3 ppg thanks to six def/ST td's (4 vs Tex St) they topped it by a little at 27.1 ppg. In '24 my computer called for 404 ypg but they came up a little short with 384 ypg and 25.8 ppg. Last year QB Raynor, and WR Rucker were back and my computer called for 384 ypg and they had 383 ypg!! This year both are gone. The offensive line is upgraded and if a QB emerges they should be close to last year despite losing the top two guys. DEFENSE - Last year ASU had a brand new defense with just one starter back from '24's squad. Things did not start out well as they allowed 498 ypg to the first 5 FBS teams they faced but 358 ypg vs the last 6 FBS teams. They had 9 sacks vs Troy. ASU actually improved from allowing 462 ypg to 413! This year they have 4 of the top 8 tacklers back so are more exprienced. There are questions up front but the back 7 looks strong. 2026 - Ark St had nine consecutive winning seasons (never ranked) but that ended in the unusual year of 2020 (4-7). In 2021 Butch Jones took over and faced a tough schedule and had losses by 5, 7, 1, 8 and 2 but fell even further to 2-10. in '22 ASU finished just 3-9 despite leading in the 4Q EIGHT times. In Jones 3rd year Ark St was beat by a combined 110-3 in the first two games but Raynor took over week 4 and they went on a 6-3 streak and got to their first bowl since 2019 and came up just 2 points short vs NIU. In '24 the Red Wolves had 16 starters back and Jones had top recruiting classes each of the previous 3 years. They went from #113 to #5 on my Exp Chart! They made my Most Improved List in 2024! ASU was 7-4 with the losses to Michigan, Iowa St, Tex St and Louisiana all on the road but did lose their home final to ODU. After a bowl win it was an 8-5 season and another year of improvement. The 8 wins were Ark St's 3rd highest win total since joining the FBS and they were only 1 of 3 programs in the FBS whose win total has increased each of the previous 3 seasons. They were -61 ypg in SBC play (pg 261) and had 7 Net Close Wins. Ark St opened 1-4 in '25 then got close comeback wins vs Tx St and USA and won 4 in a row and with a last second FG miss by App St got to a bowl at 6-6 then beat Missouri St to finish 7-6. ASU did have 4 close wins. If a QB emerges they could be even stronger this year. The defense is more experienced and Jones always fields a top notch special teams (sign of a good coach). SOUTH ALABAMA JAGUARS RB PJ MARTIN POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 Gio Lopez missed the bowl and Bishop Davenport was MVP of the bowl and threw for 604 (61%, 3-1, 161 rush) on the season. Last year Lopez left AFTER spring (to UNC)! Davenport was joined by rFr Jared Hollins (PS#83, strong arm). Davenport had ﬁrm control of the job all year but did have his ups and downs. He threw for 2072 (68%, 12-6) and ran for 326. The backup was Hollins (12-16-101). They add in Jerry Horne (Ark St), and two true frosh. Hollins will push Davenport for the job but this unit is much more experienced and Davenport is now experienced and a solid athlete with good arm talent . RUNNING BACKS - In '23 Ole Miss transfer Kentrell Bullock (PS#92) got work early and ran for 68 yards in the bowl and was #2 (448, 5.4). In '24 true frosh Fluff Bothwell led with 834 (7.4). Bullock was a strong #2 (832, 5.5). Last year Fluff transferred to Miss St. Bullock and PJ Martin (PS#169, 98, 7.5) returned plus they added PS#40JC Keenan Phillips so I said they were on par with 2024. Bullock set USA's school record for rush yards in a season with 1085 (5.0) while Phillips had 607 (4.8) and Martin added 326 (5.4). This year Bullock moves on so they add in Trae'Von Dunbar (PS#55 WVirg), rFr Julyon Jordan (PS#159) and PS#114, 121 and 133 true frosh. This unit will be solid but down a few notches. Phillips has great change of direction and is a good receiver and Martin has good vision and balance and will be 100% in the fall after an injury last year. RECEIVERS - In '22 Devin Voisin led with 871 (13.6). In '23 Voisin was OFY after just 2 games. In '24 Voisin was not 100% and was #3 (407,12.0). Last year they had to replace a 1st tm SBC WR (#1, 1126, 14.5), their #2 (649, 18.0) and 4 of the top 5 overall. Voisin was the top guy and led with 775 (11.6). RFr Jeremy Scott was #2 with 417 (17.4) and Anthony Eager was #3 (339, 8.5). This year they lose the top 2 WR and both TE's (18 st, #4 rec). Eager is back plus their #5 and #6 receivers with each starting 2+ games last year. Samford transfer Brendan Jenkins was the top guy out of spring. Eager has track speed and had a wrist injury last year but is 100%. The unit is a little more experienced but need some go to WR's to emerge. OFFENSIVE LINELINE The Jags OLine was the team's weakness in '21 but improved yearly and became a strength and in '24 they lost 3 starters and had just 21 career starts. They had a strong left side and two P4 transfers. They improved to 199 (5.8) rush with just 17 sacks. Last year they had 3+ starters back and 52 career starts are looked like one of the Sun Belt's best.They did lose their top OL LT Jordan Davis after 9 starts but were strong again with 200 (4.5) rush and just 21 sacks allowed. This year they lose 4 OL (3 strs, 42/80). They drop to two returning starters and 32 career starts but do add a two year Monmouth starter in RG Shalik Hubbard and a PS#84 LSU transfer. WESTERN MICHIGAN BRONCOS OL JEREMY SCHLEICHER POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In the 91 years of the NFL draft, a Broncos QB has never been selected. In '24 rFr PS#57 Broc Lowrey (Indiana) was the backup (4-8-21) and the #4 rusher (129, 5.4). Brady Jones, who threw for 4,456 (64%) with 44 tds at JUCO in '24 won the job at the start. They went from a 3 year starter to 9 career FBS pass att's but were more athletic. The Broncos opened 0-3. Lowry played in each of the first 3 games and was more effective than Jones and won the starting job. Lowry went 10-1 as a starter throwing for 1,803 (63%, 9-3) and was the #2 rusher with 963 (4.7). He was the first WM QB to top 100 yards rushing in a game since 1973 (Paul Jorgenson). His 14 rushing TD topped Albert Little (12 in 1978). This year Jones (136, 48%, 1-3, 4 rush) departs. They add Trey Petty (PS#47 Illinois) and a true frosh (PS#120). MAC OPOY Lowry returns and has improved his passing and should be one of the MAC's best! RUNNING BACKS - In '23 walk-on rFr Jalen Buckley (tough physical runner), had 194 & 196 yard games and 3 other 100+ games to lead with 1,003 (5.3, 2nd Tm MAC). In '24 they added an Okla St transfer who led with 921 (6.4). Buckley missed 3 early games but had two 100+ efforts finishing #2 (683, 5.3). Last year they lost their #1 and #3 (600, 5.3, #4 rec) RB. They added in Cole Cabana (PS#18, Mich) and two 1,000 yard JC RB's in Ofa Mataele and Devin Miles. Miles was one of 3 WM players to top 100 yard rush vs NIU (first team s/'17 ND) finishing #3 (425, 4.3). Buckley was #2 rusher but then had 193 vs Miami and 174 in the bowl to lead with 1,003 (5.6). Mataele added 252 (4.4). This year they lose Miles but add Arkansas transfer AJ Green (PS#16, 964, 4.7 4Y). If Buckley maintains his postseason form, this group will be one of the MAC's best. RECEIVERS - Last year WM lost their #1 (545, 14.0) and #2 WR's (412, 12.1). They added 7 transfers. Georgia St transfer Talique Williams led with just 478 (13.7). They add 5 transfers including Presbyterian TE Nate Levicki (471, 16.3). With Chenault and Brooks back along with improved QB play, the unit should be more productive. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the OLine lost two starters but had 8 of their top 10 back (92 car sts). I said the OLine should be one of the MAC's best and they were with 183 (4.9) rush allowing 23 sacks. Last year they lost 1st Tm MAC C (12/47, finalist Rimington Trophy!), 1st Tm AA G and two other starters. They added 3 transfers but none were starters. Then C Jeremy Schleicher was injured and OFY after 3 starts. Still, having a mobile QB helped the numbers improve to 204 (4.6) rush with 22 sacks allowed (1 more gm). This year they lose 4 OL (34/54) but return 3 OL with 8+ starts (1-1st tm MAC) and get Schleicher back, so are more experienced (42 car sts) and remain strong. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the Broncos allowed 192 (5.0) rush with just 19 sacks (lowest since 19 in s/'20, just 6 gm). Houston transfer Nadame Tucker was the star with 14.5 sacks and was the MAC POY. The Broncos allowed just 126 (3.7) rush while increasing their sacks to 43 (11.0%). This year they lose all 4 starters plus the top 3 backups. MIAMI REDHAWKS OL ERIC SMITH POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Last year Miami lost a six year veteran QB (#3 career passer). They brought in DeQuan Finn, who was the MAC MVP in '23 while QB at Toledo. Henry Hesson (7-17-93 '24) and rFr Thomas Gotkowski (PS#107) were the backups. Finn was injured vs UNLV and Hesson hit 8-17-134 but could not hold a 2 TD lead. Hesson hit 13-21-208 vs Lindenwood but then Finn returned. Prior to the Toledo game, Finn left the team and Hesson hit just 11-38-147-0-3 in the loss. Hesson started vs Buffalo but after leading 2 drives totaling 2 yds, Gotkowski came in. He led wins vs Buffalo and Ball St. For the season he threw for 575 (44%, 4-1, 115 rush). HC Martin said he saved their season. This year they lose Finn (1451, 59%, 9-6, #2 rush 395, 4.4) and Hesson (596, 39.8%, 4-3, -6 rush). They add David McComb (PS#34) from Kansas, Caleb Heavner from D-II Fort Hays (1590 pass, 664 rush) and true frosh Andrew Bellisari (PS#121). They have two capable QB's and could top '25's numbers. .RUNNING BACKS - In '24 Miami had to replace their first 1,000 yard (1075, 5.1) rusher here s/'05. Kenny Tracy (5 st, 250, 5.4) was then OFY in fall camp. Last year they again lost their 1,000 yard rusher along with their #2 (331, 6.6). I said new RB's would emerge but they probably would not have a 1,000 yard RB. Tracy returned and had 104 vs UNLV and 134 vs Lindenwood but then was OFY (#4, 272, 5.6). Jordan Brunson had 122 vs EMich and 123 vs Buffalo, leading with 767 (4.7). RFr D'Shawante Jones (PS#169) was #3 (277, 4.4). This year they lose 2 of their top 3 RB's but add Rodney Nelson, who rushed for 1,802 (6.2) at Merrimack, and Cade Yacamelli, who rushed for 571 (5.3) in 3 years at Wisconsin. The unit is more experienced and Martin should once again have a solid RB corps. RECEIVERS - Last year Miami lost their #1 (818, 14.4), #2 (816, 19.9) and #3 (631, 12.1) receivers. Their top 2 returnees were WR's Kam Perry (3 st, 166, 16.6) and Cole Weaver (2 st, 38, 19.0). Martin brought in 9 transfers including VHT Deion Colzie (PS#11, ND), so the unit was only slightly less experienced than '24. Perry had three 100+ efforts the first 4 games (0 after that) and led with 976 (22.7!). Weaver was a solid #2 (642, 14.3) and Keith Reynolds was #3 (352, 9.8). Colzie was #4 (178, 16.2). This year they lose 3 of the top 4 with only Reynolds back. They add in PS#22, #40 and #58 P4 transfers along with 4 others and are on par with '25 experience wise. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the OLine returned 4 starters (two 2nd tm MAC OL). The numbers were not great with just 135 (4.6) rush allowing 29 sacks but in MAC play they put up 148 (4.9) only allowing 14 sacks in 9 games. Last year they lost all 5 starters including a 1st Tm MAC RT and returned just 3 career starts (#136 FBS!). The numbers actually improved (more mobile QB) to 160 (4.1) with 18 sacks in MAC play. This year they lose 3 OL (21/23) but return three 14 games starters including 2nd tm MAC LT Eric Smith, a RG who started 7 of the last 8 and add in NIU's LT (12 st) and 4 other transfers. They return 4269 career FBS starts along with 17 FCS starts, so are much more experienced and are one of the MAC's top OLines. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the DLine went from four to two returning starters but had similar numbers allowing 137 (3.9) with 30 sacks. Last year they lost a 1st Tm MAC DE and 3 others who combined for 30 starts. I said Martin would develop a solid front but this group was much less experienced. Martin did a good job as they improved to allowing 134 (3.7) rush with 41 sacks. This year they lose 1st tm MAC DE Adam Trick (13 st, #6 tklr, 8.5 sk, 4 pbu) and two other starters. They return one starter again but add Cincinnati starter Mikah Coleman (12 st, 33 tkl) along with former Akron starter Marcus Moore (8 st, 31 tkl '24, RS Purdue '25) and are on par experience-wise with last year's unit, but will need another DE, like Trick, to emerge. LINEBACKERS - Last year the unit lost 1st Tm MAC (#1 tkl'r) and 2nd Tm MAC (#5, 5 sk) long time starting LB's. They returned their #5 & #8 tacklers. Miami held foes to 33 ypg below their average in 2024 and 7 below last year with the 3 starters all seniors. This year they lose their #2, #3 and #9 tacklers. They return Malcolm McCain, who despite just 2 starts was #4 tackler (6.5 tfl). They add Kent St and South Alabama starters, so they are on par with last year's experience-wise and Martin calls this unit the best group on defense. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '24 the secondary lost 2 starters (2nd tm MAC CB) but finished #26 in our PDR allowing a super 10-13 ratio! Last year with 3 starters back this looked like the MAC's best secondary but I said it might be tough to match 24's PDR finish with a weaker front 7. Miami finished #55 (56.5%, 22-14). This year they lose 1st tm MAC Eli Blakely (#1 tklr), 2nd tm MAC Silas Walters (#5) and their #8 tackler (7 st). Five of the top 8 are back plus they add in two B10 transfers with 8+ starts in a season along with 3 other P4 transfers, so even losing their top two, they should remain strong in the PDR. RB DUNCAN BRUNE OHIO BOBCATS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 Parker Navarro shined in MAC play and for the season threw for 2,423 yards hitting 66% with a 13-11 ratio. His legs were a key as he was #2 rusher with 1,054 (6.6, 18 td). He was the first ever Bobcat QB with 2000+ pass and 1000+ rush in the same season. JC Nick Poulos hit 22-49-271-2-1 with 149 (5.3) rush. Last year Navarro threw for 2,375 (62%, 14-11) and was #2 rusher with 886 (5.5). Poulos hit 4-8-19 but RS. They add true frosh Levi Davis (PS#89, IFS) and Matt Vezza, who threw for 2,673 (61%, 19-7) with 601 (4.0) rush for New Hampshire last year. Navarro was a veteran leader and dynamic on 3rd and 4th down and will be tough to replace but Ohio has had a 1st or 2nd tm MAC QB four straight years. RUNNING BACKS - In '23 Sieh Bangura, who had been the MAC FPOY in '22 (1078, 4.9), led again with 811 (4.6). In '24 he transferred to Minnesota and Ohio also lost their #2 RB (452, 3.3). Then-HC Tim Albin usually produced solid RB's. They added a VHT transfer from Northwestern, who led with 1,215 (5.1). True frosh Duncan Brune had 84 (3.2). Last year they again lost their top two but Bangura (4-12, 3 gm Minn) transferred back. They also signed PS#72 and #193 true frosh. The Bangura/Brune duo was the best in the MAC. Bangura became the fifth Bobcat to have two 1,000 yard seasons leading with 1,392 (5.8) while German born Brune was #2 RB with 586 (4.9). This year they lose Bangura but return Brune, who is 218 lbs with speed (10.85 100M) and a great work ethic. They add Victor Rosa, who had 636 (4.5) in '22 and 550 (4.9) in '23 for UConn. The Bobcats RB unit should once again be solid. RECEIVERS - In '24 Ohio lost their top 7 receivers including their #1 (660, 11.8) and #2 (11 st, 617, 13.1) WR's plus their top TE (11 st, #4, 243, 11.1). Then-HC Albin said the new group was the fastest set of WR's the Bobcats ever had. Leading returnee Chase Hendricks (108, 8.8 '23) improved to 471 (11.8, #2). They added a FCS transfer who exploded for a Bobcat single season record 1,245 (16.0). RFr TE Mason Williams was #4 (211, 11.1) earning Frosh AA. Last year they lost the top guy but four of the top 5 returned. Hendricks had six 100+ games the first 7 but only 10-145 the last 4 games. He had the Bobcat's 4th ever 1,000 yard season (1037, 14.6). Rodney Harris was #2 (419, 13.9). Williams was #3 with 276 (10.6). This year they lose their top 4 receivers. Their top returnee Dom Dorwart (#5, 119, 10.8) who is the offense's only returning starter (7 st). They add four P4 transfers but none have played much, so this unit is a question mark with most projected starters missing spring. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '23 with 57 career OL starts back (2 starters), Ohio improved to 214 ypg rush (5.2, #12 FBS) allowing just 21 sacks. Last year the unit lost 4 starters (two 2nd Tm MAC OL). They added starters from Dartmouth & DII Shippenburg along with a PS#165 transfer (App St/USC). They also got back Ohio 2 year starter Shedrick Rhodes, who transferred back from Rutgers (2 gm, RS). Their career starts dropped to 44 FBS starts but as all 5 OL, started all 13, they improved to 227 (5.3, #9 FBS) rush allowing just 22 sacks. This year they lose all 5 starters (1st & 2nd tm MAC, 65/138). They add 4 transfers (just one full time FCS str). They return ZERO FBS starts (37 FCS), lose their solid rushing QB and their 1000+ yd rushing RB, so their numbers figure to drop this year. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the DLine lost 3 starters and 2 backups but added 4 transfers. They did return their top sack DL. The unit was surprisingly just as dominant, allowing just 91 ypg rush (2.9) with 35 sacks. Last year they lost all 4 starters and 3 backups! They added 5 transfers with the unit's top returnee having just 12 tackles. As you would expect they dropped to allowing 144 (4.4) rush (my computer proj 143) and had just 22 sacks. This year the unit loses 3 starters (35 st, 92 tkl, 10 sk). They return Nehemiah Dukes (13 st) and Austin Mitchell (3 st). They also add a 2Y starter from Marion and a P4 transfer (Cinn/ Mich St), so are more experienced and will be solid as always. LINEBACKERS - Last year the LB corps lost two starters (#1, #3 tklr) and two backups (59 tkl). They added a pair of DII all-conf LB's and two FBS transfers, so were in the same shape as '24. In '24 they held foes to 58 ypg below their average (#23) but last year allowed foes 5 ypg below (#67). Michael Molnar started the first 8 before being OFY (ACL) but still finished as the #4 tackler. NB Jalen Thomeson led with 80 tackles (6 tfl), true Frosh Charlie Christopher was the #3 tackler and Jack Fries was #6. This year they lose the two transfers (#8, #16 tklr) plus Thompson. They return Christopher, Fries and Molnar and add Holy Cross transfer NB Eli Thompson (12 st, 2nd tm all-Patriot, 85 tkl '25) making them much more experienced. DEFENSIVE BACKS - Ohio finished #60 (63%, 14-15) in our PDR in '23 and #67 (61%, 16-11) in '24. Last year they lost 2 starters (#2, #8 tklr). They added 3 transfers, so were on par experience-wise but dropped to #99 in the PDR (64.2%, 19-12). This year they lose 3 starters (#2, #7, #9 tklr). They add in 3 FCS full time starters and return S DJ Walker (13 st, #5 tklr) who is like a coach on the field. Despite only one starter back they should still move back up in the PDR and the S's are talented but just need to add some weight over summer. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 Ohio got a Stock Market bounce back up to #45 in our STR. Last year they lost ST RANK L6Y: their K (13-16), P (37.8 net), 3rd Tm MAC RM. This year they return both Haynes and Peacock and LS Nick Hemer while adding Kent St's K (8-11) and should Stock Market bounce back up. EASTERN MICHIGAN EAGLES OL NICHOLAS GALLEGOS POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Last year the Eagles had to replace their starter (2684, 60%, 15-9). They added in Noah Kim (PS#71) from Coastal Carolina (333, 54%, 4-1). Kim was originally at Mich St, making 5 starts in '23 (1090, 57%, 6-6). Last year Kim led the MAC in passing with 2,817 (61.4%, 18-11). This year Kim was granted a 7th season, so the Eagles finally have some continuity at QB. They have not had a QB lead the team in passing in B2B years since 2017! Kim is calm in the pocket with good feet and was also EM's #3 rusher (186, 2.4) last year. They also return Soph Jace Stuckey (PS#115) and rFr Bryce Button (PS#133), who was the Scout Team POY in '25). They also add Yale transfer Brogan McCaughey (PS#158). HC Creighton feels that Kim will be the best QB in the MAC this year. RUNNING BACKS - Dontae McMillan, who had 801 (5.9) at Weber St in '22 had just 32 (3.9) here in '23. He started the first 2 in '24 but then was OFY (87, 3.8). Joey Mattford was #4 (118, 4.1) in '24. Last year they lost their top RB (799, 4.4). They added Tavierre Dunlap (PS#31, Mich) and I said they should at least match '24's production. HC Chris Creighton felt the top 4 RB's would all play and that the unit would be one of the MAC's top RB corps. He was spot on as McMillan led with 1,014 rush (5.7) and was #2 receiver (375, 11.4). McMillan was also the first ever Eagle to have 100 yards rush and 100 yards receiving in the same game (WMich). Dunlap finished #2 (428, 4.0). This year both depart with Mattford (48, 8.0) being the top returning RB. They add Syracuse transfer Malachi James and Braydon Bennett (PS#118), who had 781 (5.6) for Coastal Carolina in '24 (played w/QB Kim), plus return rFr Amareon Blue (PS#100). Despite the additions this unit won't match 25's solid production. RECEIVERS - HC Creighton is very good at developing JUCO WR's quickly. In '24 Mich St transfer Terry Lockett (PS#73), who had just 3 catches in '23, led a solid trio with 660 (14.4). Last year EM lost their #2 (651, 15.1) and #3 (639, 10.0) WR's along with their TE (#4, 232, 8.6). They had their top guy back and added in 3 transfers. Lockett was leading again but OFY week 5. Nick Devereaux had 5-121 vs Ohio and led with 510 (15.0). TE Joshua Long was #3 with 357 (9.6) earning 2nd tm MAC. True frosh Harold Mack's first game wasn't until week 8 but he had 6-179 vs Miami finishing #4 (333, 16.7). This year they lose #6 Lockett (263, 13.8) and their #5 receiver (301, 13.0) but the units top 3 are back, making this is a veteran group for once. They add in 3 transfers as well as 6 true frosh, who were all in for Spring. They could have their best output since '21. OFFENSE Jersey # in Green OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24, EM had two OL starters back (4 w/sts in '23) but returned just 28 career FBS starts. They added 3 transfers. HC Creighton produces NFL OL. EM's OLine paved the way for 142 (3.6) but allowed 35 sacks (8.4%). Last year they lost 3 starters but returned 48 career starts. I said they should have their best OLine in 3 years with better pass protection. Captain Micky Rewolinski missed the first 4 and they started the same lineup just 5 times. The unit still lived up to my expectations opening holes for 143 (4.4) rush and allowing just 11 sacks (2.7%!). This year they lose 3rd tm MAC Rewolinski (8/34) and 5 other OL (24/41). It will be tough to match '25's production but this looks like a solid unit once again with two starters back (26 car st) while adding 7 transfers (3 from P4). DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the Eagles improved slightly to allowing 164 rush (4.5) with 25 sacks. Last year they lost all 4 starters and 3 backups. They got off to a poor start (279, 6.5 rush F/5 gm) but got stronger allowing 209 (4.9) in MAC play but had just 14 sacks on the year. This year they lose 4 DL (31 st, 4.5 sk, #5, #6 & #10 tklr). They return 6 DL who had 12+ tackles including 5 who combined for 21 starts. They are led by DE Carter Evans (11 st, #9 tklr, 5.5 tfl). They also add 5 transfers including an all-SLC transfer NT from Lamar (13 st) and two, who combined for 16 sacks at JUCO making them more experienced overall and will be improved. LINEBACKERS - In '24 for the 2nd straight year EM allowed foes just over 50 ypg above their avg (#117). Last year they lost the Team MVP (#1 tkl'r, 11.5 tfl) plus the #2 and #7 tacklers. Unlike '24 they were not losing two with over 135 tackles each and did add in 2 transfers. The unit struggled with injuries as one of the transfers was OFY in game one and then a LB starter missed 3 games and wasn't fully healthy until week 10. The Eagles allowed 70 ypg above opp's average (#126). This year they lose their #4 tackler but have the most exp'd LB corps in 3 years and add 2 JUCO, who both had 86+ tackles last year. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '24 with a much less experienced group the secondary dropped all the way to #126 in our PDR allowing 63.8% with a 22-5 ratio. Last year they had two starters back and moved up some to #107 (60%, 16-7). This year they lose the #8, #12 and #13 tacklers (comb 18 st). Bryce Llewellyn was 2nd tm MAC and #1 tackler and is back along with 6 other DB's who started 3+ games last year. This unit should be more stable in 2026 and make a move up in the PDR. SPECIAL TEAMS - This unit is usually near the top of our Special Teams Rankings. In 2023 we rated them #12 and they finished #16! In '24 they unexpectedly dropped to #68 in our STR. CENTRAL MICHIGAN CHIPPEWAS DE KORVER DEMMA POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24, for a 2nd straight year CM's starter (1881, 57%, 12-8, 365 rush) transferred. They brought in Iowa's Joe Labas (PS#60). He threw for 1,114 (59%, 7-7) but he was OFY vs Ohio (gm #6). True Frosh Jadyn Glasser (PS#128) had 57 yds in 4Q vs BG and started the final 3. He finished with 439 (54%, 2-4). CM QB's combined to throw for just 163 ypg (55%, 11-12). Last year they opened with a 3-QB rotation of Labas, NAU transfer Angel Flores and Glasser but then Glasser was OFY vs Pitt. Labas was the passer (1854, 71%, 13-6) and Flores was the runner (#2, 527, 4.9). Flores missed 4 games and Marcus Beamon became the running QB (88, 2.7) but still RS. This year they lose Labas. The other 3 return along with rFr Danile Gomez (PS#184). They are moving to a power spread offense to take advantage of QB's run ability and figure to take a step back in their passing numbers. RUNNING BACKS - Last year CM lost their #1 (788, 4.9), #2 (418, 4.6) and #3 (292, 5.7) RB's. They added Tulane's Trey Cornist (PS#102, 149, 6.8). The unit was much less experienced but new HC Matt Drinkall felt they were deep and talented. QB Flores was #1 rusher until injury. Nahree Biggins had 14-113 vs EMich and led with 540 (5.1). Cornist was #3 (470, 4.5) and Brock Townsend was #4 (418, 5.1). This year the top two RB's depart but they return former Iowa transfer FB Rusty Vanwetzinga (5 st). They add Vaughn Blue (457, 4.5 3Y Liberty), Jayden Clerveaux (1704, 4.7, 2Y Holy Cross) and true Frosh Trav Moore (PS#89), who impressed in the spring. They are a little more experienced and in the new offense, should put up improved rush numbers. RECEIVERS - At one point In '24, the top 5 WR's were all out with injury. Last year they lost their #1 (just 360, 12.4), #2, (350, 18.4), #4 (186, 8.1) WR's and their TE (7 st, #7,11 rec). Despite losing their top 7 receivers, I said the unit could only be healthier and more productive. WR Tyson Davis (453, 15.1 '23) was back and they used more '12' personnel with their deep TE room. Langston Lewis became the first Chip to have B2B 100+ receiving games (WM, UB) in ten years here and led with 596 (13.6, 3rd tm MAC) with Tommy McIntosh #2 (422, 13.6, 10 st) in a run heavy based offense. This year they lose Davis #3 (270. 13.5) and McIntosh (appealing eligibility). With the top guy back and the addition of 4 transfers, they are on par with last year's unit. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the unit opened holes for 168 (4.5) rush while allowing 26 sacks (9.4%). Last year they lost 3 starters including a 2nd Tm MAC RT. They dropped to 1.5 starters back but added in 4 FCS/DII transfers with experience. New HC Drinkall was the OL coach for 24's Joe Moore Award winning Army OLine and liked the talent. CM improved to 170 (4.0) rush allowing just 19 sacks in the regular season but a poor bowl (91 rush, 5 sack) hurt their season stats (163, 3.9). This year they only lose 3 OL (13/13). They return 6 OL (52/71) plus add in three 2+ year FCS starters. They are moving to a power spread offense, so some of those retuning starters could be replaced by players who better fit the system. CM has had many successful NFL OL, so many talented OLine players choose to come here, which is huge for a non-P4 school. The OLine had 0 Senior starters last year, so are even stronger and HC Drinkall knows OLines! DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 CM allowed 170 (4.6) rush but did have 31 sacks (9.5%). Last year the DLine lost two starters and two backups but were more experienced and I said should be stronger vs the rush. CM cut it to 146 rush (4.3) but had just 28 sacks (6.8%). Their top player was DE Michael Heldman, who was #5 tackler and had 10.5 sacks, 5.5 tfl and 4 pbu! This year they lose Heldman, their starting NT and two backups along with former Iowa transfer (PS#119) who is OFY. Heldman was their havoc maker and they will need one to emerge this year. They return DE Korver Demma (13 st, 27 tkl, 3.5 sk, 5 tfl) and DE JJ Douglas, who as a true frosh had 23 tkl & 2 sk despite not starting and add 4 transfer improving their depth. LINEBACKERS - Last year the unit lost the #3 and #5 tacklers but returned their top guy in 2nd Tm MAC Jordan Kwiatkowki (#1 tkl'r, 14 tfl) along with Dakota Cochran, who did not start in '24 but was the #5 tackler (3.5 sk). CM allowed foes 28 ypg above their average (#97) but Kwiatkowski was MAC defensive POW 3 times. This year they lose their top 3 LBs in Kwiatkowski (13 st, #1 tklr, 12.5 tfl, 3 int), Cochran (13 st, #2, 5.5 tfl) and #10 tackler plus their NB (#12 tklr). They add three transfers and some very talented true frosh led by Drew Esper, who was impressive in the spring. The unit returns only returns a combined 42 tkl & 1 tfl as their top returnee is Xavier White (#12 tklr). This unit looks weaker and is my biggest question mark. DEFENSIVE BACKS - CM finished #102 (61%, 22-5) in our PDR in '21, #94 (59%, 21-4) in '22, #117 (62%, 20-5) in '23 and #93 (60.1%) in '24 but with a 17-2 ratio (only 2 int's!). Last year they lost a #7 DC but returned their #2, #4 and #9 tacklers plus added in 3 transfers and I said should have their best finish in our PDR since '20 (#82). They did exactly that moving up to #48 (58% 16-12). This year they lose 3 starters (#3, #4, #8 tklr). They add in 5 transfers but go from 3 to 1 returning starters and figure to take a drop in the PDR. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 CM climbed to #42 in our STR. Last year they lost their K, P and KR. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In '24 Central Mich was averaging 29.9 ppg but had just 12.4 ppg the last 5 (lost QB wk 6) finishing with 22.6 ppg. Last year they lost their top 4 rushers, top 7 receivers and 4 OL but my computer still called for 24.3 ppg and they almost hit it on the head with 23.8 ppg (miss by .5). This year they lose QB Labas and the top two rushers and most likely their #2 WR (appeal elig) but may have the best OLine in the MAC. They are switching the offense from a Pro style to a Power Spread to take advantage of the QB's run abilities. They are also a rare team that uses a FB, so I list them in "21" personnel! They had hoped to install this offense last year but did not have the players,this year they do and will have it be full force in '27. DEFENSE - In '24, 6 starters were back on defense and my computer called for the unit to improve to allowing just 29.2 ppg despite the tougher schedule. CM allowed 29.7 ppg!!! Last year 7 starters were back and my computer called for them to allow 357.8 ypg and they allowed 358.6 (miss by .8)! This year the defense loses 8 starters and 9 of their top 10 tacklers including their top 6. DC Sean Cronin has his work cut out for him. Last year the defense was a veteran unit but now units like the LB and secondary go from being veteran groups and a strength to a question mark. They have talent and hungry players and won't drop off too much. 2026 - Jim McElwain did a tremendous job here from 2019'24. In '24 they once again faced the toughest schedule in the MAC, as they were the only team in the league to face each of the MAC's top 5 teams (McElwain must have made the schedule maker mad!). The Chippewas opened 3-2 but then had a 2 point loss to Ohio and lost their starting QB. CM took of the 5 top MAC teams using backup QB's (100 ypg pass L/6) and went 1-4 down the stretch. Matt Drinkall took over last year and he was very happy with the program he inherited, as McElwain did a great job with culture and talent. The Chippewas figured to have much better health and went from facing the toughest MAC schedule to what looked like the 3rd easiest. They opened with 3 bowl teams on the road including Michigan but I said would flirt with bowl eligibility. Drinkall did more than that as they upset San Jose St in the opener. He is the first CM coach to win his debut game on the road since Bill Kelly (1951). Drinkall did a great job as they were tied for first in the MAC at 5-2 with 6 and 3 point losses heading into the final vs Toledo. They went 5-3 in MAC play (+11 ypg) and got to 7-5 and all 5 MAC wins were by DD's. They led eventual MAC champ WMich 21-14 4Q and just missed the MAC Title game. This group should be equally competitive. BUFFALO BULLS OL ALEX HEININGER POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Last year Buffalo had to replace their starter (2381, 57%, 19-5, 343, 2.8). They only returned Gunner Gray (4-11-41-0-1 in '24). They added Ta'Quan Roberson (PS#19, 3 yr Penn St) who in '23 threw for 2,075 (58%, 12-6) with 120 rush for UConn (10 st) despite coming off an ACL. Roberson had Buffalo up 17-0 over Troy but was injured and then missed UConn (both losses). Gray started vs UConn and played in 5, throwing for 228 (55%, 2-2). Roberson (11 st) had a solid season hitting 58% with 2,520 yards and 17 TD but had 12 int and only rushed for 117 (1.4). This year both depart. They return rFr Jason Wright (PS#131), who was used as a running QB (43, 2.9, 0 pass att). They signed true Frosh Qur'an McNeil (PS#55) and Jr Elijah Holmes, who threw for 3,040 (59%, 24-6) at D-II Wingate last year. The unit should cut down on int's and have the dual threat QB's that HC Pete Lembo covets. RUNNING BACKS - In 2024 Al-Jay Henderson was not the top guy early but took over with 142 vs Toledo, 107 vs Akron, 126 vs Ball St and 185 vs Kent St topping 1,000 in the bowl (1078, 5.3, 9 td). RFr Messiah Burch was #4 (153, 5.3) and Lamar Sperling (PS#160) was #5 (150, 3.8). Last year they lost their #3 rusher (306, 3.7). With a banged up OLine, Henderson's production dropped to 755 (4.1) with Soph Terrance Shelton, who HC Lembo called a younger version of Henderson, rushing for 244 (4.3). This year they lose their top guy and #3 Sperling had 234 (6.0). They add Chase Enlow (PS#42), who was in for spring, and the unit could top last year's output. RECEIVERS - In 2024 the unit lost their #1 (495, 12.4), #2 (451, 19.6), #3 (303, 10.5) and #4 (294, 24.5) receivers. Top returnee Nik McMillan (180, 13.9) was the leader of a young untested group but then he was OFY in week 2! Victor Snow took over as the top guy and led with 651 (11.8). Last year they lost their #2 (11 st, 536, 14.9), #3 (12 st, 243, 12.2) WR's and a TE (11 st, 101, 9.2). They added Jasaiah Gathings (307, 9.6, 9 st) from UConn. McMillan set the UB record with six straight 100+ receiving yard games to lead with 975 (15.8). Snow was #2 with 815 (13.1) and was the top PR. This year both McMillan and Snow transferred to P4 schools. They add a pair of experienced FCS TE's and an all-conf D-II WR, who will all compete right away. The unit returns Gathings (#3, 410, 13.4) and Chance Morrow (#5, 129, 16.1) but will need for some of their top guys to emerge to match last year's stats. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the unit had four starters back and the career starts climbed to 69. They opened holes for 169 (4.1) rush allowing 21 sacks (6.5%). Last year they lost two starters. They added two-time 2nd Tm NEC C Jake Timm and had 3 starters back. The unit got banged up and their numbers dropped to 132 (3.8) rush allowing 24 sacks (5.8%). This year they lose 5 OL (50/111) with just one starter back. They add three D-I transfers including two P4 (PS#67). If the unit can stay healthier, they could improve on last year's numbers but they return just 10 career FBS starts (20 FCS). DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the DLine lost 3 starters and were less experienced. Then NG George Wolo (4 st , 23 tkl, 3.5 sk in '23) was OFY after 4 starts. UB still improved to allowing 147 (4.1) rush with 33 sacks (7.5%). Last year they got Wolo back in addition to 4 other DL who started 7+ games including 2nd Tm MAC DE Kobe Stewart (9.5 sk!). The Bulls slipped to allowing 157 (3.8) but with 36 sacks (10.4%). This year they lose DE Stewart (12 st, 44 tkl, 3.5 sk), Wolo (10 st, 25 tkl, 1 sk), Malin White (12 st. #6 tklr, 3.5 sk. 4.5 tfl), Junior Poyser (7 st, 5.5 sk) and Devin Morgan (3.5 sk). Just one starter returns but they add 6 transfers and much like 2024 could have improved numbers. LINEBACKERS - In '24 the unit lost the #1 tackler. They returned #3 Red Murdock (6 st) and Shane Dolac. After basically losing all 3 starters in '23, they were much improved led by the Bash Brothers. Dolac led the FBS in tackles with 168 and Murdcok was #2 with 156! Last year they lost Buffalo's first ever Consensus All-American in Dolac. Murdock was back and they added 1st Tm Ivy LB Mitchell Gosner (65 tkl, Harvard). Murdock (#1 tklr, 142, 5 sk, 8.5 tfl, 2nd tm AA) broke Khalil Macks NCAA record of career forced fumbles with 17! This year he departs (#7 DC DEN) as does Gonser (5 st, #4 tklr, 6 tfl) and Dion Crawford (12 st, #2, 3.5 sk). They return NB Savion Brown (#7 tklr, 8 st, 6.5 tfl) and add in four transfers (2 P4) but are down a few notches losing their All-American. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '24 UB's secondary finished #103 in our PDR allowing 245 ypg pass (61%, 25-13). Last year they added in 1st Tm PSAC Miles Greer from Shephard U and returned 3 starters (#3, #5 #9 tklr) led by Soloman Brown (66 tkl, 7 pd). I called for a solid climb in our PDR and they moved up to #51 (57%, 19-14). This year they lose S Brown (12 st, #5 tklr) plus their #8 and #11 tacklers. They return Greer, who was the #3 tackler despite not starting, along with both CB's and add 3 transfers. The secondary should remain strong and Keontez Bradley and Kobi Blackwell are both all-MAC caliber CB's. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 as you would expect Lembo's Bulls rose to #54 in our STR. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In 2024 the Bulls had to replace their QB, 2 of the top 3 RB's and their top 5 receivers. The offense was a work in progress out the of the spring but New HC Pete Lembo was a magician as Buffalo outdid my computer's yardage forecast of 322 ypg with 355 ypg and 29 ppg thanks to 43 ppg the regular seasons final 4! Last year my computer called for 387 ypg but they came up short at 362 ypg. This year they lose their QB, top RB, top 2 receivers and 4 starting OL, while also bringing in a new OC. There are questions all over the offense but since last year's group underachieved, I could see this year's unit still topping last year's numbers. DEFENSE - In '22 my computer called for the Bulls allow 28 ppg and 387 ypg and they hit those on the head at 27 ypg and 396 ypg. In '23 my computer called for them to allow 26.6 ppg and 369 ypg and they again hit those numbers on the head with 27.4 ppg and 367 ypg!! In '24 my computer called for them to allow 25.2 ppg and they allowed 26.4 ppg. Last year my computer called for them to allow 24 ppg and they allowed 24 ppg!! This year they lose 9 of the top 11 tacklers. I won't tell you what I think of the defense. as with my computers accuracy you just need to check out page 43 to see what they will allow this year. 2026 - In '23 the Bulls went 3-9. Pete Lembo returned to the MAC (was Ball St HC) but stepped into a tough situation with a late start, some prior average recruiting classes and only 10 returning starters (#120 Exp Chart). It looked like a clear rebuilding year for the Bulls but two of my nine sets of power ratings actually called for 6 wins, which I said would be a great accomplishment. The Vegas Over/Under was 5.5 wins. As always Lembo outdid my expectations. The Bulls got their first win vs Top 25 team s/2008 when they upset NIU, then upset Toledo. At 4-2 they lost to WMich and Ohio but after having not won a November game since 2000 (former HC Linquist 0-9 in Nov) they won the last 4 by 17 ppg, then won the bowl game over Liberty 26-7 for an amazing 9-4 season! Buffalo was -25 ypg in MAC play and did rate an SMI of -4 in '25. Last year they went from #120 on my Exp Chart to #16. Buffalo played down to their opponents level during the season and opened just 5-4 (led Troy 17-0 4Q but lost, QB Roberson inj 3Q) but 3-1 in the MAC. They then lost their last 3 and missed out on a bowl bid! This year they have just 6 starters back overall. Buffalo has one of the lowest NIL pools in the country, which makes it tough to compete in the transfer portal era but HC Lembo is doing a solid job. Buffalo was -7 in TO's last year but +25 ypg in MAC play. They are much less experienced this year and most of my power ratings call for another losing season. AKRON ZIPS DE CYRUS DURHAM POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 the top two QB's (61%, 1015) moved on. Akron added Ben Finley (PS#64), who had 4 combined starts at NCSt and Cal. Finley threw for 2,604 (55%, 16-9). HC Joe Moorhead had used a two QB system at Penn St but last year they lost their running QB. Finley returned along with rFr Brayden Roggow (6'4" 195 PS#129). They added PS#13 Michael Johnson (Penn St, FAU, Syr). Finley hit 47% (4-2) in the first 5 games (out Toledo inj) but 53% after that. For the season he threw for 2,475 yards (51%, 19-9). Raggow played in 3 (11-17-91-1-0). Johnson was the running option (12-23-62, 42 rush). This year they only return Raggow and rFr Cibastian Broughton (PS#145). They bring in Reese Poffenbarger, who threw for 3,603 (59%, 36-13, 2nd tm CAA) for Albany in '23 and has been a backup at Miami Fl and North Texas the last two years, along with true frosh Semaj Beals (PS#64). Poffenbarger got stuck behind Cam Ward and Drew Mestemaker the last two years. He looked good in the spring and with no one in front of him, can now show his true colors. He should top Finley's stats from LY. RUNNING BACKS - Last year Akron lost their top 2 RB (664, 6.0) and (352, 4.1). They returned rFr Sean Patrick (PS#92) and added Jordan Gant (Tenn St 543, 3.8, '23 FCS Frosh AA). I said even losing their top two, the unit should at least match 2024's numbers. Patrick started the first 4 but then suffered a concussion. Gant became the starter and had 161 vs Duquesne, 176 vs CMich (Doak Walker Player of Week) and 153 vs UMass becoming the first 1,000 yard rusher (1032, 4.8) here since Dennis Kennedy in 2008! Patrick finished with 274 (4.0) and Marquese Williams (PS#25!) had 86 (4.1). This year all 3 return and Akron should have one of the MAC's top RB corps. This is the first time since Akron moved up to 1-A (FBS) in 1987 that the Zips return a 1,000 yd rusher as the only prior time was 1981 (Dennis Brumfield). Adding depth are Taven Curry (PS#163, ULM) and Chris Gee (PS#150, 854 Colgate 2Y). RECEIVERS - Last year the Zips lost their #1 (831, 19.3), #2 (446, 14.4) and #3 (308, 18.1) WR's. They added transfers from Marshall, Washington St and Pitt. Marcel Williams (Marshall) had just 15 catches after 8 games but became the main man with 30-458 over the last 4 games, finishing #1 with 641 (14.2) and earning 2nd tm MAC. RFr Kyron Mason finished #3 (481, 14.6). This year they lose #2 Israel Polk (525, 15.9, 3rd tm MAC) and #4 Myles Walker (209, 10.4). The unit is much more experienced and have some emerging stars plus the unit adds 6 transfers. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 Akron lost 3 OL starters. They returned 5 OL with starting experience and added 5 transfers. HC Joe Moorhead said they had been last in the MAC in rush yards and sacks allowed, making this unit the biggest emphasis of the spring. They were more talented overall and improved to 100 (3.5) rush with just 30 sacks allowed (7.2%). Last year they lost 3 starters and 2 backups (8/12). They had 2 starters back and Moorhead felt they hit on all 6 transfers, so I said they should improve again. They did with 135 (3.7) rush but allowed 35 sacks (8.7%). This year they lose 6 OL (35/57). The Zips return team captain C Colin Lyons plus Amarie Archer and Allen Jones, who each started 6+ games plus add 8 transfers (7 IFS). If they manage to improve again it will be the best OLine of the Moorhead era. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they had a veteran unit with 7 DT's that were 300+ lbs. Surprisingly their numbers slipped to allowing 182 rush (4.6) with just 18 sacks. Last year they lost a 1st Tm MAC DE and 6 other DL. They had zero starts back but I said the numbers wouldn't drop much after a disappointing '24 as they added 6 transfers. The front improved to allowing just 155 (4.3) rush with 26 sacks. This year they lose team captain Julien Laventure (#1 jersey, #7 tklr, 4 sk, 6.5 tfl) and a 3rd tm MAC DE (44 tkl, 12 st, 4 sk) plus a backup (5 st, 15 tkl). They add 4 transfers and are much more experienced and could improve again led by DE Cyrus Durham and DT Ronald Hull. LINEBACKERS - In '24 the unit lost the #5 tackler but returned the Zip's top 7 tacklers. Akron allowed foes 63 ypg above their average (#120). Last year they lost a 2nd Tm MAC LB (8 st, 120 tkl) and their #3 and #4 tacklers. They returned Gage Summers (#8 tklr) and Melvin Spriggs (#14). Both started slow but emerged late, with Summers (19 tkl vs KS) finishing as the #3 tackler and Spriggs the #5. This year they lose both along with Shammond Cooper (#1 tklr, 4.5 tfl). They return NB Alex Branch (#10 tklr) and add 5 transfers including Donelius Johnson (89 tkl, 9 tfl, 8 st in '24 at Kennesaw St '24) but are less experienced and outside of DE, the LB unit is the biggest question on the team with 9 guys slugging it out to fill the two deep. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '23 the Zips moved up to #72 (56%, 19-6) in my PDR. In '24 they lost all 4 starters and as expected they dropped to #122 (64%, 24-3). Last year they lost 2 starters (#2, #10 tklr) and 3 others (6 st, 30 tkl, 3 pbu). They had 8 DB's with starting experience, went from 0 to 2 ret starters and I said would climb in our PDR as Moorhead said it was the deepest, most athletic position on the team and best since he has been here. They moved up to #95 (60%, 20-11). This year they lose 4 DB's (37 st, #2, 4, 6, 11 tklr). They return their #9 tackler and 4 others who drew starts plus add in 4 transfers and should finish in the same area. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '23 the Zips, after some crucial misses (Indy, ouch!), used 3 K's in '23 who combined for 9-16 FG (L/40). In '24 they added transfers at P and ST RANK L6Y: K and as expected the unit improved up to #78, 2025 ...#130 their best finish since 2007. Last year they lost 2024 ....#78 a 1st Tm MAC P (40.3 net), K plus KO man (33 2023 ....#124 ....#114 TB) and figured to drop. They fell to #130 but P 2022 2021 ....#127 Joseph Castle avg 42.9 (35.9 net) and K Matthew 2020 ....#97 Schram took over after the starter hit 4-10 FG. Schram hit 12-13 with a long of 48. With Castle and Schram both back, I look for a solid climb in the STR this year. COACHES - Fifth year HC Joe Moorhead is originally from the nearby Pittsburgh area. He was QB coach at Akron in '04-'06 (MAC Title '05) & was OC from '07-'08. He was HC at his alma mater, Fordham ('12-'15, 38-13), OC at Penn St ('16-'17), HC at Miss St ('18-'19, 14-12) & OC at Oregon ('20-'21). He calls the offensive plays. Fifth year DC Tim Tibesar was LB coach at Wisconsin & Oregon St prior. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - Last year the Zips had one of the MAC's top QB's in Ben Finley so despite inexperience at RB and WR, Moorhead expected a big jump in the stats. My computer called for them to improve to 361.4 ypg and they had 355 ypg! This year they return their top WR and their 1,000 yard RB in Jordan Gant and should be even stronger overall. New QB Reese Poffenbarger sat behind two super QB's the last 2 years and should pilot the best offense in Moorhead's 4 years here. DEFENSE - In '23 the defense allowed just 28.0 ppg and 335 ypg. In '24 my computer called for 29.2 ppg but they slipped to allowing 32.0 ppg. Last year they lost all four DL starters and had just two starters back on the D. Moorhead did the best he could in the portal with a limited NIL budget and needed the 17+ newcomers to produce. This time my computer called for them to allow 407 ypg and 30.1 ppg and they were slightly better at 385 ypg and 27 ppg. This year they have 4 starters back and 3 of the top 11 tacklers. They should be on par with the '25 D. 2026 - Akron, since building InfoCision Stadium (30,000 seats) is just 25-59 at home vs FBS (4-5 L2Y) and has not finished a season with a winning record since 2015. Akron was -127 ypg in MAC play in '21. In '22, Joe Moorhead's first year, they improved +41 ypg! In '23 Akron returned 15 starters and 70 of their 85 players were Moorhead signees. The Zips had three OT losses plus losses by just 3 and 7. They beat rival Kent St and led Ohio by 11 at half but again finished just 2-10 (-79 ypg MAC). Akron had 3 Net Close Losses in '23, were -10 in Turnovers and had an offensive YPP of 17.1 (Going up Box each). With non-conf games vs Ohio St, Rutgers & South Carolina and the 4th toughest MAC slate, they did not make my Most Improved List. Akron opened just 2-8 but then won the Wagon Wheel game vs Kent St. With that momentum boost helping them upset Toledo in the final to get 3 MAC wins for first time since 2017. They were -10 in TO's in '24 (pg 29) and I said they would have their most wins since 2017 and they did at 5-7. Akron was an OT defeat vs Kent St from 6 wins but were not eligible for a bowl due to their APR rating. The bigger impact of their APR punishment was a reduction in practices by one day per week (Thursday) all season. With that restriction and having the lowest football budget & lowest coaching payroll in the FBS makes their 5-7 finish even more impressive. Akron improved their APR and so those restrictions are gone and they are eligible for a bowl this year. They also have perhaps their best offense under Moorhead. Akron has the acknowledged lowest NIL in the FBS, so I really like the job Moorhead is doing here and 4 of my 9 sets of power ratings call for them to be bowl eligible but of course that means 5 of them do not. 2026 PROJECTED STARTING LINEUP Jersey # Jersey # in Blue in Blue DEFENSE 6-4 275 PS#10. 5 gm, 2 tkl, 1 tfl at Ohio St as rFr. 2 gm, 2 tkl at SMU '24. BALL STATE CARDINALS OL COLE MOSIER POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '23 after being used mostly as a change of pace running QB the first 6, Kiael Kelly started the last 6 games. The Cardinals switched to an RPO offense which also helped the defense. Kelly went 3-3 as a starter with 3 close losses to the MAC's top teams. Ball St returned to a balanced offense in '24 as Kelly moved to DB/WR. Last year with the HC change, their '24 starter (2904 yds, 64%, 25-10) hit the portal. New HC Mike Uremovich's top two rushers at Butler in '24 were both QB's (1297, 441), who split the duties. Thus Kelly moved back full-time to QB. He stayed healthy all year and threw for 1,583 (56% 11-8). As expected he was the #1 rusher but with just 600 (2.8) as he absorbed 49 sacks. This year they lose Kelly. They add Keldric Luster (PS#79), who was at SMU and Texas St. He has a really big arm and is like a RB playing QB. They also add dual threat QB Tyler Mizzell, who threw for 2,889 (57%, 26-10) and rushed for 377 (5.2) at D-II Concord in '25. They return Uremovich signee rFr Khalel Wright and add true frosh Mason Adkins (PS#67). They are less experienced than last year but have QB's that fit Uremovich's system. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 the top 3 RB's departed and their two year streak of 1,000 yard rushers ended. Last year they lost their top RB (597, 4.0, #4 rec 329, 11.3) and their #2 RB (276, 4.5). They added transfers Qua Ashley (409, 3.4, Kent St) and Elijah Jackson (6-97, Purdue). The top 3 RB combined for 980 (4.2) rush in '24 but just 844 (4.4) last year. Ashley led the RB's with 547 (4.6) despite missing 2 games. True Frosh Jalen Bonds had 58 rush and 54 receiving vs Toledo. TJ Horton, a physical RB, finished with 180 (3.0). He added 294 KR yds (24.5, 1 td) and will see more time at RB this year as Ashley departs. Bonds, who played in just 3 games (129 ttl yd) will also be a bigger factor this year. They also return Jackson (54 ttl yd). They add Johnny Thompson (PS#42) from Kansas and two true frosh. This the unit could have it's most production since '23. RECEIVERS - In 2023 Qian Magwood led with 358 (8.7). Last year they lost their top 5 receivers including a TE that set the Ball St record for TE's with 839 (8.9). Magwood (6 st, 207, 9.0) was the top returnee. They added 1st Tm Patriot Eric Weatherly (865, 11.5 Bucknell) and former NIU TE Drew Cassen (8 st Butler). With a new run based offense, the production really dropped as the top 5 in '24 combined for 2,346 yards but last year's top 5 combined for just 1,060 yards. This year they lose 6 of their top 7 receivers with former Purdue transfer Donovan Hamilton (#2, 244, 12.2, 11 st) the top returnee. They add in 6 transfers and should improve over last year's poor numbers. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the Cardinals slipped to just 103 (3.3) rush with 33 sacks allowed (7.5%). Last year the unit lost 4+ starters. The career starts dropped to 11 with just one starter back. Even with a more run based offense and a mobile QB (#1 rusher) the rush numbers only improved to 132 (3.5) as they allowed 49 sacks (17.6%!). This year they lose 3 OL (26/26). They have 3 starters back and add 4 transfers including starters from Dartmouth and D-II Concord. They are in the 2nd year of the offense and return 44 career starts. They are much more experienced and the unit should be much improved. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the DLine lost all four starters and a lot of experience. As you would expect the Cardinals regressed to allowing 175 rush (5.2) with just 20 sacks. Last year they lost 3 starters, but went from 0 to one returning starter plus added in five transfers. Bryant transfer Nathan Voorhis was the top defensive player with a school record 12 sacks (Anthony Winbush 11.5 -'17). Ball St used a deep rotation and most of the numbers improved but only by a little allowing 4.7 ypc (179) with 23 sacks (6.5%). This year they lose 1st tm MAC DE Voorhis (#5 tklr) and 4 other DL (31 st, 84 tkl, 4.5 sk). They add 7 transfers. HC Uremovich likes the depth of talent, saying 12 DL can play and that it is the deepest unit on the team. The unit however has a combined 1 FBS start overall and will definitely miss Voorhis' production. LINEBACKERS - Last year the LB unit returned just 1 starter as they lost the #1 and #2 tacklers They returned the #4, #10 and #11 tacklers while also adding two transfers. Ball St allowed foes 106 ypg above their average (#129) in '24 and last year cut that to 49 ypg above (#119). This year they lose the top 6 LB's (#1, #2, #5, #6, #9, #18 tklr). They add 5 transfers but none have been starters, so the unit is even less experienced. Uremovich thinks they are more athletic and deeper than '25. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '24 the secondary lost all four starters again but returned 3 experienced backups (8 st, 62 tkl). Without a dominant front 7, they slipped in the PDR to #131 (62%) allowing a 37-8 ratio! Last year they added 4 transfers and returned two CB's, who combined to start 11 games as true frosh in '24. They were more experienced and I said they could only move up in the PDR. Ball St improved to #108 (62.7%, 209) thanks in part to DE Vorhees pass rush. This year they lose 5 DB (#3, #7, #12 tklr, 32 st). They return two DB with 7 starts each and another with 2, while adding 3 transfers. They are a little more experienced but with a less experienced front 7, may not show much improvement. They are led by CB Willizhuan Yates, FS DJ Fields and Purdue transfer SS Sterling Smith.
