PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - Last year Ball St had to replace their QB, top 3 rushers, top 5 receivers and 4 starting OL plus had a new staff and offense. They fell to just 272 ypg and 16 ppg averaging 114 ypg below what opponents allow (#133). This year they are in the second year of the new offense, have 4 QB's that Uremovich recruited for the system, have an improved OLine and are also improved at RB and WR. They will be much stronger on offense and it will show in their production numbers. DEFENSE- In '24 the Cardinals allowed 455 ypg and 40 ppg! Last year they had just 3 starters back but added a bunch of transfer. Unlike the offense, this unit made strides cutting it to 406 ypg and 30 ppg but still allowed foes 49 ypg above their average (#119) which was an improvement from '24 (-106, #129). The defense had 18 sacks after 7 games but just 4 the last 5 games. This year they have just 2 starters back and lose DE Vorhees (12 sk). HC Uremovich said the defense is what kept them in most games in 2025. They bring in a good amount of talented players, which will improve the overall depth and ability to rotate in fresh players. Their overall lack of FBS experience, however, could see them struggle, especially early in the season. 2026 - In 2020, then-HC Mike Neu led Ball St to their first MAC Title s/1996 and then upset #24 San Jose St in the bowl 34-13. Ball St finished ranked in both the AP & Coaches poll for the first time ever. Ball St then went 6-7, 5-7, 4-8 and 3-9 the next 4 years and Neu was then the first ever Ball St coach to be fired during the season (40-63 overall). In the era of the transfer portal, a new head coach usually means a massive turnover of the roster and that was the case here. Mike Uremovich did a solid job at his last stop inheriting a Butler team that was 3-14 during the spring/fall of 2021 and getting them to 7-4, 7-4 and 9-3 in his first 3 years with 3 playoff berths. It was tougher here last year with just 1 returning starter on offense and 3 on defense from 24's squad and of course a new system on Offense. I called it a rebuilding year for the Cardinals. Ball St was competitive at home going 4-1 with conference wins over Akron, Kent St and surprisingly Ohio but were non-competitive on the road losing by an average of 36-10 and -195 ypg. Ball St got to 4-5 after the win vs Kent St but lost their last 3 games by 21.6 ppg to finish 4-8, which was still a one game improvement. This year they again lose most of their starters. While they have just 6 starters back it may be a nod to HC Uremovich that he even has that many, as those who stayed, turned down lots of offers. Uremovich has a solid crop of his rFr signees from last year but still brought 25 transfers and is slowly upgrading the overall talent. Ball St should be an improved team but draws a tough slate and only one set of my power ratings calls for a bowl, in what looks like another rebuilding year. 2026 PROJECTED STARTING LINEUP Jersey # Jersey # in Red in Red DEFENSE 6-2 255 13 gm, 8 tkl as rFr. 1 st, 8 tkl, 1.5 tfl LY. 39 Maverick Gracio (6'4" 252 Jr) QB 6 Keldric Luster Jr. 5-10 248 PS#79. 7 gm, 85 ttl yd SMU '23-'24. 2 gm, 28 ttl yd Texas St LY. 9 Tyler DE 7 Ben Marsh Jr. Mizzell (6'1" 176 Jr), 1 gm Wake Forest rFr. 2889 (57%, 26-10), 377 rush (5.2) D-II Concord LY. 13 Khalel Wright (6'1" 194 rFr). MASSACHUSETTS MINUTEMEN RB ELIJAH FAULKNER POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In 2024 UMass' starter was OFY and true Frosh AJ Hairston (PS#108) threw for 480 (55%, 5-0) in his 4 games. Last year they added Brandon Rose (PS#37) from Utah and Grant Jordan (9 st, 1938, 66%, 22-3, 360 rush) from Yale. Rose won the job but was injured week two and only played in 4 games after that. Jordan started vs Iowa then Hairston started the next 7, throwing for 957 (49%, 4-4). Jordan saw most of the action the last two and threw for 593 (57%, 3-2, 112 rush). The three QB's combined to throw for 1,976 (54%, 8-9). This year all 3 depart. They add William "Pop" Watson (PS#30), who had 2 starts for Virginia Tech in 2024 being named ACC Off Player of week vs Virginia. He is a 5'11" dual threat QB with a lot of confidence, who grew up nearby. They also add RJ Johnson, who threw for 2,597 (65%, 18-4, 12 st) with Florida A&M last year and Logan Inagawa (1393 , 68%, 9-4, 8 st, 398 rush, true) from Drake. True frosh Aeden McCarthy (PS#137) could have the strongest arm of unit. Watson should have this unit a lot more productive, under their new OC. RUNNING BACKS - Last year the Minutemen lost their top 7 rushers including the top 3 RB's. Their top returnee had just 20 (2.5) in '24. They added Rocko Griffin, who had 483 (5.3) at UTSA in '23 and rFR Brandon Hood (PS#114 Colo). Hood had a 90 yard run vs Buffalo (24-179) and led with just 368 (3.8). Griffin led in rushing 4 times with 165 after 4 games but missed 3, finishing with just 245 (4.6). True Frosh Elijah Faulkner was #3 (114, 2.9). This year the top two depart. They add Justin Williams-Thomas (PS#77, Tenn, Cal, Marshall), Jordan Washington (PS#175, 340, 3.9, Murray St '25), Curtis Kimmons (892, 5.5, NAIA) and true frosh Justin Lewis (PS#71). This is an under-whelming group but can only be more productive. RECEIVERS - Last year the unit lost their #1 WR (839, 16.8). They returned #2 T.Y. Harding (334, 17.6) and #3 JacQuon Gibson (270, 11.7). The preseason talk was of the top notch speed and solid size of the unit. Using 3 QB's did not help nor did having Harding OFY after 3 games. Gibson was the bright spot with 100+ efforts in weeks 1 & 12, He led with 616 (9.7). This year they lose Gibson, their #2 (260, 9.6) and #4 (144, 9.0). Harding returns with TE's Max Dowling (#3, 199, 10.0, 10 st) and Reece Adkins (#5, 133, 14.7, 7 st). They add BC/Wisc transfer Joseph Griffin (PS#44) & D-II WR Jabari Lewis (9 st '24). This unit should be more productive in 2026. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 the unit was strong with 164 ypg rush (4.1) but allowed 30 sacks (9.2%). Last year they lost 4 starters (44/145).They added Harvard and Dartmouth starters (both 1st Tm Ivy) plus top 100 OL's from West Virginia and Northwestern. The career starts retuning dropped to 20. Their Duke transfer LT was OFY in August. They had just 82 ypg rush (2.8) and allowed 34 sacks (8.2%). This year they lose 7 OL (50/65). They return 3 OL who combined for 10 starts last year and move in a TE (2 st). They add a 12 game starter from Colorado St and 2 two year FCS starters (40 FCS starts). They also get back LT Zachary Franks (PS#99) after missing '25. Their career starts increase to 28 and Harasymiak feels that they are the 2nd best unit on the team and will surprise everyone. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 UMass' rush D improved to allowing 198 ypg rush (5.2) but the sacks fell to just 16 (5.9%). Last year they lost two starters. Tim Grant-Randall was back (10 st, 27 tkl) and they added in DE Joshua Nobles, who had 10 sacks at Jackson St along with four other transfers. Nobles then was OFY before the opener. DE Marques White was the top DL and led with 5 sacks. UMass allowed 221 (5.0) rush and had just 13 sacks. This year they lose all 4 starters (#7, #10, #11, #14 tklr, 8 sk) and 5 backups (10 st, 96 tkl). They add 10 transfers (4 P4) and get back Nobles. Like the OLine, this unit is rebuilt but could be the most improved unit on defense. LINEBACKERS - Last year the unit returned the #5 and #13 tacklers, had four back with starting experience and added 3 transfers (none were starters). They looked decent despite losing 3 of their top 4. UMass allowed foes 103 ypg above their average (#135). Tyler Martin earned 3rd Tm MAC (104, 4 tfl), Timmy Hinspeter was the #4 tklr (69 tkl, 2 sk) despite being injured and OFY after 7 games. This year they lose their #2 and #5 tacklers but are much more experienced, as they return Martin (#1 tklr) and get back Hinspeter plus they add 4 transfers. DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '24 UMass finished #97 (58%, 19-6) in our PDR. Last year they lost all 4 starters. They added five transfers (4 full time st'rs but 3 FCS) making them less experienced and I said would drop in our PDR. Davidson transfer CB TJ Magee was OFY after 3 starts. UMass fell all the way to #135 (67.3%, 29-4!). This year they lose a CB (11 st, #9 tklr) and 3 DB's, who combined for 7 starts. They return both starting safeties (#3, #6 tklr), get Magee back and add two transfers making much more experienced. That combined with more pressure (16 sk '25) from an improved DLine will lead to the secondary making a solid climb in the PDR. SACRAMENTO ST HORNETS LB DEREK HOUSTON POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In 2023 Carson Conklin (PS#73) made 2 starts (744, 54%, 6-2) but RS. In '24 the starter was OFY week 2. Conklin took over throwing for 2,876 yards (62%, 28-8) but was not a rush threat (-19 rush). He was a Jerry Rice Award ﬁnalist but then transferred to Fresno St. The Hornets brought in Tulsa's Cardell Williams (PS#94, 4 st, 1149, 60%, 10-7 in '23) and VHT QB Jaden Rashada (PS#6!), who threw for 485 (54%, 4-3) at Ariz St in '23 (DNP '24 at Georgia). Rashada started game one in then-HC Brennan Marion's unique offensive system but hit just 13-32 passes. Williams started vs Nevada (11-13) and took over. His best passing game was 332 yards vs Nevada. In a ground oriented attack Williams had 3 games under 100 yards passing but had 139 rush vs Weber St. For the season he threw for 1,621 (63%, 10-7) with 378 (3.8) rush with 12 rush td. Both QB's depart. Conklin (3 st, 354, 49%, 1-2 Fresno) returns. They also add Jaylen Patterson (PS#148, NMSt), Jackson Sharman, who threw for 332 yards (57%, 2-5) in 3 years at Idaho St, and JC QB Brian Salazar. They switch offenses again but it is back to the future with Conklin's return. RUNNING BACKS - Last year the Hornets lost their #1 (950, 5.2, 7 td, 317 rec) and #2 (361, 5.6) RB's. They brought in 4 FBS transfers including Rodney Hammond (PS#30) from Pitt (1546, 5.1, 14 td car). Hammond and Jaquail Smith each topped 100 vs Weber St, NColo and Idaho. Hammond had 208 vs EWash and led with 1,216 (6.5). Smith only played in 8 games but still ﬁnished #3 (511, 6.7). Colorado St transfer Damian Henderson was #2 (565, 6.2). This year the top 5 RB's depart. The top returnee is Jamar Curtis (155, 4.2) who RS due to injury. Curtis had 1,460 (6.2) and 1,139 (5.0) in '23 & '24 at Lafayette. Curron Borders had 361 (5.6) here in '24 but could miss his 2nd straight season with injury. They add Davion Godley, who had 1,142 (5.8) in 2 years for Weber St, Cincere Rhaney (PS#128 SDSt) and two JC's. It will be tough to match '25's production, especially with the change in offense and no VHT top RB. RECEIVERS - In '24 Danny Scudero was the #3 receiver (664, 12.8). Last year they had to replace a 2nd Tm Big Sky WR (797, 14.2), 4th Tm Big Sky WR (782, 13.3), Scudero, plus their TE (9 st, 191, 7.6). DEFENSE - In 2024 they lost 14 of their top 17 tacklers. The defense took a step back, allowing 424 ypg and 34.8 ppg (#8 Big Sky) and they allowed foes to gain 30 ypg above their average (#74 FCS). The Hornets lost to defending champ South Dakota St in the opener then only lost by 3 at Nevada. Alonzo Carter was excited to get the HC job, he was excited with a future move to the FBS, but when he was informed that move would be this year, it was after signing day and after the transfer portal closed. After spring he brought in over 13 additional players many from the JC ranks to face a now FBS schedule. CUSA CONFERENCE USA –– PHIL’S 2026 FORECAST–– 1. Liberty - Jamey Chadwell did a great job at Coastal Carolina and went 13-0 in 2023 with a Jan 1 bowl slot vs Oregon. In ‘24 they were the clear favorite to win CUSA again. Liberty played down to their opponents level and trailed at some point in all 12 games. They had one game cancelled by a hurricane. A depleted Flames squad was dominated in the bowl and were 8-4. I expected a bounce back last year but they shockingly opened 1-4. Liberty won 3 in a row and were back in contention for the CUSA crown but then blew a 10 pt lead and lost to Missouri St on a TD pass with :27 left then lost B2B2B games in OT and were just 4-8. This year they bring in some solid transfers like RB Kanye Udoh who was a 1,000 yard rusher for Army in 24. Liberty is my #1 Most Improved Team and is my choice to win CUSA. Liberty rates a +6.5 in my StockMarket and had 4 Net Close Losses and 4 New upsets and the Flames were #1 in CUSA at +67 ypg despite their 3-5 record. 2. WKU - WKU enters year 13 of CUSA play and has 8 bowl wins the last 12 years with only Georgia and Minnesota having more. Tyson Helton is 34-22-1 in CUSA play with 7 winning years out of 7 but has yet to win a conference title playing in just one title game. Every year he develops players and then loses a bunch to the portal. Last year just 2 starters were back on D and they lost 1st tm CUSA QB and 1631 yd rusher. WKU was upset by FIU but at 6-1 had a title game berth on the line at Jax St and led 28-17 but lost on a FG at :00 then beat SMiss in the bowl. They were +11 ypg in CUSA play. This year they have just 7 ret strs. QB Rodney Tisdale is back after starting the last 6 and providing a run threat at QB. They host Jax St and are 51-21 at “the Houch” since 2014 and could this be the year that Helton breaks through? 2. Jax State - Rich Rodriguez took over a 5-6 team and Jax St would have made the FCS playoffs if eligible going 9-2 in a transition year. In ‘23 Rich Rod exceeded my expectations going 9-4 in their first year of the FBS! In ‘24 they had just 9 ret strs. Jax St was #2 in my Power Poll in CUSA but did face both WKU and Liberty on the road. Jax St opened 0-3 but won the next 8 including a win at Liberty to clinch the CUSA title game. They lost a meaningless game to WKU then whipped WKU the next week in the title game. Last year Charles Kelly inherited just 4 ret strs from the CUSA champs. They faced both WKU and Liberty at home and got back to the title game but lost to Kennesaw St then beat Troy in the bowl for a 9-5 year. The Gamecocks return QB Creel but do lose AA RB Cook. They were +22 ypg in CUSA play and have 9 strs back and do avoid Liberty in CUSA play. 4. Kennesaw St - Kennesaw St fired coach Bohannon after a 72-38 record! They were 2-10 in ‘24 and -154 ypg in CUSA. New HC Mack brought in some solid talent and Kennesaw St was picked at the bottom of league in the preseason but Mack did a remarkable job and they not only got to the CUSA title game at 7-1 and +14 ypg in CUSA but then on the road beat Jax St 19-15 and won the CUSA crown! The defending champs do lose QB Odom to Syracuse but bring in Rickie Collins (PS#12, LSU/Syr) to replace him. They have just 9 ret strs and hit the portal hard again. The conference road trips are manageable and the Owls are capable of defending their crown! They do rate a -7.5 in my SMI and had 4 Net Close wins in ‘25 (signs pointing down). 4. Delaware - The Blue Hens were a super 9-2 last year and +115 in CAA play but did face 5 of the league’s bottom teams. Ryan Carty is 23-4 at home as a head coach and while they faced CUSA’s toughest schedule my main set of power ratings had them had them at 5-3. The Blue Hens did well in their FBS debut and were +37 ypg in CUSA play with a pair of 3 point losses and went 4-4 and 6-6 then beat Louisiana in a bowl for a solid 7-6 year. They have 12 ret strs this year including QB Minicucci and top RB Silver. They host Liberty and Jax St and avoid WKU and if they keep that great home edge could find their way to the title game. 4. FIU - In ‘24 they had 14 returning starters and were much better than their 4-8 record. They were +20 ypg in CUSA play. Willie Simmons inherited a team in much better shape than it was when MacIntrye took over and they had 4 Net Close Losses last year! Simmons brings a South Florida type of attitude and brought in a bunch of transfers. He had been a head coach for 8 years and has had 8 winning seasons. Expectations were low but Simmons was confident and he made it 9 for 9! At 3-5 the Panthers won the last 4 and were +42 ypg (#2!) in CUSA play. They have just 7 ret starters but who is to doubt is Simmons makes it 10 for 10. PHIL STEELE'S 2026 PRESEASON CUSA TEAM 1ST TEAM 2ND TEAM 3RD TEAM 7. New Mexico St - In 2022 Jerry Kill went an amazing 7-2 down the stretch including a 49-14 win over Liberty and a bowl win with their wins being two more than the previous 3 years combined! In 2023 with QB Pavia they were 10-3 dropping the CUSA title game to Liberty and the bowl to Fresno. In ‘24 Kill and Pavia went to Vandy and they rated a -5.5 in my SMI and were -7 ypg in CUSA play. New HC Sanchez had been on the staff during that remarkable revival but had just 10 returning starters. They fell to 3-9. In the final they led UTEP 24-7 but allowed 2 fumble return TD’s. Last year they figured to be improved but after a 3-2 start had 4 conf losses by 7 or less and were 4-8 and -76 ypg. This year they have just 10 ret strs but the defense should be much improved. Sanchez has yet to have a winning season as a HC but they will contend for one this year. 8. Middle Tennessee - In ‘24 MTSU let go of their long time coach and had just 7 starters back and were #107 on my Experience Chart with a new HC. They were pegged 4th in CUSA by the media but I called it a rebuilding year and pegged them 9th and they finished in a 3 way tie for eighth. In HC Derrick Mason’s 2nd year they were #36 on my Exp Chart and had a veteran QB in Nick Vattiato. Middle figured to be improved and they were going from -79 ypg in CUSA play to +18 (4th best). Unfortunately the record was the same 2-6 with losses by 8, 2, 3 and 3 in their first 4 games but they did finish strong with a pair of wins. HC’s usually hit their stride in year 3 and QB Gagliano who led those two wins is back with MT putting up 487 ypg in his 3 starts. This is Masons best team in his 3 years. 9. Missouri St - Ryan Beard guided the Bears thru the jump from the FCS to the FBS returning his top player in QB Jacob Clark. They faced the 2nd toughest schedule in the CUSA and Beard did a great job getting them to 7-5 and a bowl in his third year overall but first in the FBS. The Bears were 7-2 with a great shot at the title game but gave up a TD with :27 left and lost to Kenn St, then lost to LT at home. Beard took the Coastal Carolina job so the new HC is Casey Woods who was OC for SMU and his dad Sparky (17 yr HC) is on the staff. They have the fewest ret strs in CUSA with 5 and this figures to be a rebuilding year. 10. Sam Houston - In ‘23 SHSt opened an agonizing 0-8 with 4 close losses. SH went 3-1 the last 4 giving them momentum for 2024 plus they rated a SMI of +5.0 and had 3 Net Close Losses with all indicators pointing up. KC Keeler got them to 10-3 with road losses to UCF, WKU and Jax St in ‘24 but left for Temple. New HC Longo had just 7 ret strs. Most indicators were pointing down as they were +12 in TO’s, had 6 Net Close Wins and rated a SMI of -6. They also played their home games an hour away from campus so basically played 12 road games. The Indicators were correct as they opened 0-8 before a fortunate win vs Oregon St (outgained 474-157) and upset Delaware but were 2-10 and -119 ypg in CUSA (#9). This year they have 7 starters back and should be improved but they did have a lot of ground to make up. They do rate a +4.5 on my SMI and will be excited for their new home stadium. OL JOEP ENGBERS LIBERTY FLAMES expected last year as they have a chance to make more plays downfield which was lacking in '25. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '23 new OL coach Bill Durkin came over from Coastal and they had 72 career starts. In the new offense they improved immensely to 293 (6.1) rush with just 9 sacks (3.0%). In '24 the career starts dropped to 52. In '23 all 5 starters started all 13 games but in '24 they had injuries. The Flames still rushed for 251 ypg (5.5) with 22 sacks. Last year they lost a 1st tm CUSA RT (10/39). They had 2.5 starters back but the career starts dropped to 39. LT Trey Bedosky was OFY after two 2 starts and that shuffled the line which took some time to gel. They dropped to 194 (4.6) rush with 25 sacks. This year they have 4 starters back, plus add 3 transfers and should be one of CUSA's best. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 Liberty allowed 155 (4.0) rush and had just 20 sacks. Last year they lost 4 DL (30 sts) and two of those losses were post spring. They added NCSt and App St transfers then Florida St & Purdue transfers post spring. CJ Bazile was the CUSA Preseason Defensive POY but was injured week 2, missed 3 starts and only had 27 tackles and 5 tfl. The Flames allowed 179 (4.7) rush with just 16 sacks. This year They lose Bazile (9 st), and 4 other DL (11 st, 58 tkl, 5 sk). They add 3 transfers (see PSL) and have 6 DL back who drew starts last year and should be much tougher up front. LINEBACKERS - Liberty runs a 4-2-5 defense & I include the STAR in this unit. Last year they lost their #3, #6, #10 tacklers (14 sts). They added Florida, Michigan and App St transfers and had their top guy back and coach Chadwell told me that it was the best LB group he has had from top to bottom. Joseph Carter (#1 tklr '24) was #1 tackler by far when OFY week 7. This year they lose Carter (7 st, #2 tklr, 3.5 tfl) and their Star (9 st, #4 tklr) but they return Derrell Farrar who stepped in and was #1 tackler, Aidan Vaughn (6 sts) and add USF's Izaiah Guy (10 st 30 tkl '24). DEFENSIVE BACKS - In '24 they lost a 2nd tm CUSA S (10 st, #7 tkl'r), 1st tm CUSA CB (13 st, #8 tkl'r, 4 int) and a S (13 st, #2 tkl'r). I said they would drop some in the PDR and they did to #73 (59%, 11-8). Last year they had their most experienced unit since '22 and I said would make a solid climb in the PDR with all 4 starters all conf caliber. Their top guy, Brylan Green, missed a couple of games. Liberty still rose to #71 (58%, 17-7) in the PDR. This year they lose Green (5 st, #7 tklr, 5 pbu), plus their #3, 6, 8 and 9 tacklers. They add 7 transfers but are much less experienced could be susceptible to big plays. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 Liberty moved ST RANK: L5Y up to #75 in my STR. JAX STATE GAMECOCKS QB CADEN CREEL POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Last year they lost their starter who rushed for 1,344 (5.9, 15 td) and threw for 2,543 (61%, 14-7) plus his two backups. They added Gavin Wimsatt (PS#7) who started 19 games for Rutgers, rFr Caden Creel (PS#200) and true frosh Jack Moran (PS#98). Wimsatt won the job and started the first 5 with Creel being used at QB, RB, WR and PR at times. Creel moved the team better vs SMiss and won the job starting the last 8. He threw for 1,514 (61.6%, 9-4) and rushed for 1,076 (5.9). Wimsatt played in relief and had a key 62 yard Hail Mary before half vs Kenn St. He departs but Creel and Moran are back and rFr Kadyn Mitchell is similar athletically to Creel. As long as Creel stays healthy they should have improved stats and he is one of CUSA's best. RUNNING BACKS - In '24 they lost their top guy (896, 6.1) but added Georgia transfer Andrew Paul (PS#89) and D2 AA Trey Stewart (Limestone, 1361, 7.3). Stewart had just 41 ypg the first 3 games as he did not arrive til the summer but with three 200+ efforts led with 1,638 (5.9). QB's were #2 and #3 rushers. Last year only Paul (167, 4.3) returned. They added Cam Cook (PS#33) who was TCU's top rusher with 460 (3.9) and three rFr. I said it would be tough to match Stewart's production but I was wrong. Cook led the nation in all purpose yards with 1,945 (5.5) rush including 286 (9.5) receiving! Again QB's were #2 and #3 with Khristian Lando adding 201 (3.9) and Paul 127 (4.2). Without Cook in the bowl Lando led with just 11-44 and they did not add any super transfers so this unit will take a step back in production. Jalen Likely (52, 7.4) can make you miss and Justus Savage runs with power and can catch. They will be more of a committee and their top RB's all have a different style. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost their #1 WR (803, 16.7). Michael Pettway was #2 (454, 18.2). TE Brock Rechsteiner was #3 with 241 (15.1) and both returned. 6'8" Deondre Johnson was #4 in receptions but had almost double the yards of the #2 man with 724 (24.1!). He is back but they lose Rechsteiner (383, 10.6), their #3 (RB #4) and #5 receivers plus Pettway (859). They add 5 transfers including Jamill Williams (642, 14.9 Albany St), Darius Cannon (737, 9.6, Murray St) and Ronnel Johnson (463, 13.2 Missouri St). Johnson will be one of CUSA's top WR's and Gabe Glover is explosive. This unit is upgraded. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they had 3 starters back including a 3rd Team AA OL and 67 career starts. Having QB's rush for 1500+ helped and Jax St rushed for 251 (5.4) with 22 sacks. Last year they had just one starter back and lost three LT's to injury during the year. It was the same efficient unit, led by super OL coach Rick Trickett (78 yrs old) as they opened holes for 247 (5.3) and allowed just 24 sacks. This year Trickett left for West Virginia and they lose 4 starters (47/57) including 1st tm CUSA Cameron Griffin and "Bubba" Grayson. They add 8 transfers including 4 FCS starters. HC Kelly feels they hit on the guys they brought in and that this is one of the strengths of their team. DEFENSIVE LINE - In 2024 they lost a 1st tm CUSA DE (8.5 sk) and two other starters. They were undersized and allowed 175 (4.3) with 22 sacks. Last year they lost a 2nd tm CUSA DE (14 st, #8 tklr, 4 sk, 7 tfl) and a NG (5 st, 23 tkl, 2 tfl) but I said could be more productive. Kelly said it was the strength of the D and the most experienced unit on the team. 6'7" Emmanuel Oyebadejo (2nd year American FB) was #7 tackler and had 4.5 sacks. The unit improved, allowing 144 (4.0) rush with 28 sacks. This year they lose Oyebadejo, a NG (14 st, #5 tklr), DE (9 st, 32 tkl, 3 sk) and 2 backups DT (5.5 sk). They add a 2nd tm CAA DT, 2nd tm GAC (D2) DT, and two other transfers and have 3 DL back that started last year including Khurtiss Perry (PS#13 orig Ala). DT Jawaun Campbell was their best DL before he got hurt last year and Tae Floyd took off in spring. They are close to '25 experience wise and go 10-12 deep on the Dline. LINEBACKERS - In '24 the top returnee was the #7 tackler. Rich Rod felt it was the best they had been at LB here. Jax St gave up 48 ppg the first 3 games then 21.6 ppg the last 9 games. Last year they lost their #1, #4, #5, #6 and #7 tacklers. They allowed foes 13 ypg above their average. True frosh Mac Sanders was #2 tackler. Six different LB's started and four return. They lose their NB (#5 tklr) and their #9 tackler (5 sts). They get Morven Joseph (PS#50, orig Tenn) back from injury. Sanders was a Frosh AA and is one of the best LB's in CUSA. This unit is more experienced and Kelly feels their top 4 are as good as any in the league. DEFENSIVE BACKS- Jax St finished a strong #35 in my PDR in their first FBS year ('23), allowing just 58.5% with a super 15-16 ratio. In '24 they had 6 of the top 8 back, all with starting experience. They dropped in the PDR to #86 (60%, 21-12). Last year the unit's top 6 tacklers were gone. Caleb Nix had 4 int's and set the school record for int return yards (191) in a season. They surprisingly moved up a little to #72 (61%, 19-14). This year they lose 2 starters (#4, #10 tklr) but are more experienced and should move up again led by CB Tre'Quon Fegans (PS #25, orig USC) and Caleb Nix (Bo's bro) who Kelly calls the best S in CUSA. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 K Garrison Rippa hit both fg's in the bowl including the game-winner and hit 14-19 (L51). The return game was average and they were just #123 ST RANK L3Y: in my STR. Last year they lost their P (39.7 net). 2025 .. #127 True frosh Conor Donaghy avg 39.6 (net 36.9). 2024 ..#123 Rippa hit 21-28 fg (4 GW fg incl 52 yd vs SH ) 2023 ....#97 and had 32 TB on 67 KO. They were -4.7 on PR's and -4.8 on KR's and were just #123. This year everyone is back and they should have a good sized jump in the STR. . COACHES - Second year HC Charles Kelly has deep ties to the state of Alabama. He played at Auburn ('86-'89), was an ass't at Jax St ('94-'98), was on Florida St ('13) and Alabama ('20) National Title staffs and was DC at Colorado in '23 and assoc DC under Nick Saban at Alabama ('19-'22). New OC Taylor Housewright was TE coach here in '25 and was OC at Montana St ('21-'22). 2nd year DC is Brian Williams who was the DC at Maryland ('22-'24). 2nd year STC is Max Thurmond who has been an ass't in the OVC for 11 years and was offensive analyst at Tennessee the last 3 years. PHIL'S FORECAST OFFENSE - In Rich Rod's final year they had 442 ypg and 36.0 ppg. Last year just two starters returned. They did add experienced VHT's at QB and RB (TCU's #1 rusher). The offense did not change much as it was still be reliant on the run. My computer analyzed all the factors and called for them to have 29.2 ppg and they had 28.1 ppg!! This year they lose RB Cook and 4 starting OL but return QB Creel, exciting WR Johnson and HC Kelly likes the Oline so my computer calls for 27.4 ppg. DEFENSE - In '24 my computer called for them to allow 25.0 ppg and they almost hit it right on the head with 26.1 ppg!! Last year just three starters returned but new DC Brian Williams did a great job as my computer called for them to allow 29 ppg in the regular season and they beat that by a little, yielding 27 ppg. This year HC Kelly is bullish on all 3 areas calling the D-line the strength, LB Sanders and S Nix the best in CUSA. 2026 - Jax St was in the Ohio Valley Conference (9 titles) from 2003-2020. They made it to the FCS title game in 2015. In '23 the Gamecocks had 16 starters back and after facing just one FBS team, they faced 11 moving to CUSA. My 9 sets of power ratings had them anywhere from 2 to 10 wins, the biggest gap of any team. Jax St went a super 8-4 (Vegas win total 4.5) with a close loss at South Carolina and got to the New Orleans bowl where they beat Louisiana 34-31 despite allowing 3 defensive TD's! Jax St was the first ever team to win a bowl in it's first year of transition from FCS to FBS (FCS teams were 0-4 prior). In '24 they lost their QB, top 2 RB's, top 2 WR and 5 of the top 6 tacklers with just 9 starters back. While many indicators were pointing down, this was a deeper team than '23 (many more FBS recruits) that I said was capable of contending for the CUSA title. Jax St got off to an 0-3 start but then won 8 in a row (Hail Mary TD vs LT) and at home beat WKU 52-12 in the title game for the CUSA title. In the bowl Jax St had 16 players in the portal (Rich Rod at WVU) and Ohio none! Last year Charles Kelly had 6 returning starters (just 4 from '25). The defending CUSA champs had a brand new roster and I said it would be tough to match 2025's 9 win total but after a 2-3 start then Caden Creel took over at QB and got them to 7-1 in CUSA and hosting the CUSA title game once again! They are 16-4 at home the last 3 years but came up short, allowing a 4&14 conversion then a TD with :52 left. Jax beat Troy in the bowl for a 4th straight 9 win season! They did benefit from +10 TO's and 4 Net Upsets (both signs pointing down) plus lose AA RB Cook and face both Kenn St and WKU on the road. In non conf they face G6 powers NDakota St and Ohio on the road. KENNESAW STATE OWLS DB KODY JONES POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - Last year they moved Davis Bryson who threw for a school record 1,495 (55%, 6-10) and was #3 rusher (297, 2.6) in '24 to WR. They added Dexter Williams (PS#81) who had two starts at Indiana in '22 (165 rush, 184 pass). They also added Amari Odom (8 st, Wofford, 1565, 56%, 7-6). Skyler Williams (PS#247) the QB of the future was IFS. Dexter started the opener but Odom took over and blew away the school record, throwing for 2,594 (65% 19-8) and was #3 rusher (347, 2.9). He missed LA Tech and Williams was CUSA Off Player of week (27-36-290-4-0). Both depart and in what looks like a trade, Odom heads to Syracuse while the Owls bring in Rickie Collins (PS#12, orig LSU) from Syracuse (I hope KSt got some draft picks in deal). Last year Collins was #1 out of spring, got beat out by a ND transfer then started 5 games when the starter was injured. He threw for 1,042 (54%) with just a 6-10 ratio and had 126 rush yards. They also add Landon Varnes (PS#122JC) who threw for 3,296 last year. Odom had similar numbers at Wofford to Collins '25 numbers so Mack should turn Collins into a solid starter. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they had to replace their #1 (542, 3.9) and #2 (409, 3.4, #2 rec) RB's. Coleman Bennett would have started at Rice in '24 if not for a foot injury and he had 101 vs Middle Tennessee and led with 764 (4.9). D2 transfer Chase Belcher had 566 (5.3) and Alexander Diggs added 281 (3.9). All three depart so they are in the same shape as last year. They add Latrelle Murrell (893, 5.1, West Georgia), Tristan Morgan (809, 5.0 Benedict), PS#157JC Boogie Woods (928, 5.6) and true frosh Celley Davis (PS#74). HC Mack feels they have a 3-headed monster in Murrell, Morgan and Woods and they all bring something different to the table. RECEIVERS - In '23 RB Gabriel Benyard had 123 vs UTC and 136 vs Furman (both playoff teams) and led with 333 (23.8) in just four games. No WR/TE topped 300 yards. In '24 the top WR had 289 (12.0). Last year I said Benyard should be the top guy and that they should have a WR top 300 yards. Christian Moss jumped off the tape to HC Mack and he wondered why he had just 22 rec's (14.7) in '24. Benyard led the way with 949 (15.8) and Moss was #2 with 689 (15.3). RB Bennett was #3 (314, 11.6) and true frosh Clayton Coppock was #4 (311, 11.1). Seven of the top 8 depart including the top four. Javon Rogers (9-236) and converted QB Davis Bryson are the only returnees. They add productive starters from Tulsa, Tenn St and N Colo so Mack should form a solid receiving corps. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 KSU dropped to 115 (3.0) rush but allowed just 18 sacks (6.1%). Last year they added 10 transfers (14 OL were not on '24 roster) with an emphasis on size and girth and I said could have improved rush numbers in their 2nd year of FBS play despite losing four starters. They had just one missed start all year from the starting five and made solid improvement to 159 (4.1) rush with just 27 sacks. This year they only lose 3 starters but all were 1st or 2nd team CUSA (41/66). The Owls return two starters plus add a Middle Tenn starter and 3 FCS full time starters. They have good size (317 lb avg) and Mack will build another strong offensive front. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '23 they allowed 119 rush ypg with just 3.3 ypc. In '24 they lost one starter. Being at a size deficit vs most FBS teams they allowed 176 (4.6) rush and had 22 sacks. Last year they lost a 3rd tm Sun Belt DE (12 st, 45 tkl, 3 sk) and their NT (9 st, 26 tkl) but added six transfers and were bigger up front. They increased the sacks to 31 but the rush D was the same (185, 4.6). This year they lose 3 starters plus 1st Tm CUSA Elijah Hill who had 9 sacks as a true frosh. They return DE Marcus Patterson (14 st), DE Donovan Westmoreland (4 sk) plus add four transfers. DT Jaiden Grimes has gone from 245 to 290 lbs and is powerful inside. They are less experienced but have added size and the rush D could improve while the sacks will likely decrease. LINEBACKERS - Baron Hopson had 24 tackles in just four games in '23 and redshirted. In '24 Hopson had 19 tackles in 4 games then was OFY. Gabriel Benyard missed one game and was #7 tackler. Last year they lost their #1 and #2 tacklers. Benyard was OFY after 7 starts (#7 tklr, 1 int). Hopson finally stayed healthy and led CUSA with 138 tkls (9 tfl). This year Hopson returns as does Tywon Christopher who took Benyard's spot and was #2 tackler, plus NB Kody Jones. They added three experienced transfers and should be one of CUSA's top LB corps. DEFENSIVE BACKS- In '24 they lost their #1 and #2 tacklers. Versus much tougher competition they allowed 67% with a 21-4 ratio and were #122 in my PDR. Walk on Milon Jones was #3 tackler. Last year they returned all 4 starters, added 5 transfers and I said should make a solid move up the PDR. The unit was hit hard by injuries (13 missed starts) but still moved up to #87 in my PDR (61%, 19-9). This year they lose 5 DB's (47 st, #4, #5, #6 tklr). Tyler Hallum had 11 starts in '24 and DNP in '25 and returns as does Issac Paul (#3 tklr). They add 7 transfers. HC Mack likes their length and athleticism, and they should remain healthier so won't drop much in the PDR. SPECIAL TEAMS - In their first year of my Special Teams rankings KSU finished a solid #47! Last year everyone was gone including their LS. Two K's hit 12-18 fg (L50), P ST RANK L2Y: Joshua Huiet avg 41.4 (39.4 net) and they only 2025.... #89 fell a little to #69. This year they lose PR Gabriel 2024 ....#47 Benyard (25-19.4) and their P (38.4 net) but true frosh Daniel Kinney was an upgrade at K (6-7) is back and new P McKenzie has a big leg so they won't drop too much. COACHES - HC Jerry Mack was the RB coach for the NFL Jaguars/Titans. He was a 4Y HC at NC Central with a share of 3 consecutive MEAC titles (31-15). In his 5th year as a HC he won the CUSA for his 4th conference title and was awarded an extension thru 2031. 2nd OC Mitch Militello was an ass't under Josh Huepel at Tennessee, UCF and Missouri. The DC is Marc Mattioli who was the HC of Paris in the European League ('22-'23) and was an asst with Stanford and Vandy. STC Kyle Blocker was STC at Miami (OH) in '24 and a Special teams analyst at Tenn ('22-'23). PHIL'S FORECAST OFFENSE - The Owls switched away from the option offense in '23 and in 2024 my computer called for a drop to 20 ppg but they even missed that at 17 ppg and 251 ypg. Option teams usually have smaller mobile OL's and HC Mack brought in 14 new OL who added size and girth to the front. I said the offense would be much more potent in 2025 and my computer called for a jump of over a TD per game in the new hurry up offense. They opened with just 9 ppg vs two P4 teams but hit that goal with 27 ppg and 402 ypg with QB Odom the leader. This year they traded QB's with Syracuse and lose their top 9 rushers and top 4 receivers so should take a step back. DEFENSE - In '23 they were solid on D and allowed just 18 ppg and 309 ypg in FCS action. In '24 my computer called for them to almost double the ppg and allow 33.4 ppg and 438 ypg and they were very close at 31.2 ppg and 413 ypg. Last year they were bigger up front and my computer called for the Owls to improve to 381 ypg and 28.4 ppg and they allowed a few more ypg (405) but did better at ppg (25.5). This year they retained more guys on defense so are more experienced and have a bigger defensive front, 4 all conf caliber LB's and increased the size and athleticism of the DB's so should improve some more. 2026 - KSU only started playing football in 2015, but won the Big South three times and made the FCS playoffs 4 times, twice advancing to the quarterfinals. In 2024 they had 16 returning starters and close to 85 scholarships but I said it would be tough to top 23's three win total. Kennesaw opened 0-6 then somehow upset Liberty. Two games later after a 2OT loss to UTEP they fired coach Bohannon after a 72-38 record! They did upset FIU but were shutout for the first time in school history in the final. Kennesaw St has the smallest stadium in the FBS (10,200) with a 5 year average attendance of 6,319. New HC Jerry Mack had 4 winning seasons in 4 years at NC Central and hit the portal hard with 62 new guys and more size on both lines of scrimmage. They opened with losses to Wake Forest (10-9) and eventual National Champ Indiana (56-9) then had a remarkable year going 9-1 and winning the CUSA title game to go from worst to first! Their 8 win improvement was the 7th largest in college football history. The bowl game was a poor matchup as I used Western Michigan on the Phil Steele Plus tour with Kenn St allowing 236 rush (5.6) the last 4 weeks vs a WMich team that runs the ball and they lost 41-6. This year they lose QB Odom who was the key to the offense but Mack did well last year with a similarly experienced offense and has an improved D. Most indicators are pointing down with a -7.5 SMI and +4 Net Close Wins and they were just +14 in CUSA play. DELAWARE BLUE HENS QB NICK MINICUCCI POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '23 with both QB's out true frosh Nick Minicucci started the playoff game and led a win over Lafayette, (198-3-3). Minicucci on the year threw for 474 (61%, 5-5) and was #5 rusher (162, 4.7). In '24 It was deja-vu all over again as the starter was OFY after 3 games, his backup Zach Marker was OFY after 4 starts and Minicucci started the last 4. The 3 QB's combined for 2,718 yards (60%, 28-4!) with 207 rush. Last year they added UCF transfer Riley Trujillo (PS#43). Marker won the job but was OFY week 1! Minicucci threw for 3,683 (63% 23-7) with 235 (2.1) rush. RFr Braden Streeter (PS#178) hit 12-19-98 and both return as does Trujillo and rFr EJ Archield (PS#179). PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In 2023 my computer called for FIU to have 327 ypg and 20.6 ppg and they had 320 ypg and 20.1 ppg! In '24 my computer called for the offense to be almost a full TD per game better than the previous two years at 25.9 and 356 ypg and they hit it perfect with 26.3 ppg and 350 ypg. Even with just 3 starters back in '25 it called for improvement to 27.9 ppg and they had 28.5! FIU had 22.3 ppg the first 8 then exploded for 43 ppg the next 4. This year the Panthers lose their QB, 1,334 yard RB, top WR and 4 starting OL. They added a VTH transfer QB and a 1st Tm All CAA WR but are a little less experienced than '25 and may take time to get rolling again. DEFENSE - In '24 the Dline was the most improved unit so they didn't have to blitz as much. They improved to allowing 371 ypg (best s/2014) and 25.8 ppg. Last year they had 5 starters back on D. Coach Simmons felt it was a speedy back 7 so the key was how quickly a young DLine produced. My computer said they would allow 28.2 ppg and they gave up 27.8 (miss by .4!) in the reg ssn. This is year two of the defense and they return 7 of the top 14 tacklers. HC Simmons felt they were more of a finesse defense last year but are rocked up, more aggressive and will hit you this year so he expects improvement. 2026- FIU was 1-11 in 2021. Mike MacIntyre turned them 2026 around to 4-8 his first year and 4-8 his second. In '24 FIU actually out-scored their opponents but had FIVE close losses. They were much better than their 4-8 record. New head coach Willie Simmons took over a team in much better shape than it was 4 years prior. They did lose a lot of transfers (7 to P4 schools) so talent was not the problem. HC Simmons hit the portal hard and filled most of the holes. He was happy with the speed on defense and thought the offense would surprise. They were +15 ypg in CUSA play and had 4 Net Close Losses in '24 so as mentioned were better than their record. Simmons had been a head coach for 8 years and has had 8 winning seasons (12-1 his last year at FAMU) and kept that streak going last year. They opened last year just 3-5 but won their final 4 games for 7-5 and their first bowl since 2019! Simmons joined Butch Davis as the only FIU HC's to have a winning season in their first year. The 4 game win streak tied a program record (2010, 2018). FIU led 14-0 but was 1-10 on 4th down and lost the bowl to UTSA 57-20. Simmons is in year two and the Panthers face a tough conference road slate of Liberty, Jax St, Kenn St and Delaware. With that schedule they will need to pull some upsets to contend for the CUSA title but I have to figure that Simmons will get his 9th winning season out of 9 this year. MISSOURI STATE BEARS LB COOPER ROY POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '23 Minnesota transfer Jacob Clark started the first four games (1018, 62.9%, 10-2) but was OFY. Clark had great size at 6'5" 226 and was a capable runner. He stayed healthy in '24 and threw for 3,604 (70%, 26-6) guiding an unexpected 8 wins. Last year Clark returned and even vs tougher foes had a solid year, throwing for 3,244 (66%, 28-11). He was injured vs WKU and Cole Feuerbacher was listed as backup but true frosh Deuce Bailey (PS#173) finished the game and started the win vs Middle Tenn. He threw for 335 (49%, 2-0) and was #3 rusher with 81 (3.0). Clark leaves as the #2 all time leading passer here and Bailey transferred. Feuerbacher (6-8-28) is back but they add Skyler Locklear who started 7 for UTEP (1478, 56%, 13-11) and Henry Belin (PS#55) who had 2 starts for Duke in 3 years. Both are solid but it will be tough to come near Clark's numbers. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they lost their #1 (12 st, 824, 4.5) and #2 (460, 6.8!) RB's. They added Shomari Lawrence was 3rd tm CUSA with FIU in '23 (586, 4.5). Lawrence had a big finish to the year with 104 vs FIU, 109 vs UTEP and 173 vs Kenn St to lead with 1,021 (5.1). Soph Ramone Green was #5 RB in August but grabbed the #2 spot and rushed for 278 (5.3) and was #5 receiver (446, 15.4!). King Davis (PS#188) is a rFr with speed. They also add Breezy Dubar (PS#85 Boise (335, 5.4 true '23) and Josh Joyner (PS#98, Wash St). They do lose their 1,000 yard rusher but have more returning than they did last year and won't drop much. RECEIVERS - In '24 they lost their #1 (991, 13.6, 1st tm MVFC) and #2 WR (528, 18.9). RFr Jmariyae Robinson was #3 with 500 (11.1) and was 2nd Tm Frosh AA. Six receivers topped 350 yards (4 in '23). In '24 Robinson led in 100+ games with 3 and was #3 with 585 (15.4). Last year they lost their TE (#2, 590, 17.4), 2nd tm MVFC WR (12 st, #1, 770, 12.2), and their #4 (406, 16.2). They added two transfers so were a little more experienced. This time Robinson was #2 with 632 (14.4). He is back. True frosh Tristian Gardner was #3 (465, 15.5), Ronnel Johnson was #4 (463, 13.2). ULM transfer Dash Luke was #1 (640, 14.9) and all 3 depart. They return Makai Cope (8 st, 269, 13.5) James Blackstrain (6 st, 224, 10.2) and TE Jeron Askren (11 st, 224, 11.8) so are more experienced despite losing 3 of the top 4. HC Woods feels this is as talented a WR room as any in CUSA. OFFENSIVE LINE - This was a young Oline in '23, with 8 of their 9 OL making their first career starts. The entire unit returned in tact in '24 (57 car sts) but the numbers were similar with 119 (3.8) rush and 40 sacks allowed. Last year they only lost two backups (5/11) so had 67 career starts. They did lose their RG in August (11 st '24) and RT (5 st '24) after 3 starts. Taking on tougher competition they improved by putting up almost identical numbers a 3rd straight year, with 112 (3.5) rush but allowed 52 sacks! This year they lose 6 OL who combined for 58 starts (all 5 starters) so are starting from scratch and have just one career FBS start! DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 with 3 starters back the Bears allowed 178 (4.8) rush but did increase to 31 sacks. Last year they lost their top two sack DE's (7 & 6.5 sk) along with 300 lb DT (5 st, 14 tkl). They returned 6'3" 325 DT Sterling Smithson and added Penn St and WKU transfers. They dropped from 3 to 2 returning starters and I said should improve vs the run though the sack numbers would drop. Gilles Tchio (7 st '24) was OFY week 1. The Bears allowed 153 (4.6) with just 24 sacks. This year they lose 8 DL (45 st, 14 sk, 173 tkl). They return 3 DL who combined for 4 starts and add 6 transfers including Kellen Lindstrom (PS#48, Tenn) and Dylan Brooks (PS#5 Kansas) but lose 7 of the top 9. This is a total rebuild and a pass rusher needs to emerge but they do have 3 solid DT's. LINEBACKERS - In '24 they only returned their #4 tackler as they lost their #2, #6 and #14 tacklers. Missouri St did allow foes 19 ypg above avg (#75). Last year they lost their #1, #2 and #4 tacklers. Kanye Young (#6 tklr) was the only returnee. They added Jalen Brooks (118 tkl Campbell). Missouri St only allowed foes 9 ypg above their average. This year they lose their #2 and #5 tacklers but return Jared Lloyd (13 st, #1 tklr), NB Dylan Dixson (6 st, #7 tklr) and Cooper Roy (6 st, 3 tfl) so they are more experienced and this is the strength of the defense. DEFENSIVE BACKS- In '24 their top six DB's were back (comb 26 pbu's, 7 int's). Missouri St finished a solid #45 overall in my PDR allowing 60% (21-11). Last year they lost 4 DB's (29 st, #5, #8, #12 tkl) then suffered the tragic loss of their captain S Todric McGee who passed away. JJ O'Neal (8 st, 43 tkl) was the lone returnee and he redshirted after 4 games. They fell to #91 in my PDR (64%, 19-8). This year they lose 3 starters again (#3, #5, #14 tklr). They return Christian Ford (#6 tkl), get back O'Neal and add 5 transfers so are more experienced and should rise in the rankings but CB is a total rebuild. SPECIAL TEAMS - In '24 their 3rd Tm AA P returned and they added Mich St's Yousef Obeid. Obeid ST RANK LY: hit 11-12 fg (L/50) with 23 TB on 74 KO. Last year 2025 ..#132 they lost their top notch P (39.7 net) and KR (23.4). They added Bethune Cookman's P (39.3 net!). Unfortunately Obeid only hit 14-22 fg, Two P's comb for a 34.2 net, and they were -4 on Blk/TD's and finished #132. With K and P back they should have a Stock Market jump in the STR as Obeid was not 100% in '25 and has a big leg. COACHES - New HC is Casey Woods who was TE coach at Missouri ('20-'21) and SMU OC ('22-'25). His dad Sparky Woods is on the staff and has 48 years of coaching experience including 17 as a HC. His OC is Mark Cala who was QB coach at TCU ('23-'24) and OC at UTEP in '25. His DC is Jack Curtis who was DC at Georgia Southern ('11-'15), Tulane ('16-'20), and co-DC at Liberty ('21'-'23). He has been a defensive analyst with Auburn ('23-'25). Sparky Woods is the father of Casey and runs the Offensive ST's while Blake Shrader runs the Defensive ST's. PHIL’S FORECAST OFFENSE - In '23 the Bears put up 29.8 ppg (#6 in Valley) and 401 ypg (#5 in Valley). PS#47 QB Jacob Clark led the Bears to season highs with 59 points and 672 yards vs Utah Tech but was OFY after 4 games. In '24 Clark was back and Missouri St had 35 ppg and 425 ypg. Last year QB Clark was back along with 3 OL starters and two of the top 3 WR's but took on a tougher FBS schedule. Naturally they dropped but only to 392 ypg and 25.6 ppg. This year they have just 2 starters back and lose a 1,000 yard RB, QB Clark and all 5 OL and figure to take another step back offensively. DEFENSE - In '23 they lost five of their top six tacklers and allowed 30.3 ppg and 426 ypg. Ten starters returned in '24, they got back their top five tacklers and 16 of their top 20. They still allowed 30 ppg and 392 ypg. Last year six starters were back and they faced a tougher schedule but still managed to improved to 383 ypg and 28.8 ppg. This year they lose 11 of the top 15 tacklers. They are led by LB Jared Lloyd but with the DL and CB rooms in total rebuild it will be tough to improve much. 2026 - In 2020 the Bears made a splash hire, bringing in Bobby Petrino. The Bears shared the Missouri Valley title, and got a spot in the FCS Playoffs, both their first conference championship and playoff trip since 1990! In '21 they nearly upset Okla St in the opener, losing 23-16. The Bears won their final four regular season games but lost in the first round of the FCS Playoffs to UT Martin. (8-4, +65 ypg). In '22 they were preseason top 10 but finished just 5-6 (8th in MVFC, -45 ypg). All six of their losses came by double-digits. Petrino took the OC job at Texas A&M and DC Ryan Beard took over. The Bears lost QB Clark to injury vs SIU and finished 4-7 (-42 ypg). In '24 they had 19 starters back and were not eligible for the MV crown in a transition year. They opened a super 6-0 in MV play (best s/1978) with their longest win streak since 1988-89 before losses to super powers NDSt and SDSt. Their other two losses were to Montana (by 5) and Ball St (by 8). Last year Missouri St had just 10 returning starters for their step up to FBS and were wiped out 73-13 by USC week 1. Beard did a remarkable job as after a 2-3 start they won 5 in a row but with a shot at the CUSA title game they lost the last two. At 7-5 they made a bowl game in their first year of FBS play! This year Beard left for Coastal Carolina and they lose their QB, 1,000 yard RB, 3 of top 4 receivers, all 5 OL and 11 of the top 15 tacklers on defense. They have a rugged non conf schedule and the toughest CUSA slate and had 4 Net close wins last year. SAM HOUSTON BEARKATS RB ALTON McCASKILL POSITION OUTLOOK FOR 2026 QUARTERBACKS - In '24 they added Hunter Watson who led his JUCO team to a National Title. Watson won the job and was more dangerous with his legs (647, 3.9) as he topped 200 yards passing just four times but one was in the big win over Liberty and another in the bowl win. Last year they added Mabrey Mettauer (PS#30, Wisc), rFr DJ Bailey (PS#133), and true Frosh Landyn Locke (PS#66). Watson, a strong runner, was not a great fit for the Air Raid but won the job, and when healthy started but DNP the last 4 games. Mettauer started vs Hawaii and Oregon St but Locke took over late vs OSU and started the last three. The 3 QB's combined to hit 54.8% with a 12-10 ratio. This year Locke and Bailey are back. They added PS#162 and#207 true frosh. While the unit is less experienced, this is the second year in the offense with Locke more of a passing QB that could fit the offense better and they could top last year's numbers. RUNNING BACKS - Last year they lost the top 3 RB's (#1 745, 4.7 - #2 647, 3.9 - #3 481, 5.0). Elijah Green (PS#54) had 558 (4.3) for Longo at North Carolina in '22. Alton McCaskill (PS#37) was the AAC ROY when he led Houston with 961 (5.1) as a true frosh. Landan "Coco" Brown (PS#188) was their best overall back in the spring. McCaskill missed 4 games and was #3 (371, 4.2). Brown had 110 vs UTEP and 109 vs Delaware and led with 487 (5.8), plus was #3 receiver (237, 6.4). Green missed 3 games and was #2 (391, 6.7). This year they lose Green but have two of the top 3 back. Their RB room was a strength last year but couldn't produce behind a weak Oline. Longo feels the Oline will support them more this year so I'm expecting a solid improvement and McCaskill could return to his 2021 production and be one of CUSA's top RB's. RECEIVERS - Last year they lost their #1 (474, 11.0) #3 (313, 7.8) and #4 (271, 9.0) WR's plus their TE (13 st, 14 rec). I expected increased production in the new Air Raid offense but Chris Reed led with just 460 (15.3), Grady O'Neill was #2 with 392 (10.3), RB Brown was #3 and Tim Burns was #4 (228, 19.0). The top 4 all return plus they add 8 transfers so they are a lot more experienced. O'Neill has a knack for getting open and can create separation. Burns has really good speed while Reed is their best overall WR. NCSt transfer Christian Zachary is their big body with range, size and speed. They are a little undersized with 9 WR's under 6'0" but should be a lot more productive in year two of the offense. They do need a go to receiver to emerge which was lacking last year. OFFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they only lost a RT (10/28) plus they bulked up with most OL over 300 lbs. The numbers improved greatly to 180 (4.2) and 30 sacks allowed. Last year they had 3 starters back and 65 career starts. The numbers dropped to 132 (4.3) with 36 sacks in the Air Raid offense. This year they lose all 5 starters and a pair of backups. They return Cam Todd (2 sts) and add 7 transfers including 1st tm CUSA C Josiah Chenault (14 st, Kenn St) two others with FCS starting experience. The Oline was a weakness last year but Longo retooled the room and feels that it will be a more productive group. The career starts drop to 27 but this is the second year of the new offense. DEFENSIVE LINE - In '24 they allowed 145 (4.0) rush and 28 sacks. Last year they lost 9 DL who combined for 46 starts. They added 5 transfers but were much less experienced. The D dropped to allowing 208 (5.4) rush and had just 21 sacks. This year they lose 5 DL (24 sts, 71 tkl, 8 sk) but return 5 DL who combined for 20 starts, 109 tackles and 6.5 sacks. Dylan Frazier (41 tkl, 2 sk) is the leader and an All-CUSA caliber DT. They add 7 transfers (0 sts, 0 tkl LY) but are more experienced and will be tougher up front and Longo feels this is the strength of the defense. LINEBACKERS - In '24 SH held foes to 64 ypg below their average (#20). Last year they lost all 4 starters including their top 3 tacklers. WHAT EXACTLY IS A... PS#? One very important part of my College Football Preview Magazine is an individual player’s “PS#.” You will see them on almost every page and I ﬁnd them vital in my analysis of a team. If you have purchased my magazine before, I am sure you are very familiar with the term PS# and you know what it means. This article is for those of you picking up my magazine for the ﬁrst time and are asking the question, “what exactly is a PS#?” The simple deﬁnition of a PS# is my own ranking of players at their respective positions coming out of high school, or their Junior College (JUCO or JC) rating. The “PS” naturally stands for Phil Steele, with the number representing a player’s rank at their respective position. I do not scout high school games or players since my coverage of college football consumes all 52 weeks out of the year. Rather, I compile my own PS#’s based on a composite ranking generated with the aid of many different recruiting services across the country. You will see some of these services listed on the bottom left of this page. When we receive a recruiting publication or report, we translate each player’s ranking into a point system, generally ranging from 1-100. A member of my staff, Adam Jones, then logs each and every player into the computer that gives him a point total derived from each source. This is a very timeconsuming process. Each year our Freshmen List has well over 10,000 names on it! Many players are listed by just one or two sources. The higher rated recruits are mentioned by almost every source. The higher they are rated in each publication or report, the more total points they accrue. After months of entering all of this information, the list is sorted by each position and by total points. Naturally, the QB with the most total accrued points becomes the PS#1QB for that year. If a player is PS#99QB, that means he ranks 99th in total points of all QB’s coming out of high school that year. Some positions simply do not have as many players as others. For example, this year’s PS#100TE totaled 399.3 points in my system, while this year’s PS#100OL has 473.1 points. The reason is simple: there are FIVE offensive linemen and sometimes just one TE on the ﬁeld. Naturally, there are 4-5 times as many OL’s to choose from as TE’s, making it much more competitive. A player with 399.3 points on the offensive line is rated as a PS#276OL this year. The PS# is not their overall rank in the freshmen class, but their overall rank AT THAT POSITION in the freshmen class. A JUCO is a player who went to a Junior College (JC) after high school. Pending a waiver, they exhaust a year of college eligibility for every year they play at a JC. Most JUCO’s eventually sign their NLI’s as rising Juniors (played two years at a JC, have two years of eligibility remaining), although some arrive as Sophomore qualiﬁers after playing just one year of JC football. JUCO’s are older, more seasoned players who can often ﬁll a void or make an immediate impact. Every year a notable number of players end up at Junior Colleges who were once highly-rated players coming out of high school. They ended up at JC’s for various reasons: some were non-qualiﬁers coming out of high school, some had off-the-ﬁeld issues that affected their recruitment, and some players were dismissed at schools they previously signed at and use Junior College as a second chance to get back to FBS or FCS football. However, some players choose to go the JUCO route simply to gain more experience and exposure. They may have been overlooked in the recruiting process coming out of high school and use the opportunity to springboard themselves onto a school’s radar. Unlike incoming high school recruits, a player’s PS number out of a JUCO is not separated by position. Rather, all JUCO players at all positions get a PS# with the “JC” designation. So what is the big deal about where they are ranked out of high school? I equate it to where a player ranks in the NFL Draft. Obviously, there are some outstanding players in the NFL who were low-round draft picks, or even signed as undrafted free agents. However, the RECRUITING SOURCES: majority of the all-stars in the NFL are higher-round draft picks and ﬁrst-round 247 SPORTS picks who usually make an impact much Brentwood, TN www.247sports.com quicker. Colleges are much the same. There are plenty of players without a On3 Brentwood, TN high PS# who end up making it big. For www.on3.com example, Eric Fisher was a 250-lb tackle who only had one year of experience on ESPN Bristol, CT the OL in high school when he joined www.espn.com Central Michigan. Lightly scouted, he was a PS#498OL in 2009. Fisher then RIVALS New York, NY grew to 6-8 306 lbs, had an impressive www.rivals.com 116-inch broad jump and a blazing 4.44 TOM LEMMING 20-yard shuttle time to showcase his Schaumburg, IL www.tomlemmingprepfootball.com agility at the combine. Thereafter, Fisher was selected as the first pick in the GATORADE 2013 NFL Draft (highest ever for a MAC playeroftheyear.gatorade.com player). Some players enter college at 17 or 18, undersized and not yet matured, KOHL’S CAMPS www.kohlskicking.com but then grow into big, strong, fast players and make all-conference teams. Just CHRIS SAILER like the NFL, there are a good number www.ChrisSailerKicking.com of these types of stories. For example, CHRIS RUBIO 2000 MVP Kurt Warner was not drafted www.RubioLongSnapping.com and played in NFL Europe and the Arena PRO KICKER Football League. Other notable UFA’s www.prokicker.com were QB Tony Romo (Cowboys), TE Jeremiah Smith signed with Ohio State rated as the PS#1WR in 2024 coming out of ChaminadeMadonna Prep. Smith started 15 of the 16 games he appeared in as a true freshman and recorded 76 receptions for 1,315 yards (17.3 ypc). He was named a 1st Team All-American, 1st Team All-Big 10 pick and was named the Big Ten Freshman of the Year. Last year (‘25), Smith started 14 of the 15 games he appeared in and posted 87 receptions for 1,243 yards (14.3 ypc) and earned 1st Team All-American (unanimous selection) and 1st Team Big 10 honors for the second consecutive season, respectively. Smith will very likely be a high Lottery Pick in the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft. Antonio Gates (Chargers) and WR Wes Welker (SD, MIA, NE, DEN, STL). Also, just like the NFL, there are MORE cases of those players who come in highly ranked out of high school becoming stars and making an immediate impact in college. Here are some examples of the previously mentioned highly-ranked high school players that made an immediate impact in the NFL. In 2010, Cam Newton was a PS#2JC and after just one year at Auburn, was selected as the #1 overall pick by Carolina and went on to set an NFL rookie record with 4,051 pass yards and added 706 (5.6) rushing. Eric Berry, a PS#1DB in 2007, was taken as the #5 overall pick in 2010 and ﬁnished his rookie year with 92 tackles and 4 interceptions. In 2012, Andrew Luck (PS#8) was selected as the #1 pick in the draft. The 2015 draft was a great example as Jadeveon Clowney was a PS#1 and was the #1 pick, Greg Robinson was a PS#8 and was the #2 pick, Sammy Watkins was a PS#3 and was the #4 pick and Jake Matthews was a PS#4 and was the #6 pick. In 2016 it was easy to ﬁnd a standout as PS#14 RB Ezekiel Elliott, who was the #4 pick, became just the 5th rookie since 1970 to lead the NFL in rushing with 1,631 yards (318 more than the #2 rusher!). In 2017, Myles Garrett PS#3 was drafted #1 overall. Many times after players graduate, the talent behind them is unknown because the backups have not played a lot of college football. You would expect a 1st or 2nd round draft pick in the NFL to be able to step into an open starting spot rather quickly and the higher-rated players can usually do just that in college as well. That is the value of a PS#. On each individual right-hand team page, we list that year’s signees list for each school, which includes both freshmen and JUCO’s. These are ranked by each player’s combined frosh rating (not by their PS#’s), so the top player listed earned the highest ranking in the combined frosh rating (which takes total points into account). Who is a VHT and who is an HT? To the right you PHIL STEELE’S will see a chart simplifying our distinctions between these categories. To use the QB’s as an example: any 2026 PS RANKINGS QB from PS#1 through PS#30, I consider a VHT (Very POS VHT HT Highly Touted). QB’s from PS#31 through PS#100 are QB 30 100 40 125 HT’s (Highly Touted). Some recruiting publications do RB not distinguish between OT, OG and C for their OL. As WR 60 175 a general rule, we put them all into the OL category so TE 15 40 that position has the largest amount of players. OL 100 250 Also included on every signee list is the number of VHT’s DL 75 250 and HT’s that each team brings. For example, Alabama LB 75 200 signed the largest number of VHT’s (25) in 2014. While 24 DB 75 250 of their signees in 2015 were a VHT, in 2018 “only” 14 out of K 10 35 their 21 signees were VHT’s (5 HT’s). In 2023 the Crimson 3 10 Tide was back at it with 27 VHT’s! But in 2024 (after Nick LS Saban surprisingly announced his retirement), Alabama JC 100 200 signed 17 VHT’s. This is also a nice way to compare how your favorite team did in the recruiting wars vs other conference foes. A few quick notes about the players in my write-ups. First, sometimes on the offensive line I will mention that a player was a top-notch wrestler in high school. To me, a top wrestler has very good body control and athleticism, which often makes for a quality lineman. Second, I list when a player is from Canada. I do this because some recruiting services do not cover Canada, so Canadian players are generally rated lower in their PS#’s than their U.S. counterparts. As such, the top player out of Canada is often an NFL prospect, but typically only has a PS# around 150 or 200. Canadian players, therefore, are often more talented than their PS# would suggest. 2026 FROSH RECRUITING RANKINGS My recruiting ratings differ a little from the other fine recruiting publications because I take into account the strength of the Top 5 signees, the Top 10 signees and the average signing grade per player for the overall class. This list is not about the quantity of the recruits signed, but the overall quality of the classes. Sometimes a team with a class of fewer than 20 players may rate higher than one with 30. A perfect example would be South Carolina, which I rank #13 overall. The Gamecocks signed just 17 players, while most of the teams in the Top 20 averaged 27 players signed. The #1 recruiting class this year was signed by Oregon. This marks the 1st time in the last 18 years that the Ducks signed the #1 class, and also marks the 5th time in the last 18 years that Oregon has signed a class ranked in the Top 10. It is also worth noting that for the eighth consecutive year, Florida St has finished outside the Top 10. Recruiting rankings are a good tool to help predict a team's future success, but they are only a part of a team's achievements. Great coaches like Bill Snyder of Kansas St achieved seven winning seasons in his last nine years despite not signing a single Top 25 recruiting class! One final note, the ratings for Air Force, Army and Navy are not complete because the service academies do not release official signee lists until summer (and even so, most recruits head to prep schools). I hope your favorite team did well in the recruiting wars! 2026 PASS EFFICIENCY DEFENSE RANKINGS Here are my rankings for pass efficiency defense. They take into account the total yards, td’s, int’s and completion % just like the NCAA does. THE KEY DIFFERENCE between the NCAA pass D rankings and mine is that I also factor in the strength of opposing pass attacks. When looking at teams I have ranked higher than the NCAA, you’ll notice 3 of the top 9 teams that I rank higher (incl the top 3) are in the SEC conference all with double-digit differences: Kentucky (+30), Florida (+24) and Arkansas (+16). On the flip side 7 of the 10 CUSA teams ranked lower compared to the NCAA all with double-digit differences: Kennesaw St (-21), Delaware (-18), UTEP (-17) are the top 3. In conference play the CUSA did not have to face QB’s like Arch Manning, Trinidad Chambliss, Gunner Stockton and Marcel Reed. . The CUSA had just one QB in the Top 50 in pass efficinency. Let me show you a few underrated and overrated secondaries on the NCAA pass D chart from over the years. Oklahoma finished 12-2 in 2008 and went to the BCS Title game, but finished #46 in the NCAA pass D rankings. They allowed 252 ypg passing, but that came against the 7th toughest slate of opposing QB’s. The Sooners faced 8 of the top 17 QB’s in the NCAA’s pass efficiency rankings. The Big 12 was loaded at QB as OU faced Heisman runner-up Colt McCoy (#3, 3,859 yds), Zac Robinson (#5, 3,064), Graham Harrell (#8, 5,111), Chase Daniel twice (#10, 4,335), Joe Ganz (#14, 3,568), Todd Reesing (#17, 3,888) as well as #1DC Josh Freeman (#34, 2,945), all in conference play. They also faced ’07 Heisman winner Tim Tebow (#4, 2,746) in the National Title game. The Sooners only allowed 55.4% comp with a 22-19 ratio against a star-studded class of QB’s. Clearly, the Sooners were better than the #46 pass defense in the country and my Pass Efficiency Defense numbers ranked them #11. In 2012, I had TCU as my #6 Pass Eff D while the NCAA had them ranked #26. The difference once again was my factoring in the opponents as they faced my 6th toughest passing offenses including FIVE TEAMS that finished in the NCAA’s Top 10 passing offenses in #2 Texas Tech, #4 Baylor, #5 Oklahoma, #7 Oklahoma St, and #10 West Virginia. Vanderbilt was 2-10 in ‘09 but ranked #33 in the NCAA pass D rankings. The main reason is they only allowed 165 ypg passing, but that had a lot to do with their opponents. Georgia Tech & Army finished #116 and #120 in pass offense as both ran the option. Vanderbilt also faced the #113 pass offense of Mississippi St, #114 Kentucky, #97 LSU and #84 Rice. They even faced Western Carolina, who was the #91 pass offense in the FCS! Overall Vandy did not face a single passing offense that finished in the Top 40 and my pass D rankings had them at #77! Let’s look at another example, this one is from 2013. Iowa was #17 in the NCAA’s final Pass Eff D rankings while they were #45 in mine. The Hawkeyes’ opponents’ avg pass offense was #79 and at season’s end, they faced only one Top 50 pass offense which was LSU. And even that one against the Tigers came against a QB making his first ever start! If you would like to get my PDR (updated weekly), go to PhilSteele.com on Friday by 5:00 PM during football season and get my current pass D rankings, which take into account the strength of opponents faced and give you a much more accurate grade for your teams’s pass defense. # TEAM (NCAA Rank) GRADE 1. 2025 SPECIAL TEAMS RANKINGS Welcome to my ﬁnal 2025 Special Teams Rankings. As most of you are aware, I am always crunching numbers in order to better analyze teams and their talent and so I’ve continued to reﬁne my special teams formula throughout the years. In my ﬁrst magazine in 1995, the entire special teams grade consisted of just 4 categories. Since then, I’ve made a plethora of changes including some recent improvements. Years ago, before each team used and formulated net punting, I used it for both the team and their opponents, which also included punt returns and punt return defense that gave me a much more accurate number. Now, I’ve also added net kickoffs and with research, I discovered just how misleading KR and KR D categories really are. One quick example would be Kent St from 2012. The Flashes’ Dri Archer had 16 KR’s for a 36.9 avg so teams naturally kicked away from him and used many squib kicks. Kent St as a team ﬁnished #51 (avg 22.6 per/KR), but they were #1 in the country in average start position, which was at the 34.5 yard line, making them 50 spots better than their NCAA rank. After having just 4 categories to start as I mentioned above, I continued to look closely at the importance of the FG kicker. My current numbers now grade overall %, a breakdown of 10 yard increments, and also punishes misses based on a sliding scale. A kicker’s grade is hurt more by a missed short FG and much less if the miss was from 40-49 yards. I also gave no penalty for FG’s that were missed from 50+ because I feel that a very long made FG beneﬁts a team greatly, but a miss doesn’t negatively affect them (and just attempting it often means a team has an elite kicker). I also have a net td/blk’s category. A negative number means a team allowed more blocks & td’s than they garnered. A positive number means that they blocked more kicks and scored more td’s than they allowed. If a team blocked a punt AND returned the same punt for a td, I only give credit for one td/blk. However, if a team fumbled a punt snap and the other team recovered, I counted that as a blocked punt. I usually do not count blocked FG’s in the category as a missed FG has the same result and is not a game-changing play. The only time I do count a blocked FG, is if it was returned for a td. Finally, I also adjust each grade to weigh them on attempts or number of plays relative to all combined ST plays. Michigan is a good example from 2016 with its ﬁne season on offense and defense. They had 95 KO’s while their opponents only had 42 KO’s on the season, which means that I weighed their KO’s 2.26 more times than their opponents. Congratulations to Iowa for ﬁnishing #1 in my 2025 rankings & remember, you can receive weekly updates at PhilSteele.com every Friday during the football season, to see how well your favorite program’s special teams are really performing! In 2011, he released his ﬁrst National Coach of the Year Award for the FBS. The inaugural winner was Bill Snyder of Kansas State, who led the Wildcats to a 10-win season after they had not topped seven wins the previous seven seasons. This year Phil is proud to announce that the 15th annual winner of the National Collegiate Coach of the Year for 2025 is Curt Cignetti of Indiana. PHIL STEELE’S 2025 COACH OF THE YEAR Curt Cignetti moved from James Madison to Indiana of the Big Ten and did a remarkable job operating the portal and taking the Hoosiers to unexpected heights. In 2024 the Big Ten media picked his new team Indiana #17 out of 18 teams in the Big Ten Preseason Poll. Indiana went from a losing record to the playoff and he was my 2024 coach of the year. Last year many expected a step back but this time he guided the team to a perfect regular season at 12-0 including a road win at Oregon. They knocked off Ohio St in the Big Ten Title game for their ﬁrst Big Ten title since 1945. They went to the Rose Bowl for the ﬁrst time since 1967 and blew out Bama 38-3, destroyed Oregon 56-22 and beat Miami 27-21 for their ﬁrst-ever college football national title!! In two years, they are the only playoff team to win after the bye. That was good enough for coach Cignetti to be just the 2nd repeat winner of my award, joining Dabo Swinney of Clemson! I told coach Cignetti when I talked to him this spring that if he wins it again this year I may have to add his name to the trophy in the future. The award annually recognizes the nation’s Most Outstanding Offensive Line Unit that best displays toughness, effort, teamwork, consistency, technique and ﬁnishing. The voting body is comprised solely of people who played or coached the position, including all of the current offensive line coaches at the Division I/FBS level as well as former players, coaches, colleagues of Coach Moore and select media. Previous Award Winners Awarded to the Best Interior Lineman The Outland Trophy is awarded to the best United States college football interior lineman by the Football Writers Association of America. It is named after John H. Outland. One of only a few players ever to be named AllAmerica at two positions, Outland garnered consensus All-America honors in 1897 at tackle and consensus AllAmerica honors at halfback in 1898. The Football Writers Association of America, a nonproﬁt organization founded in 1941, consists of more than 1,200 men and women across North America who cover college football for a living. The membership includes journalists, broadcasters and publicists, as well as key executives in all the areas that involve the game. The FWAA works to govern areas that include gameday operations, major awards, a national poll and its annual All-America team. Previous Award Winners Nation's Best Collegiate Quarterback What began in 1977 as the Davey O’Brien Memorial Trophy, awarded to the best player in the Southwest region, was expanded in scope and limited to the quarterback position in 1981, becoming the Davey O’Brien National Quarterback Award®. The Davey O’Brien is awarded to the nation’s best collegiate quarterback, evaluating each candidate on the criteria of quarterback skills/athletic ability, academics, reputation as a team player, character, leadership and sportsmanship. The award honors the legacy of Davey O’Brien, the ﬁrst player ever to win the Heisman, Maxwell and Walter Camp trophies in the same year, while leading TCU to one of their two National Championships. The Davey O’Brien National Quarterback Award is overseen by the Davey O’Brien Foundation, which is headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas, and provides scholarships and university grants to help high school and college athletes transform leadership on the ﬁeld into leadership in life. Finalists must exemplify Davey O’Brien’s enduring character while exhibiting teamwork, sportsmanship, leadership and character in both the athletic and academic arenas. Jim Thorpe Award Best Collegiate Defensive Back The Jim Thorpe Award is one of college football’s most sought after and prestigious awards. It is named after history’s greatest all-around athlete, a man who excelled not only as a running back, passer and kicker on oﬀense, but also was an awesome defensive back. Recognized in the Pro Football Hall of Fame simply as “The Legend,” Thorpe also played professional baseball and won Olympic gold medals in the decathlon and pentathlon. The candidates for the award are selected by a screening committee of Jim Thorpe Association members who follow several players throughout the season, watching games and researching information sources to grade Thorpe Award candidates on the basis of performance on the ﬁeld, athletic ability and character. The committee then narrows the ﬁeld down to three ﬁnalists and the names of these ﬁnalists are submitted to a national panel of about 50 sports writers, sportscasters, coaches and former players who vote to determine the winner. Each week during the football season, Phil Steele reviews the candidates issued by the school, the conference and distinguished committee members. After including Phil's own personal input, the weekly winner is announced every Thursday at oklahomasportshalloﬀame.org and PhilSteele.com.
